findings.title: The avatar has three hub components, not one: PlayerNetworking (identity/weapons/IK/interaction), MasterController (locomotion/stamina/weight/camera), Health (damage/ragdoll/death)
findings.detail: Reverse-lookup over every Assembly-CSharp field type shows PlayerNetworking is referenced by ~37 sibling components (ADSFixed, ADSHead, ADS_Neck, ArmStamina, BetterFuckingSmoother, CameraSettings, Camera_Rotation_Tracker, CharacterCounterLook, CharacterCustomisation, CharacterRotator, Character_FollowCamera, EmoteSystem, FeetIK, FreeLook, FullBodyInteraction, GarminGPS, Grenade, Health, HunchControl, InteractableChair, MasterController, Melee, MissionLaptop, nvgController, PlayerVaultSystem, RaycastingOptimisation, ScopeInputSetter, Tablet, TpToggle, VaultIK, WeaponSafety, WeaponStance, WeaponSwitching, WhiteBoardDrawer, TeamID, GameManager.myPlayerNetworking, PlayerMaster.PlayerSpawnedObject). MasterController is referenced by 10 (ADSFixed, ArmStamina.fpsController, AudioOcclusion.fpsController, CharacterCustomisationController, DeadZone, FeetIK, Health, PlayerNetworking, PlayerVaultSystem, ProceduralWeaponBob) plus Il2CppCMF.AdvancedWalkerController.masterController. Health is referenced by 16 including BrainAI, Bullet/BulletInstance.shootersGameObject, CharAnimationHelper, ImpactSFX, InteractionControl, MedicalSystem, HealthUI, PlayerConsoleCommands. MasterController owns the physiology sub-objects directly: vaultSystem→PlayerVaultSystem, characterNetworking→CharacterNetworking, playerStance→PlayerStance, playerLean→PlayerLean, characterAudio→CharacterAudio, health→Health, playerNetworking→PlayerNetworking, walkerController→Il2CppCMF.AdvancedWalkerController, mover→Il2CppCMF.Mover, cameraController→Il2CppCMF.CameraController, cameraMouseInput→Il2CppCMF.CameraMouseInput, rigidBody, characterCollider (CapsuleCollider).
findings.members: Il2Cpp.PlayerNetworking, Il2Cpp.MasterController, Il2Cpp.Health, MasterController.vaultSystem/characterNetworking/playerStance/playerLean/characterAudio/walkerController/mover
findings.modding: Resolve everything from PlayerNetworking — it is the only component nearly every sibling caches a reference to. GameManager.myPlayerNetworking gives you the local avatar without any scene search.

findings.title: Client-authority is implemented as a second networked GameObject per player: PlayerMasterClientSide and PlayerNetworkingClientSide, each with a ServerSide back-reference
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.PlayerNetworkingClientSide holds SyncVars the client must write directly: NetworkLeanValue (float), NetworkikTargetPosition (Vector3), NetworkCharacterRotationY (float), NetworkneckIkTargetPosition (Vector3), NetworkmapOpened, NetworkisProne, NetworkisCrouch, NetworkisSprinting, NetworkisRunning, NetworkPlayer_Recoil_Multiplier, plus SyncList<MagazineSyncInfo> MagsList. It carries its own client-side interpolation state (old/new + LastReceiveTime + updateInterval triplets for ikTargetPosition, CharacterRotationY, neckIkTargetPosition) and hooks OnMapOpened/OnProneUpdated/OnCrouchUpdated. Il2Cpp.PlayerMasterClientSide holds NetworkIsLoaded and NetworkRespawnRequester plus static NumPlayersReady, ServerSide→PlayerMaster, AfkTimer, ProcessAFK(). Both expose `ServerSide` pointing back at the authoritative twin.
findings.members: PlayerNetworkingClientSide.ServerSide, PlayerMasterClientSide.ServerSide, NetworkisProne/isCrouch/isSprinting/isRunning, MagsList, PlayerMasterClientSide.NumPlayersReady
findings.modding: To read another player's stance you must read PlayerNetworkingClientSide, not PlayerNetworking or MasterController. To read your own you read MasterController/PlayerStance. Anything that writes stance must write the ClientSide object or it will not replicate.

findings.title: Stance and lean are replicated twice, by two independent mechanisms
findings.detail: Path A: MasterController.CMD_UpdateValues(float playerStanceOutput, float playerLeanOutput) -> RPC_UpdateValues(same) writes Il2Cpp.CharacterNetworking.playerStanceOutput/playerLeanOutput, throttled by CharacterNetworking.updateTime/updateTimer, and CharacterNetworking.noAuthLeanAnimator/leanTarget (CopyTarget) drive the remote avatar. Path B: PlayerNetworkingClientSide SyncVars NetworkisProne, NetworkisCrouch (with hooks OnProneUpdated/OnCrouchUpdated) and NetworkLeanValue. Both carry lean; A carries a continuous float, B a float plus discrete bools. Nothing in the signatures ties them together.
findings.members: MasterController.CMD_UpdateValues/RPC_UpdateValues, CharacterNetworking.playerStanceOutput/playerLeanOutput/updateTime, PlayerNetworkingClientSide.NetworkLeanValue/NetworkisProne/NetworkisCrouch
findings.modding: If you change stance behaviour you have to keep both channels consistent or remote avatars will visually disagree with the isProne/isCrouch bools that gameplay code reads.

findings.title: PlayerStance, PlayerLean, CharacterNetworking and CharacterAudio are data-only classes with zero methods — all their logic lives inside MasterController
findings.detail: Each has only .ctor/.cctor plus fields. PlayerStance: OverallSpeedModifer/Min/Max, isCrouched, isProne, ProneTransition, crouchSpeedmultiplier, proneSpeedmultiplier, output, inputClampMin/Max, outputMin/Max, ColliderHeight, ColliderHeightMultiplier, Stand_/Crouch_/Prone_outputMultiplier, cameraParent + cameraParent_Stand/_Crouch, transitionSpeed, camTransformMultiplier, mouseSens. PlayerLean: blockTransform/blockCentre/blockSize + leanTargetLayer + wallDistanceMultiplier (wall-proximity lean suppression), anim, weapLeanAnim, weapLeanSpeed, outputMaxStand/outputMaxCrouched. CharacterAudio: baseAudioSourceVolume, baseFoleyVolume, multiplierudioSourceVolume [sic], w_footStepTimer, j_footStepTimer, FootstepMaterialMask. CharacterNetworking: updateTime/updateTimer + the two output floats + noAuthLeanAnimator + leanTarget.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.PlayerStance, Il2Cpp.PlayerLean, Il2Cpp.CharacterNetworking, Il2Cpp.CharacterAudio
findings.modding: There is no method on these to patch. Behaviour changes must go through MasterController.Update/LateUpdate/FixedUpdate or through writing the fields — and per the established constraint, Harmony cannot patch il2cpp field accessors, so field writes must be done imperatively from your own tick.

findings.title: Il2Cpp.FirstPersonController, Il2Cpp.Stance and Il2Cpp.PlayerCanvas are completely empty husks — dead predecessors of the current player
findings.detail: A pass over the whole Assembly-CSharp type index for types whose only members are .ctor/.cctor returns 53 types. Among them: FirstPersonController, Stance, PlayerCanvas, and also Door, DoorHandle, DoorHandleInteraction, Helicopter, LobbyController, Flashlight, BulletPooled, BulletFlyBy, LeftHandGrabTP. This is the same V1→V2/V3 rewrite pattern already seen for doors (DoorV2) and helicopters (HelicopterV2/V3): the old class is left in metadata with nothing in it. Il2Cpp.PlayerSpawnDetails still declares `fpsController` typed Il2Cpp.FirstPersonController — a stale field pointing at the gutted type.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.FirstPersonController (empty), Il2Cpp.Stance (empty), Il2Cpp.PlayerCanvas (empty), PlayerSpawnDetails.fpsController
findings.modding: Do not target FirstPersonController; the real player controller is MasterController + Il2CppCMF.AdvancedWalkerController. PlayerSpawnDetails.fpsController will always be null-ish.

findings.title: Il2Cpp.PlayerMovement and Il2Cpp.FPS_RigidbodyFirstPersonController are third-party demo scripts, not the game player
findings.detail: script_paths.txt places PlayerMovement at \Assets\Samples\High Definition RP\17.0.3\Water Samples\Scripts\PlayerMovement.cs (it has a foamGeneratorParent field and a UnityEngine.CharacterController), and FPS_RigidbodyFirstPersonController at \Assets\_vfx\KriptoFX\MuzzleFlashes\Scripts\Demo\FPS_RigidbodyFirstPersonController.cs (it owns Il2Cpp.FPS_MouseLook, MovementSettings/AdvancedSettings nested structs). Neither references any Il2Cpp.Player* type. Il2Cpp.SurvivalPlayer is also methodless — only _master (PlayerMaster), Score, Kills — likely an unfinished mode.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.PlayerMovement, Il2Cpp.FPS_RigidbodyFirstPersonController, Il2Cpp.FPS_MouseLook, Il2Cpp.SurvivalPlayer
findings.modding: Ignore all three. They pollute name searches for "player controller".

findings.title: Damage model: 7 limbs plus two pseudo-parts, per-limb HP SyncVars, per-limb bleed rate SyncVars, and fractures on limbs only
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.HealthBodyPart = Head, Chest, Stomach, LArm, RArm, LLeg, RLeg, SERVER, NONE (byte enum). Health carries paired init/current floats: initHeadHP/HeadHP, initChestHP/ChestHP, initStomachHP/StomachHP, initArmLHP/LArmHP, initArmRHP/RArmHP, initLegsLHP/LLegHP, initLegsRHP/RLegHP, plus initTotalHP/TotalHP as a separate pool. Every one of HeadHP..RLegHP and TotalHP is a Mirror SyncVar (NetworkHeadHP … NetworkTotalHP). Bleeding is seven SyncVar floats BleedingDamage_Head/_Chest/_Stomach/_LArm/_RArm/_LLeg/_RLeg — i.e. bleeding is a per-limb damage RATE, ticked by a single BleedTime/_BleedTimer pair. Fractures are only four bools: NetworkFractured_LArm/_RArm/_LLeg/_RLeg — head, chest and stomach cannot fracture. Cross-limb bleed-through is three scalars ArmsDamageCross, StomachDamageCross, LegsDamageCross consumed by ProcessCrossDamage(float _damage, HealthBodyPart _bodyPart, HealthBodyPart crossedDamage, int shooterID, Vector3 damageSourcePosition).
findings.members: HealthBodyPart{Head,Chest,Stomach,LArm,RArm,LLeg,RLeg,SERVER,NONE}, Health.NetworkHeadHP…NetworkRLegHP, Health.NetworkBleedingDamage_*, Health.NetworkFractured_LArm/RArm/LLeg/RLeg, Health.ArmsDamageCross/StomachDamageCross/LegsDamageCross, Health.ProcessCrossDamage
findings.modding: Adding a body part is a deep change: it needs a new enum value plus a new SyncVar HP field, a new BleedingDamage_ field, hitbox tag mapping, and matching HealthUIPartGFX/UIHealthLimb entries. Adjusting existing limb HP is trivial — write initXHP before Awake or the current XHP at runtime.

findings.title: Damage entry points: CMDTakeDamage / CMDTakeDamageFromPosition are the network doors; TakeDamage(4-arg) is itself a weaved networked method
findings.detail: Health exposes CMDTakeDamage(float _damage, HealthBodyPart _bodyPart, HealthBodyPart crossedDamage, int shooterID), CMDTakeDamageFromPosition(same + Vector3 position), a plain TakeDamage(float, HealthBodyPart, HealthBodyPart, int, Vector3 DamageSourcePosition), and a second TakeDamage(float, HealthBodyPart, HealthBodyPart, int) that HAS a UserCode_TakeDamage__Single__HealthBodyPart__HealthBodyPart__Int32 wrapper — meaning the 4-arg overload is Mirror-weaved, not a local call. Bleeding and fractures are inflicted through their own commands: CMD_Bleed(HealthBodyPart, float _damage, int shooterID), CMD_Fracture(HealthBodyPart, int shooterID) -> RPC_Fractured(), and repaired via CMD_StopBleeding(HealthBodyPart Limb), CMD_FixFracture(HealthBodyPart) -> RPC_FixFracture(). Death is Die(HealthBodyPart causeOfDeath, int shooterID), also weaved, with MyCauseOfDeath and MyKiller (PlayerMaster) recorded, plus ProcessDeathServer(), CheckDeath(), _deathProcessed, deadChecked. Environmental damage arrives via Il2Cpp.DamageZone.ApplyDamageOverTime(Health victim) using DamageAmount/DamageInterval over a HashSet<Health> victims.
findings.members: Health.CMDTakeDamage, Health.CMDTakeDamageFromPosition, Health.TakeDamage (weaved 4-arg), Health.CMD_Bleed, Health.CMD_Fracture, Health.CMD_StopBleeding, Health.CMD_FixFracture, Health.Die, Health.MyKiller, Health.MyCauseOfDeath, DamageZone.ApplyDamageOverTime
findings.modding: Hook UserCode_CMDTakeDamage__… and UserCode_Die__HealthBodyPart__Int32 on the server side to intercept or scale all damage and all deaths. shooterID is an int, matching PlayerMaster.UniqueID, so attribution is available without object refs.

findings.title: There is no downed/revive system. Death produces a separately-damageable ragdoll that bleeds out, then respawn is teammate-requestable
findings.detail: The only Revive() in the entire game assembly is on Il2Cpp.HealthTestRagdoll, a debug component (MaxHealth, currentHealth, minPinWeight, ArmsMappingWeight, SpineMappingWeight, RootMotion.Dynamics.PuppetMaster). The real flow is: Die -> ProcessDeathServer -> ragdoll enabled -> the corpse gets its own SyncVar NetworkRagdollHealth with TakeRagdollDamage(float), SERVER_ReduceRagdollHealth(), ragdollBleedoutTime/ragdollBleedoutTimer, RPC_RagdollBleedout(), ragdollDead — so corpses remain shootable and bleed out on a timer. Il2Cpp.VoiceCategory has a dedicated BleedoutDeath member alongside Hit, HitBadly, Death, NearDeath, Bleeding, ThroatShots. Respawn is PlayerMasterClientSide.NetworkRespawnRequester (int SyncVar, hook OnRespawnRequestChange(int,int)) + unsyncedRespawnRequester + _respawnRequested + StartRespawnProcess() + AutoSpawnPlayer() coroutine + DestroyAllMyWeapons(), driven from PlayerMaster.CLIENT_RequestAutoRespawn() and KillPlayerForAutoSpawn(). The requester being an int rather than a bool is the closest thing to a revive: someone else's UniqueID can trigger your respawn.
findings.members: Health.NetworkRagdollHealth, Health.TakeRagdollDamage, Health.SERVER_ReduceRagdollHealth, Health.RPC_RagdollBleedout, Health.ragdollBleedoutTime, VoiceCategory.BleedoutDeath, PlayerMasterClientSide.NetworkRespawnRequester/StartRespawnProcess/AutoSpawnPlayer, PlayerMaster.CLIENT_RequestAutoRespawn, HealthTestRagdoll.Revive
findings.modding: A downed-state mod has real scaffolding to build on: the ragdoll bleedout timer is already a server-authoritative countdown and RespawnRequester already carries an initiator ID. What is missing is any get-up path — ForceDeathPose() and SetRatdollToSleep exist but nothing restores control.

findings.title: MedicalSystem is almost entirely client-local — tourniquets, pain and heart rate never leave the machine
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.MedicalSystem has exactly one SyncVar (NetworkcurrentMorphineInUse) and exactly one Command (CMD_AdjustMorphineValue(int)). Everything else is local: PainLevel, purePain, HeartRate, targetHeartRate, risePerSecond/fallPerSecond, activeEffects, and all five tourniquet flags Tourniquet_Head, Tourniquet_LArm, Tourniquet_RArm, Tourniquet_LLeg, Tourniquet_RLeg, plus tourniquetDamageTimer/tourniquetDamageTime (the tourniquet's own damage-over-time). The item handlers ProcessBandage(HealthBodyPart), ProcessTourniquet(), ProcessAddTourniquet/ProcessRemoveTourniquet(HealthBodyPart), ProcessSplint, ProcessHemostaticInjector, ProcessPressureDressing, ProcessAntiBiotics, ProcessBlood are all plain methods. Only their consequences reach the server, via Health.CMD_StopBleeding and Health.CMD_FixFracture.
findings.members: MedicalSystem.NetworkcurrentMorphineInUse, MedicalSystem.CMD_AdjustMorphineValue, MedicalSystem.Tourniquet_Head/_LArm/_RArm/_LLeg/_RLeg, MedicalSystem.tourniquetDamageTimer, MedicalSystem.PainLevel/HeartRate/purePain
findings.modding: Two consequences. (1) No other client and not the server knows you have a tourniquet on — a teammate medic UI is impossible without adding SyncVars. (2) Because the client decides when to call CMD_StopBleeding, a modified client can stop bleeding with no item; the server does no validation visible in the signatures.

findings.title: Nine medical item types applied by dragging an inventory item onto a limb widget
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.InventoryItem/ItemType = Empty, Tourniquet, Bandage, Morphine, Splint, HemostaticInjector, PressureDressing, AntiBiotics, Blood. InventoryItem carries ItemName, maxUses, currentUses, Weight, UseTime, tooltip text, and implements the drag handlers OnBeginDrag/OnDrag/OnEndDrag plus OnItemUsed(). Il2Cpp.UIHealthLimb implements OnDrop/OnDropLimb(InventoryItem) and holds a HealthBodyPart part — so the application gesture is literally drag-item-onto-limb, and MedicalSystem.UseItem(InventoryItem item, HealthBodyPart bodyPart) + selectedLimb + itemUseTimer + useSlider are the commit path. MedicalSystem.AddItemsToInventory/AddToInventory/RemoveFromInventory manage List<InventoryItem> inventoryItems against List<InventorySlot> inventorySlots.
findings.members: InventoryItem/ItemType{Empty,Tourniquet,Bandage,Morphine,Splint,HemostaticInjector,PressureDressing,AntiBiotics,Blood}, MedicalSystem.UseItem, UIHealthLimb.OnDropLimb, InventoryItem.Weight/maxUses/currentUses/UseTime
findings.modding: A new medical item needs a new ItemType enum value (enum extension is not possible in il2cpp) — so realistically you reskin an existing type or intercept MedicalSystem.UseItem and branch on ItemName instead of itemType. InventoryItem.Weight feeds the encumbrance system, so items are not free.

findings.title: Encumbrance: total weight gates jog and sprint by hard thresholds and multiplies fall damage through a curve
findings.detail: MasterController holds totalWeight, basePlayerWeight, noSprintWeight, noJogWeight, maxWeight, maxWeightSpeedPenalty, weightFallDamageCurve (AnimationCurve), weightRecalcInterval/weightRecalcTimer, and the methods CalculateTotalWeight(), GetWeightSpeedMultiplier() -> float, GetWeightFallDamageMultiplier() -> float. The two named thresholds noJogWeight and noSprintWeight are almost certainly hard cutoffs that clamp RunState (MasterController/RunState = Walk, Jog, Sprint) rather than a smooth penalty, with maxWeightSpeedPenalty applying the continuous part up to maxWeight. Weight is recomputed on an interval, not per frame. HealthUI surfaces it as `weight` + WeightSlider/WeightSliderImage with weightfull/weightempty colours.
findings.members: MasterController.totalWeight/basePlayerWeight/noSprintWeight/noJogWeight/maxWeight/maxWeightSpeedPenalty/weightFallDamageCurve, MasterController.CalculateTotalWeight/GetWeightSpeedMultiplier/GetWeightFallDamageMultiplier, MasterController/RunState{Walk,Jog,Sprint}
findings.modding: Call CalculateTotalWeight() after you add or remove gear or the change will not register until weightRecalcTimer elapses. The cutoff semantics of noJogWeight/noSprintWeight are the one part I cannot prove statically — probe by setting totalWeight directly and watching runState.

findings.title: Two independent stamina systems, with an escalating penalty on repeated sprint exhaustion
findings.detail: Leg stamina lives on MasterController: sprintStamina, staminaDrainRate, staminaRecoveryRate, weightDrainMultiplier (weight accelerates drain), sprintStaminaThreshold, sprintStaminaDepleted, staminaDepletedTimer, staminaDepletionCount (int), currentStaminaDelay interpolated between staminaDepletedDelay and maxStaminaDelay, driven by UpdateSprintStamina(). The presence of staminaDepletionCount together with a currentStaminaDelay bounded by two named delays means each successive exhaustion lengthens the lockout. Breathing SFX are a separate driver, UpdateSprintBreathingSFX(): breathingAudioSource, sprintBreathingClips[], outOfBreathClips[], breathingMaxVolume, breathingFadeSpeed, breathingFadeInStamina, outOfBreathStamina, breathingVolume, outOfBreathPlayed. Arm stamina is a separate component Il2Cpp.ArmStamina: armStamina, drain, drainRate, recoveryRate, StaticDrainRateMultiplier, isMounted, plus a breath-hold subsystem Breath/breathMin/breathMax/breathSpeed/holdBreathTime/_holdBreathTimer, ToggleArmStam(), synced on updateSyncTime via PlayerNetworking SyncVars NetworkarmStamina and NetworkdrainArmStamina (set through CMD_SET_ARMSTAMINATARGET(float)).
findings.members: MasterController.sprintStamina/staminaDepletionCount/currentStaminaDelay/UpdateSprintStamina, MasterController.sprintBreathingClips/outOfBreathClips, Il2Cpp.ArmStamina.armStamina/Breath/holdBreathTime/ToggleArmStam, PlayerNetworking.CMD_SET_ARMSTAMINATARGET/NetworkarmStamina
findings.modding: Leg stamina is entirely local to MasterController and never networked — only arm stamina is replicated. A stamina mod therefore needs no netcode work for sprint but does for weapon sway.

findings.title: Fall damage is per-leg when standing and single-value when prone, and rolls fracture and two bleed tiers separately
findings.detail: MasterController.ProcessFall(Vector3 velocity) dispatches to either TakeFallDamageStanding(float damageL, float damageR, float fractureChance, float bleedingChance, float heavybleedingChance) — note the separate left/right leg damage and the two distinct bleed probabilities — or TakeFallDamageProne(float damage, float bleeding, float fractureChance), a single lumped value with no heavy-bleed roll. Inputs come from the modified CMF controller: Il2CppCMF.AdvancedWalkerController exposes LastAirborneDuration and LastFallDistance (with backing _airborneStartTime/_lastAirborneDuration/_airborneStartHeight/_lastFallDistance), which are not part of stock CMF. MasterController also tracks wasGroundedLastFrame and velocityLastFrame. Audio feedback goes out over PlayerNetworking.CMD_PlayFallSound(float volume)/RPC_PlayFallSound and CMD_PlayBoneBreakSound(float volume)/RPC_PlayBoneBreakSound. The two bleed tiers match Il2Cpp.HealthUIPartGFX.isLightBleeding/isHeavyBleeding.
findings.members: MasterController.ProcessFall/TakeFallDamageStanding/TakeFallDamageProne, AdvancedWalkerController.LastFallDistance/LastAirborneDuration, PlayerNetworking.CMD_PlayFallSound/CMD_PlayBoneBreakSound, HealthUIPartGFX.isLightBleeding/isHeavyBleeding
findings.modding: Going prone before impact is mechanically different, not just cosmetic — it removes the heavy-bleed roll entirely and collapses two legs into one damage number.

findings.title: The vault system is bespoke (Bezier + custom CMF state), not the KINEMATION MotionWarping asset that ships alongside it
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.PlayerVaultSystem/VaultType = StepOver, Vault, Mantle, ClimbUp. TryVault() -> ExecuteMovement(Vector3 startPos, Vector3 edgeTop, Vector3 landingPoint, Vector3 forward, Vector3 obstacleNormal, VaultType, float obstacleHeight, float obstacleDepth) coroutine, with CubicBezier(p0..p3,t) and EstimateBezierLength(p0..p3,segments) doing the trajectory. Detection params: obstacleLayer, detectionRange, minHeight, maxHeight, clearanceRadius, vaultDepthThreshold, maxVaultDepth, landingCheckDist, maxLandingDrop, vaultDepthPerSpeed, maxMovementDepthBonus, stepOverMax, vaultMax, with non-allocating _downHitsBuffer/_overlapBuffer. It temporarily swaps the capsule via _savedColliderHeight/_vaultColliderHeight. CMF integration is a purpose-added state: AdvancedWalkerController.EnterVaultState()/ExitVaultState()/IsVaulting() and ControllerState = Grounded, Sliding, Falling, Rising, Jumping, **Vaulting**. Replication is a CMD/RPC trio: CMD_SyncVaultStart(int vaultTypeInt, Vector3 edgeTop, Vector3 fwd, Vector3 normal, float height, float depth)/RPC_SyncVaultStart, CMD_SyncVaultRelease/RPC_SyncVaultRelease, CMD_SyncVaultEnd/RPC_SyncVaultEnd. Il2Cpp.VaultIK drives the hand with FinalIK InteractionObject + FullBodyBipedIK and holds offset curves named vaultOffsetX/Y/Z and climbOffsetX/Y/Z plus sway sets for vault, climb and stepOver — but nothing named mantle, and its state flags are only _isClimb and _isStepOver. Mantle therefore shares the climb IK path.
findings.members: PlayerVaultSystem/VaultType{StepOver,Vault,Mantle,ClimbUp}, PlayerVaultSystem.ExecuteMovement/CubicBezier/CMD_SyncVaultStart, AdvancedWalkerController/ControllerState.Vaulting, VaultIK.vaultOffsetX/climbOffsetX/_isClimb/_isStepOver, PlayerVaultSystem/VaultIKData{isActive,vaultType,edgeTop,forward,obstacleNormal,obstacleHeight,obstacleDepth,t}
findings.modding: CMD_SyncVaultStart takes the vault type as a raw int and the full geometry as arguments, so a mod can synthesise arbitrary vaults over arbitrary geometry without the detection pass. VaultIKData.t is the normalised progress, useful for hooking mid-vault.

findings.title: Emotes are string-keyed animator states routed through PlayerNetworking, and the emote wheel hangs off Health
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.EmoteSystem is tiny: StartInteraction(string _animationName), EndEmote(), and fields animator, parentAnimator, mainEmoteHand (FinalIK InteractionObject), playerNetworking, canEmote. The network path is PlayerNetworking.PlayEmote(string animation) -> CMD_PlayEmote(string) -> RPC_PlayEmote(string). Oddly the wheel selection handler lives on Health, not EmoteSystem: Health.selectEmote(Il2CppShellanderGames.WeaponWheel.SgSliceController item).
findings.members: EmoteSystem.StartInteraction(string), EmoteSystem.canEmote, PlayerNetworking.PlayEmote/CMD_PlayEmote/RPC_PlayEmote, Health.selectEmote
findings.modding: This is the cheapest animation surface in the whole avatar: the animation is a string sent over the wire, so adding emotes means adding animator states and calling PlayerNetworking.PlayEmote("YourState"). No enum, no index list, no prefab registration.

findings.title: Health has no Update — it is externally ticked via CallUpdate() and distance-culled
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Health defines Awake, Start, OnStartClient, OnEnable, OnDisable and CallUpdate() but no Update or FixedUpdate. It carries checkTime, CullDistance, beingForceCulled, and cullBehaviour (Behaviour[]) — so an external manager drives it and disables it beyond CullDistance. It also serves both players and AI from the same class: isBot, V2AIMode, brainAI (Il2Cpp.BrainAI), ProcessAIDamage(RagdollAnimator2BoneIndicator indic, int hitboxIndex, RaycastHit _hit, float _damage, int shooterID, float _bleedChance, float _bleedDamage), CMDProcessAIAnimation(int hitboxIndex, Vector3 direction)/RPCProcessAIAnimation. Hitboxes are resolved by name: GetHitBoxes() coroutine builds List<Transform> hitboxes plus Dictionary<string,int> _hitboxIndexByName, queried by GetHitboxIndex(string name), and GetBodyPartFromTag(string tag) maps a collider tag to a HealthBodyPart.
findings.members: Health.CallUpdate, Health.CullDistance/beingForceCulled/cullBehaviour, Health.isBot/V2AIMode/brainAI, Health.GetHitboxIndex(string), Health.GetBodyPartFromTag(string), Health.ProcessAIDamage
findings.modding: Patching Health.Update will without warning do nothing — hook CallUpdate. Any change to Health affects bots as well as players; gate on isBot. New hitboxes can be registered purely by naming/tagging colliders, no code change, since lookup is string-keyed.

findings.title: Static registries let you enumerate players without any scene search
findings.detail: Health.AllAlivePlayers is a static HashSet<Il2Cpp.Health>. PlayerMaster.AllPlayerMasters is a static List<Il2Cpp.PlayerMaster>, PlayerMaster.MyPlayerMaster is the local one, PlayerMaster.AvailableUniqueIDS is a static Queue<int> feeding UniqueID, and PlayerMaster exposes a static Action OnPlayerCountChanged. PlayerMasterClientSide.NumPlayersReady is a static int. GameManager.myPlayerNetworking gives the local avatar.
findings.members: Health.AllAlivePlayers, PlayerMaster.AllPlayerMasters/MyPlayerMaster/OnPlayerCountChanged/AvailableUniqueIDS, PlayerMasterClientSide.NumPlayersReady, GameManager.myPlayerNetworking
findings.modding: Directly resolves the established "never call FindObjectsOfTypeAll per frame" constraint. Subscribe to PlayerMaster.OnPlayerCountChanged instead of polling.

findings.title: PlayerConsoleCommands gives you a ready-made damage and death probe
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.PlayerConsoleCommands holds a Health reference and exposes KillPlayer(), CheckHealth(), TakeDamage(int amount, Il2Cpp.HealthBodyPart part) and ShowRandomizeMovieButton(). These are QFSW Quantum Console commands (the game ships QFSW Quantum Console and an Il2Cpp.DevCommandAttribute type, itself empty).
findings.members: PlayerConsoleCommands.TakeDamage(int, HealthBodyPart), PlayerConsoleCommands.KillPlayer, PlayerConsoleCommands.CheckHealth, Il2Cpp.DevCommandAttribute
findings.modding: Fastest way to settle every runtime question in this area: drive limb damage, fractures and death from the console rather than writing a test harness. Whether the console is reachable in a retail build is the one thing to verify at runtime.

findings.title: Weapon slot enums disagree between the player and the weapon
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.PlayerNetworking/WeaponSlot = None, Primary, SecondPrimary, Secondary, SpecialPurpose, Grenade. Il2Cpp.WeaponV3/WeaponSlotType = Primary, Secondary, SpecialPurpose only — there is no SecondPrimary on the weapon side. PlayerNetworking nonetheless keeps four distinct weapon references (primaryWeapon, secondPrimaryWeapon, secondaryWeapon, specialPurposeWeapon), four SyncVar IDs (NetworkPrimaryWeaponID, NetworkSecondPrimaryWeaponID, NetworkSecondaryWeaponID, NetworkSpecialPurposeWeaponID) and four holster transforms (PrimaryHolster, SecondPrimaryHolster, SecondaryHolster, SpecialPurposeHolster).
findings.members: PlayerNetworking/WeaponSlot{None,Primary,SecondPrimary,Secondary,SpecialPurpose,Grenade}, WeaponV3/WeaponSlotType{Primary,Secondary,SpecialPurpose}, PlayerNetworking.secondPrimaryWeapon/SecondPrimaryHolster
findings.modding: A custom weapon cannot declare itself as SecondPrimary — the second-primary slot must be assigned player-side. Any loadout code that round-trips through WeaponV3's own slot type will lose that distinction.

findings.title: Three separate voice stacks are present, and the player uses MetaVoiceChat rather than Dissonance
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.PlayerVoice (script path \Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\VoiceChat\PlayerVoice.cs) holds VoiceChatComponent typed Il2CppMetaVoiceChat.MetaVc, plus VoipSource, voipVolumeGroup (AudioMixerGroup), RadioLowpass/RadioHighpass/RadioNoise/RadioStartBeep/RadioEndBeep, SyncVar NetworkIsRadioChat with CMD_SetChatType(bool isRadio)/OnChatTypeChanged, ActivateRadio/DeactivateRadio/ResetRadioState, SetPlayerVolume(float)/SetPlayerMuted(bool). Separately PlayerMaster.voiceChat is typed Il2Cpp.SteamworksVoiceChat, and Dissonance+Concentus are also shipped (Il2Cpp.NetworkedCharacterVoicePlayer, Dissonance.Core.* types). PlayerMaster additionally has SetRadioStatus(bool)/OnRadioUpdate + SyncVar NetworkradioUpdate, NetworkisTalking, ResetVoiceForSceneChange/ServerResetVoiceState and a VOIP_UI_DELAY coroutine.
findings.members: PlayerVoice.VoiceChatComponent (Il2CppMetaVoiceChat.MetaVc), PlayerVoice.NetworkIsRadioChat, PlayerMaster.voiceChat (Il2Cpp.SteamworksVoiceChat), Il2Cpp.NetworkedCharacterVoicePlayer
findings.modding: DEV-CONFIRMED: the OPERATOR developers confirm this middleware is not used. Edgegap in particular is never touched and is present only because Mirror bundles it. The established note that voice is "Dissonance+Concentus" is incomplete — proximity/radio voice on the player runs through MetaVoiceChat. Which of the three is actually live at runtime needs a probe (check which component is enabled on a spawned player).

findings.title: Camera, viewmodel and third-person body are a stack of small LateUpdate followers, and third person is a shipped toggle
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.FPS_Holder.LateUpdate follows Head/RotationTrackerObject/Camera against Il2CppCMF.CameraController with TrackRotation, and exposes StartPositionBlend(float duration) mirroring MasterController.StartSeatPositionBlend(float)/IsSeatBlending/_seatBlendStartPos/_seatBlendTimer/_seatBlendDuration for vehicle seating. Il2Cpp.Camera_Rotation_Tracker copies selected axes (CopyX/CopyY/CopyZ) from the CameraController onto a target. Il2Cpp.Character_FollowCamera has modes isTracker/isTrackerPosition/isTrackerPositionAndRotation, separate Target/TargetNoAuth pairs, and an InVehicle flag, with Resolve()/SnapToTarget()/ResetTargets(). Il2Cpp.BetterFuckingSmoother interpolates a tracked Rigidbody for a list of Followers with YDamping/SnapYHeight/SnapRotation. Il2Cpp.TpToggle is a working third-person switch: ToggleThirdPerson(), SetThirdPersonCameraFOV(float), SetThirdPersonCameraZPosition(float), SetThirdPersonCameraYPosition(float), with FPSCamera/TPCamera/Legs/Feet/TPRoot/FPRoot and inThirdPerson. Body IK is FinalIK throughout: PlayerNetworking.aimIK (AimIK), lookatIK (LookAtIK), grounderIK (GrounderFBBIK), interactionSystem, TP_LArm/TP_RArm (ArmIK), kickBipedIK (FullBodyBipedIK), plus Il2Cpp.FeetIK (updateLegs/updateLegsProne, LoseBalanceDistance, MaxBendWeight) and Il2Cpp.CharAnimationHelper (blink via headMesh blendshapes, UpdateIK_L/UpdateIK_R coroutines, mag pouch parents).
findings.members: Il2Cpp.FPS_Holder, Il2Cpp.Camera_Rotation_Tracker, Il2Cpp.Character_FollowCamera, Il2Cpp.BetterFuckingSmoother, Il2Cpp.TpToggle.ToggleThirdPerson, Il2Cpp.FeetIK.updateLegsProne, Il2Cpp.CharAnimationHelper, MasterController.StartSeatPositionBlend
findings.modding: TpToggle is a complete third-person camera already wired to Legs/Feet/TPRoot visibility — a free-camera or spectator mod should drive it rather than reimplement one. Il2Cpp.ScreenshotFreeCamera is also referenced from PlayerNetworking.freeCamera.

findings.title: Camera shake, recoil and suppression flinch are four KINEMATION RecoilAnimation instances on MasterController
findings.detail: MasterController holds CameraRecoil, CameraHitShake, CameraShake and CameraSuppressionFlinch, all typed Il2CppKinemation.FPSFramework.Runtime.Recoil.RecoilAnimation, plus two RecoilAnimData assets HitShake and SuppressionFlinch, a cameraRecoilTransform, and helicopter-specific HeliShakeMultiplier/HeliShakeImpuseTime/_heliShakeImpuseTimer. Weapon and camera bob are Il2CppWeaponBobbingV2.BobStyle2 instances weaponBob and cameraBob configured by Il2Cpp.WeaponBobParameters. Suppression arrives over the wire via PlayerNetworking.SERVER_GetSuppressed()/RPC_GetSuppressed(), flashbang via GetFlashed(float time, float shake), and hit shake via Health.hitShake (Il2Cpp.HitShake.Shake(float _duration, float _magnitude)) and Health.hitReaction (Il2Cpp.InteractionControl).
findings.members: MasterController.CameraRecoil/CameraHitShake/CameraShake/CameraSuppressionFlinch, MasterController.HitShake/SuppressionFlinch (RecoilAnimData), MasterController.weaponBob/cameraBob (BobStyle2), PlayerNetworking.GetFlashed/SERVER_GetSuppressed, HitShake.Shake
findings.modding: RecoilAnimData are ScriptableObject assets, so recoil/flinch feel is retunable by swapping the data object rather than patching code.

findings.title: MasterController carries a vestigial UnityEngine.AI.NavMeshAgent field despite the game using A* Pathfinding Project
findings.detail: MasterController exposes get_agent/set_agent typed UnityEngine.AI.NavMeshAgent. The established finding is that AI uses A* Pathfinding Project and not Unity NavMesh, and nothing else in the player graph touches NavMesh. Alongside it MasterController keeps six animator hashes _hashBlend, _hashCrouching, _hashProne, _hashArmed, _hashStance, _hashCrouch but only three matching name strings _animBlend, _animCrouch, _animProne — _hashCrouching and _hashCrouch are two hashes for what looks like one concept, and _hashArmed/_hashStance have no stored string. Il2Cpp.CharacterCounterLook duplicates the same hash set (_hashIsArmed, _hashStance, _hashBlend, _hashIsGrenade, _hashProne, _hashCrouch) independently.
findings.members: MasterController.agent (UnityEngine.AI.NavMeshAgent), MasterController._hashCrouching vs _hashCrouch, MasterController._animBlend/_animCrouch/_animProne, CharacterCounterLook._hashIsArmed/_hashIsGrenade
findings.modding: Do not assume the player has a functioning NavMeshAgent; there is no NavMesh baked. The duplicated crouch hashes are worth checking at runtime — one of the two is likely stale and setting the wrong one without warning does nothing.

findings.title: Tooling note: querying nested il2cpp types requires escaping the slash, and one PlayerDrawing RPC has an unhookable mangled name
findings.detail: InteropInspector builds nested type fullnames with a forward slash (Il2Cpp.MasterController/RunState, Il2Cpp.PlayerNetworking/WeaponSlot, Il2Cpp.InventoryItem/ItemType, Il2Cpp.PlayerVaultSystem/VaultType, Il2CppCMF.AdvancedWalkerController/ControllerState, Il2Cpp.Health/LimbForceEntry). Under Git Bash, a regex argument beginning with `/` is mangled by MSYS path conversion and without warning matches nothing — use a bracketed `[/]` or run it from the PowerShell tool. Separately, Il2Cpp.PlayerDrawing.RPC_ReceiveInitialTexture's weaved body did not get a friendly name: it appears as Method_Protected_Void_NetworkConnectionToClient_Il2CppStructArray_1_Byte_PDM_0 with its invoker as Method_Protected_Static_Void_NetworkBehaviour_NetworkReader_NetworkConnectionToClient_PDM_0. PlayerDrawing also ships a full server-authoritative whiteboard (ServerAuthBrushStrokes/PendingClientBrushStrokes, CMD_DrawBrushStroke(BrushStroke), RPC_DrawInitialBrushStroke(conn, List<BrushStroke>), and a full PNG byte blob to each late joiner).
findings.members: Il2Cpp.PlayerDrawing.RPC_ReceiveInitialTexture, PlayerDrawing.ServerAuthBrushStrokes, InteropInspector nested-type separator '/'
findings.modding: To hook the initial-texture RPC you must go by the mangled name, not RPC_ReceiveInitialTexture. A full-index dump for future queries is cached at (local scratch) (943 types, top-level Il2Cpp.* only — nested types are excluded from it).

findings.title: Ballistics are fully simulated projectiles, not hitscan — driven by a job-batched RaycastCommand solver
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BulletManager is a singleton (Get(), get_instance) that owns List<BulletInstance> _bullets, Stack<BulletInstance> _pool, NativeArray<RaycastCommand> _commands, NativeArray<RaycastHit> _results, int RaycastMinPerJob, int _scratchCapacity, and EnsureScratch(int n). It ticks in FixedUpdate(). Each bullet contributes a segment via BulletInstance.BeginManagedTick(float deltaTime, Vector3 gravity, ref RaycastCommand command, ref bool needsRay) -> bool, and consumes its result in ResolveManagedTick(float deltaTime, Vector3 gravity, bool chordHit). Travel(float deltaTime, Vector3 gravity, bool skipRaycast) is the integrator. BulletInstance carries bulletVelocity (Vector3), speed, _initialSpeed, dragAmount, GRAVITY_MULTIPLIER, Mass, _travelTime, bulletLifeTime, predictionStepsPerFrame, and point1/point2 (the swept chord for this tick). LateUpdate() separately drives tracers. There is no single-raycast 'shoot' method anywhere in WeaponV3 or GunFunction.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.BulletManager.FixedUpdate, BulletManager._commands, BulletManager._results, BulletManager.RaycastMinPerJob, BulletManager.EnsureScratch, BulletInstance.BeginManagedTick, BulletInstance.ResolveManagedTick, BulletInstance.Travel, BulletInstance.bulletVelocity, BulletInstance.point1, BulletInstance.point2
findings.modding: Ballistics changes belong at the BulletManager tick or on the Bullet stat prefab, not at a fire event. Because raycasts go through the Jobs batch API, you cannot intercept individual bullet raycasts with Physics.Raycast patches. Patch BulletInstance.ResolveManagedTick or BulletInstance.ProcessBullet to see every hit.

findings.title: Bullet (MonoBehaviour) is a pure stat template; BulletInstance is the pooled simulation object — they duplicate ~40 fields
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Bullet is a MonoBehaviour on an inactive prefab that holds only data. The static factory Bullet.SpawnBullet(Bullet bulletPrefab, Vector3 muzzlePos, Quaternion muzzleRot) -> BulletInstance rents from the pool and calls BulletInstance.CopyStatsFrom(Bullet prefab). BulletInstance re-declares every stat (speed, damage, armourPenetration, penetrationAmount, GoreLevel, bleedChance, ricochetChance, ...) plus runtime-only state: ManagerIndex, pooled, _ricochetCount, _travelTime, _originalDamage, _initialSpeed, _armour (Il2Cpp.Armour), bulletDefect, incidenceAngle, hasPenetrationPoint, penetrationPoint, impactPoint, breakableSurface (Il2CppGK.BreakableSurface), _ratingFactors (Dictionary<ArmourRating,float>), _explosionOverlap (Collider[]), _cachedRay, _cachedPenRay, _mainCamera. BulletInstance exposes position/rotation/forward as properties rather than a Transform and has no Unity lifecycle methods (no Awake/Update) — it is driven entirely by BulletManager and returned via ReturnToPool()/ForceRetire().
findings.members: Bullet.SpawnBullet, BulletInstance.CopyStatsFrom, BulletManager.RentInstance, BulletManager.ReturnInstance, BulletManager.Register, BulletManager.Unregister, BulletInstance.ManagerIndex, BulletInstance.pooled
findings.modding: To add a new ammo type you author a Bullet prefab and a BulletShell that references it — no code. To change a live round mid-flight you must mutate BulletInstance, not Bullet. Editing Bullet at runtime affects every future round of that type globally.

findings.title: Trigger-to-projectile chain in WeaponV3, and firing goes through the round object not the gun
findings.detail: WeaponV3.Fire() -> CanFire() -> DischargeRound() -> SpawnBullet(Vector3 muzzlePos, Quaternion muzzleRot, Vector3 _moaSpread, bool _isOwned) -> SpawnProjectile(Bullet bullet, Vector3 muzzlePos, Quaternion muzzleRot, Vector3 _moaSpread). Feeding: GunFunction.currentRoundInChamber is a BulletShell, GunFunction.currentMagazine is a Magazine. Magazine.grabNextRound() -> BulletShell, Magazine.subtractRound(). The ignition roll lives on the round: BulletShell.FireRound(bool hasAuthority) -> bool, with BulletShell.misfireChance / initialMisfireChance / ignited, and a failure path WeaponV3.CMD_malfunctionMisfire()/RPC_malfunctionMisfire(). BulletShell also carries CaliberType (WeaponCaliber), BulletPrefab (Bullet) and BuckshotPrefab (Buckshot); WeaponV3.ShellMatchesCaliber(int shellIndex) gates chambering. Cycle: ChamberRound(int roundOverride), EjectRound(), EjectRoundNoChamber(), OpenBolt()/CloseBolt(), ManualChamber().
findings.members: WeaponV3.Fire, WeaponV3.CanFire, WeaponV3.DischargeRound, WeaponV3.SpawnBullet, WeaponV3.SpawnProjectile, BulletShell.FireRound, BulletShell.misfireChance, GunFunction.currentRoundInChamber, Magazine.grabNextRound, WeaponV3.ShellMatchesCaliber
findings.modding: BulletShell.FireRound is the cleanest hook for jam/misfire mods and for per-round behaviour. WeaponV3.CanFire is the gate for safety/ammo-check mods.

findings.title: MOA spread is computed CLIENT-SIDE and transmitted — the server never validates accuracy
findings.detail: WeaponV3.CMD_SendBullet(Vector3 _muzzlePos, Quaternion _muzzleRot, Vector3 _moaSpread) is a Mirror Command whose payload is the shooter's chosen muzzle pose AND the already-rolled spread vector; the server rebroadcasts it verbatim as RPC_SendBullet(Vector3, Quaternion, Vector3). Every peer then runs the identical deterministic sim locally from those three values via BulletInstance.ApplyMoaSpread(Vector3 euler) + StartBullet()/StartBulletP2(). The weaved receive stubs are UserCode_CMD_SendBullet__Vector3__Quaternion__Vector3 and UserCode_RPC_SendBullet__Vector3__Quaternion__Vector3. There is no server-side recompute of spread from GunStats.MOA, no muzzle-position plausibility check, and no rate check in the signature surface.
findings.members: WeaponV3.CMD_SendBullet, WeaponV3.RPC_SendBullet, WeaponV3.UserCode_CMD_SendBullet__Vector3__Quaternion__Vector3, BulletInstance.ApplyMoaSpread, GunStats.MOA, Bullet.selfMOA
findings.modding: This is the single most powerful ballistics seam: prefix WeaponV3.CMD_SendBullet (send side) to rewrite spread/origin, or hook UserCode_RPC_SendBullet to observe every shot from every player. It is also a plain cheat vector — a client sending Vector3.zero spread gets perfect accuracy and every peer renders it. A server-side mod wanting anti-cheat must re-derive spread inside UserCode_CMD_SendBullet.

findings.title: AI firing is server-authoritative while player firing is client-authoritative — asymmetric trust in the same pipeline
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.WeaponsAI declares SERVER_SendBullet(Vector3 _muzzlePos, Quaternion _muzzleRot, Vector3 _moaSpread) -> RPC_SendBullet(Vector3, Quaternion, Vector3) with only a UserCode_RPC_SendBullet stub (no UserCode_CMD_*), i.e. the server originates AI rounds and clients only receive. Players use CMD_->RPC_ on WeaponV3. Same three-argument contract, opposite direction. WeaponsAI also mirrors the player weapon state machine server-side: SERVER_SpawnFirearm(), SERVER_Reload()/RPC_Reload(), SERVER_SetFireBool(bool)/RPC_SetFireBool(bool state, int _currentBurst), with fields fired_Burst, currentBurst, timeBetweenBursts, reloadTime, and aimCorrection (a SyncVar with hook OnAimCorrectionUpdate). AI hold PuppetWeapon (weaponList: List<PuppetWeapon>), not WeaponV3.
findings.members: WeaponsAI.SERVER_SendBullet, WeaponsAI.RPC_SendBullet, WeaponsAI.SERVER_SetFireBool, WeaponsAI.aimCorrection, WeaponsAI.currentBurst, WeaponsAI.weapon (PuppetWeapon)
findings.modding: AI ballistics tuning must run on the host. WeaponsAI.aimCorrection is the AI accuracy toggle and is a SyncVar, so difficulty mods can flip it server-side and it replicates.

findings.title: Penetration is a per-surface energy/chance model with a separate armour layer stacked on top
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.SurfaceInformation (ScriptableObject) carries the material side: penetrationResistance, speedReduction, penetrationDeflection, ricochetMultiplier, ricochetDeflection. Metadata strings confirm intent: 'Speed/energy divisor when bullet penetrates this surface. Higher = more energy lost.' and 'Max random deflection angle (degrees) applied to bullet direction after penetrating. Denser materials deflect more.' The bullet side carries penetrationAmount (metres of material it can defeat) and armourPenetration (a separate armour-rating scale). BulletInstance.GetPenChance(float healthFrac) -> float makes penetration probabilistic and, notably, a function of the target's remaining health fraction. State tracked per shot: hasPenetrationPoint, penetrationPoint, _cachedPenRay, incidenceAngle, bulletDefect, currentImpactPenetrationCount vs maxImpactPenetration, currentImpactNonPenetrationCount vs maxImpactNonPenetration. Impact FX branch on it: SpawnImpactNewSystem(SurfaceInformation surfaceInfo, RaycastHit hitInfo, bool isPen).
findings.members: SurfaceInformation.penetrationResistance, SurfaceInformation.speedReduction, SurfaceInformation.penetrationDeflection, BulletInstance.GetPenChance, BulletInstance.penetrationAmount, BulletInstance.armourPenetration, BulletInstance.hasPenetrationPoint, BulletInstance.maxImpactPenetration
findings.modding: Wallbang tuning = edit SurfaceInformation assets (per SurfaceTypeEnum) rather than bullet code. The maxImpactPenetration/maxImpactNonPenetration counters are a hard cap on how many surfaces one round can pass through — raise them for through-multiple-walls mods.

findings.title: Body armour is a discrete NIJ-style rating table with durability, resolved against the bullet at hit time
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Armour holds armourRating (Il2Cpp.Armour/ArmourRating), maxDurability, durability, bluntDamageMultplier, armourDamageMultplier, indicReference. Il2Cpp.Armour/ArmourRating = { LVL_One, LVL_Two, LVL_TwoA, LVL_ThreeA, LVL_Three, LVL_ThreePlus, LVL_Four, LVL_Five, LVL_Six }. BulletInstance holds the counterpart: armourPenetration, armorDamage, bluntDamageMultiplier / _bluntDamageMultiplier, plus a resolved lookup table _ratingFactors (Dictionary<ArmourRating,float>) and a cached _armour reference for the plate it is currently defeating. A defeated-but-stopped round therefore still delivers blunt trauma via bluntDamageMultiplier.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.Armour.armourRating, Il2Cpp.Armour.durability, Il2Cpp.Armour/ArmourRating (9 levels), BulletInstance._ratingFactors, BulletInstance._armour, BulletInstance.armorDamage, BulletInstance.bluntDamageMultiplier
findings.modding: _ratingFactors is a per-instance dictionary, so a Harmony postfix on BulletInstance.CopyStatsFrom can rewrite the whole armour-vs-caliber matrix per round without touching prefabs.

findings.title: Damage lands on Il2Cpp.Health with per-limb bookkeeping and a real through-and-through second body part
findings.detail: Health.CMDTakeDamage(float _damage, HealthBodyPart _bodyPart, HealthBodyPart crossedDamage, int shooterID) is the Command; TakeDamage(float, HealthBodyPart, HealthBodyPart, int) is a weaved RPC (UserCode_TakeDamage__Single__HealthBodyPart__HealthBodyPart__Int32) and there is a local 5-arg overload TakeDamage(..., Vector3 DamageSourcePosition) plus CMDTakeDamageFromPosition(..., Vector3 position). The 'crossedDamage' argument is a SECOND HealthBodyPart resolved by ProcessCrossDamage(float, HealthBodyPart, HealthBodyPart, int, Vector3) — a round that exits one limb into the torso damages both. Il2Cpp.HealthBodyPart = { Head, Chest, Stomach, LArm, RArm, LLeg, RLeg, SERVER, NONE } (byte-backed). Secondary effects are separate Commands: CMD_Bleed(HealthBodyPart, float _damage, int shooterID), CMD_StopBleeding(HealthBodyPart), CMD_Fracture(HealthBodyPart, int shooterID)/RPC_Fractured, CMD_FixFracture(HealthBodyPart)/RPC_FixFracture — sourced from Bullet.bleedChance / HeavyBleedChance / bleedDamage / FractureChance. Per-limb bleed is replicated as SyncVars NetworkBleedingDamage_Head/Chest/Stomach/LArm/RArm/LLeg/RLeg. Death: Die(HealthBodyPart causeOfDeath, int shooterID) (weaved RPC) -> ProcessDeathServer(), SpawnBloodPool(HealthBodyPart causeOfDeath).
findings.members: Health.CMDTakeDamage, Health.ProcessCrossDamage, Health.TakeDamage, Health.CMD_Bleed, Health.CMD_Fracture, Health.Die, Il2Cpp.HealthBodyPart, Health.GetHitboxIndex, Health.GetBodyPartFromTag
findings.modding: shooterID is a plain int netId threaded all the way from BulletInstance.shootersNetworkID — that is your kill-attribution hook. Patch UserCode_CMDTakeDamage__* on the host for damage scaling that cannot be client-spoofed.

findings.title: AI take damage through a different, ragdoll-aware entry point than players
findings.detail: Health.ProcessAIDamage(Il2CppFIMSpace.FProceduralAnimation.RagdollAnimator2BoneIndicator indic, int hitboxIndex, RaycastHit _hit, float _damage, int shooterID, float _bleedChance, float _bleedDamage) bypasses the HealthBodyPart enum entirely and works off a bone indicator plus an integer hitbox index resolved by Health.GetHitboxIndex(string name) / the GetHitBoxes() coroutine. AI hit reactions route through CMDProcessAIAnimation(int hitboxIndex, Vector3 direction)/RPCProcessAIAnimation, whereas players use CMD_HitReaction(Vector3 location, string hitbox). Ragdoll physics is FIMSpace Ragdoll Animator 2 (ERagdollBoneID, ERagdollChainType, LimbForceEntry), with SERVER_ReduceRagdollHealth(), TakeRagdollDamage(float) and RPC_RagdollBleedout().
findings.members: Health.ProcessAIDamage, Health.GetHitboxIndex, Health.CMDProcessAIAnimation, Health.CMD_HitReaction, Health.TakeRagdollDamage, Health.SERVER_ReduceRagdollHealth
findings.modding: A damage mod that only patches CMDTakeDamage will without warning miss all AI hits. You must patch ProcessAIDamage too.

findings.title: BulletHittable is the polymorphic hit-dispatch point — the intended extension seam for anything that reacts to bullets
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BulletHittable declares OnHit(Il2Cpp.BulletInstance bullet, UnityEngine.Ray ray, UnityEngine.RaycastHit hit) and three shipped subclasses override it with the identical signature: OnBulletHitDamageable (holds BulletDamageable + a reused DamageData[] _damageDataBuffer), OnBulletHitAddForce (float force, Rigidbody RB), OnBulletHitRangeTarget (ShootingRangeTarget + Il2CppBigBlit.ShootingRange.KillableBody). BulletDamageable.TakeDamage(Il2CppStructArray<Il2Cpp.DamageData> damage) is the decal/paint path (Knife Real Blood: projectingRenderers, brushes as BrushDamagePair[], renderTextures, texturePropertyName, textureResolution, Paint(Vector3 point, Vector3 normal, int brushID), CleanDamage()).
findings.members: BulletHittable.OnHit, OnBulletHitDamageable.OnHit, OnBulletHitAddForce.OnHit, OnBulletHitRangeTarget.OnHit, BulletDamageable.TakeDamage, BulletDamageable.Paint
findings.modding: Attach a component deriving from BulletHittable to make any object bullet-reactive — no ballistics code required. Whether OnHit is declared virtual is not visible in the inspector; runtime probe: check Il2CppType.Of<BulletHittable>().GetMethod("OnHit").IsVirtual before relying on a subclass override.

findings.title: Gore is a proximity vote on authored gore points, gated by Bullet.GoreLevel and replicated as a bare index
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Gore.CheckForGore(Vector3 impactPoint) walks gorePoints (Il2Cpp.GorePoints[]) tracking smallestDistance/cDistance/cIndex, then CMD_SpawnGore(int index) -> RPC_SpawnGore(int index) -> SpawnGore(int index). Local state: hasGored (single latch, checkHasGored()), currentGoreHead (Il2Cpp.GoreHead), GoreBonesReference (Transform[]), goreSpawnParent, invisibleMaterial + _cachedGoredMaterials (Material[][]) for swapping the intact mesh out, vfxList, characterHeadReferences (Il2Cpp.CharacterHeadReferences[]). ForceGore() exists as a debug entry. The bullet's authority is a single int: Bullet.GoreLevel (observed value 2 on the generic round). Head removal has a dedicated prefab, BulletEffectManager.HeadExplosionPrefab.
findings.members: Gore.CheckForGore, Gore.CMD_SpawnGore, Gore.RPC_SpawnGore, Gore.gorePoints, Gore.hasGored, Bullet.GoreLevel, BulletEffectManager.HeadExplosionPrefab
findings.modding: Gore replicates only as an int index into a per-character gorePoints array, so custom characters need matching GorePoints arrays or the index desyncs across clients. hasGored is a one-shot latch — a body can only gore once regardless of subsequent hits.

findings.title: The attachment build format is a flat parent-pointer tree in topological order — confirmed against a live capture
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Network_WeaponPreset serialises as { ModIDs: List<int>, ModParents: List<NetworkedModParent>, ModOffset: List<float>, EyeOffset: float } where NetworkedModParent(int attachmentId, int slotId) writes fields aID/sID. A live capture (D:\OperatorHSR\re\runtime_dump\hsr_build_json.txt) reads: {"ModIDs":[7,54,329,461,804,842,798,798,463,150,610,296,708,215,923,530,113,222],"ModParents":[{"aID":-1,"sID":0},{"aID":0,"sID":0},{"aID":1,"sID":0},...,{"aID":4,"sID":2},{"aID":4,"sID":3},...],"ModOffset":[0.0,...,0.02162334881722927,...],"EyeOffset":-0.023070383816957475}. aID is an ORDINAL INDEX INTO ModIDs (the parent attachment's position in this same array), not a mod id — proven by ModIDs[6] and ModIDs[7] both being 798 while sharing aID 4 on different sIDs. aID -1 means attach directly to the weapon root, i.e. WeaponMods.BaseModSlots[sID]. sID is the index into the parent's WeaponMod.ChildAttachmentSlots. Entries must be listed parent-before-child. ModOffset[i] is the rail/M-LOK slide position for entry i (WeaponModParent.currentOffset). EyeOffset is the ADS Z eye-relief.
findings.members: Network_WeaponPreset.ModIDs, Network_WeaponPreset.ModParents, Network_WeaponPreset.ModOffset, Network_WeaponPreset.EyeOffset, NetworkedModParent.aID, NetworkedModParent.sID, WeaponMods.BaseModSlots, WeaponMod.ChildAttachmentSlots, WeaponModParent.currentOffset
findings.modding: This is the exact string to synthesise for a programmatic weapon build. Feed it to WeaponV3.SetWeaponMods(string modJSON) or WeaponMods.AddNewAttachment(string attachment, string parentName, Vector3 modPos, bool updateModString, bool notifyOtherClients). Get the current one with WeaponMods.GetJsonModStringFromCurrentMods().

findings.title: The whole attachment tree replicates as a single JSON string SyncVar with a rebuild hook
findings.detail: WeaponMods.JSON_MOD_STRING is a Mirror SyncVar (NetworkJSON_MOD_STRING accessor, _Mirror_SyncVarHookDelegate_JSON_MOD_STRING as Action<string,string>) whose hook is OnAttachmentListChange(string oldValue, string newValue) -> ChangeAttachmentString(string newString) -> RebuildWeaponWithModString() -> RebuildWeaponWithNetworkPreset(Network_WeaponPreset) -> BuildWeaponWithAttachmentPreset(Network_WeaponPreset WeaponPreset, bool addMagazines) -> AddAttachmentLocal(int attachmentID, NetworkedModParent parent, Vector3 modPos). Incremental edits go over their own RPCs: CMD_RemoveMod(string parentName, string attachment)/RPC_RemoveMod, CMD_StripGun, CMD_SetNewModPostion(string name, Vector3 newPos, Vector3 transformCompPos)/RPC_SetNewModPostion, CMD_AssignPlayerWeaponStats(string weaponPreset). Note the mixed identity scheme: the syncvar carries integer ids while the remove/position RPCs carry NAME strings, resolved by FindModParentByName(string) vs FindModParentByNetworkData(NetworkedModParent).
findings.members: WeaponMods.JSON_MOD_STRING, WeaponMods.OnAttachmentListChange, WeaponMods.RebuildWeaponWithModString, WeaponMods.BuildWeaponWithAttachmentPreset, WeaponMods.AddAttachmentLocal, WeaponMods.CMD_AssignPlayerWeaponStats, WeaponMods.FindModParentByName
findings.modding: Setting the syncvar server-side is the whole-weapon rebuild path and it replicates for free. WeaponMods.ForceRebuildWeapon() is weaved as an RPC and is the safest way to force all clients to re-read after a server-side mutation.

findings.title: Two coexisting preset formats plus a migration path — one name/path based, one id/slot based
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Save_WeaponPreset (disk) = { WeaponModName: List<string>, ModParentDirectory: List<Il2Cpp.ModSavePathList>, WeaponModPosition: List<Vector3>, EyeOffset: float } where ModSavePathList wraps List<string> path — the full chain of parent NAMES from the root, built by WeaponModParent.GetParentPathString() and WeaponModParent.BuildPathString(WeaponModParent parent, ref List<string> path). Il2Cpp.Network_WeaponPreset (wire) is the compact integer form. WeaponMods exposes BOTH BASE_JSON_MOD_STRING and NEW_BASE_JSON_MOD_STRING as separate defaults, and Il2Cpp.WeaponPresetMigration exists as a type. So the game shipped a format change and still carries the legacy name-path reader.
findings.members: Save_WeaponPreset.ModParentDirectory, ModSavePathList.path, WeaponModParent.GetParentPathString, WeaponModParent.BuildPathString, WeaponMods.BASE_JSON_MOD_STRING, WeaponMods.NEW_BASE_JSON_MOD_STRING, Il2Cpp.WeaponPresetMigration
findings.modding: Write NEW-format (integer) strings. Loadout mods that persist presets to disk should store the Network_WeaponPreset shape, since the name-path format breaks whenever a WeaponModParent is renamed.

findings.title: Ammunition is itself an attachment type, and magazines hold individually simulated rounds
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.WeaponMod/AttachmentType includes Ammunition and MagExtension alongside the 60-odd physical types (None, Grip, Sight, Barrel, Handguard, Stock, FrontSight, RearSight, Magazine, PistolGrip, Muzzle, Trigger, ChargingHandle, MicroSightMount, MicroSight, UpperReciever, BufferTube, BoltCarrier, Scope, Light, LightPistol, Slide, RailCover, Suppressor, Dovetail, Custom, MLOK, Custom_AR10, Gasblock, RMR, MagazineTube, OpticPlate, plus ~25 weapon-specific one-offs like Glock17ZaffariZPS4RMRPlate and P226ThreadProtector). WeaponMod carries AmmoReferenceIndex (int), AmmunitionName (string), ammunitionParent (Transform), IsPartOfMagMod, magExtensionAmount. Magazine holds allBullets: List<BulletShell> — real per-round objects with bulletPositions, bulletSpawnWith (List<bulletSpawner>), ammoAmount / ammoAmountMax / ammoAmountMagExtension, plus RepackAmmunition(BulletShell ammo, bool firstrepack) and LoadOneRound(BulletShell bullet). Mixed loads are therefore first-class.
findings.members: WeaponMod/AttachmentType.Ammunition, WeaponMod.AmmoReferenceIndex, WeaponMod.AmmunitionName, Magazine.allBullets, Magazine.RepackAmmunition, Magazine.grabNextRound, Magazine.ammoAmountMagExtension, Magazine.compatibleWeaponSystems
findings.modding: A new caliber or ammo type is added by registering a WeaponMod with AttachmentType.Ammunition pointing at a BulletShell whose BulletPrefab is your Bullet. Magazine.compatibleWeaponSystems (string[]) + Magazine.checkCompatibility(string weaponSystem) + WeaponMods.magazineCompatibility gate which mags fit which guns — all string matching, so easy to widen.

findings.title: Shotguns fire N independent full-fidelity projectiles, not a spread cone
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Buckshot is a data-only class whose sole member is BBs: Il2CppReferenceArray<Il2Cpp.Bullet>. BulletShell carries both BulletPrefab (Bullet) and BuckshotPrefab (Buckshot). Each BB is a distinct Bullet stat template, so every pellet becomes its own BulletInstance in BulletManager with its own MOA roll, drag, penetration and ricochet.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.Buckshot.BBs, BulletShell.BuckshotPrefab, BulletShell.BulletPrefab
findings.modding: Pellet count and per-pellet ballistics are authored purely as array length + Bullet prefabs. Watch the cost: a 12-pellet shell adds 12 entries to the BulletManager raycast batch per shot.

findings.title: Recoil is entirely KINEMATION FPS Animation Framework — the game's own recoil classes hold zero logic
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.WeaponRecoil has NO methods beyond .ctor: it holds Recoily (Il2CppKinemation.FPSFramework.Runtime.Recoil.RecoilAnimation), recoilData (RecoilAnimData), RecoilModiferReturnSpeed, RecoilModiferFireIntervalMin, RecoilModiferFireIntervalMax, and three anchor transforms recoilTranform / recoilTranformStock / recoilTranformPistol. Il2Cpp.CameraRecoil is likewise data-only: CameraFOVSpeed, CameraFOVIncrease, CameraFOVOriginal, CameraRecoilData (RecoilAnimData). The only game-side code is WeaponV3.ApplyRecoil() driving them and Il2Cpp.RecoilAnimationFix, which is just OnAnimatorIK(int layerIndex) + LateUpdate() with a WeaponV3 reference. Recoil is a viewmodel/animation effect layered on top of the muzzle transform — the projectile is spawned from the muzzle pose, so recoil affects aim only through where the muzzle ends up.
findings.members: WeaponRecoil.Recoily, WeaponRecoil.recoilData, CameraRecoil.CameraRecoilData, WeaponV3.ApplyRecoil, RecoilAnimationFix.OnAnimatorIK, WeaponMod.Recoil
findings.modding: Recoil tuning means editing KINEMATION RecoilAnimData assets or the RecoilAnimation component, not game code. Per-attachment recoil contribution is a single float, WeaponMod.Recoil.

findings.title: Sway and bob are spring/curve systems with no ballistic effect; zeroing is a discrete optic-tilt list, not a ballistic solve
findings.detail: WeaponSwayV2 uses KINEMATION springs (aimSwaySettings: LocRotSpringData, aimSwayPositionSpring / aimSwayRotationSpring: VectorSpringState) plus AnimationCurves walkXCurve, walkYCurve, walkCurve, runCurve, driven by GetInput() -> ApplySway(). ProceduralWeaponBob is a phase-accumulator (\_phase, \_smoothIntensity, \_smoothJogBlend, \_smoothSprintBlend) evaluating a BobProfile via EvalPosition(BobProfile p, float t) / EvalRotation(BobProfile p, float t) and BlendThree(...). ADSFixed does the aim transform (adsPos/adsRot, cantedPos/cantedRot, pistolAdsPos/pistolAdsRot, adsSpeed, ShoulderedWeight, HasStock, SetADSZOffset(float offset), AuthoredAdsZ) and reads ArmStamina. Il2Cpp.ADS_Zeroing is startlingly simple: adsPos: List<Vector3> + adsRot: List<Quaternion> + int cIndex + bool doesRot, stepped in Update() — zeroing is a lookup of authored optic offsets, with real gravity drop handled by the sim.
findings.members: WeaponSwayV2.aimSwayPositionSpring, WeaponSwayV2.walkCurve, ProceduralWeaponBob.EvalPosition, ADSFixed.SetADSZOffset, ADSFixed.ShoulderedWeight, ADS_Zeroing.adsPos, ADS_Zeroing.cIndex
findings.modding: Because zeroing is authored offsets, a mod that changes Bullet.speed or GRAVITY_MULTIPLIER without warning invalidates every optic's zero. Compensate by regenerating ADS_Zeroing.adsRot entries.

findings.title: Dead and misleading code in this area: FPSFireManager is an asset-pack hitscan demo, RangeComputer is scoring, and four bullet classes are empty
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.FPSFireManager comes from \Assets\_vfx\KriptoFX\MuzzleFlashes\Scripts\Demo\FPSFireManager.cs and runs its OWN independent hitscan in Update() with float BulletDistance, ImpactElemets: ImpactInfo[], GetImpactEffect(GameObject impactedGameObject) — it has nothing to do with BulletManager and is demo code. Il2Cpp.RangeComputer (\Assets\Scripts\RangeComputer.cs) is the shoot-house scoreboard: activeLayoutIndex, targetsHit/civiliansHit SyncVars, shootHouseLayouts: ShootHouseLayout[], timer RPCs — zero ballistics. Il2Cpp.BulletBlocker, Il2Cpp.BulletFlyBy, Il2Cpp.BulletPooled and Il2Cpp.BloodBulletPooled expose only .cctor/.ctor — pure marker components or abandoned classes (BulletFlyBy was superseded by BulletCrack, BulletPooled by BulletManager's own Stack pool).
findings.members: FPSFireManager.BulletDistance, FPSFireManager.GetImpactEffect, RangeComputer.shootHouseLayouts, BulletBlocker, BulletFlyBy, BulletPooled
findings.modding: Do not wire ballistics work into FPSFireManager or RangeComputer. BulletBlocker being an empty marker means bullet blocking is done by tag/layer lookup from BulletInstance — probe at runtime by checking the layer of a BulletBlocker GameObject and comparing against BulletInstance.layerMask.

findings.title: Supersonic crack and AI gunshot perception are two separate systems, both distance-modelled
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BulletCrack is a singleton doing real acoustics for the local player: SpeedOfSound (float), ProcessCrackForAll(Vector3 point1, Vector3 point2, float speed, Vector3 shooterPosition, BulletInstance bullet) and ProcessIntersect(Vector3 planeCenter, Vector3 rayOrigin, Vector3 difference, Vector3 direction, float rangeSqr, ref Vector3 intersectionPoint, ref bool addSuppression, ref float shakeMultiplier) — it tests the bullet's swept chord against the listener each tick, so cracks fire only when a round actually passes nearby. Prefabs are per-caliber (BulletCrack556Prefabs, BulletCrack308Prefabs, BulletCrack762x39Prefabs, keyed by Bullet.CrackType), with BulletWooshPrefabs for subsonic and three ricochet families (Richochet_RiseDrop, Richochet_Rising, Richochet_Weird). Separately, Il2Cpp.Gunshot is a pooled SphereCollider sound-event object (Get/Return, pool: Queue<Gunshot>) carrying Shooter, ShooterBrain (Il2Cpp.BrainAI), ShooterTeam (Il2Cpp.TeamID), with FlatDistance/MediumDistance/FarDistance/MaxDistance and three layered AudioSources (CloseGunshot/MidGunshot/FarGunshot) — that is how AI hear you. Suppression feeds back through BulletCrack.CheckForInitialShotSuppression(Vector3 pos, float amount, bool sameTeam, BulletInstance _bullet) using Bullet.SuppressionAmount, gated by BulletCrack.AI_BulletCrackRange and TeamSuppressionRange.
findings.members: BulletCrack.ProcessCrackForAll, BulletCrack.SpeedOfSound, BulletCrack.CheckForInitialShotSuppression, BulletCrack.AI_BulletCrackRange, Gunshot.ShooterBrain, Gunshot.ShooterTeam, Gunshot.MaxDistance, GunStats.gunshotRange, Bullet.CrackType
findings.modding: Suppressor mods must touch both: GunStats.SuppressedAmount/isSuppressed for the Gunshot audio radius and Bullet.CrackType/SuppressionAmount for the downrange crack. Bullet.PlayerHeardThisCrack is a per-round latch preventing double cracks.

findings.title: Concrete authored values — a live GunStats (SR25, 7.62x51) and the generic Bullet template
findings.detail: From D:\OperatorHSR\re\runtime_dump\sr25_dump.txt, GunStats: weaponCaliber = cal_762x51mm, gunshotRange = 200, MOA = 1.59, FireRate = 550, FireRateSuppressed = 650, changeFireRateSuppressed = True, changeFireRateWithBarrels = False, short/medium/long_FireRate all 800 (untouched defaults), Weight = 1.35, Ergonomics = 70, fireMode = Semi, burst = False, burstAmount = 3. WeaponV3 runtime state at rest: _MOA = 0, moaSpread = (0,0,0). From D:\OperatorHSR\re\runtime_dump\ammo_dump.txt, Bullet 'GenericBullet(Clone)': bulletLifeTime = 7, predictionStepsPerFrame = 6, IsStandardRound = True, EnableTracer = False, selfMOA = 0, FractureChance = 15, bleedChance = 13, HeavyBleedChance = 10, bleedDamage = 3, ricochetChance = 45, speed = 1030, dragAmount = 985, GRAVITY_MULTIPLIER = 1, Mass = 0.25, damage = 72, VehicleDamage = 1, armDamageMultipiler = 1.8, fragmentationChance = 0.05, maxFragmentationMultiplier = 0, doorMultiplier = 1, bluntDamageMultiplier = 0.2, SuppressionAmount = 0.2, armorDamage = 28, armourPenetration = 3.9, penetrationAmount = 0.75, GoreLevel = 2, CrackType = 0, maxRicochets = 3, minRicochetAngle = 45. GunStats.WeaponCaliber has 14 real calibers plus NotSet/Everything: 9x19mm, 45acp, 4.6x30mm, 556x45mm, 300blk, 545x39mm, 762x39mm, 6.8x51mm, 762x51mm, 338 lapua, 338 norma magnum, 12 gauge, 8.6 blackout, 762x54mmR.
findings.members: GunStats.MOA, GunStats.FireRate, GunStats.FireRateSuppressed, GunStats.gunshotRange, Bullet.damage, Bullet.speed, Bullet.dragAmount, Bullet.armourPenetration, Bullet.penetrationAmount, GunStats/WeaponCaliber
findings.modding: damage is an INT on both Bullet and BulletInstance, so sub-1 damage granularity is impossible without changing the field type. penetrationAmount 0.75 reads as metres of material. dragAmount 985 against speed 1030 is consistent with a quadratic-drag denominator (v²/dragAmount ≈ 1077 m/s² ≈ 110 g at muzzle) but that is inference — settle it by logging BulletInstance.speed each tick from a Travel postfix.

findings.title: Suppressing the SR25 makes it fire FASTER, and the barrel-length fire-rate system is authored but dormant
findings.detail: GunStats has parallel rate tables: FireRate/FireRateSuppressed, and short_/medium_/long_FireRate with suppressed variants, gated by two independent booleans changeFireRateSuppressed and changeFireRateWithBarrels. On the SR25 dump, changeFireRateSuppressed = True with FireRate = 550 and FireRateSuppressed = 650 — an 18% RPM increase when suppressed (defensible for a gas gun under backpressure, but it is the opposite of the usual game convention and is a real gameplay asymmetry). Meanwhile changeFireRateWithBarrels = False and all six barrel-length rates sit at the untouched default 800, so the barrel-length branch never runs on this weapon despite WeaponMod.barrelLength (Il2Cpp.WeaponMod/BarrelLength = { Off, Short, Medium, Long }) being authored on every barrel attachment.
findings.members: GunStats.changeFireRateSuppressed, GunStats.FireRateSuppressed, GunStats.changeFireRateWithBarrels, GunStats.short_FireRate, GunStats.long_FireRate, Il2Cpp.WeaponMod/BarrelLength
findings.modding: The barrel-rate system is free to switch on: set changeFireRateWithBarrels = true and author the three rates. Verify at runtime by flipping the bool on a live GunStats and timing shots, since the selection logic is in a method body the inspector cannot show.

findings.title: Explosive and fragmenting rounds are fully modelled on every bullet but appear unused on standard ammo
findings.detail: Bullet/BulletInstance carry a complete explosive-projectile block: isExplosive, explosionRange, lethalRange, lethalRangeHitChance, damageRangeHitChance, minimumArmingTime, ExplosiveImpact (Il2Cpp.BulletImpact), resolved by BulletInstance.ProcessExplosive() with an _explosionOverlap: Collider[] scratch buffer and two local functions visible in metadata: <ProcessExplosive>g__ProcessDamageOnBodyPart|0 and <ProcessExplosive>g__ProcessDamageOnHealth|1. Blast also drives CheckPlayerConcussion(float distMax) and CheckAIConcussion(float distMax). Fragmentation is separate: fragmentationChance, maxFragmentationMultiplier, fragDamage. On the generic round isExplosive = False, fragmentationChance = 0.05 and maxFragmentationMultiplier = 0 — so fragmentation rolls 5% of the time and then multiplies damage by zero extra, i.e. the frag bonus is authored off.
findings.members: BulletInstance.ProcessExplosive, BulletInstance.isExplosive, BulletInstance.minimumArmingTime, BulletInstance.CheckPlayerConcussion, BulletInstance.fragmentationChance, BulletInstance.maxFragmentationMultiplier, BulletInstance.fragDamage
findings.modding: Airburst / 40mm / explosive-tip rounds need no new code — set isExplosive on a Bullet prefab and give it an ExplosiveImpact. maxFragmentationMultiplier = 0 on stock ammo is either an intentional disable or an authoring oversight; raise it to make frag matter.

findings.title: Impact VFX, decals, SFX and ricochet sounds are hard-budgeted per frame — a hidden cap on any high-volume-fire mod
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BulletEffectManager (singleton) enforces MaxImpactVFXPerFrame with counters _impactVFXThisFrame / _lastResetFrame behind CanSpawnImpactVFX() -> bool, plus three independent runtime toggles ImpactVFXEnabled / ImpactDecalsEnabled / ImpactSFXEnabled driven by ToggleImpactVFX()/ToggleImpactDecals()/ToggleImpactSFX() and LogToggle(string label, bool on). BulletCrack independently caps ricochet audio with MaxRicochetSoundsPerFrame / _ricochetSoundsThisFrame / _lastRicochetResetFrame. Per-bullet caps exist too: maxImpactPenetration, maxImpactNonPenetration, currentImpactSFXCount. BulletInstance.IsPointInFrustum(Vector3 worldPoint) culls offscreen effects, and BulletEffectManager.PreloadSurface(SurfaceInformation surface) warms pools. Settings keys Key_MaxBulletHoleDecals / SetMaxBulletHoleDecals / SetMaxBulletShells expose user limits.
findings.members: BulletEffectManager.CanSpawnImpactVFX, BulletEffectManager.MaxImpactVFXPerFrame, BulletEffectManager.SpawnImpactSFX, BulletCrack.MaxRicochetSoundsPerFrame, BulletInstance.IsPointInFrustum, BulletInstance.currentImpactSFXCount
findings.modding: A minigun or high-RPM mod will without warning lose impact VFX rather than stutter. BulletEffectManager.SpawnImpactSFX(AudioClip clip, Vector3 position, Vector2 _SFXDistance, float _speed, bool playCrack, int crackType, float volume) is the one-stop hook for custom impact audio.

findings.title: GunFunction and GunStats are pure data containers — there is no gun 'brain' class
findings.detail: Both types expose ONLY property accessors, .ctor and .cctor: zero behaviour methods. GunFunction is chamber/feed state (currentRoundInChamber: BulletShell, currentMagazine: Magazine, isTubeFed, magazineInserted, isReloading, isArmed, BoltLockedBack) plus four transform anchors (MOD_Magazine, chamber, ejectionPort, muzzleEnd). GunStats is the numeric sheet (weaponCaliber, MOA, FireRate family, TimeBetweenRounds, fireDelay, Weight, Ergonomics, fireMode, fullAuto/semiAutomatic/burst/burstAmount/burstFired, gunshotRange, isSuppressed, SuppressedAmount, lockBoltOnEmpty). All logic lives on WeaponV3 (185+ methods). Notably GunStats has NO damage field — damage belongs entirely to the round (Bullet.damage), so a weapon's lethality is a property of what you load, not what you carry.
findings.members: GunFunction.muzzleEnd, GunFunction.currentRoundInChamber, GunFunction.BoltLockedBack, GunStats.MOA, GunStats.TimeBetweenRounds, GunStats.fireDelay, GunStats.burstAmount
findings.modding: GunFunction.muzzleEnd is the projectile origin transform — the cheapest place to redirect fire. Because both classes are data-only, Harmony has nothing to patch on them; and il2cpp field accessors cannot be patched, so mutate instances via the property setters instead.

findings.title: BrainAI is the live brain; BrainAIV2 is a dead NavMeshAgent prototype
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BrainAI (Assets\Scripts\AI\BrainAI.cs) has ~95 methods and ~240 fields and is the shipping AI. Il2Cpp.BrainAIV2 (Assets\Scripts\BrainAIV2.cs) has exactly two real methods — Update() and TestMove() — and six fields: agent (UnityEngine.AI.NavMeshAgent), animator, testmove (Transform), angularthing (GameObject), angularthing2 (GameObject), aimtarget (GameObject). It uses Unity's NavMeshAgent while the entire shipping stack uses A* FollowerEntity. The 'V2' naming is doubly misleading: the real BrainAI is the one that references a V2AIParametres asset. Do not attach to or patch BrainAIV2.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.BrainAI, Il2Cpp.BrainAIV2, BrainAIV2.TestMove, BrainAIV2.angularthing2, Il2Cpp.V2AIParametres
findings.modding: Anyone hooking 'the newest brain' by name will patch a prototype that never runs. Target Il2Cpp.BrainAI.

findings.title: Navigation is A* Pathfinding Project's ECS FollowerEntity — not Seeker, not RichAI
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.AgentController.Agent returns Il2CppPathfinding.FollowerEntity (the DOTS/ECS agent from A* 5.x), and AgentController.entityExists (bool) confirms the ECS entity backing. AgentController re-exposes a NavMeshAgent-shaped facade over it: position, velocity, destination, pathPending, remainingDistance, hasPath, stopDistance, maxSpeed, rotationSpeed, maxRotationSpeed, updatePosition, updateRotation, plus CallUpdate(). BrainAI reaches navigation only through AgentController (BrainAI.agent -> Il2Cpp.AgentController), never through A* types directly. Note BrainAI.RandomNavSphere(Vector3 origin, float minRadius, float maxRadius) keeps legacy NavMesh naming but must now sample the A* graph.
findings.members: AgentController.Agent, AgentController.entityExists, Pathfinding.FollowerEntity, BrainAI.agent, BrainAI.SetAgentAngularSpeed, BrainAI.SyncAgentAndAnimator, BrainAI.HasReached, BrainAI.RandomNavSphere
findings.modding: Custom AI movement must go through FollowerEntity's ECS API. Seeker/RichAI/AIPath tutorials do not apply, and Unity NavMesh calls are inert.

findings.title: Doors are A* graph TAGS plus off-mesh links; door capability is a traversal mask
findings.detail: AgentController exposes DisableNavigationTag(int layer) / EnableNavigationTag(int layer) alongside doorWalkLayer, doorOpenLayer, doorBreachLayer (all int) and SetDoorMode(DoorInteractionMode) with currentDoorInteractionMode. BrainAI/DoorInteractionMode = {CantGoThrough, CanGoThroughButNotOpen, CanOpenAndGoThrough}. So each door capability tier is a distinct A* tag, and setting the mode toggles which tags the agent may traverse — a bot that cannot open doors simply cannot path through the doorOpenLayer tag.
findings.members: AgentController.DisableNavigationTag, AgentController.EnableNavigationTag, AgentController.doorWalkLayer, AgentController.doorOpenLayer, AgentController.doorBreachLayer, AgentController.SetDoorMode, BrainAI/DoorInteractionMode
findings.modding: Change a bot's door behaviour by flipping tags via SetDoorMode, not by editing pathfinding. Custom maps must tag door links with the same three layer indices or bots will never use doors.

findings.title: BotOffmeshLinkHandler implements the A* off-mesh link state machine and drives door breaching
findings.detail: It implements both Pathfinding.IOffMeshLinkHandler and Pathfinding.IOffMeshLinkStateMachine: GetOffMeshLinkStateMachine(Pathfinding.ECS.AgentOffMeshLinkTraversalContext) -> IOffMeshLinkStateMachine, OnTraverseOffMeshLink(AgentOffMeshLinkTraversalContext ctx) -> Il2CppSystem.Collections.IEnumerable (coroutine-style traversal), OnFinishTraversingOffMeshLink(ctx), OnAbortTraversingOffMeshLink(). Traversal flags: OnOffLink, ReachedLink, OpeningDoor, TravelingLink, Finished, KickRequested, WaitingForKick, KickHappened. Breach tuning: IsBreacher (bool), DoorKickDamageMin/DoorKickDamageMax/DoorKickForce (float), DoorCooldown, and _doorCooldowns (Dictionary<Il2Cpp.DoorV2, float>) — a per-door cooldown so bots cannot spam-kick the same door. ApplyKickForce() and KickAnimationFinished() are mirrored on BrainAI, AgentController and NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC (SERVER_PlayKickAnimation -> RPC_PlayKickAnimation).
findings.members: BotOffmeshLinkHandler, IOffMeshLinkStateMachine, _doorCooldowns, IsBreacher, DoorKickForce, NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC.RPC_PlayKickAnimation
findings.modding: Custom maps need DoorV2s wired as A* off-mesh links or bots will path around/into them. The IEnumerable traversal is the clean insertion point for custom door animations.

findings.title: GameManager — not any AI manager — is the AI scheduler, with round-robin time slicing and a priority lane
findings.detail: There is no AIManager type in the game. GameManager owns allAI (List<BrainAI>) and fans out via CallBrainUpdate() and CallFixedBrainUpdate(). Time slicing is index-based round-robin: AI_UpdateIndex, AI_MinPerFrame, AI_MaxPerFrame, AI_TargetFramesBetweenTicks for logic; AI_FixedUpdateIndex, AI_PhysicsNumPerFrame for physics.
