A priority lane exists: _priorityBrainUpdates (HashSet<BrainAI>), RequestPriorityBrainUpdate(BrainAI ai), AI_MaxPriorityPerFrame. Two more independent round-robins: allAIAimCorrection (List<BotAimCorrection>) with AIweaponCollisionUpdatePerFrame/_lastAIweaponCollisionUpdated, and allBotHealth (List<Health>) with Health_BotLastUpdateIndex/Health_BotNumPerFrame. BrainAI receives BrainAI.CallUpdate(float minSqrDistToPlayer), CallBrainUpdate(), CallPhysicsFixedUpdate() and computes its own delta via _lastCallUpdateTime/_callUpdateDt because ticks are irregular; RunBrainTick(float dt) is the real body. BrainAI also keeps a static AllBrainAI (HashSet<BrainAI>).
findings.members: GameManager.allAI, GameManager.CallBrainUpdate, GameManager.CallFixedBrainUpdate, GameManager.RequestPriorityBrainUpdate, GameManager.AI_MaxPerFrame, GameManager.AI_TargetFramesBetweenTicks, BrainAI.CallUpdate, BrainAI.RunBrainTick, BrainAI._callUpdateDt, BrainAI.AllBrainAI
findings.modding: Never add per-frame work in BrainAI — it is already amortised. To force a bot to think now, call GameManager.RequestPriorityBrainUpdate. Hook BrainAI.RunBrainTick(float) for one call per bot per logical tick. Runtime probe: log call counts on GameManager.CallBrainUpdate vs BrainAI.RunBrainTick over 60 frames with N bots to confirm the fan-out and slice size.

findings.title: The state machine has only six states; Attack/Chase/Suppress-fire are methods, not states
findings.detail: BrainAI/States = {Idle, TargetSighted, WasSighted, FallBack, Suppress, Evade}. That is the entire FSM. Attack(bool suppressing), Chase(), CautiousAdvance(), Patrol(float dt), Wander(float dt), Idle(), TargetSighted(float dt), WasSighted(float dt), FallBack(float dt), Suppress(float dt), Evade() are methods invoked from inside UpdateStateMachine(float dt). Sub-modes are orthogonal enums: BrainAI/IdleStates {Idle, Wander, Patrol, Random}, BrainAI/ReactType {Defensive, Offensive, Random}, BrainAI/Stance {Stand, Crouch, Prone}, BrainAI/PeekState {None, InCover, PeekingOut, Returning}. SetNewAiState(States newState) is the single transition point. ShouldBeInCombat() and ShouldBeInCombatReady() gate combat entry. WasSighted is the search-after-losing-contact state, bounded by _searchSweepCount/MAX_SEARCH_SWEEPS.
findings.members: BrainAI/States, BrainAI.SetNewAiState, BrainAI.UpdateStateMachine, BrainAI/IdleStates, BrainAI/ReactType, BrainAI/PeekState, BrainAI.MAX_SEARCH_SWEEPS, BrainAI.ShouldBeInCombat
findings.modding: Harmony-patch SetNewAiState(States) for a complete, low-noise transition log — it is the only funnel. Adding a actually new state means patching UpdateStateMachine's dispatch, since the enum is baked into il2cpp.

findings.title: Perception is scored, stance-aware, and split into three passes
findings.detail: EyesAI runs Vision(), DoorVision() and Hearing() as separate passes. Eye height follows stance via StandingEyesOffset/CrouchEyesOffset/ProneEyesOffset, and visibility of each posture is independently gateable by CanSeeIfStanding/CanSeeIfCrouching/CanSeeIfProne — a bot can be configured unable to see prone targets at all. LOS test is TestIfCanSeeAtHeight(Vector3 height, Transform target) -> bool. Target choice is a scoring function, not nearest-first: FindTarget() -> Transform driven by ScoreTarget(Transform candidate, float maxRange) -> float; FindClosestsTarget() exists separately as a fallback. BrainAI supplies the cones: EyesFOVAngle, EyesFOVDistancePerfect, EyesFOVDistanceDecimateMultiplier (graduated acuity, not a hard cutoff), DetectionRange/originalDetectionRange, HasNVG. Throttling via _lastEyesUpdateTime and _teamListRefreshTimer.
findings.members: EyesAI.Vision, EyesAI.DoorVision, EyesAI.Hearing, EyesAI.ScoreTarget, EyesAI.TestIfCanSeeAtHeight, EyesAI.CanSeeIfProne, BrainAI.EyesFOVDistanceDecimateMultiplier, BrainAI.originalDetectionRange
findings.modding: ScoreTarget is the single lever for threat prioritisation (e.g. make bots prefer the loudest player). originalDetectionRange being stored separately means something scales DetectionRange at runtime — GameManager.SetBotViewDistanceMultiplier(float) is the likely writer.

findings.title: Static audio hooks are the seam by which the whole game feeds the AI's ears
findings.detail: EyesAI exposes two STATIC entry points that any system can call: EyesAI.FootstepPlayed(UnityEngine.Vector3 footstepPosition, UnityEngine.GameObject shooterRoot, UnityEngine.Transform lookPosition) and EyesAI.DoorSoundPlayed(UnityEngine.Vector3 doorPosition, float hearingRadius). BrainAI then has public per-bot reaction entry points: HeardTarget(Vector3 position, float _distance, Transform _target), ReactToBulletCrack(Vector3 shooterPosition, Vector3 bulletPosition, Vector3 bulletDirection), ReactToGunFire(Vector3 shooterPosition, float _dis, bool shooterInInterior), GetFlashed(float timer, Vector3 explosionLocation). Hearing is context-sensitive: HearingRange, IndoorHearingRange, IndoorGunshotHearingRange, CombatHearingMultiplier, YellTargetPositionRange. A literal AI_MinimumCrackDistance exists for the supersonic-crack threshold. Il2Cpp.Gunshot is a pooled (Queue<Gunshot>, Get/Return) sphere-collider audio propagator carrying Shooter, ShooterBrain and ShooterTeam with FlatDistance/MediumDistance/FarDistance/MaxDistance tiers.
findings.members: EyesAI.FootstepPlayed, EyesAI.DoorSoundPlayed, BrainAI.ReactToBulletCrack, BrainAI.ReactToGunFire, BrainAI.HeardTarget, BrainAI.GetFlashed, Gunshot.ShooterBrain, BrainAI.IndoorGunshotHearingRange
findings.modding: A custom weapon or noise source only needs to call the two static EyesAI methods to be heard — no per-bot registration. Conversely, a silenced/no-op weapon that skips them is invisible to hearing entirely.

findings.title: Radio comms are queued with a deliberate delay, not applied instantly
findings.detail: EyesAI.TryComms(Il2Cpp.BrainAI friendlyBrain) (rate-limited by CommsCooldown/_lastCommsTime) leads to BrainAI.CalledBackup(Vector3 position, Transform comrade, Transform Target), which does NOT act immediately. It stages _pendingCommsResponse (bool), _pendingCommsPosition, _pendingCommsComrade, _pendingCommsTarget and starts _commsDelayTimer toward _commsDelayTarget rolled between CommsDelayMin and CommsDelayMax. BrainAI.ProcessPendingComms(float dt) later fires ExecuteBackupResponse(Vector3 position, Transform comrade, Transform Target). Gated by useComms and CanCallBackup. Related: AlertedByCommsTimer, backupCaller (Transform).
findings.members: EyesAI.TryComms, BrainAI.CalledBackup, BrainAI.ProcessPendingComms, BrainAI.ExecuteBackupResponse, BrainAI.CommsDelayMin, BrainAI._pendingCommsResponse, BrainAI.CanCallBackup
findings.modding: Patching CalledBackup gets you the callout; patching ExecuteBackupResponse gets you the actual reaction. Zeroing CommsDelayMin/Max makes a squad react as one organism — a cheap difficulty knob.

findings.title: Bot memory is four independent position channels, each with its own timestamp
findings.detail: BrainAI tracks LastKnownTargetPosition, LastHeardTargetPosition, LastCommsTargetPosition and LastSuppressTargetPosition as separate properties over separate backing fields (_lastKnownTargetPosition, _lastHeardTargetPosition, _lastCommmsTargetPosition [sic, triple m], _lastSuppressTargetPosition), each paired with a change timestamp: LastTimeTargetPositionChanged, LastTimeHeardTargetPositionChanged, LastTimeCommsTargetPositionChanged, LastTimeSuppressTargetChanged. Target identity is also split: CurrentSeenTarget, PreviousTarget/PreviousTargetActual, _hasVisuallySeenPreviousTarget (bool) — the bot distinguishes 'told about' from 'actually saw'. Forgetting is governed by ForgetTime/forgetTimer and Patience.
findings.members: BrainAI.LastHeardTargetPosition, BrainAI.LastCommsTargetPosition, BrainAI.LastSuppressTargetPosition, BrainAI._hasVisuallySeenPreviousTarget, BrainAI.PreviousTargetActual, BrainAI.ForgetTime
findings.modding: This is a real sensor-fusion memory model. Reading all four channels plus their timestamps gives an accurate picture of what a bot believes and how it learned it — good for a debug overlay.

findings.title: Cover is fully procedural at runtime with a frame budget and an anti-clumping reservation system
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.DynamicCoverFinder (singleton via Instance) generates cover on demand — no baked cover volumes. FindBestDynamicCover(Vector3 searcherPos, Vector3 threatPos, float maxDist) -> DynamicCoverPoint, fed by GenerateSamplePoints(Vector3 origin, Vector3 threat, float maxDist) -> int with ring sampling (sampleDensity, maxSamplePoints, maxPointsPerRing, minCoverHeight, maxCoverHeight, obstacleMask, groundMask). It is Burst/job-batched: _cmds (Unity.Collections.NativeArray<UnityEngine.RaycastCommand>), _results (NativeArray<UnityEngine.RaycastHit>), RaycastMinPerJob, EnsureScratch(int n). Hard frame budget: TryAcquireQuerySlot() -> bool, maxQueriesPerFrame, _queriesThisFrame, _lastBudgetFrame, maxCandidatesPerQuery. Points are pooled: Rent()/Return(DynamicCoverPoint p), s_pool (Stack), s_candidates (List). Crucially there is a reservation system preventing two bots stacking on one spot: RegisterCoverPosition(Vector3)/UnregisterCoverPosition(Vector3)/IsTooCloseToActiveCover(Vector3) over _activeCoverPositions (List<Vector3>) with MinCoverSeparation.
findings.members: DynamicCoverFinder.FindBestDynamicCover, DynamicCoverFinder.TryAcquireQuerySlot, DynamicCoverFinder.IsTooCloseToActiveCover, DynamicCoverFinder.MinCoverSeparation, DynamicCoverFinder._cmds, DynamicCoverPoint.Score
findings.modding: Custom maps need no cover authoring — cover emerges from colliders on obstacleMask. Bumping maxQueriesPerFrame is the direct lever if bots feel slow to take cover. Forgetting to ReleaseCover leaks a reservation and blocks that spot for everyone.

findings.title: DynamicCoverPoint carries firing geometry, and peeking is a real four-state sub-machine
findings.detail: DynamicCoverPoint exposes position, forward, coverNormal, coverHeight, isDynamic, wallHitPoint plus four derived firing poses: GetStandPosition(), GetCrouchPosition(), GetPeekLeft(), GetPeekRight(). Its Score(Vector3 evaluatorPos, Vector3 threatPos, bool losBlocked, float losHitDist) -> float takes the LOS result as input rather than recomputing it. On the brain side: FindNewCover(Vector3 targetPosition), ReleaseCover(), _currentCover, coverTime/coverTimer, coverQueryCooldown/_lastCoverQueryTime, and _coverThreatPosWhenChosen — cover is re-evaluated when the threat has moved from where it was when the spot was picked. Peeking: UpdateCoverPeek(float dt) -> bool with _peekState (BrainAI/PeekState {None, InCover, PeekingOut, Returning}), PeekChance ('Chance to peek from cover instead of leaving it'), PeekExposureTime, PeekCoverTime, PeekBurstsBeforeReposition, _peekTimer, _peekCount, _peekPosition, _coverReturnPosition.
findings.members: DynamicCoverPoint.GetPeekLeft, DynamicCoverPoint.Score, BrainAI.UpdateCoverPeek, BrainAI.PeekBurstsBeforeReposition, BrainAI._coverThreatPosWhenChosen, BrainAI.coverQueryCooldown
findings.modding: PeekBurstsBeforeReposition and PeekChance are the two fields that most change how 'sticky' bots feel in a firefight.

findings.title: CoveringController is a shader/material component with nothing to do with AI cover
findings.detail: Despite sitting in the AI type list, Il2Cpp.CoveringController's members are coveringColor (Color), coveringBaseColor/coveringNormal/coveringMask/coveringHeight (Texture2D), commonCoveringController/foliageCoveringController/variantCoveringController (float), windMultiply, wetness, vertexAOStrength, smoothnessCoveringRemap (Vector2), coveringTillingMultiply, covering (bool), with Start()/OnValidate()/UpdateMaterials(). It is a snow/dust/moss surface-covering material driver. AI cover lives entirely in DynamicCoverFinder/DynamicCoverPoint.
findings.members: CoveringController.UpdateMaterials, CoveringController.coveringTillingMultiply, CoveringController.wetness
findings.modding: Pure name collision — do not waste time here when investigating AI cover.

findings.title: The AI does not roll to hit — it fires real bullets at a deliberately offset aimpoint
findings.detail: BrainAI.GenerateNearMissOffset(float dt) -> UnityEngine.Vector3 and GetDifficultyKillShotOffset() -> UnityEngine.Vector3 produce an aimOffset applied to IK_AIMING_TARGET/AimingTargetTransform, refreshed on nearMissUpdateTime/nearMissUpdateTimer. WeaponsAI then fires real projectiles: SERVER_SendBullet(Vector3 _muzzlePos, Quaternion _muzzleRot, Vector3 _moaSpread) -> RPC_SendBullet(...), with spread expressed in MOA. Tunables on BrainAI: baseHitChance, difficultyAccuracy (tooltip literal '0 = stormtrooper, 1 = aimbot'), maxEffectiveRangeFalloff, WeaponInaccuracy, WeaponInaccuracyDistance, AimSnap/MinAimSnap/BaseAimSnap, AimCentreMass (bool), SkillRandomness, ReactionTime/_baseReactionTime, TimeToContact/TimeToContactMultiplier, TurnSpeed/turnSpeedMultiplier. UpdateAccuracyAndSnap(float dt) drives it. Difficulty is Il2Cpp.GameManager/AIDifficulty {Easy, Trained, Realistic, Tier1}, set by GameManager.SetAIDifficulty(AIDifficulty) and applied per-bot by BrainAI.SetDifficultyAndStats().
findings.members: BrainAI.GenerateNearMissOffset, BrainAI.GetDifficultyKillShotOffset, BrainAI.difficultyAccuracy, BrainAI.SetDifficultyAndStats, GameManager/AIDifficulty, WeaponsAI.SERVER_SendBullet
findings.modding: Two functions control all AI lethality. Patch GenerateNearMissOffset and GetDifficultyKillShotOffset to retune difficulty without touching damage, health or the FSM.

findings.title: Suppression is bidirectional, squad-coordinated, globally capped, and has a counter-fire sub-system
findings.detail: Outgoing: BrainAI.Suppress(float dt), SuppressLOSBlocked(Vector3 suppressPoint) -> bool, UpdateSuppressionTarget(float dt), AssignSuppressionSector() (squad members divide a sector), SuppressionLeadFactor ('How far ahead of the target's velocity to lead suppression fire'), SuppressionIntelInterval/_suppressionIntelTimer ('Seconds between recalculating suppression target position'), _targetVelocityEstimate, _prevSuppressionTargetPos, _baseSuppressPosition, SuppressRange, SuppressLOSForgivenessMeters, DebugDrawSuppressLOS, _suppressDuration. Globally throttled by GameManager.allAIActiveSuppressing (List<BrainAI>) capped at MaxActiveSuppressionAI. Counter-fire: doesCounterFire, counterFireChance ('...this AI will counter-fire when shot at enough times'), coverInsteadOfCounterFireChance ('...counter-fire is replaced with finding cover instead'), counterFireShotsMin/Max, _counterFireThreshold, _counterFireShotCount, counterFireDuration ('How long (seconds) the AI will counter-fire'), counterFireSpread ('Extra inaccuracy (meters) added to counter-fire aim'), _isCounterFiring, _counterFireTimer, _counterFireTarget, doesReactionarySuppression. Incoming: underFire, UnderFireTimer/UnderFireTime, suppressionResistance ('Resistance to accuracy loss from incoming suppression fire'), UpdateSuppressionAndEvadeLogic(), Evade()/evadeTimer/evadeTime/EvasionSpeed. Player-facing effect is SuppressionPostFX (Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\Suppression System\).
findings.members: BrainAI.AssignSuppressionSector, BrainAI.SuppressionLeadFactor, BrainAI.coverInsteadOfCounterFireChance, BrainAI.suppressionResistance, GameManager.MaxActiveSuppressionAI, BrainAI.SuppressLOSForgivenessMeters
findings.modding: MaxActiveSuppressionAI is a hard global cap — raising bot counts without raising it means most of the squad will never suppress. SuppressLOSForgivenessMeters is why bots shoot slightly through cover edges.

findings.title: Flanking and grenades share one 'advanced tactics' probability gate
findings.detail: BrainAI.TryProactiveFlank() -> bool is governed by ProactiveFlankChance ('Chance per evaluation to attempt a proactive flank while engaging'), FlankOffsetMin/FlankOffsetMax ('Min/Maximum perpendicular offset distance when flanking'), FlankTriggerDistance ('Minimum distance to target before flanking is considered'), FlankCooldown/_flankCooldownTimer ('Seconds to wait between flank attempts'), _isActiveFlanking. Grenades: BrainAI.EvaluateGrenadeUse(float dt) on GrenadeEvaluationInterval/_grenadeEvalTimer, calling WeaponsAI.CanThrowGrenade(Vector3 targetPos) -> bool then SERVER_ThrowGrenade(Vector3 targetPos, bool useFlashbang). Both sit behind TacticsChance ('Percent chance to use advanced tactics (flanking, grenades) per evaluation'). Being flanked is separately detected by EyesAI.CheckFlanker(Vector3 flankerPos, float distance, Transform flankerTarget).
findings.members: BrainAI.TryProactiveFlank, BrainAI.TacticsChance, BrainAI.FlankTriggerDistance, BrainAI.EvaluateGrenadeUse, WeaponsAI.CanThrowGrenade, EyesAI.CheckFlanker
findings.modding: TacticsChance is a single scalar that turns the AI from static shooters into manoeuvring opponents. It gates both systems, so raising it changes grenade frequency too.

findings.title: RaidManager is the real bot spawner and exposes a clean name-based custom-AI hook
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.RaidManager (singleton, NetworkBehaviour) owns spawning: ServerSpawnAI(bool _custom), ServerSpawnHVTs(), SpawnStaticVehicleAI(), SERVER_SpawnIEDs(), InstantiateBot(UnityEngine.GameObject pfab, UnityEngine.Vector3 position, UnityEngine.Quaternion rotation, UnityEngine.Transform parent) -> UnityEngine.GameObject, GetValidSpawnPoint(ref List<GameObject> spawnList) -> Transform, CanSpawn(Vector3 pos, float radius) -> bool, and ApplyBotSpawnSettings(UnityEngine.GameObject bot, Il2Cpp.BotSpawnDetails details) — the single place authored spawn config lands on a brain. Pools: standardAI (GameObject[]), hvtAI, staticVehicleAI, customAI (List<GameObject>), botSpawnPoints, hvtSpawnPoints, botSpawnDelay, spawnChancePerPoint, maxStaticVehicles. The modding seam is SERVERONLY_CustomAISpawnList_AddAI(string botName), SERVERONLY_CustomAISpawnList_RemoveAll(), RespawnCustomAI(), RespawnAI() — paired with GameManager.allAITypes_s (Il2CppStringArray) and GameManager.AllAITypes (List<GameObject>) as the name-to-prefab registry. HVT flow: CMD_HVT_ConfirmKIA(string hvtName, uint hvtID) -> RPC_HVT_ConfirmKIA(string hvtName, int remaining).
findings.members: RaidManager.ServerSpawnAI, RaidManager.ApplyBotSpawnSettings, RaidManager.SERVERONLY_CustomAISpawnList_AddAI, RaidManager.InstantiateBot, RaidManager.CanSpawn, GameManager.allAITypes_s
findings.modding: Registering a bot type name into GameManager.allAITypes_s/AllAITypes and calling SERVERONLY_CustomAISpawnList_AddAI is the intended path for custom enemies — no prefab patching of the spawner required. ApplyBotSpawnSettings is the best hook to override any authored bot config globally.

findings.title: BotSpawner and AiTeam are superseded legacy; two 'CMD' methods are not Mirror Commands
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BotSpawner has spawnCode (UnityEngine.KeyCode) — a press-a-key dev spawner — plus SpawnTargets() (IEnumerator), GetRandomPoint(Vector3 center, float maxDistance), nextSpawnPosition(), isRandom, mixedSpawns, FindSpawns, randomSpawnChance, MaxLocalBotAmount/LocalBotAmount, and uniquely random_DayFOV/random_NightFOV/random_DetectionRange/random_NightDetectionRange (day-night perception variants). It is Weaved as a NetworkBehaviour but has zero SyncVars and zero RPCs, and its CMDSpawnTargets() has NO corresponding UserCode_ method — so despite the name it is a plain local call, not a Mirror [Command]. Same trap in Il2Cpp.aiReinforcement: its CMD_StartReinforcement/RPC_StartReinforcement are real (UserCode_CMD_StartReinforcement and UserCode_RPC_StartReinforcement both exist) but its CMDSpawnTargets() is not. Il2Cpp.AiTeam carries the same five fields as Il2Cpp.TeamID (teamID, thisTeam, hasComms, commsRange, friendlyTeams) but has zero methods — no Awake, Start or OnEnable — and both are superseded by TeamIdentifier/TeamStats.
findings.members: BotSpawner.spawnCode, BotSpawner.CMDSpawnTargets, aiReinforcement.CMDSpawnTargets, aiReinforcement.UserCode_CMD_StartReinforcement, Il2Cpp.AiTeam, Il2Cpp.TeamID
findings.modding: The presence of UserCode_X is the only reliable test for whether an X named CMD_/RPC_ actually crosses the wire. Patching BotSpawner or AiTeam affects nothing in a real mission.

findings.title: Reinforcements are vehicle-borne and trigger-driven, with a timed fallback
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.aiReinforcement models an arriving vehicle: CMD_StartReinforcement() -> RPC_StartReinforcement() (both actually weaved), SpawnBots(), Bots (GameObject[]), Spawns (GameObject[]), animator (the arrival animation), vehicleHealth (Il2Cpp.VehicleHealth), gameObjectsToEnable (GameObject[]), activated (bool). Il2Cpp.ReinforcementTrigger.OnTriggerEnter(UnityEngine.Collider other) references reinforcement — a volume the player walks into. RaidManager drives the timed path: hasReinforcements, timedBackup, reinforcementMinMaxTimer (Vector2), minAIBackupAmount, Reinforcements (aiReinforcement[]), CheckIfCanSendReinforcementsTimed(), AI_BackupCondition() -> bool, UpdateAICount(), SERVER_NotifyPlayerAIAmount(int) -> RPC_NotifyPlayerAIAmount(int).
findings.members: aiReinforcement.RPC_StartReinforcement, aiReinforcement.vehicleHealth, ReinforcementTrigger.OnTriggerEnter, RaidManager.AI_BackupCondition, RaidManager.reinforcementMinMaxTimer
findings.modding: Destroying the reinforcement vehicle (it has VehicleHealth) is a plausible way to cancel a wave. Custom maps get reinforcements by placing an aiReinforcement vehicle plus a ReinforcementTrigger volume.

findings.title: BotSpawnDetails authors ranges; the brain stores rolled scalars
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BotSpawnDetails is the per-spawn-point authored config consumed by RaidManager.ApplyBotSpawnSettings: idleState (IdleStates), reactType (ReactType), doorInteractionType (DoorInteractionMode), DetectionTimeMultiplier, DetectionRange, HearingRange, FOV, maxEffectiveRange, useComms, DoesCounterSuppression, WanderDistance, modifyStance/doesCrouch/doesProne, isSpawnGroup with GroupSpawnPoints (List<GameObject>), hvtLinkedSpawnGroup (BotSpawnDetails — ties a bodyguard group to an HVT), patrol route (patrolPoints List<Transform>, PatrolSpeed, PatrolLooping, patrolWaitTime), disableNavmesh, isProne, plus editor gizmos DrawPatrolRoute()/DrawArrowGizmo(...). Note crouchDistance and proneDistance are UnityEngine.Vector2 here but plain float on BrainAI — a min/max range is authored and a value rolled per bot at spawn. Il2Cpp.AIPatrol is data-only (patrolPoints, currentWayPointIndex, Looping, patrolWaitTime, onReachDestination : AIPatrol/OnReachDestination {Wait, MoveImmediately}) with no methods; BrainAI.Patrol(float dt) drives it.
findings.members: BotSpawnDetails.hvtLinkedSpawnGroup, BotSpawnDetails.crouchDistance, BrainAI.crouchDistance, AIPatrol/OnReachDestination, BotSpawnDetails.DrawPatrolRoute
findings.modding: Per-bot variety comes from the Vector2 ranges, so overriding BrainAI's scalars post-spawn makes a squad uniform. Patrol routes are plain Transform lists — trivially generated for custom maps.

findings.title: Only intent crosses the wire; all tactical reasoning is server-only and clients re-simulate presentation
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC carries the entire bot presentation state as SyncVars, each with a hook: SpeedXTarget, SpeedYTarget, agentVelocity (Vector3), aimTargetPosition (Vector3), CurrentRotation (float), isCrouching (OnCrouchUpdate), isProne (OnProneUpdate), inCombat (OnCombatUpdate), inCombatReady (OnCombatReadyUpdate), isArmed (OnArmedUpdate), InInteriorCollider/InOpenInteriorCollider (OnInInteriorColliderUpdate), CurrentRotation (OnCurrentRotationChanged), plus StartTurnInPlaceAnimation(bool isLeft) and SERVER_PlayKickAnimation()/RPC_PlayKickAnimation(). Clients then locally re-run AiAnimationController, AiRotationController (which has an explicit ClientSideLogic()) and BotAimCorrection. BrainAI is itself a NetworkBehaviour but its ONLY weaved RPCs are the suicide-bomber pair (RPC_BomberActivated, RPC_BomberExplode(Vector3)) — no state, target or cover decision is ever replicated. Bot transform send-rate is tuned globally on GameManager: botTransformSyncRate, botSendThreshold, SetBotSendThreshold(float), disableFixedBotSendRate, ToggleFixedBotSendRate().
findings.members: NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC.aimTargetPosition, NetworkAnimatorSyncNPC.OnCombatReadyUpdate, AiRotationController.ClientSideLogic, BrainAI.UserCode_RPC_BomberExplode__Vector3, GameManager.botSendThreshold
findings.modding: A client-side mod can never read a bot's state, target or cover — only the animator SyncVars. Any AI-behaviour mod must run on the host. Hook the UserCode_* receive side for client-visible reactions.

findings.title: WeaponsAI is server-authoritative with burst logic, IK range-culling and full grenade ballistics
findings.detail: NetworkBehaviour with SyncVars puppetWeaponIndex (hook OnPuppetWeaponIndexUpdate(int previous, int current)), puppetWeaponID, aimCorrection (hook OnAimCorrectionUpdate(bool, bool)), grenadesRemaining, flashbangsRemaining, enableWeaponAnimator. Fire path: SERVER_SetFireBool(bool state) -> RPC_SetFireBool(bool state, int _currentBurst); SERVER_SendBullet(...) -> RPC_SendBullet(...); SERVER_Reload() -> RPC_Reload() -> ReloadWeapon(); CMD_DropWeapon() -> RPC_DropWeapon(). Burst: currentBurst, fired_Burst, timeBetweenBursts/init_timeBetweenBursts, _fireTimer, reloadTime, isReloading, fireWeapon. Grenades: CanThrowGrenade(Vector3 targetPos), SERVER_ThrowGrenade(Vector3 targetPos, bool useFlashbang), grenadeMinDistance/grenadeMaxDistance/grenadeThrowChance/grenadeCooldown/_grenadeCooldownTimer, ballistics grenadeThrowForceMin/Max and grenadeLaunchSpeed, and animation timing grenadeThrowAnimation (string), grenadeThrowAnimBlend, grenadeWindUpDelay, grenadeReleaseDelay. Perf: maxIKdistance + IK_RangeCheck() disables ikBehaviours (Behaviour[]) and the FinalIK LeftArmIK/RightArmIK (RootMotion.FinalIK.ArmIK) beyond a distance; _sqrDistanceToCamera, renderingMask, noWeaponTimer. Weapons are Il2Cpp.PuppetWeapon in weaponList (List<PuppetWeapon>) selected by INDEX.
findings.members: WeaponsAI.SERVER_SetFireBool, WeaponsAI.RPC_SetFireBool, WeaponsAI.IK_RangeCheck, WeaponsAI.grenadeReleaseDelay, WeaponsAI.weaponList, WeaponsAI.puppetWeaponIndex
findings.modding: puppetWeaponIndex syncs as a list index, so weaponList is append-only across host and clients — the same constraint as LoadoutManager.Game_Weapons. RaidManager.prohibitedWeapons/mapSpecificWeapons (PuppetWeapon[]) gate what bots may carry per map.

findings.title: Aim correction rotates the parent so the muzzle child points at the target, with wall-collision fallbacks
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BotAimCorrection's core trick is RotateParentToMakeChildLookAt(UnityEngine.Transform parent, UnityEngine.Transform child, UnityEngine.Vector3 targetPosition) — animation drives the pose, then the arm parent is rotated so the actual muzzle transform lands on target. Pipeline: PerformLogic() -> CorrectAim()/PointGunAtTarget()/SetGunForward(), weighted by AimCorrectionWeight and ComponentStrength, blended toward IdleAnimationRotationOffset or CombatIdleRotationOffset by IsInCombat/IsInCombatReady. Muzzle-into-wall handling: SetupWeaponCollision()/CheckWeaponCollision()/HasWeaponCollided() over Il2Cpp.SimpleWeaponCollision with three distinct posture offsets — WallCollisionOffset, WallCollisionOffsetCrouched, WallCollisionOffsetIdle (pre-baked as _qWallStanding/_qWallCrouched/_qWallIdle/_qCombatIdle/_qIdleAnim Quaternions) — plus SetGunUp(bool _gunUp). Driven both by its own LateUpdate() and by CallLateUpdate() from GameManager's allAIAimCorrection round-robin.
findings.members: BotAimCorrection.RotateParentToMakeChildLookAt, BotAimCorrection.CheckWeaponCollision, BotAimCorrection.WallCollisionOffsetCrouched, BotAimCorrection._qWallStanding, BotAimCorrection.CallLateUpdate, SimpleWeaponCollision
findings.modding: Custom bot weapons need a correctly oriented muzzle child transform and a SimpleWeaponCollision, or bots will visibly aim off-target and clip guns through walls.

findings.title: Rotation is decoupled body/spine with an explicit leg-correction fixup; animation params are dirty-gated
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.AiRotationController separates spine aim from foot rotation: _spineTransform, SpineRotationOffset, MaxSpineAngle, SetBotRotationTarget(UnityEngine.Quaternion rotationTarget), SetAiLookAtTarget(UnityEngine.Vector3 LookAt), _lookingAtPositionTarget, RotationAcceleration with _targetRotationSpeed/_currentRotationSpeed and MaxRotationSpeed, StartTurnInPlace(float angle), Tick(float dt), ClientSideLogic(). A dedicated leg-correction sub-system unwinds accumulated spine twist: _correctingLegRotation, _legCorrectionTime, _legAngleCorrectionTargetAngle, _amountLegCorrected, _legAngleCorrectionAmount. Il2Cpp.AiAnimationController caches all Animator param hashes (_speedXHash, _speedYHash, _crouchHash, _proneHash, _inCombatHash, _isArmedHash, _turnLeftHash, _turnRightHash) and only pushes values past SPEED_DIRTY_THRESHOLD, via SetSpeedXTarget/SetSpeedYTarget/SetMoveTowardsSpeed/SetProne/SetCrouch/SetInCombat/SetIsArmed/StartTurnInPlace(bool isLeft) and Tick(float dt).
findings.members: AiRotationController._legAngleCorrectionAmount, AiRotationController.MaxSpineAngle, AiRotationController.ClientSideLogic, AiAnimationController.SPEED_DIRTY_THRESHOLD, AiAnimationController._turnLeftHash
findings.modding: Custom bot rigs must expose a spine transform and matching Animator parameter names, since hashes are resolved once at init from fixed names.

findings.title: BotNetworking and BotHandIK are data-only markers with no behaviour
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.BotNetworking has exactly one member — scriptsToDisable (Il2CppReferenceArray<UnityEngine.Behaviour>) — and no methods at all, not even Awake. Despite the name it performs no networking; it is a manifest of behaviours some other system strips on non-authoritative instances. Il2Cpp.BotHandIK likewise has only botIndex (int) and LeftHandRotationOffset (Vector3) with no methods; the actual work is done by Il2Cpp.HandIkApplicator (FBIK : RootMotion.FinalIK.FullBodyBipedIK, executionOrder : RootMotion.FinalIK.IKExecutionOrder, LateUpdate()). Il2Cpp.AITest is a leftover dev tool (GrabAllGrounderIK/DisableGroundIK/EnableGroundIK/GrabAllIK/DisableIK/EnableIK over GrounderBipedIK[] and FullBodyBipedIK[]), and Il2Cpp.BotAnimationTriggerDebug has a single PlayKickAnimation().
findings.members: BotNetworking.scriptsToDisable, BotHandIK.botIndex, HandIkApplicator.FBIK, AITest.GrabAllGrounderIK, BotAnimationTriggerDebug.PlayKickAnimation
findings.modding: Patching BotNetworking or BotHandIK accomplishes nothing — there is no code to patch. Find the reader instead.

findings.title: VehicleAI is a complete second AI implementation that shares no code with BrainAI
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.VehicleAI reimplements the whole perception and firing stack for turrets: its own Vision(), Comms(), FindTarget(), FindClosestsTarget(), SetEyesForward(Vector3 forward), GenerateNearMissOffset(), DetectionLayerMask, TurretFOV, DetectionDistance, DetectionMultiplier, CommunitcationsDistance [sic], HasNVG, ReactionTime, TimeToContact/TimeToContactMultiplier, SuppressionTime, and its own accuracy triple baseHitChance/difficultyAccuracy/maxEffectiveRangeFalloff with aimOffset. Firing: FireCannon(), SpawnProjectile(Il2Cpp.Bullet bullet, Vector3 muzzlePos, Quaternion muzzleRot, Vector3 _moaSpread), minBurst/maxBurst/currentBurst/fired_Burst, ShootingFrequency with min/max, Firerate, timeBetweenRounds. Turret kinematics: TurretAimer, TurretY, TurretGun, TurretSpeed, MaxElevation, MinElevation, SyncVar AimingPosition (hook OnAimingPositionUpdate) and IsFiring. It ALSO spawns a BrainAI gunner puppet: ServerSpawnTurrentAI(), turrentBot (BrainAI), TurrentSpawn, InstantiateBot(...), Cmd_SetBrain(Mirror.NetworkIdentity target), RPC_SetTurrentAITypeShit(NetworkConnectionToClient target, BrainAI brain). Combat lights: SERVER_SetCombatLights/CMD_SetCombatLights/RPC_SetCombatLights(bool), HasCombatLightsAtNight.
findings.members: VehicleAI.Vision, VehicleAI.FireCannon, VehicleAI.turrentBot, VehicleAI.ServerSpawnTurrentAI, VehicleAI.RPC_SetTurrentAITypeShit, VehicleAI.TurretFOV
findings.modding: Any perception or accuracy change must be applied twice — once to BrainAI/EyesAI and once to VehicleAI — or manned turrets will behave inconsistently with infantry.

findings.title: Suicide bombers are a full subsystem on BrainAI, including cook-off on death
findings.detail: BrainAI carries isSuicideBomber plus a complete bomber pipeline: SERVER_ActivateBomber() -> RPC_BomberActivated(), SERVER_BomberExplode() -> RPC_BomberExplode(UnityEngine.Vector3 position), with bomberDetonationRange, bomberFuseTime/_bomberFuseTimer/_bomberFuseStarted, bomberExplosionRadius, bomberExplosionDamage (int), bomberDeathExplodeChance (float — a probability the vest cooks off when the bot is killed rather than reaching the target), bomberExplosionPrefab (GameObject), bomberActivationSFX (AudioClip), bomberAudioSource, _bomberActivated, BomberExploded, and _bomberOverlapBuffer (Collider[]) for the damage query. These two are BrainAI's only weaved RPCs.
findings.members: BrainAI.SERVER_ActivateBomber, BrainAI.RPC_BomberExplode, BrainAI.bomberDeathExplodeChance, BrainAI._bomberOverlapBuffer, BrainAI.isSuicideBomber
findings.modding: Setting isSuicideBomber on any standard bot prefab should work without a special archetype, since all the tuning lives on BrainAI itself.

findings.title: Team confidence, fallback and defensive posts form an emergent morale layer
findings.detail: BrainAI.UpdateTeamConfidence(float dt) maintains teamConfidence (float) on _teamConfidenceTimer over a TEAM_AWARENESS_RADIUS, fed by cached rosters allFriendlyBrains (List<BrainAI>), allEnemyBrains (List<BrainAI>), allEnemyPlayers (List<PlayerMaster>). FallBack is a first-class state with _fallBackTimer. ReactType.Defensive bots have a post to hold: DefensiveInitialPosition (Vector3) and DefensiveInitialRotation (Quaternion). Related per-tick updaters: UpdateRespondingLogic(float dt) with responding/respondtimer, UpdateStanceAndCombatState(), UpdateStanceBasedOnDistance() (proneDistance/crouchDistance/proneMinCombatTime/stayProne/useStanceOnTarget), UpdateFlashedAndDetection(float dt) with isFlashed/flashedTimer, UpdateStuckDetection(float dt) with _stuckCheckPos/_stuckTimer/STUCK_CHECK_INTERVAL/STUCK_DISTANCE_THRESHOLD, and OnKill() -> IEnumerator. Rosters are refreshed via TeamManager.GrabAllEnemyBrains(int teamID), GrabAllAiTeamMembersBrains(int), GrabAllEnemyPlayers(int) and the allocation-free TeamManager.GetPossibleTargets(int myTeam, List<UnityEngine.Transform> results).
findings.members: BrainAI.UpdateTeamConfidence, BrainAI.TEAM_AWARENESS_RADIUS, BrainAI.DefensiveInitialPosition, BrainAI.UpdateStuckDetection, TeamManager.GetPossibleTargets, TeamManager.GrabAllEnemyBrains
findings.modding: teamConfidence is the most promising single value for a 'morale' mod. Runtime probe: read teamConfidence across a squad while killing members one at a time and watch for FallBack transitions via SetNewAiState.

findings.title: Movement speed is a layered model with slope sampling, chase ramp-up and smoothed direction
findings.detail: BrainAI.CalculateDynamicSpeed(float baseSpeed) composes: base speeds PatrolSpeed, TacticalCombatSpeed, FastCombatSpeed, ChaseSpeed, EvasionSpeed; multipliers SpeedApproachMultiplier and SpeedSprintMultiplier; a chase ramp via ChaseAccelerationRate and _chaseSpeedBonus (bots accelerate the longer they pursue); smoothing via SpeedAcceleration, SpeedDeceleration, DirectionChangeRate and _smoothedDirection; and terrain via GetSlopeSpeedMultiplier() with SlopeUpSpeedMultiplier, SlopeDownSpeedMultiplier, MaxSlopeAngle, _currentSlopeMultiplier and — importantly — _cachedSlopeMultiplier gated by _slopeCheckTimer/SlopeCheckInterval so the slope raycast is not per-frame. UpdateMovementRotation() and SyncAgentAndAnimator() bridge to the agent and animator; LookAtTarget(UnityEngine.Vector3 position, bool requireTarget, bool flatY, bool speed0) is the look primitive.
findings.members: BrainAI.CalculateDynamicSpeed, BrainAI.GetSlopeSpeedMultiplier, BrainAI._chaseSpeedBonus, BrainAI.SlopeCheckInterval, BrainAI._smoothedDirection, BrainAI.LookAtTarget
findings.modding: Writing AgentController.maxSpeed directly will be overwritten each tick by CalculateDynamicSpeed — patch that method or the base speed fields instead.

findings.title: V2AIParametres is the shared bot archetype asset, including per-limb death clips and an incapacitated state
findings.detail: BrainAI.AI_Parametres -> Il2Cpp.V2AIParametres holds everything shared per bot archetype: Ragdoll (Il2CppFIMSpace.FProceduralAnimation.RagdollAnimator2 — bots use FIMSpace Ragdoll Animator 2, not PuppetMaster), FallImpactPower, Force (UnityEngine.ForceMode), Sleep, weapon-style animator controllers PistolController/PistolStyle2Controller/PistolStyle3Controller/RifleController (RuntimeAnimatorController), meshRenderers (SkinnedMeshRenderer[]), scriptsDisableAfterLookFade (Behaviour[]), and animation-name string arrays selected by which body part was hit: HitReactionsBody, DeathHeadClips, DeathNeckClips, DeathChestClips, DeathStomachClips, DeathBackClips, DeathLArmClips, DeathRArmClips, DeathLLegClips, DeathRLegClips — plus IncapacitatedBackClips, IncapacitatedChestClips, IncapacitatedStomachClips, evidencing a downed-but-not-dead state.
findings.members: V2AIParametres.Ragdoll, V2AIParametres.DeathHeadClips, V2AIParametres.IncapacitatedChestClips, V2AIParametres.RifleController, V2AIParametres.scriptsDisableAfterLookFade, BrainAI.AI_Parametres
findings.modding: A custom bot archetype is mostly a new V2AIParametres asset. The clip arrays are animation state NAMES (strings), so new death animations only need matching state names in the controller. Incapacitation clips exist for only three body regions — either an unfinished feature or deliberately limited.

findings.title: A usable debug console surface already exists for AI
findings.detail: GameManager exposes QFSW Quantum Console commands confirmed by both signatures and metadata literals: SetAI_UpdateFreqency(float time) [sic — misspelled in the game], SetAI_UpdateIntervals(int frameCount), SetBotViewDistanceMultiplier(float value), SetAIDifficulty(AIDifficulty difficulty), SetBotSendThreshold(float threshold), ToggleFixedBotSendRate(), SetAIAgentsState(bool state), SetAIAnimationState(bool state), SetAIRagdollState(bool state), GetAICount(), DebugDestroyAllAi(), DebugDestroyAllAiNonCheat(), DebugSetAIcullMode(UnityEngine.AnimatorCullingMode animatorCullingMode), Debug_DumpAI_InCombatState(). Matching literals include 'AI_ToggleBrainAI', 'Debug_DumpAI_InCombatState', 'SetAI_UpdateFreqency', 'SetAI_UpdateIntervals'. BrainAI additionally has DebugLogs (bool), DebugDrawSuppressLOS (bool), OnDrawGizmosSelected(), and per-bot render LOD control DisableShadows()/EnableShadows()/_currentCullingMode (AnimatorCullingMode).
findings.members: GameManager.Debug_DumpAI_InCombatState, GameManager.SetAI_UpdateIntervals, GameManager.DebugSetAIcullMode, GameManager.SetAIAgentsState, BrainAI.DebugLogs, BrainAI.DebugDrawSuppressLOS
findings.modding: Use these before writing any instrumentation — Debug_DumpAI_InCombatState and SetAIAgentsState(false) alone cover most AI debugging, and SetAI_UpdateIntervals lets you slow the brain to observe transitions.

findings.title: EyesAI batches its LOS raycasts, but the buffer ownership is not visible statically
findings.detail: EyesAI holds _candidateIndices (Il2CppSystem.Collections.Generic.List<int>), RaycastMinPerJob (int) and cacheHit (UnityEngine.RaycastHit) — the RaycastMinPerJob field name is the standard UnityEngine.RaycastCommand.ScheduleBatch parameter, strongly implying batched job raycasts for candidate visibility. However, unlike DynamicCoverFinder — which explicitly owns _cmds (NativeArray<RaycastCommand>) and _results (NativeArray<RaycastHit>) plus EnsureScratch(int n) — EyesAI declares no NativeArray fields, so it must either allocate them transiently per Vision() call or borrow a shared buffer from elsewhere. Which of those it does materially affects per-frame allocation cost with high bot counts.
findings.members: EyesAI.RaycastMinPerJob, EyesAI._candidateIndices, EyesAI.cacheHit, DynamicCoverFinder._cmds, DynamicCoverFinder.EnsureScratch
findings.modding: Runtime probe: attach a Unity profiler sample or a GC.GetTotalMemory delta around EyesAI.Vision() with 30+ bots active. If allocations scale with bot count, per-call NativeArray allocation is confirmed and is a worthwhile optimisation target for a performance mod.

findings.title: NetworkManagerVectorGames is the Mirror NetworkManager subclass and owns the whole session lifecycle
findings.detail: Static singleton (`get_instance`). Overrides the full Mirror surface: `Awake`, `OnStartServer`, `OnStopServer`, `OnStartClient`, `OnClientConnect`, `OnClientDisconnect`, `OnServerConnect(NetworkConnectionToClient)`, `OnServerDisconnect(NetworkConnectionToClient)`, `OnServerAddPlayer(NetworkConnectionToClient)`, `ServerChangeScene(string)`, `OnClientChangeScene(string, Il2CppMirror.SceneOperation, bool)`, `OnClientSceneChanged()`. Custom scene plumbing: `SwitchSceneAfterSeconds(string) -> IEnumerator`, `ApplyServerSceneChange(string)`, `SwitchToLobby()`, `LeaveMatch()`. Session state fields: `selectedOperation` (string), `MenuScene` (string), `allOperations` (List<string>), `isServerHost` (bool), `GameManagerNetworkPrefab` (GameObject). Also carries an unrelated global AI knob, `Bot_Attack_Tick_Rate` (float). Static events `OnClientConnected` / `OnClientDisconnected` (Il2CppSystem.Action) are the cleanest mod hook for connect/disconnect — they are add/remove accessors, so a mod can subscribe without Harmony.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.NetworkManagerVectorGames; instance; isServerHost; selectedOperation; MenuScene; allOperations; GameManagerNetworkPrefab; Bot_Attack_Tick_Rate; OnClientConnected; OnClientDisconnected; SwitchToLobby; LeaveMatch; ServerChangeScene; SwitchSceneAfterSeconds; ApplyServerSceneChange
findings.modding: Subscribe to the static Action events instead of patching. GameManagerNetworkPrefab is settable, so a mod can swap/extend the spawned game-manager object. Bot_Attack_Tick_Rate is a one-property difficulty lever.

findings.title: Only two transports are wired: a Steam transport and an 'offline' transport — plus a shipped direct-IP KCP client path
findings.detail: `NetworkManagerVectorGames` exposes exactly two Transport-typed properties, `Steam` (Il2CppMirror.Transport) and `OfflineTransport` (Il2CppMirror.Transport), toggled by `transportSteam()` and `TransportOffline()`. Separately there is a public `startClientKCP()` and a private `ToggleConnectionMenu()`, alongside `managerHUD` (Il2CppMirror.NetworkManagerHUD) and `networkPing` (Il2CppMirror.NetworkPingDisplay). That is Mirror's stock debug HUD shipped in the retail build with a direct-address KCP connect path that bypasses Steam entirely. The 'offline' transport is how solo play works: `SteamLobby.HostLobbySolo()` exists alongside `HostLobby()`.
findings.members: Steam; OfflineTransport; transportSteam(); TransportOffline(); startClientKCP(); ToggleConnectionMenu(); managerHUD; networkPing
findings.modding: startClientKCP() is a public instance method — a mod can call it directly for LAN/direct-IP play without touching Steam matchmaking. Assigning a KcpTransport to the `Steam` slot before StartHost would give a fully Steam-free dedicated-ish host.

findings.title: Four Mirror transports and two lobby SDKs ship in the binary; most are dead weight
findings.detail: Confirmed present as real types: `Il2Cppkcp2k.KcpTransport` (assembly Il2CppMirror.Transports), `Il2CppMirror.LiteNetLibTransport` (own assembly Il2CppLiteNetLibTransport), `Il2CppMirror.TelepathyTransport`, `Il2CppMirror.SimpleWeb.SimpleWebTransport`, `Il2CppMirror.LatencySimulation`, `Il2CppMirror.MultiplexTransport`, `Il2CppMirror.FizzySteam.FizzySteamworks` (own assembly Il2CppFizzySteamworks). Also present but unreferenced by game code: the entire Edgegap relay + Edgegap lobby service stack (`Edgegap.EdgegapKcpTransport`, `EdgegapLobbyKcpTransport`, `LobbyApi`, `LobbyCreateRequest`, ...) and `DiscordGameSDK\LobbyManager.cs`. Mirror's own `NetworkLobbyManager`/`NetworkRoomManager`/`NetworkRoomPlayer` are compiled in but the game uses none of them — it rolls its own Steam lobby.
findings.members: Il2Cppkcp2k.KcpTransport; Il2CppMirror.LiteNetLibTransport; Il2CppMirror.TelepathyTransport; Il2CppMirror.SimpleWeb.SimpleWebTransport; Il2CppMirror.LatencySimulation; Il2CppMirror.MultiplexTransport; Edgegap.LobbyApi; Mirror.NetworkRoomManager
findings.modding: DEV-CONFIRMED: the OPERATOR developers confirm this middleware is not used. Edgegap in particular is never touched and is present only because Mirror bundles it. LatencySimulation and MultiplexTransport are usable as-is: wrap the Steam transport in LatencySimulation for netcode testing, or Multiplex Steam+KCP so Steam friends and direct-IP clients can join the same host.

findings.title: FizzySteamworks is the Steam transport, and lobby ping estimation implies SteamNetworkingSockets (next-gen) mode
findings.detail: `Il2CppMirror.FizzySteam.FizzySteamworks` has `UseNextGenSteamNetworking` (bool), `AllowSteamRelay` (bool), `InitRelayNetworkAccess()`, `Timeout` (int), `Channels` (Il2CppStructArray<Steamworks.EP2PSend>), `STEAM_SCHEME`, and `ServerGetClientAddress(int connectionId) -> string`. Both implementation families are compiled in (`Mirror.FizzySteam.LegacyClient/LegacyServer/LegacyCommon` = old P2P; `NextClient/NextServer/NextCommon` = SteamNetworkingSockets). `SteamLobby.EstimateLobbyPing(CSteamID lobby, ref Steamworks.SteamNetworkPingLocation_t local)` and `WaitForPingLocation()` use the SteamNetworkingUtils ping-location API, which only exists in the next-gen stack — strong evidence `UseNextGenSteamNetworking` is true and relay is on.
findings.members: Mirror.FizzySteam.FizzySteamworks; UseNextGenSteamNetworking; AllowSteamRelay; InitRelayNetworkAccess(); ServerGetClientAddress(int); STEAM_SCHEME; Mirror.FizzySteam.NextServer; Mirror.FizzySteam.LegacyServer
findings.modding: ServerGetClientAddress returns the peer SteamID string — that is the server's only trustworthy identity source (see the SetMyName finding). Reading UseNextGenSteamNetworking at runtime settles Legacy-vs-Next.

findings.title: Session creation and discovery live entirely in Il2CppVectorGames.SteamLobby, a singleton wrapping Steam matchmaking
findings.detail: Hosting: `HostLobby()` / `HostLobbySolo()` -> Steam `LobbyCreated_t` -> `OnLobbyCreated(LobbyCreated_t)`, which writes lobby metadata via `SetLobbyData(string key, string value)` / `SetLobbyDataInt(CSteamID, string, int)`. Metadata key names are fields: `HostAddressKey`, `MapIDKey`, `LobbyDataKey`, `LobbyLocationKey`, plus `LobbyName`, `LobbyPassword`, `lobbyType` (Steamworks.ELobbyType), `MigratingHostID`. Joining: `JoinLobby(CSteamID)`, `OnGameLobbyJoinRequested(GameLobbyJoinRequested_t)` (Steam friends 'Join Game'), `OnLobbyEntered(LobbyEnter_t)` -> read HostAddressKey -> StartClient; failures go through `ReportFailedLobbyEnter(EChatRoomEnterResponse)`. Leaving is enumerated: `LeaveLobbyReason { HostClosedServer, HostDisconnected, SelfLeaveLobby, HostKickedMe, HostBannedMe }` consumed by `LeaveLobby(LeaveLobbyReason)`. Player cap goes through `SetMaxConnections(int i_connections)`, and `PublishLobbyPlayerCountDetails()` republishes occupancy so the browser stays accurate.
findings.members: Il2CppVectorGames.SteamLobby.singleton; HostLobby(); HostLobbySolo(); JoinLobby(CSteamID); LeaveLobby(LeaveLobbyReason); SetMaxConnections(int); SetLobbyData(string,string); SetLobbyDataInt(CSteamID,string,int); HostAddressKey; MapIDKey; LobbyName; LobbyPassword; lobbyType; MigratingHostID; PublishLobbyPlayerCountDetails()
findings.modding: SteamLobby.singleton.SetLobbyData is the hook for advertising a mod tag in lobby metadata so modded clients can filter for each other. lobbyType is settable at runtime to force public/friends-only.

findings.title: The server browser works around Steam's 50-result cap with time-bucketed lobby keys — and this is a hard cross-build compatibility constraint
findings.detail: `GetBucketCount()`, `GetCurrentBucketIndex()`, `BuildBucketKey(int bucketIndex)`, `GetHostLobbyKey()`, `BuildSearchKeys()`, `RequestNextSearch()`, `_searchKeys` (List<string>), `_currentSearchKeyIndex`, `_isSearching`, controlled by `UseLobbyKey`, `LobbyKey`, `UseTimeBucketedKeys`, `LobbyKeyBucketMinutes`, `IncludeLegacyKeyInSearch`. A shipped tooltip literal states it plainly: bucket length in minutes, 10 = 6 buckets/hour, up to 6x50 results, and 'MUST match across all host & client builds'. `FindGame()` fires `RequestNextSearch()` repeatedly and accumulates through `OnLobbyMatchListReceived(LobbyMatchList_t)`; dedup via `_seenLobbyIds` (HashSet<CSteamID>) and `_shownLobbies` (HashSet<ulong>); staleness via `IsLobbyStale(CSteamID)`, `UpdateLobbyTimestamp(CSteamID)`, `MaxAgeMinutes` (double). Results are then ordered by `SortJoinableLobbiesByPing()` using `EstimateLobbyPing`.
findings.members: UseTimeBucketedKeys; LobbyKeyBucketMinutes; IncludeLegacyKeyInSearch; BuildBucketKey(int); GetHostLobbyKey(); BuildSearchKeys(); RequestNextSearch(); _seenLobbyIds; _shownLobbies; MaxAgeMinutes; IsLobbyStale(CSteamID); SortJoinableLobbiesByPing()
findings.modding: A mod that changes LobbyKey or LobbyKeyBucketMinutes without warning partitions modded hosts out of the vanilla browser (and vice versa). That is either a bug source or a deliberate way to build a modded-only server list.

findings.title: Player movement is owner-authoritative: Smooth Sync relays owner -> server -> non-owners
findings.detail: The replication asset is `Smooth.SmoothSyncMirror` (script path `\Assets\_tools\Smooth Sync\Mirror\Smooth Sync Asset\SmoothSyncMirror.cs`). Its two networked entry points appear verbatim in metadata as `SmoothSyncFromOwnerToServer` and `SmoothSyncFromServerToNonOwners`, alongside `SmoothSyncUpdate`, `InitialSmoothSync`, `SmoothSyncForcedUpdateTimer`, `childObjectSmoothSyncs`, `mainSmoothSync`. That naming is unambiguous: the owning client is the source of truth for its own transform and the server is a relay, not an authority. `GameManagerNetwork.CMD_RequestSmoothsyncForceUpdate()` -> `SetSmoothSyncForceUpdate()` lets a client ask for a full resend (used on join/scene load).
findings.members: Smooth.SmoothSyncMirror; SmoothSyncFromOwnerToServer; SmoothSyncFromServerToNonOwners; InitialSmoothSync; childObjectSmoothSyncs; GameManagerNetwork.CMD_RequestSmoothsyncForceUpdate()
findings.modding: No server-side movement validation exists anywhere in the type graph. Speed/teleport/noclip are client-side and will replicate as-is. Conversely, a mod that wants to move a remote player cannot — it must move its own.

findings.title: MilkTransformSync implements request/grant ownership arbitration and pushes updates via TargetRpc, not ClientRpc — per-client interest management done by hand
findings.detail: Ownership handshake: `CMD_RequestOwnership(NetworkConnectionToClient sender)` -> `ProcessOwnershipRequest(...)` -> `Server_SetOwner(NetworkConnectionToClient)` -> `TargetRPC_GrantOwnership(NetworkConnectionToClient)`; release via `CMD_RequestRevokeOwnership(...)` -> `ServerRevokeOwner`/`RevokeCurrentOwner` -> `TargetRPC_RevokeOwnership(...)`, with callbacks `OnBecameController()` / `OnLostControl()` and state `currentOwner` (NetworkConnectionToClient), `IsCurrentOwner`, `HasOwner`. Data path: owner sends `SendPosition(Vector3, NetworkConnectionToClient)`, `SendRotation(Quaternion, NetworkConnectionToClient)`, `SendPositionAndRotation(...)`, `SendPositionAndRotationHotReloadSafe(...)` (connection LAST = Mirror Command with injected sender); the server then emits `ReceivePosition(NetworkConnectionToClient, Vector3)`, `ReceiveRotation(NetworkConnectionToClient, Quaternion)`, `ReceivePositionAndRotation(NetworkConnectionToClient, Vector3, Quaternion)` (connection FIRST = TargetRpc). The CMD_/TargetRPC_ naming on the sibling `MilkRigidbodySync` confirms that parameter-position convention. There is no ClientRpc, so the server must be looping connections and target-rpc'ing each one individually — which is exactly what `NetworkLOD.ShouldUpdate(Vector3 objectPosition, int stableId)` with `SQR_CLOSE`/`SQR_MID`/`SQR_FAR` is for: per-recipient distance culling and staggered rates.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.MilkTransformSync; CMD_RequestOwnership; TargetRPC_GrantOwnership; Server_SetOwner; ReceivePositionAndRotation; SendPositionAndRotationHotReloadSafe; currentOwner; UpdatesPerSecond; NetworkLOD.ShouldUpdate(Vector3,int); SQR_CLOSE; SQR_MID; SQR_FAR
findings.modding: Any modded interactable that needs client-driven motion should reuse MilkTransformSync rather than Mirror NetworkTransform — it already handles the authority handoff. `stableId` phase-offsets updates, so mods spawning many synced objects must pass distinct ids or they will all tick on the same frame.

findings.title: MilkRigidbodySync adds a delayed-revoke grace window so thrown objects do not snap on release
findings.detail: `CMD_SetVelocity(Vector3 Velocity, Vector3 AngularVelocity, NetworkConnectionToClient client)` and `CMD_ReleaseWithVelocity(Vector3 velocity, Vector3 angularVelocity, NetworkConnectionToClient client)` (Commands), `TargetRPC_SetVelocity(NetworkConnectionToClient, Vector3, Vector3)` (TargetRpc). State: `releaseOwnershipDelay` (float), `revokeTimer` (float), `pendingRevokeClient` (NetworkConnectionToClient), `TryCancelPendingRevoke() -> bool`, `savedLinearVelocity`, `savedAngularVelocity`, plus `SetNormalRB()` / `SetKinematicRB()` — non-owners run the body kinematic.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.MilkRigidbodySync; CMD_ReleaseWithVelocity; TryCancelPendingRevoke(); releaseOwnershipDelay; pendingRevokeClient; SetKinematicRB(); SetNormalRB()
findings.modding: Grabbing a physics prop twice in quick succession takes the TryCancelPendingRevoke path — a mod adding new grabbables must respect releaseOwnershipDelay or ownership will thrash.

findings.title: Voice is MetaVoiceChat over Mirror RPCs, broadcast to every client — proximity and radio filtering are purely cosmetic and client-side
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.PlayerVoice.VoiceChatComponent` is typed `Il2CppMetaVoiceChat.MetaVc`, so MetaVoiceChat (Opus, `MetaVoiceChat.Opus.VcEncoder`/`VcDecoder`, `Output.VcJitter`) is the live stack. Transport is `MetaVoiceChat.NetProviders.Mirror.MirrorNetProvider : NetworkBehaviour`, whose entire wire surface is `CmdRelayFrame(MirrorFrame frame)` and `RpcReceiveFrame(MirrorFrame frame)` — a Command up and an unfiltered **ClientRpc** back down, serialized by `MirrorFrameReaderWriter.WriteMirrorFrame/ReadMirrorFrame`. `MirrorFrame` carries `index`, `timestamp`, `additionalLatency`, `data` (ArraySegment<byte>). Because the return leg is a broadcast ClientRpc, every client receives every speaker's audio; the distance falloff and the radio band-pass (`PlayerVoice.RadioLowpass` AudioLowPassFilter, `RadioHighpass`, `RadioNoise`, `RadioStartBeep`, `RadioEndBeep`) are applied locally on an AudioSource. Mute/deafen are also local: `MetaVc.isDeafened`, `isInputMuted`, `isOutputMuted`, `CannotSpeak`, and `playerBoardItem.MutePlayer(bool)` / `SetPlayerVolume(float)` -> `PlayerVoice.SetPlayerMuted(bool)` / `SetPlayerVolume(float)`.
findings.members: MetaVoiceChat.NetProviders.Mirror.MirrorNetProvider; CmdRelayFrame(MirrorFrame); RpcReceiveFrame(MirrorFrame); MirrorFrameReaderWriter; MetaVc.StartClient(INetProvider,bool,int); MetaVc.SendFrame(int,float[]); MetaVc.ReceiveFrame(int,double,float,ReadOnlySpan<byte>); PlayerVoice.RadioLowpass; PlayerVoice.SetPlayerMuted(bool)
findings.modding: Two consequences. (1) A modded client can hear every player on the map regardless of distance or radio state — nothing server-side prevents it. (2) All voice traffic is host-relayed through the same Mirror/Steam pipe, so host upstream scales with players squared; a mod that raises the player cap will hit voice bandwidth before it hits anything else. MirrorNetProvider.Instances is a static list of every voice endpoint — the clean hook point.

findings.title: Voice is server-authoritative in exactly one place: networked character voice lines, with nonce-based dedup
findings.detail: `NetworkedCharacterVoicePlayer` runs a real propose/validate/broadcast loop: client calls `Cmd_ClientProposedPlay(VoiceCategory category, int index, uint nonce, float clientTime)`; the server re-picks via `Server_TryPickIndex(List<VoiceLineEntry>, ref int chosen)` against `GetSrvCooldowns(List<VoiceLineEntry>) -> float[]`, `_srvCooldowns` (Dictionary<List<VoiceLineEntry>, float[]>), `_srvNextGlobalTime`, `_effectiveGlobalCooldown`; then broadcasts `Rpc_Play(VoiceCategory, int index, uint nonce)`. The client keeps `_lastSentNonce` so it can suppress double-playing its own locally-predicted line. Line-set selection is a SyncVar: `currentLibraryIndex` with hook `OnLibraryIndexUpdate(int previous, int current)`, seeded by `ServerSetRandomLibraryIndex()`.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.NetworkedCharacterVoicePlayer; Cmd_ClientProposedPlay(VoiceCategory,int,uint,float); Server_TryPickIndex; GetSrvCooldowns; _srvNextGlobalTime; _effectiveGlobalCooldown; Rpc_Play(VoiceCategory,int,uint); _lastSentNonce; currentLibraryIndex
findings.modding: Adding new VoiceCategory values requires server-side cooldown tables to agree, or Server_TryPickIndex will reject the proposal and the line will without warning never play.

findings.title: Three voice implementations ship; two are dead, and Dissonance is dead weight in its own assembly
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.VoiceChat` (`Cmd_SendData(byte[] data, uint size)` -> `Target_PlaySound(byte[] DestBuffer, uint BytesWritten)`) and `Il2Cpp.SteamworksVoiceChat` (`StartRecordingVoice`, `SendDataToServer(byte[], uint)`, `ReceiveVoiceDataClient(byte[], uint)`, `OnAudioRead(float[])`, `OnAudioReadRadio(float[])`, `WriteToClip`, plus its own radio AudioSources) are both complete, weaved Steam-voice implementations that nothing current points at — `PlayerVoice` uses MetaVc. `PlayerMaster.voiceChat` is still typed `Il2Cpp.SteamworksVoiceChat`, a leftover reference. Dissonance is a whole separate assembly `Il2CppDissonanceVoip` (`Dissonance.DissonanceComms` with Rooms/PlayerChannels/RoomChannels/TextChat) with no game-code references found. `Il2Cpp.VoiceChatEnabler` is an empty class — no members beyond constructors.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.VoiceChat; Il2Cpp.SteamworksVoiceChat; PlayerMaster.voiceChat; Dissonance.DissonanceComms; Il2Cpp.VoiceChatEnabler
findings.modding: DEV-CONFIRMED: the OPERATOR developers confirm this middleware is not used. Edgegap in particular is never touched and is present only because Mirror bundles it. Do not hook SteamworksVoiceChat or Dissonance expecting live audio. Runtime probe to confirm: check whether any active scene object has a SteamworksVoiceChat or DissonanceComms component enabled.

findings.title: Moderation is host-only by construction: kick/ban are [Server] methods, not Commands
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.playerBoardItem` (the scoreboard/lobby row, a NetworkBehaviour) exposes `KickPlayer()` and `BanPlayer()` as the UI click handlers, which route to `SERVER_KickPlayer()` and `SERVER_BanPlayer()`. Neither has a generated `UserCode_`/`InvokeUserCode_` pair — the only weaved remote call on the type is `TARGETRPC_SetDisconnectReason(NetworkConnection networkConnection, string reason)`. That proves SERVER_Kick/Ban are plain server-side methods (Mirror `[Server]`), so a non-host client calling them does nothing over the wire. `I_KickPlayer(PlayerMaster) -> IEnumerator` is the coroutine that delays the actual disconnect so the reason TargetRpc lands first; the victim maps it to `SteamLobby.LeaveLobbyReason.HostKickedMe` / `HostBannedMe`.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.playerBoardItem; KickPlayer(); BanPlayer(); SERVER_KickPlayer(); SERVER_BanPlayer(); I_KickPlayer(PlayerMaster); TARGETRPC_SetDisconnectReason(NetworkConnection,string); AllPlayerBoardItems
findings.modding: Correct and safe as shipped. `playerBoardItem.AllPlayerBoardItems` is a static List<playerBoardItem> — the cheap way for a mod to enumerate every connected player with stats without FindObjectsOfType.

findings.title: Bans are a plain string list of Steam IDs on the NetworkManager, checked at connect time
findings.detail: `NetworkManagerVectorGames.bannedPlayers` is a `List<string>` and `CheckBanned(string steamId, NetworkConnectionToClient conn)` is private, called from the connect path. Identity for that check comes from `TryGetSteamId(NetworkConnectionToClient conn, ref Steamworks.CSteamID steamId) -> bool` (private static), which can only be reading the transport's `FizzySteamworks.ServerGetClientAddress(connectionId)` — i.e. the Steam-authenticated peer identity, not anything the client asserts. The manager also keeps `bySteamId` (Dictionary<ulong, NetworkConnectionToClient>) for reverse lookup, and a `Steamworks.Callback<PersonaStateChange_t> personaChanged` -> `OnPersonaStateChange(PersonaStateChange_t)` to refresh display names.
findings.members: bannedPlayers; CheckBanned(string,NetworkConnectionToClient); TryGetSteamId(NetworkConnectionToClient, ref CSteamID); bySteamId; personaChanged; OnPersonaStateChange(PersonaStateChange_t)
findings.modding: bySteamId is the correct SteamID -> connection map for any mod-side moderation or per-player state. Persistence of bannedPlayers across sessions is not visible in signatures — worth checking Easy Save 3 keys if a mod needs durable bans.

findings.title: Clients self-report their own SteamID64 to the server via a Command
findings.detail: `PlayerMaster.SetMyName(string myName, Steamworks.CSteamID cSteamID)` is weaved (`UserCode_SetMyName__String__CSteamID`) with no NetworkConnectionToClient parameter — a Command. It populates the SyncVars `thisPlayerName` (hook `OnNameUpdate(string,string)`) and `thisPlayerSteam64` (ulong), which is what `playerBoardItem.ulong_cSteamID` / `OnSteamIDChanged(ulong,ulong)` / `SetPFP(ulong)` display. So the identity shown on the scoreboard, and used to fetch the Steam avatar, is whatever the client claims. This is distinct from the transport-derived identity used by CheckBanned/TryGetSteamId, so it is not necessarily a ban bypass — but it is a spoofable display identity.
findings.members: PlayerMaster.SetMyName(string, CSteamID); thisPlayerName; thisPlayerSteam64; playerBoardItem.ulong_cSteamID; OnSteamIDChanged(ulong,ulong); SetPFP(ulong)
findings.modding: Runtime probe to settle whether it matters: on the host, compare PlayerMaster.thisPlayerSteam64 against TryGetSteamId(conn) for the same connection. If they can diverge, name/avatar impersonation is trivial and a mod could add the cross-check the game omits.

findings.title: Team assignment is an unvalidated client Command, and the team-deathmatch mode is a completely empty class
findings.detail: `PlayerMaster.CMD_SetTeam(int team)` takes an arbitrary int straight from the client (weaved: `UserCode_CMD_SetTeam__Int32`), reached from the UI via `playerBoardItem.SelectTeam(int value)`. It drives the SyncVar on `TeamIdentifier` (`TeamID` int, hook `OnTeamChanged(int previous, int current)`), which feeds `TeamManager.OperatorTeams` (Dictionary<int, TeamRuntimeData>) and the friend/foe resolution used by AI (`TeamRuntimeData.AllEnemies`, `AllEnemyBots`, `AllEnemyPlayers`, `TeamStats.FriendlyTeams`). Meanwhile `Il2Cpp.Mirror_TeamDeathmatch` has **no members at all** except the weaver's `Weaved()` stub — the mode was scaffolded and abandoned. Friendly fire is a server SyncVar (`GameManagerNetwork.FriendlyFire`) with team-kill accounting (`PlayerMaster.NumTeamKills`, `playerBoardItem.TeamKills` / `OnTeamKillsChanged`).
findings.members: PlayerMaster.CMD_SetTeam(int); TeamIdentifier.TeamID; OnTeamChanged(int,int); TeamManager.OperatorTeams; TeamManager.EnsureTeam(int); TeamRuntimeData.AllEnemyPlayers; TeamStats.FriendlyTeams; Il2Cpp.Mirror_TeamDeathmatch
findings.modding: CMD_SetTeam with no range check plus TeamManager.EnsureTeam(int) means a mod (or a cheat) can conjure arbitrary team ids at runtime. For a PvP mod that is a feature; for anything competitive it needs a server-side clamp. Mirror_TeamDeathmatch is a free, already-registered NetworkBehaviour type to hang a mode on.

findings.title: Character appearance is a client-authored JSON blob the server stores and rebroadcasts without inspection
findings.detail: `CharacterModSync.CMD_SetCharacter(string json, string jsonMods)` writes directly to the SyncVars `characterJSON` and `characterModsJSON` (hooks `OnCharacterJSONChanged(string,string)`, `OnCharacterModsJSONChanged(string,string)`), and every client applies it through `OnStartClient()` -> `ApplyCurrentModPreset()` / `ApplyNewPresetToClient()`. Because it is a SyncVar rather than an Rpc, late joiners get the current appearance in the initial state payload automatically — that is how mid-session join reconstructs everyone's look. `ChangeCharacterPresetID(int id)` switches presets locally.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.CharacterModSync; CMD_SetCharacter(string,string); characterJSON; characterModsJSON; ApplyCurrentModPreset(); ApplyNewPresetToClient(); ChangeCharacterPresetID(int)
findings.modding: This is the cleanest seam for custom cosmetics: any string a mod can round-trip through the client's own parser will replicate to all clients that share the mod, with zero server changes. Unmodded clients will fail to resolve unknown ids — behaviour on parse failure is unproven, probe ApplyCurrentModPreset with a garbage json.

findings.title: Weapon pickup is server-mediated but the modification string is client-supplied
findings.detail: `GameManagerNetwork.CMD_AuthoriseWeaponPickup(PlayerNetworking requestedPL, int puppetWeaponID, string jsonMODstring)` -> `RPC_SpawnFirearm(PlayerNetworking playerNetworking, GameObject firearm, int puppetID)`. The server arbitrates *who* gets the weapon (guarded by the SyncVar `lastPuppetWeaponID`), but the attachment configuration travels as an opaque client string. Same shape on `PlayerMaster.CMD_SpawnWeapon(string weaponName)` — a client naming the weapon it wants spawned. Magazines follow the same pattern: `CMD_PickupMagazine(int id, PlayerNetworking)` -> `RPC_PickupMagazine(int i, PlayerNetworking)`, with server-side cleanup via `DestroyMags(List<int>)`, `CleanupDroppedMagsList()`, `DestroyAllGroundWeapons()`, `DestroyAllGroundMags()`.
findings.members: GameManagerNetwork.CMD_AuthoriseWeaponPickup(PlayerNetworking,int,string); RPC_SpawnFirearm(PlayerNetworking,GameObject,int); lastPuppetWeaponID; PlayerMaster.CMD_SpawnWeapon(string); CMD_PickupMagazine(int,PlayerNetworking)
findings.modding: Because both the weapon name and the mod JSON cross the wire as strings rather than as indices into a fixed list, custom weapon *configurations* replicate without touching the append-only Game_Weapons index list — a much lighter path than registering new weapons.

findings.title: GameManagerNetwork is the authoritative match-state object, and exfiltration is the one actually server-run subsystem
findings.detail: Server-only methods with no weaved remote-call pair (so Mirror `[Server]`): `ServerAddToExfil(int connectionId)`, `ServerRemoveFromExfil(int connectionId)`, `ServerPruneExfilOccupants()`, `ServerTickExtraction()`, `ServerSetExtracting(bool state)`, `ServerCompleteExfil()`, `GetRemainingExfilSeconds() -> float`, `SERVER_FailOperation()`, `SetNumAlivePlayers()`, `SetPlayerNextTeam(PlayerMaster)`. Results broadcast via `RpcExfiltrate()` and `RPC_FailOperation()`. The replicated match state is a wide SyncVar set: `hostNetID` (uint), `AllowRespawns`, `FreezeAllPlayers`, `AlivePlayers` (int), `PlayersInAnyExfil` (int), `canExtract`, `isExtracting`, `extractionStartTime` (double), `FriendlyFire`, `ReadyPlayers` (int), `lastPuppetWeaponID`, `EnableScoreBoard`, `AllPlayersLoaded` (hook `OnAllPlayersLoaded(bool,bool)`), `selectedOperation`, `UserOperationName`, `maxPlayers` (float), `expectedEnemies` (float), `DemiGM`, `ArmorySafety`. Host controls: `SERVER_ToggleRespawns()`, `SERVER_SetRespawns(bool)`, `SERVER_RespawnALL()`, `SERVER_RemoveKitForAllPlayers()`, `SetDemiGodMode(bool)`, `UpdateAdminPanelOnStart()`.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.GameManagerNetwork; ServerTickExtraction(); ServerCompleteExfil(); RpcExfiltrate(); extractionStartTime; canExtract; isExtracting; PlayersInAnyExfil; AllPlayersLoaded; ReadyPlayers; ArmorySafety; SERVER_SetRespawns(bool); SetDemiGodMode(bool)
findings.modding: Exfil timing uses `extractionStartTime` as a synced double against NetworkTime, so client-side prediction of the timer is safe. Caution: `SERVER_RespawnALL` and `SERVER_RemoveKitForAllPlayers` DO have UserCode_/InvokeUserCode_ pairs, meaning they are real Commands despite the SERVER_ prefix — whether requiresAuthority is false (letting any client fire them) is unprovable from signatures.

findings.title: Several SERVER_-prefixed methods are actually client Commands — requiresAuthority is the open question
findings.detail: Naming does not track weaving. Confirmed Commands (they have `UserCode_X` + `InvokeUserCode_X(NetworkBehaviour, NetworkReader, NetworkConnectionToClient)`): `GameManagerNetwork.SERVER_RespawnALL()`, `SERVER_RemoveKitForAllPlayers()`, `CMD_RequestSmoothsyncForceUpdate()`, `DestroyMags(List<int>)`, `DestroyObjectFailsafeCheckBecauseMirrorIsFuckingGayAsFuck(uint id, NetworkConnectionToClient sender)`. Confirmed NOT weaved (plain [Server] methods): `SERVER_FailOperation()`, `SERVER_ToggleRespawns()`, `SERVER_SetRespawns(bool)`, `playerBoardItem.SERVER_KickPlayer()`, `SERVER_BanPlayer()`. GameManagerNetwork is a server-spawned singleton object, so a client normally has no authority over it — meaning the weaved ones must be declared `[Command(requiresAuthority = false)]` to be callable at all, or they are host-only in practice.
findings.members: UserCode_SERVER_RespawnALL; InvokeUserCode_SERVER_RemoveKitForAllPlayers; SERVER_ToggleRespawns(); SERVER_SetRespawns(bool); Mirror.RemoteCalls.RemoteProcedureCalls
findings.modding: Settle it at runtime by reading Mirror's remote-call registry: `Mirror.RemoteCalls.RemoteProcedureCalls.remoteCallDelegates` maps the function hash to an `Invoker` carrying the `cmdRequiresAuthority` flag. If SERVER_RespawnALL is requiresAuthority=false, any client can force a full-team respawn — a griefing vector worth a mod-side guard.

findings.title: A pair of profanely-named failsafe RPCs exists purely to paper over Mirror spawn desync
findings.detail: `GameManagerNetwork.DestroyObjectFailsafeCheckBecauseMirrorIsFuckingGayAsFuck(uint id, NetworkConnectionToClient sender)` (Command — connection last) and `OhShitHomieYouGotFuckedBecauseMirrorIsDogShit(NetworkConnectionToClient target, uint ID)` (TargetRpc — connection first), plus `TestAllGayUnspawnedObjects()`, `SpawnObjectsFailSafe() -> IEnumerator`, `FromSceneStarterFailsafe()`, `LoadingFailsafe()`, `CloseAllFailScreens()`, and the scene hook literally named `OnSceneLoadedMirrorHookFuckMirrorIHateMirror()`. The pattern is a client noticing a netId it cannot resolve, asking the server about it, and the server target-rpc'ing a correction to that one client.
findings.members: DestroyObjectFailsafeCheckBecauseMirrorIsFuckingGayAsFuck(uint,NetworkConnectionToClient); OhShitHomieYouGotFuckedBecauseMirrorIsDogShit(NetworkConnectionToClient,uint); TestAllGayUnspawnedObjects(); SpawnObjectsFailSafe(); OnSceneLoadedMirrorHookFuckMirrorIHateMirror()
findings.modding: These are load-bearing, not jokes — the density of spawn failsafes says object spawn/scene-load races are a live problem. A mod that spawns networked objects around scene transitions should expect to hit the same races and should spawn after AllPlayersLoaded flips.

findings.title: Mid-session join appears permitted with no join-in-progress gate; readiness is counted, not enforced
findings.detail: The only connect-time rejection visible is `CheckBanned`. `OnServerAddPlayer(NetworkConnectionToClient)` is overridden, `ServerChangeScene(string)` is wrapped in `SwitchSceneAfterSeconds(string)`/`ApplyServerSceneChange(string)`, and the client side runs `OnClientChangeScene(string, SceneOperation, bool)` -> `OnClientSceneChanged()`. A joining client warms up via `PlayerMaster.WarmSceneAndSignalReady() -> IEnumerator` and announces itself with `SERVER_SendJoinMessage()` -> `RPC_SendJoinMessage(string playerName)`; the server tallies `GameManagerNetwork.ReadyPlayers` (SyncVar int) and flips `AllPlayersLoaded` (SyncVar bool, hook `OnAllPlayersLoaded(bool,bool)`) which drives `ShowLoadingScreen()`/`HideLoadingScreen()`/`HideLoadingScreenDelay()`. Ownership of the local pawn is handed over by `PlayerMaster.TargetRPC_GetSetPlayerObject(NetworkConnection, NetworkIdentity)`, after which `PlayerNetworking.HasAuthSetup()` or `NoAuthSetup()` runs. Late-joiner reconstruction is SyncVar-driven throughout: appearance (`CharacterModSync`), scoreboard rows (`playerBoardItem`, including a `forLobby` flag distinguishing lobby list from in-mission board), mission UI (`OperationUiSync.CurrentLocation/OperationTime/InfilName`), and op settings (`MenuControllerV2_Sync.selectedOperation/maxPlayers/expectedEnemies`).
findings.members: OnServerAddPlayer(NetworkConnectionToClient); PlayerMaster.WarmSceneAndSignalReady(); SERVER_SendJoinMessage(); RPC_SendJoinMessage(string); ReadyPlayers; AllPlayersLoaded; TargetRPC_GetSetPlayerObject(NetworkConnection,NetworkIdentity); playerBoardItem.forLobby; OperationUiSync; MenuControllerV2_Sync
findings.modding: Runtime probe: attempt a Steam join against a host already inside an operation scene and watch whether OnServerAddPlayer runs or the connection is dropped. If joins are allowed mid-op, a mod adding new networked mission state must expose it as a SyncVar (not a one-shot Rpc) or late joiners will desync.

findings.title: PlayerNetworking splits local vs remote player by toggling designer-assigned component arrays — the best mod seam on the player prefab
findings.detail: `HasAuthSetup()` and `NoAuthSetup()` switch on six inspector-populated arrays: `scriptsEnableAuth` (Behaviour[]), `scriptsDisableAuth` (Behaviour[]), `gameObjectseEnableAuth` (GameObject[], note the typo), `gameObjectsDisableAuth` (GameObject[]), `scriptsDisableNoAuth` (Behaviour[]), `gameObjectsDisableNoAuth` (GameObject[]), plus `AuthShadowedParents` (GameObject[]) and `rotationTrackerNoAuth` (Transform). `Il2Cpp.BotNetworking` uses the identical idea reduced to one array, `scriptsToDisable` (Behaviour[]) — AI proxies simply have their brains stripped on clients, confirming AI is host-authoritative.
findings.members: PlayerNetworking.HasAuthSetup(); NoAuthSetup(); scriptsEnableAuth; scriptsDisableAuth; gameObjectseEnableAuth; gameObjectsDisableNoAuth; AuthShadowedParents; rotationTrackerNoAuth; BotNetworking.scriptsToDisable
findings.modding: A mod adding a component to the player prefab must append it to the correct array or it will run on remote proxies too (or not run locally). These are plain arrays on a MonoBehaviour — mutable at runtime without Harmony.

findings.title: Text chat does not exist as a player-typed feature; ChatController is a display sink for system messages
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.ChatController` has exactly one real method, `AddToChatOutput(string newText)`, over `ChatInputField` (TMP_InputField), `ChatDisplayOutput` (TMP_Text), `ChatScrollbar` (UI.Scrollbar) — no Command, no Rpc, no NetworkBehaviour base. The only thing observed feeding it is `PlayerMaster.RPC_SendJoinMessage(string playerName)`. Dissonance's `TextChat` is present in the unused Dissonance assembly. So the input field is wired to nothing over the network.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.ChatController; AddToChatOutput(string); ChatInputField; PlayerMaster.RPC_SendJoinMessage(string); Dissonance.TextChat
findings.modding: DEV-CONFIRMED: the OPERATOR developers confirm this middleware is not used. Edgegap in particular is never touched and is present only because Mirror bundles it. Adding real text chat means adding a Command/ClientRpc pair on PlayerMaster and calling AddToChatOutput on receipt — the UI half already exists and is already in the scene.

findings.title: Access control is a client-side remote allowlist fetched over HTTP, and achievements are freely resettable
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.SteamAuthID` holds `jsonURL` (string), runs `getData(string URL) -> IEnumerator` (a UnityWebRequest coroutine), and branches to `passed()` or `failed()` while showing `stateText` (TextMeshProUGUI). The payload deserializes to `Il2Cpp.jsonData { List<Il2Cpp.jsonSteamIDs> steamIDs }` where `jsonSteamIDs { string user; string steamID64; }` — a named allowlist, consistent with `SteamLobby.PreAlphaStatus` (int), `SetPreAlphaStatus()` and a `watermarkText`. This is a build-access gate evaluated entirely on the client, not a server-side anti-cheat. Separately, `SteamLobby` exposes `CheckAchivement(string id)`, `UnlockAchivement(string id)` and — shipped in retail — `ClearAchivement(string id)` (misspelled throughout). No VAC/EAC integration is present anywhere in the type graph beyond Steamworks' informational `ISteamApps.BIsVACBanned` binding.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.SteamAuthID; jsonURL; getData(string); passed(); failed(); Il2Cpp.jsonData.steamIDs; Il2Cpp.jsonSteamIDs.user; steamID64; SteamLobby.UnlockAchivement(string); ClearAchivement(string); PreAlphaStatus
findings.modding: Overall anti-cheat posture is: none. Host-side ban list plus a client-side access allowlist. Everything else — movement, health, team, weapon config, appearance, achievements — is client-asserted. Mods should assume a fully trusting server and, if they care, add their own validation host-side.

findings.title: Dead and empty types confirmed in the netcode area
findings.detail: Types that exist in metadata with no members beyond constructors (verified by inspector — no methods, no properties, no fields): `Il2Cpp.LobbyController` (from `\Assets\Scripts\LobbyController.cs`), `Il2Cpp.VoiceChatEnabler`, `Il2Cpp.SpawnNetworkedObject`, `Il2Cpp.Mirror_TeamDeathmatch` (only the weaver's `Weaved()`). `Il2Cpp.NetworkSyncRigidbody` has only `Start()` and `Update()` and no networking at all despite the name. `Il2Cpp.PlayerConsoleCommands` is nearly empty and entirely local — `KillPlayer()`, `CheckHealth()`, `TakeDamage(int amount, HealthBodyPart part)`, `ShowRandomizeMovieButton()` — so there is no networked admin console. Live-but-odd: `Il2Cpp.Mirror_DayNight` has SyncVar `isDay`, arrays `DayObjects`/`NightObjects`, and a no-argument client Command `CMD_SetDayNight()` that toggles global lighting for everyone.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.LobbyController; Il2Cpp.VoiceChatEnabler; Il2Cpp.SpawnNetworkedObject; Il2Cpp.Mirror_TeamDeathmatch; Il2Cpp.NetworkSyncRigidbody; Il2Cpp.PlayerConsoleCommands; Il2Cpp.Mirror_DayNight.CMD_SetDayNight()
findings.modding: Do not build against LobbyController — the lobby lives in Il2CppVectorGames.SteamLobby. Mirror_DayNight.CMD_SetDayNight() is a working, argument-free way for any client to flip day/night globally, which is either a useful mod hook or a griefing vector depending on requiresAuthority.

findings.title: God mode and a dev connection menu ship in the retail build on the network manager itself
findings.detail: `NetworkManagerVectorGames` carries `GM` (bool) and `ToggleGodMode()`, and `GameManagerNetwork` carries the SyncVar `DemiGM` with `SetDemiGodMode(bool)` — a networked 'demi god mode'.
