Alongside them sit Mirror's stock debug UI (`managerHUD` of type NetworkManagerHUD, `networkPing` of type NetworkPingDisplay), `ToggleConnectionMenu()`, and `startClientKCP()`. Lobby-list UI also carries a `LobbyItem.VersionMismatchObject` (GameObject), so build version travels in lobby metadata but a mismatch is only *displayed* — nothing in the connect path rejects it.
findings.members: NetworkManagerVectorGames.GM; ToggleGodMode(); managerHUD; networkPing; ToggleConnectionMenu(); GameManagerNetwork.DemiGM; SetDemiGodMode(bool); LobbyItem.VersionMismatchObject
findings.modding: ToggleGodMode() and SetDemiGodMode(bool) are directly callable — no need for a mod to reimplement invulnerability. Version mismatch being cosmetic means modded and vanilla clients can attempt to connect to each other; a mod that changes networked state should advertise itself through SteamLobby.SetLobbyData and refuse mismatched peers itself.

findings.title: Lobby name profanity filtering is client-side substitution, not rejection
findings.detail: `SteamLobby.WordsToFilter` is a `List<SteamLobby/BadWordStruct>` where `BadWordStruct { string BadWord; string GoodWord; }` — a replacement table, not a blocklist — supplemented by `NoNoWords` and `YesYesWords` (both Il2CppStringArray). Applied when building the browser rows (`BuildLobbyListUI()`, `lobbylistItems` of type List<Il2CppVectorGames.LobbyItem>). Because it runs on the viewing client against metadata the host wrote, the host's real `LobbyName` is unaffected.
findings.members: SteamLobby.WordsToFilter; SteamLobby/BadWordStruct.BadWord; GoodWord; NoNoWords; YesYesWords; BuildLobbyListUI(); lobbylistItems
findings.modding: Cosmetic only; a mod can clear WordsToFilter with no network consequence.

findings.title: There are exactly 7 game modes in the GameMode enum, and it is a NESTED type Il2Cpp.OperationsManager/GameMode — not the class Il2Cpp.GameMode
findings.detail: Two distinct things share the name. `Il2Cpp.GameMode` (Assets\Scripts\GameModes\GameMode.cs) is the abstract NetworkBehaviour base class for mode controllers. The *enum* is a nested type `Il2Cpp.OperationsManager/GameMode` with members, in declaration order: StandardPVE, StandardPVP, FFAPVP, PVE_HVTKILL, PVE_FINDINTEL, PVE_WAVESURVIVAL, PVE_ASSETDESTROY (so 0..6). The InteropInspector prints nested types with a '/' separator and renders them bare in signatures, which is why every earlier `^Il2Cpp\.GameMode$` query returned only the class. Regex `/GameMode$` finds the enum.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.OperationsManager/GameMode {StandardPVE, StandardPVP, FFAPVP, PVE_HVTKILL, PVE_FINDINTEL, PVE_WAVESURVIVAL, PVE_ASSETDESTROY}; Il2Cpp.GameMode (class)
findings.modding: Any mod that wants to force a mode writes the enum by ordinal into OperationsManager.CurrentGameMode or passes it to DebugStartOperation. Use `Il2Cpp.OperationsManager/GameMode` when resolving the type by name — `Il2Cpp.GameMode` resolves to the wrong thing.

findings.title: Only FOUR classes derive from Il2Cpp.GameMode, and InfiltrationManager is the PVE mode controller
findings.detail: `Server_AllPlayersLoaded()` is declared abstract-virtual on Il2Cpp.GameMode and is implemented by exactly four types across all 206 assemblies: Il2Cpp.FFA, Il2Cpp.InfiltrationManager, Il2Cpp.PvpGameode, Il2Cpp.WaveSurvival. So the 7-value enum is served by 4 controllers: StandardPVE / PVE_HVTKILL / PVE_FINDINTEL / PVE_ASSETDESTROY all run through InfiltrationManager (the objective variant is expressed in RaidManager data, not in a distinct class); StandardPVP -> PvpGameode; FFAPVP -> FFA; PVE_WAVESURVIVAL -> WaveSurvival. The base exposes `static GameMode singleton`, `bool isNight`, `bool didStartClient`, virtual `PlayerDied(PlayerMaster master, bool serverDeath)`, virtual `LoadingCompleteClient()`, `Client_AllPlayersLoaded()`, and coroutines `WaitForPlayerMasterAndWarm`, `WarmShadersAndSignalReady`, `WaitForPlayers`.
findings.members: GameMode.singleton, GameMode.Server_AllPlayersLoaded, GameMode.PlayerDied(PlayerMaster,bool), GameMode.LoadingCompleteClient, FFA, InfiltrationManager, PvpGameode, WaveSurvival
findings.modding: GameMode.singleton is the one-stop handle for the active mode; cast it to identify the mode at runtime. Adding a actually new mode means injecting an il2cpp subclass of GameMode, which will NOT get Mirror weaving (no SyncVars/RPCs) — the practical route is to Harmony-patch an existing subclass's UserCode_* and Server_* methods instead.

findings.title: RaidManager is NOT a game mode — it is the per-map PVE content director that sits beside InfiltrationManager
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.RaidManager has its own `static RaidManager singleton`, Awake/OnStartServer/Update, and does NOT override Server_AllPlayersLoaded or PlayerDied. It owns AI population (standardAI[], customAI, hvtAI[], hvtSpawnPoints[], botSpawnPoints, botSpawnDelay, InstantiateBot, CanSpawn(Vector3,float), GetValidSpawnPoint(ref List<GameObject>), ApplyBotSpawnSettings(GameObject, BotSpawnDetails), ServerSpawnAI(bool _custom), ServerSpawnHVTs()), reinforcements (hasReinforcements, timedBackup, reinforcementMinMaxTimer Vector2, minAIBackupAmount, aiReinforcement[] Reinforcements, CheckIfCanSendReinforcementsTimed, AI_BackupCondition), IEDs (hasIEDs, IED, IED_locations[], iedChance, iedCount, SERVER_SpawnIEDs), static vehicle AI (spawnVehicleAI, spawnChancePerPoint, maxStaticVehicles, staticVehicleSpawnPoints[], staticVehicleAI[], SpawnStaticVehicleAI), weapon gating (prohibitedWeapons PuppetWeapon[], mapSpecificWeapons PuppetWeapon[]), and the objective/exfil wiring. It carries a live custom-AI API: SERVERONLY_CustomAISpawnList_RemoveAll(), SERVERONLY_CustomAISpawnList_AddAI(string botName), RespawnCustomAI(), RespawnAI().
findings.members: RaidManager.singleton, ServerSpawnAI(bool), ServerSpawnHVTs(), SERVERONLY_CustomAISpawnList_AddAI(string), RespawnCustomAI(), prohibitedWeapons, mapSpecificWeapons, aiReinforcement[]
findings.modding: SERVERONLY_CustomAISpawnList_AddAI(string botName) + RespawnCustomAI() is a ready-made, string-keyed server-side bot spawner — the cleanest seam for a custom-encounter mod, no prefab plumbing needed. prohibitedWeapons/mapSpecificWeapons is where per-map weapon bans live.

findings.title: RaidManager has only 3 SyncVars and 5 network calls; HVT confirmation and exfil requests are client-authoritative Commands
findings.detail: SyncVars: GlobalCombatTimer (float), collectedItemsCount (int), collectedImportantItemsCount (int) — accessible as NetworkGlobalCombatTimer / NetworkcollectedItemsCount / NetworkcollectedImportantItemsCount. Network surface: RPC_NotifyPlayerAIAmount(int amount) [fed by SERVER_NotifyPlayerAIAmount(int) / UpdateAICount()], RPC_CanExfil() [fed by EnableGlobalExtraction()], CMD_HVT_ConfirmKIA(string hvtName, uint hvtID) -> RPC_HVT_ConfirmKIA(string hvtName, int remaining), and CMD_clientRequestExfil(int infilIndex). Both Commands take fully client-supplied payloads: the client names the HVT and its netId, and names the infil index it wants to exfil at.
findings.members: RaidManager.CMD_HVT_ConfirmKIA(string,uint), UserCode_CMD_HVT_ConfirmKIA__String__UInt32, RaidManager.CMD_clientRequestExfil(int), RaidManager.RPC_CanExfil, EnableGlobalExtraction, SERVER_PickupObjective(bool isImportant), SERVER_MissionAssetDestroyed(VehicleHealth)
findings.modding: Hook UserCode_CMD_HVT_ConfirmKIA__String__UInt32 and UserCode_CMD_clientRequestExfil__Int32 on the server side to gate or extend objective completion. Conversely these are the two spots where a hostile client can assert progress — whether the server re-validates hvtID against OperationsManager.AI_HVTs is unprovable from signatures and needs a runtime probe (send a bogus name/id as a non-host client and watch RPC_HVT_ConfirmKIA fire).

findings.title: Objective flow: ObjectiveSetter[] gives per-raid objective randomization; ObjectiveObject is the networked collectible
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.ObjectiveSetter is a plain serializable pair {string name; ObjectiveObject[] objectives}, and RaidManager.objectives is an ObjectiveSetter[]. RaidManager.ServerSetObjectives() picks/activates a set (body unreadable, but the array-of-named-sets shape is the classic randomize-per-raid pattern). Il2Cpp.ObjectiveObject is a NetworkBehaviour with SyncVars isObtained (hook OnObjectPickup(bool,bool)) and IsImportant (hook OnSetImportant(bool,bool)), plus non-synced DisplayName (string), confirmHVT (bool), hvtName (string). Pickup path: ObjectiveInteractable.Interacted(PlayerNetworking) -> ObjectiveObject.PickupObject() -> CMD_PickupObject(PlayerMaster playerMaster) -> server -> RaidManager.SERVER_PickupObjective(bool isImportant) which bumps collectedItemsCount / collectedImportantItemsCount. ObjectiveObject.confirmHVT + hvtName is what makes an objective a body-confirm rather than a pickup, feeding RaidManager.CMD_HVT_ConfirmKIA.
findings.members: ObjectiveSetter{name, objectives}, ObjectiveObject{DisplayName, isObtained, IsImportant, confirmHVT, hvtName, CMD_PickupObject(PlayerMaster)}, ObjectiveInteractable.Interacted(PlayerNetworking), RaidManager.objectives, RaidManager.objectiveObjects, RaidManager.ImportantObjectiveObjects
findings.modding: A custom intel/HVT objective needs only an ObjectiveObject + ObjectiveInteractable on a networked prefab and registration into RaidManager.objectiveObjects / ImportantObjectiveObjects. CMD_PickupObject takes the PlayerMaster from the client, so pickup credit is client-asserted.

findings.title: The mission board's runtime tuning is NOT carried in the StartOperation command — game mode, AI count and PVP/FFA limits never cross the client->server boundary in the payload
findings.detail: OperationsManager.StartOperation(string sceneName, int prepTime, string displayName, string infilTime, string _activeAchievement, float targetTime) is mirrored exactly by CMD_StartOperation(same 6 args) -> RPC_StartOperation(int defaultInfil) -> SERVER_LoadOperation(). There is no gameMode, MinAI/MaxAI, difficulty, HVT count or PVP/FFA limit in that payload. Yet OperationBoardUI exposes SetAI_COUNT(float), SetAI_HVT_COUNT(float), SetOpforDifficulty(int), SetHVTSpawnPoint(int), SetPVPTimeLimit(int), SetPVPRoundLimit(int), SetFFATimeLimit(int), SetFFAKillLimit(int), SetPVPParam1(int), SetPVPParam2(int) — and neither OperationBoardUI nor CerebusOpboard is a NetworkBehaviour (no UserCode_*/Serialize­SyncVars members on either). OperationsManager.FFA_TimeLimit / FFA_KillLimit / PVP_TimeLimit / PVP_RoundLimit are plain fields with NO Network* accessor, i.e. not SyncVars. OperationsManager.CurrentGameMode IS a SyncVar (hook GameModeChanged(GameMode,GameMode)), so only the server's value counts.
findings.members: OperationsManager.StartOperation(string,int,string,string,string,float), CMD_StartOperation(same), RPC_StartOperation(int), SERVER_LoadOperation(), OperationsManager.CurrentGameMode (SyncVar), FFA_TimeLimit, FFA_KillLimit, PVP_TimeLimit, PVP_RoundLimit (plain), OperationBoardUI.Set*
findings.modding: Static per-opboard config (GameModeOverride, MinAI/MaxAI, Difficulty) is identical on every client because it comes from the same prefab, so the server reads a correct copy. Runtime slider changes made by a NON-HOST client have no synced channel and are very likely dropped. Runtime probe: as a joined client, move the AI-count / FFA-kill-limit sliders and start the op, then read OperationsManager.singleton.FFA_KillLimit on the host. A mod that wants client-configurable rules must add its own Command.

findings.title: CerebusOpboard selects the mode via AffectGamemode + GameModeOverride, and also owns the achievement contract
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.CerebusOpboard fields: AffectGamemode (bool), GameModeOverride (GameMode enum), TARGETPACKAGE (TARGETPACKAGE_DETAILS[]), AvailableInfils (string[]), MinAI/MaxAI (int), MapPrefab (GameObject), Difficulty (AIDifficulty), HVTSpawnIsRandom (bool), PrepTimeInSeconds, SelectedInfiltrationTime, INFILTRATION_TARGET/INFILTRATION_TIME (string), requireEnoughInfils / requireEnoughExfils (bool), isLocked + unlockCode (string), exfilUnlockingKey, UnlockOnExfil (string), isCompleted, isSimulation, TargetRaidTime (float), and the achievement triple AchievementName (string) + achievement_aiDifficulty (AIDifficulty) + achievement_min_ai_amount (int). Methods: CreateInstance(Transform parent, MissionLaptop laptop), SwitchToActiveOperation(), SwitchToSimulationOperation(), SetAI_COUNT(float), SetAI_HVT_COUNT(float), Start_Operation().
findings.members: CerebusOpboard.AffectGamemode, GameModeOverride, AchievementName, achievement_aiDifficulty, achievement_min_ai_amount, TargetRaidTime, requireEnoughInfils, requireEnoughExfils, unlockCode, exfilUnlockingKey, UnlockOnExfil
findings.modding: AffectGamemode=true + GameModeOverride is the ONLY data-driven way to make a board entry launch PvP/FFA/Survival. achievement_min_ai_amount + achievement_aiDifficulty encode the 'you must play it at >= this difficulty with >= this many AI' gate — patchable if you want a custom mission to award a real Steam achievement, and the reason low-AI runs without warning fail to unlock.

findings.title: AIDifficulty has 4 tiers and lives on GameManager, not on any mode class
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.GameManager/AIDifficulty { Easy, Trained, Realistic, Tier1 }. GameManager exposes SetAIDifficulty(AIDifficulty difficulty), get_AI_Difficulty, get_botHVTAmount, and the spawn-selection API: SpawnPointsInScene, Pspawns, Espawns, heliSpawns, RandomSpawns (bool), SetRandomPlayerSpawns(bool), nextSpawnPosition(bool useTeams, int team, int iteration), nextSpawnPositionRandom(), nextEnemySpawnPosition(), BestFFASpawn(int startIndex), MovePlayerToSpawn(Vector3, Quaternion), ToggleRespawns(), CloseAllDoors().
findings.members: GameManager/AIDifficulty{Easy,Trained,Realistic,Tier1}, GameManager.SetAIDifficulty, GameManager.BestFFASpawn(int), GameManager.nextSpawnPosition(bool,int,int), GameManager.botHVTAmount
findings.modding: Tier1 is the top difficulty and is what CheckTier1Challenge/CheckTier1NightChallenge on GameManagerNetwork gate on. SetAIDifficulty is a plain public method — trivially callable mid-raid, which is also how a mod would accidentally invalidate an achievement run.

findings.title: FFA is fully implemented with a real spawn-safety solver, but scoring is not synced — it is recomputed on every client
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.FFA has only TWO SyncVars: RoundTimer (hook OnRoundTimerUpdate(int,int)) and CurrentScoreUI (hook ScoreUIIndexChanged(int,int)). Everything on the scoreboard — FirstPlacePlayerName/SecondPlacePlayerName/ThirdPlacePlayerName (string), firstScore/secondScore/thirdScore (ushort), playerIsFirst (bool) — is plain local state recomputed by CalculatePlayerScore() from the per-player playerBoardItem SyncVars. Config: KillsToWin (int), RoundTimer (int), gameObjectsToDisable (GameObject[]). Round machinery: StartGame(), CalculateClock(), ClockCountDown() coroutine, CalculateRoundEnd(), WaitForReturnToOperationRoom() coroutine, RespawnPlayers()/RespawnTimer(PlayerMaster)/SpawnSinglePlayer(PlayerMaster)/ReEnableSpawnPoint(SpawnPoint) coroutines, RPC_ResetGame(), RPC_PlayMusic(int state), flags _respawningPlayers/_gameEnded. Spawn safety is a real solver: EvaluateSpawn(SpawnPoint spawn, List<PlayerMaster> players, PlayerMaster ignore) -> FFA/SpawnEvaluation {SpawnThreat Threat; float NearestPlayerSqrDistance} with FFA/SpawnThreat {Safe, Visible, Near, Exposed}, tuned by SpawnProtectProximityRadius, SpawnProtectEyeHeight, SpawnProtectViewHalfAngle, FFASpawnProtectLayerMask (LayerMask).
findings.members: FFA.instance, FFA.KillsToWin, FFA.RoundTimer (SyncVar), FFA.CurrentScoreUI (SyncVar), FFA.EvaluateSpawn, FFA/SpawnThreat{Safe,Visible,Near,Exposed}, FFA/SpawnEvaluation, FFA.gameObjectsToDisable
findings.modding: FFA has BOTH its own EvaluateSpawn solver and GameManager.BestFFASpawn(int) — two independent FFA spawn pickers, one of which is likely vestigial. Because the leaderboard is client-recomputed, a client-side mod can change what it displays without desync; changing who actually wins requires the server (CalculateRoundEnd).

findings.title: PvpGameode is a full round-based team mode (Search-and-Destroy shape) with freeze time and a Tie state
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.PvpGameode SyncVars: currentRound, RoundTimer (hook OnRoundTimerUpdate), Team1Score (hook Team1ScoreChanged), Team2Score (hook Team2ScoreChanged), CurrentScoreUI (hook ScoreUIIndexChanged). Config: MaxRounds, RoundsToWin, RoundTime, Team1SpawnPoints/Team2SpawnPoints (List<SpawnPoint>), Team1Players/Team2Players (List<TeamIdentifier>). Round state machine: StartNewRound(), WaitForStartRound(), EndRound(), CalculateRoundEnd(), CalculateRoundWinner() -> PvpGameode/RoundWinType {Tie, Team1, Team2}, Server_RoundEndPlayMusicShowUI(RoundWinType winner), IsTeam1Dead(), IsTeam2Dead(), AllRoundPlayersDespawned(), WaitForRespawnPlayers()/RespawnPlayers(). Timers/flags: _roundEnded, _roundEndTimer, _waitingForPlayerSpawn, _waitingForPlayerSpawnTimer, _respawningPlayers, _freezeTimer, _isFreezeTime, _roundActive. Full blufor/opfor announcer set including Round/Game Win/Lose/Draw clips. Zero Commands — entirely server-authoritative with RPC_ResetGame() and RPC_PlayMusic(int state, int _winner).
findings.members: PvpGameode.instance, MaxRounds, RoundsToWin, RoundTime, Team1SpawnPoints, Team2SpawnPoints, CalculateRoundWinner()->RoundWinType, PvpGameode/RoundWinType{Tie,Team1,Team2}, _isFreezeTime
findings.modding: Team1SpawnPoints/Team2SpawnPoints are scene-wired List<SpawnPoint> on the PvpGameode component — a raid map with no PvpGameode component and no populated team spawn lists cannot host StandardPVP no matter what GameModeOverride says. That is the hard blocker for making arbitrary maps PvP-playable.

findings.title: WaveSurvival is the most complete mode and has a dual wave-source design (inline structs vs ScriptableObjects) unified by GetWave
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.WaveSurvival SyncVars: survivalTimer (float), currentWave (hook OnCurrentWaveUpdate), enemysAlive (hook OnEnemiesAliveUpdate), totalKills, totalScore. Wave data has two parallel representations: `List<SurvivalWave> survivalWaves` (inline serializable: difficulty AIDifficulty, voicelineType_StartRound, BossMusic, overrideSpawns, EnemySpawnPoints List<Transform>, EnemiesMinMaxSpawnCount Vector2, Enemies List<GameObject>) and `List<SurvivalWaveEntry> survivalWaveEntries` (waveObject: SurvivalWaveObject ScriptableObject + per-entry EnemiesMinMaxSpawnCount/overrideSpawns/EnemySpawnPoints overrides). `bool useScriptableObjectWaves` picks which, and `GetWave(int index) -> WaveSurvival/ResolvedWave` + `get_WaveCount` normalize the two. SurvivalWaveObject is the SO half (difficulty, voicelineType_StartRound, BossMusic, Enemies) — asset menu path 'Wave Survival/Survival Wave', create label 'New Survival Wave'. Server loop: Server_AllPlayersLoaded -> SERVER_StartWave -> RPC_StartWave(int n); SERVER_OnEnemyDeath/OnEnemyDeath -> RPC_AlertEnemyCount(int); SERVER_EndWave -> RPC_EndWave(int n); SERVER_WinGame -> RPC_WinGame(int n). Config: startGame, AllowRespawns, timeBetweenWaves, timeToNextWave, ISR_roundUnlock (int). Voiceline variants enum SurvivalWave/VoicelineType_StartRound {standard, spetsnaz, armoured, suicidebombers, crackheads} with a matching clip list each (roundStart_Spetsnaz, roundStart_ArmouredAI, roundStart_SuicideBombers, roundStart_CrackHeads).
findings.members: WaveSurvival.instance, GetWave(int)->ResolvedWave, useScriptableObjectWaves, survivalWaves, survivalWaveEntries, SurvivalWaveObject, SurvivalWave/VoicelineType_StartRound{standard,spetsnaz,armoured,suicidebombers,crackheads}, ISR_roundUnlock, RPC_ActivateISR, SurvivalOnlyGameobjects
findings.modding: Because SurvivalWaveObject is a ScriptableObject and GetWave abstracts the source, a mod can append to survivalWaveEntries at runtime without touching the scene — the easiest custom-content surface in the whole mode layer. Note the enemy prefabs are List<GameObject> references, so new bot types still need a spawnable networked prefab.

findings.title: ISR is not a game mode — it is the drone/gunship station unlocked mid-Survival, with a live debug cheat left in
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.ISR (Assets\Scripts\ISR.cs) is a camera + Hellfire station: ISRcamera (Camera), renderTexture, MinFOV/MaxFOV/FOVSmooth/controlSpeed, currentVisionMode + BHot/WHot GameObjects + SwitchThermalMode() coroutine, TargetPostion (sic, Vector3), MissileCount (int), AGM114_Hellfire (GameObject), SERVER_Firemissile(), TimeBetweenBombs/timeSinceLastBomb, ToggleISR_RenderTexture(). Full voiceline set over RPCs: RPC_SFX_OnStation(int), RPC_SFX_Firing(int), RPC_SFX_NoAmmo(int), RPC_SFX_SplashKills(int), RPC_SFX_SplashNoJoy(int idx, int idxNoJoy). WaveSurvival owns it via `GameObject ISR`, `ISR ISRcontroller`, `int ISR_roundUnlock` and `RPC_ActivateISR()`. Shipped debug members: `bool debugControl`, `DebugGetISRInformation()`, and `ISR_Add500Missiles()`. Il2Cpp.ISR_Editor is an editor-only helper (single method SetISR_Rotation(Transform)) that got compiled into the shipping build and is dead at runtime.
findings.members: ISR.SERVER_Firemissile(), ISR.MissileCount, ISR.ISR_Add500Missiles(), ISR.debugControl, ISR.SwitchThermalMode(), WaveSurvival.ISR_roundUnlock, WaveSurvival.RPC_ActivateISR(), ISR_Editor.SetISR_Rotation(Transform)
findings.modding: ISR_Add500Missiles() and debugControl are unguarded public entry points — a one-line mod gives unlimited Hellfires. SERVER_Firemissile() is the server-side fire call, so a client-side patch to ISR_Add500Missiles only helps if you are host.

findings.title: Two mode types are dead code: Mirror_TeamDeathmatch is completely empty and PVP is a bare stub
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Mirror_TeamDeathmatch (Assets\Scripts\Mirror_TeamDeathmatch.cs) has literally no members other than .cctor, .ctor, .ctor(nint) and Weaved() — no fields, no methods, no SyncVars. It is a weaved NetworkBehaviour with zero behaviour. Il2Cpp.PVP has only Start(), Update(), and the ctors — no fields at all. Neither is referenced by any other type's signature. The real PvP implementation is Il2Cpp.PvpGameode (note the shipped typo, 'Gameode' not 'Gamemode', in both the type name and Assets\Scripts\GameModes\PvpGameode.cs).
findings.members: Il2Cpp.Mirror_TeamDeathmatch (empty), Il2Cpp.PVP (Start/Update only), Il2Cpp.PvpGameode (real)
findings.modding: Do not target Mirror_TeamDeathmatch or PVP — they do nothing. Anything searching for 'TeamDeathmatch' will find the wrong class; StandardPVP routes to PvpGameode.

findings.title: AlarmSystem is a self-contained networked audio state machine that no other type references
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.AlarmSystem is a NetworkBehaviour with SyncVars syncedState (AlarmSystem/AlarmState) and syncedAlarmClipIndex (int), plus RpcUpdateAudioState(AlarmState state, int alarmClipIndex), SetState(AlarmState newState), ApplyState(AlarmState, int). Enum AlarmSystem/AlarmState { None, Idle, Alarm }. Config: audioSource, idleClip, alarmLoopClips (AudioClip[]), fadeSpeedAlarm, fadeSpeedIdle, idleTime, clipChangePause; runtime: idleTimer, currentState, currentAlarmClipIndex, targetVolume, pendingClip, waitingForFadeOut, pauseTimer. Across all 206 assemblies, no type outside AlarmSystem itself exposes an AlarmSystem-typed field, property or parameter — the only other hits are Mirror's GeneratedNetworkCode reader/writer for AlarmState. So nothing in code holds a reference to it.
findings.members: AlarmSystem.SetState(AlarmState), AlarmSystem.RpcUpdateAudioState(AlarmState,int), AlarmSystem/AlarmState{None,Idle,Alarm}, AlarmSystem.alarmLoopClips
findings.modding: It is purely an ambience/alarm siren, NOT a detection or alert-level system — nothing about AI awareness touches it. Signatures cannot rule out a GetComponent<AlarmSystem>().SetState(...) call inside another method's body, or a scene UnityEvent wiring. Runtime probe: FindObjectsOfTypeAll<AlarmSystem>() in a loaded raid scene and watch whether syncedState ever leaves None while you trip the AI.

findings.title: Win/lose, extraction and the end screen all live on GameManagerNetwork, not on any GameMode class
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.GameManagerNetwork is the outcome hub. Failure: SERVER_FailOperation() -> RPC_FailOperation() -> FailOperation(). Success: CompleteOperation() -> ShowMissionCompleteScreen() with SetEndTimeStats(), SetEndStatus(), SetEndHealthStatus(), SetEndStats(), SetMiscInfo(), CalulateRating() [sic], CloseMissionCompleteScreen(), SaveLoadout(). Survival gets its own screen: ShowSurvivalEndScreen(bool fail), Survival_SetEndTimeStats/SetRoundStats/SetPointsStats/SetKillStats/SetDeadlistOperator [sic], GetTop3ByKills_NoAlloc. Extraction is a second, parallel implementation to ExfilZone's: SyncVars PlayersInAnyExfil, canExtract, isExtracting, extractionStartTime (double) plus ServerAddToExfil(int connectionId)/ServerRemoveFromExfil(int)/ServerPruneExfilOccupants()/ServerTickExtraction()/ServerSetExtracting(bool)/ServerCompleteExfil()/RpcExfiltrate()/GetRemainingExfilSeconds(). Also RestartOperation(), EndOperation(), SERVER_RespawnALL(), SERVER_ToggleRespawns()/SERVER_SetRespawns(bool), SetNumAlivePlayers(), ToggleScoreBoard() + ShowScoreboard SyncVar, FriendlyFire SyncVar, SetDemiGodMode(bool).
findings.members: GameManagerNetwork.SERVER_FailOperation, CompleteOperation, ShowMissionCompleteScreen, ShowSurvivalEndScreen(bool), CalulateRating, ServerTickExtraction, ServerCompleteExfil, RpcExfiltrate, extractionStartTime, canExtract
findings.modding: Patch SERVER_FailOperation / CompleteOperation for any custom win condition — they are the single choke point for all four PVE modes. Note extraction state is duplicated: ExfilZone has its own canExtract + PlayersInExfil SyncVars AND GameManagerNetwork has canExtract + PlayersInAnyExfil + isExtracting. Which one is authoritative for the actual extract timer needs a runtime probe (watch both while standing in an exfil).

findings.title: Achievements are checked once, at mission complete, and are gated by an anti-cheat SyncVar
findings.detail: GameManagerNetwork.CheckAchievements(), CheckTier1Challenge(), CheckTier1NightChallenge(). The contract comes from CerebusOpboard (AchievementName, achievement_aiDifficulty, achievement_min_ai_amount, TargetRaidTime) and is carried into the raid on OperationsManager as the SyncVar activeAchievementName (string) plus RaidTargetTime (float). OperationsManager also tracks the stat inputs as SyncVars: IntelCollected, IntelSpawned, TotalKills, TotalBots, TotalOperatorsInRaid, HVTdead, WasNight — with adders ResetStats(), AddKill(), AddIntelCollected(), AddIntelSpawned(), AddOperator(), AddBot(), AddHVTBot(BrainAI hvtBrain) and List<BrainAI> AI_HVTs. Cheat gating: SyncVar HasCheated (bool), plain DevCheatBypass (bool), and computed property EffectiveHasCheated (bool).
findings.members: GameManagerNetwork.CheckAchievements/CheckTier1Challenge/CheckTier1NightChallenge, OperationsManager.activeAchievementName (SyncVar), HasCheated (SyncVar), DevCheatBypass, EffectiveHasCheated, AI_HVTs, AddHVTBot(BrainAI)
findings.modding: EffectiveHasCheated is the single gate a mod trips — it is a computed getter over the HasCheated SyncVar and DevCheatBypass, so patching the getter is the clean way to keep achievements while modding, and setting HasCheated is how the game marks a run dirty. WasNight + Tier1 difficulty are the two axes of the two named challenges.

findings.title: InteractableSceneTransition is a second, board-bypassing entry point that carries a GameMode directly
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.InteractableSceneTransition has gameMode (GameMode enum), sceneName (string), infilName (string), InfilTime (int), areaName (string), timesRequested (int), and a vote-style network path: EnterScene(), SendRequest(string playerName) -> CMD_SendRequest(string playerName, int) -> RPC_SendRequest(string playerName, int). Unlike CMD_StartOperation, this route does carry a mode. Alongside it, OperationsManager.DebugStartOperation(string sceneName, string infilName, GameMode _gamemode) is the only other API that takes the mode explicitly.
findings.members: InteractableSceneTransition.gameMode, sceneName, infilName, CMD_SendRequest(string,int), OperationsManager.DebugStartOperation(string,string,GameMode)
findings.modding: DebugStartOperation is the practical way to launch ANY of the 7 modes on ANY of the 31 scenes (level0..level30) from a mod, including PVE_WAVESURVIVAL and PVE_ASSETDESTROY which have no board tuning UI. InteractableSceneTransition is the in-world door equivalent and is likely how survival/training areas are actually entered.

findings.title: Board reachability: only PVP and FFA have board tuning UI; WaveSurvival and AssetDestroy have none
findings.detail: OperationBoardUI's complete setter list is SetInfiltrationTime, SetInfilTimeUI, SetPreparationTime, SetPrepTimeUIValue, SetAI_COUNT, SetAICountUI, SetOpforDifficulty, SetAI_HVT_COUNT, SetHVTSpawnPoint, SetPVPTimeLimit, SetPVPRoundLimit, SetFFATimeLimit, SetFFAKillLimit, SetDifficultyUI, SetPVPParam1, SetPVPParam2, SetActiveInfilsMaskUI(long mask), InfilTargetButtonPressed(int,bool), SetSimulationParametersActive(bool) — plus HVT-specific widgets (HVTSimulationParameters, HVTEnemyCountSlider, HVTOpforDifficultySlider, HVTCountSlider, HVTDifficultySlider) and gating buttons NotEnoughInfilsButton / NotEnoughExfilsButton. There is NO wave/survival setter and no mission-asset setter. Flow: MissionLaptop -> CerebusOperation[] (OperationsManager.ActiveOperations vs SimulationOperations, split by IsSimulation) -> CerebusOpboard.TARGETPACKAGE (TARGETPACKAGE_DETAILS[]) -> OperationBoardUI.ExecuteOperationButtonPressed -> EnableConfirmationMenu -> StartOperationButton -> CerebusOpboard.Start_Operation. So StandardPVE / PVE_HVTKILL / PVE_FINDINTEL / StandardPVP / FFAPVP are board-reachable; PVE_WAVESURVIVAL and PVE_ASSETDESTROY are reachable only via a scene transition or DebugStartOperation.
findings.members: OperationBoardUI.SetPVPTimeLimit/SetPVPRoundLimit/SetFFATimeLimit/SetFFAKillLimit, ExecuteOperationButtonPressed, EnableConfirmationMenu, StartOperationButton, AbortOperationButtonPressed, NotEnoughInfilsButton, NotEnoughExfilsButton, OperationsManager.ActiveOperations, SimulationOperations
findings.modding: Which specific opboard prefabs actually set AffectGamemode/GameModeOverride is scene/prefab data the inspector cannot read — settle it at runtime by walking OperationsManager.singleton.ActiveOperations and SimulationOperations and printing each CerebusOpboard's AffectGamemode + GameModeOverride. That listing is the definitive board-reachability answer.

findings.title: A whole legacy mission-board stack (CERBERUS_* uppercase) still ships alongside the live Cerebus* one
findings.detail: Two parallel families exist: the live Il2Cpp.CerebusOperation / Il2Cpp.CerebusOpboard / Il2Cpp.OperationBoardUI, and the legacy ALL-CAPS Il2Cpp.CERBERUS_OPERATION / Il2Cpp.CERBERUS_OPBOARD / Il2Cpp.CERBERUS_TARGETPACKAGE. Both carry a `gameMode` of the same GameMode enum. The legacy CERBERUS_OPBOARD still has its own Start_Operation(), SwitchToActiveOperation/SwitchToSimulationOperation, SetInfiltrationTime(int), SetInfiltrationTarget(int), SetPreparationTarget(int), SetOpforDifficulty(int), SetAI_COUNT(float), and holds its UI widgets directly (opforCountSlider, horizontalSelector_InfilTime/InfilTarget/PrepTarget, SimulationButton, ActiveOperationButton) — i.e. it predates the UI/data split that OperationBoardUI + CerebusOpboard now implement. The new CerebusOpboard added requireEnoughInfils/requireEnoughExfils, AchievementName, TargetRaidTime, UnlockOnExfil and HVTSpawnIsRandom, none of which the legacy one has.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.CERBERUS_OPBOARD, Il2Cpp.CERBERUS_OPERATION, Il2Cpp.CERBERUS_TARGETPACKAGE (legacy) vs Il2Cpp.CerebusOpboard, Il2Cpp.CerebusOperation, Il2Cpp.TARGETPACKAGE_DETAILS, Il2Cpp.OperationBoardUI (live)
findings.modding: Target the lowercase Cerebus* family. Anything patching CERBERUS_OPBOARD.Start_Operation will without warning no-op on current content. Note OperationsManager.ActiveOperations/SimulationOperations are typed CerebusOperation[] (new family), which confirms which stack the runtime actually walks.

findings.title: Team model is int-keyed and shared by AI and players; PvP relies on it but the enum-less design leaves 'team' as a raw int everywhere
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.TeamManager (static instance) holds Dictionary<int, TeamRuntimeData> OperatorTeams and TeamStats[] AllTeams, with EnsureTeam(int id), AddOperatorToTeam(int, TeamIdentifier), RemoveOperatorFromTeam(int, TeamIdentifier), NumAliveTeamMembers(int teamId), GrabAllTeamMembers/GrabAllAiTeamMembersBrains/GrabAllEnemies/GrabAllEnemyBrains/GrabAllEnemyPlayers(int teamID), GetPossibleTargets(int myTeam, List<Transform> results). Il2Cpp.TeamIdentifier is the per-entity NetworkBehaviour with SyncVar TeamID (hook OnTeamChanged(int,int)), StartingTeamStats/TeamStats (Il2Cpp.TeamStats SO: TeamName, HasComms, CommsRange, FriendlyTeams TeamStats[], ThisTeamId), TargetPool (TargetList), MyPlayerMaster. TeamRuntimeData caches TeamMembers, TeamBots, AllTeamsTargets, AllEnemies, AllEnemyBots, AllEnemyPlayers with AddTarget/RemoveTarget/GetPossibleTargets. Assignment: OperationsManager.AutoSetTeams(), AssignTeamsPVE(), AssignTeamsTDM(), AutoAssignTeamOnPlayerJoin(PlayerMaster), GetShortTeam(); manual pick via playerBoardItem.SelectTeam(int). SpawnPoint carries {bool CanSpawnPlayer; int Team}. Legacy Il2Cpp.TeamID (teamID int, thisTeam string, hasComms, commsRange, friendlyTeams string[]) is the string-based predecessor and has a method literally named `dostuff()`.
findings.members: TeamManager.instance, TeamManager.GrabAllEnemyPlayers(int), TeamIdentifier.TeamID (SyncVar), TeamStats{TeamName,HasComms,CommsRange,FriendlyTeams,ThisTeamId}, SpawnPoint{CanSpawnPlayer,Team}, OperationsManager.AssignTeamsTDM(), TeamID.dostuff()
findings.modding: TeamManager.instance plus TeamIdentifier.TeamID is the complete handle for friend/foe in any custom mode — AI and players share it, so a mod can flip a bot to the player team with a single SyncVar write on the server. Il2Cpp.TeamID (string-based, with dostuff()) is the superseded version; use TeamIdentifier/TeamStats.

findings.title: Per-player scoring lives on PlayerMaster + playerBoardItem, and Survival points are a separate currency
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.PlayerMaster exposes AddKill(PlayerMaster killed), AddBotKill(), AddDeath(), AddIntelCollected(), AddSurvivalPoints(int score), and readers NumKills, NumDeaths, NumTeamKills, NumIntelCollected, currentlySpawnedAndAlive, MyTeamIdentifier, thisPlayerSteam64. The networked scoreboard row is Il2Cpp.playerBoardItem, whose SyncVars are Kills (ushort, hook OnKillsChanged), Deaths (ushort, OnDeathsChanged), TeamKills (ushort, OnTeamKillsChanged), Points (ushort, OnPointsChanged), IntelCollected (ushort, OnIntelPickupChanged), HVTKilled (bool, OnHVTKilledChanged), plus name/steamID/ping and a cached _lastGameMode (GameMode). Il2Cpp.SurvivalPlayer is a separate lightweight per-player record for WaveSurvival {PlayerMaster _master; int Score; int Kills} held in WaveSurvival.players.
findings.members: PlayerMaster.AddSurvivalPoints(int), PlayerMaster.NumKills/NumDeaths/NumTeamKills/NumIntelCollected, playerBoardItem SyncVars {Kills, Deaths, TeamKills, Points, IntelCollected, HVTKilled}, playerBoardItem._lastGameMode, SurvivalPlayer{_master,Score,Kills}
findings.modding: playerBoardItem's ushort SyncVars are the canonical replicated per-player score — read those rather than PlayerMaster if you need values on a non-host client. Note the ushort width: kill/point counts saturate at 65535. AddSurvivalPoints is the only scoring call that is mode-specific.

findings.title: Exfil zones tie to infils by name and duplicate the extraction state that GameManagerNetwork also owns
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.ExfilZone SyncVars: PlayersInExfil (int, hook OnPlayersInExfilChanged) and canExtract (bool, hook OnCanExtractChanged). Fields: exfilName (string), unlockingKey (string), linkedInfils (List<string>) — the name-based tie to InfilMethods.infilName / CerebusOpboard.AvailableInfils — isHelicopter, helicopter (Il2Cpp.Helicopter), InfiltrationAnimationPrefab, ExfilAnimationName, exfilSpawned, InfilMarker/ExfilMarker GameObjects, _occupants (HashSet<int> of connectionIds), notificationCooldown/_notifT. Methods: OnTriggerEnter/Exit(Collider), PruneDisconnected(), ServerForceRemoveConnection(int connectionId), SetMarker(), SpawnExfilVehicle() -> RPC_SpawnExfilVehicle(), TargetHint(NetworkConnectionToClient conn, string message, PopupType type), RPCHint(string message, PopupType type). RaidManager holds List<ExfilZone> exfilZones and gates them all at once via EnableGlobalExtraction() -> RPC_CanExfil(). CerebusOpboard.exfilUnlockingKey / UnlockOnExfil pair with ExfilZone.unlockingKey to unlock later missions on a specific exfil.
findings.members: ExfilZone.linkedInfils (List<string>), ExfilZone.unlockingKey, ExfilZone.canExtract (SyncVar), ExfilZone.PlayersInExfil (SyncVar), ExfilZone.ServerForceRemoveConnection(int), RaidManager.EnableGlobalExtraction(), RaidManager.RPC_CanExfil()
findings.modding: linkedInfils is string-matched, so a custom infil whose name is not present in some ExfilZone.linkedInfils will have no valid exfil and the raid becomes unwinnable. CerebusOpboard.exfilUnlockingKey + ExfilZone.unlockingKey + UnlockOnExfil is the mission-progression graph — that is where 'which mission unlocks which' is encoded, and it is all string keys, so a mod can rewire progression without touching prefabs.

findings.title: Steam leaderboards exist and are wired for kills/deaths/hours, and are separate from the in-raid scoreboard
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.SteamLeaderBoard: UpdateScore(int score), GetLeaderBoardData(ELeaderboardDataRequest ...), OnLeaderboardFindResult/OnLeaderboardUploadResult/OnLeaderboardDownloadResult callbacks. Il2Cpp.HighScoreUI drives three boards — FillLeaderBoardKills(), FillLeaderBoardDeaths(), FillLeaderBoardHours() — plus BtnBeginFillLeaderboardGlobal(), RefreshLeaderboard(), AddPlayerTop(LeaderboardEntry_t), FillHighscorePrefab(GameObject, LeaderboardData ...), OnDownloadedEntriesForUsers, with s_currentLeaderboard (SteamLeaderboard_t), entries (int), type (int). Row prefab is Il2Cpp.LeaderBoardPlayer.SetData(CSteamID, int type, float ...) with maintext/rankText/subText/killsText/deathsText/profileImage.
findings.members: SteamLeaderBoard.UpdateScore(int), HighScoreUI.FillLeaderBoardKills/Deaths/Hours, LeaderBoardPlayer.SetData(CSteamID,int,float)
findings.modding: These are global Steam stats, not per-match. A mod that inflates PlayerMaster kill counts will push to the public leaderboard through SteamLeaderBoard.UpdateScore — patch or no-op UpdateScore if you do not want modded runs uploaded.

findings.title: Two generations of interaction API coexist; only the newer one is extensible
findings.detail: There are two unrelated idioms. LEGACY: bespoke `StartInteraction(PlayerNetworking)` implemented independently by `Il2Cpp.BreakerSwitch`, `Il2Cpp.InteractableChair`, `Il2Cpp.FullBodyInteraction` (plus param-less variants on `nvgController`, `Tablet`, `InteractionControl`, `EmoteSystem`). These live in `\Assets\Scripts\*.cs`. MODERN: `Il2Cpp.InteractableComponent` with `AccessInteractable(PlayerNetworking)`, virtual `Interacted(PlayerNetworking)`, and two UI strings `InteractableName` / `InteractableContext`. It lives in `\Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\InteractableComponent.cs`. `InteractableComponent` carries NO Mirror members, so it is a plain MonoBehaviour — each subclass does its own networking.
findings.members: InteractableComponent.AccessInteractable(PlayerNetworking), InteractableComponent.Interacted(PlayerNetworking), InteractableComponent.InteractableName, InteractableComponent.InteractableContext, BreakerSwitch.StartInteraction(PlayerNetworking), InteractableChair.StartInteraction(PlayerNetworking)
findings.modding: New interactables should derive from InteractableComponent — it is the only path that feeds the prompt UI generically. The legacy classes are almost certainly matched by explicit GetComponent<T> checks inside ProcessInteractable, so a mod cannot add to that set without patching. Note the IL2CPP constraint: subclassing requires ClassInjector.RegisterTypeInIl2Cpp with InteractableComponent as base, not a plain C# subclass.

findings.title: Only four types derive from InteractableComponent, and nothing anywhere holds one as a field
findings.detail: Exhaustive search of all 785 Assembly-CSharp types for `Interacted(PlayerNetworking)` yields exactly four subclasses: `AmmoReloader`, `ProjectorToggler`, `MilkRigidbodyRequestOwnership`, `ObjectiveInteractable`. `AmmoReloader` and `MilkRigidbodyRequestOwnership` override nothing but `Interacted` — zero fields. `ProjectorToggler` adds `Projector: LaptopProjector`; `ObjectiveInteractable` adds `Objective: ObjectiveObject`. Separately, NO member of any type in the assembly is typed `Il2Cpp.InteractableComponent`. Since nothing caches one, `PlayerNetworking.ProcessInteractable()` must resolve it by GetComponent on the ray hit each time.
findings.members: AmmoReloader.Interacted, ProjectorToggler.Interacted, ProjectorToggler.Projector, MilkRigidbodyRequestOwnership.Interacted, ObjectiveInteractable.Interacted, ObjectiveInteractable.Objective
findings.modding: The abstraction is barely used, so it is cheap to extend and unlikely to conflict. MilkRigidbodyRequestOwnership is the interesting one — it is the sanctioned way to take Mirror authority over a physics prop before pushing it, which any mod that wants player-manipulable physics objects must replicate.

findings.title: PlayerNetworking is the interaction discovery seam: raycast first, proximity fallback
findings.detail: `PlayerNetworking` owns the whole scan/dispatch/UI loop: `ScanForInteractable() -> bool` (backed by field `_interactableRayHit: UnityEngine.RaycastHit`), `ScanForNearbyInteractable() -> bool` (backed by `interactionDetectionRange: float`), and `ProcessInteractable() -> void`. Two TMP labels are driven from it: `interactTxt` and `InteractionContextText`, which map one-to-one onto `InteractableComponent.InteractableName` / `.InteractableContext`. The interact key is cached in `_cachedInteractKey: UnityEngine.KeyCode`. There is also `CMD_ResumeInteraction`/`RPC_ResumeInteraction` and a direct `chair: InteractableChair` field plus `SitInHelicopter(FullBodyInteraction)`.
findings.members: PlayerNetworking.ScanForInteractable(), PlayerNetworking.ScanForNearbyInteractable(), PlayerNetworking.ProcessInteractable(), PlayerNetworking._interactableRayHit, PlayerNetworking.interactionDetectionRange, PlayerNetworking._cachedInteractKey, PlayerNetworking.interactTxt, PlayerNetworking.InteractionContextText
findings.modding: Hook `PlayerNetworking.ProcessInteractable` to inject custom interactables without touching the base class, or hook `ScanForInteractable` to override what the ray reports. `_cachedInteractKey` being a cached KeyCode means rebinding at runtime may not take effect until whatever populates it re-runs.

findings.title: Destructible is a hand-authored 3-section prefab swap, not runtime fracture — and it is a actually well-built netcode design
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.Destructible` (from `\Assets\Scripts\Destructible.cs`) swaps between authored prefabs: `HealthyObject`, `DestroyedObject`, `LeftFracturedObject`, `MiddleFracturedObject`, `RightFracturedObject`, with matching debris arrays `destroyedRBsLeft/Middle/Right: Rigidbody[]`. State is a byte bitmask SyncVar `_destructionState` with constants `LEFT`/`MIDDLE`/`RIGHT` (byte) and hook `OnDestructionStateChanged(byte oldState, byte newState)`. `CalculateSections(Vector3 explosionPos, int overrideValue) -> byte` picks sections from the blast position. Cascade rules are authored booleans: `leftDestroysBoth`, `rightDestroysBoth`, `middleDestroysBoth`, `middleDestroysLeft`, `middleDestroysRight`. The late-join path is the good part: `OnStartClient` + `_initialStateApplied` + SyncVars `Network_lastExplosionPos/Radius/Force` replay through `ApplyExplosionVisuals(pos, radius, force, byte sections, bool skipForces)` with skipForces=true, so a joining client sees debris already settled instead of re-exploding.
findings.members: Destructible.CmdRequestExplosion(Vector3,float,float,int), Destructible.ServerApplyExplosion(...), Destructible.CalculateSections(Vector3,int), Destructible.ApplyExplosionVisuals(Vector3,float,float,byte,bool), Destructible.ActivateSection(Rigidbody[],Vector3,float,float,bool), Destructible.OnDestructionStateChanged(byte,byte), Destructible._destructionState, Destructible.DebugExplode(Vector3,float,float)
findings.modding: Destruction is content, not simulation — a modded destructible needs five authored prefabs and three debris arrays, and the section granularity is fixed at three. `DebugExplode(pos, radius, force)` is a public non-networked entry point that is trivially callable from a mod for testing.

findings.title: Nothing in the codebase references Destructible — it may be built but unwired
findings.detail: Searching all 46,370 member signatures in Assembly-CSharp, no member of any type is typed `Il2Cpp.Destructible`, and there is no central explosion-damage dispatcher that could hold one. Every explosive implements damage independently: `GrenadeExplosive.DoExplosion()`, `SlapChargeExplosive.DamageLogic()`, `Missile.SERVER_Explode(Vector3)`, `ProximityExplosive.SERVER_BigBoom()`, `Landmine.CMD_Explode(Health)`. None of them expose a Destructible field. The only non-networked public entry on Destructible is literally named `DebugExplode`. `DestructibleLink` exists solely to hold `destructible: Destructible` (a proxy component so child colliders can find the parent), which is consistent with GetComponent-based lookup.
findings.members: Destructible.DebugExplode, DestructibleLink.destructible, GrenadeExplosive.DoExplosion, SlapChargeExplosive.DamageLogic, Missile.SERVER_Explode, ProximityExplosive.SERVER_BigBoom
findings.modding: If it is unwired, a mod can own the whole destruction feature by calling CmdRequestExplosion from an explosion hook. Probe: patch `Destructible.CmdRequestExplosion` and `ApplyExplosion` with a logging prefix, load an operation scene, and detonate a grenade next to a wall carrying the component; also count `Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll<Destructible>()` after scene load to see whether any shipped map even uses it.

findings.title: RayFire ships as 20 compiled components but appears to be dead weight
findings.detail: `Il2CppRayFireAssembly` contains the full product: RayfireRigid, RayfireRigidRoot, RayfireShatter, RayfireBomb, RayfireGun, RayfireBlade, RayfireConnectivity, RayfireCluster, RayfireActivator, RayfireDebris, RayfireDust, RayfireMan, RayfireCombine, RayfireRecorder, RayfireRestriction, RayfireSnapshot, RayfireSound, RayfireUnyielding, RayfireVortex, RayfireWind. But the only Assembly-CSharp glue is `Il2Cpp.ConnectivityEventScript`, whose shape (`globalSubscription`/`localSubscription` bools, `LocalMethodConnectivity`/`GlobalMethodConnectivity(RayfireConnectivity, List<RFShard>, List<RFCluster>)`) is a verbatim copy of RayFire's shipped demo event-subscription sample. Additionally, `rayfire` appears zero times across `bundle_names.txt` (~4990 bundles) and `catalog_strings.txt`. The game's actual destruction is `Destructible` (authored) and `GK.BreakableSurface` (glass); neither references RayFire.
findings.members: Il2CppRayFire.RayfireMan, Il2CppRayFire.RayfireRigid, Il2Cpp.ConnectivityEventScript.LocalMethodConnectivity, Il2Cpp.ConnectivityEventScript.localConnectivityComponent
findings.modding: Caveat: catalog strings are asset names, so a prefab could still carry a RayfireRigid without the word appearing. But RayFire needs a `RayfireMan` singleton to demolish anything at all. Probe: after loading an operation scene, check `RayfireMan.inst != null` and count `Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll<RayfireRigid>()`. If both are empty, a mod could adopt RayFire wholesale for real runtime fracture since the runtime is already compiled in — that is a large free capability.

findings.title: Glass is the only true runtime fracture, via a Voronoi library — and it is not networked at all
findings.detail: `Il2CppGK.*` is Oskar Sigvardsson's Delaunay/Voronoi library (DelaunayCalculator, DelaunayTriangulation, VoronoiCalculator, VoronoiClipper, VoronoiDiagram, Geom, VectorExtensions) driving `Il2CppGK.BreakableSurface`. It actually computes a Voronoi diagram at the impact point and builds shard meshes at runtime via `MeshFromPolygon(List<Vector2> polygon, float thickness) -> Mesh`. It is planar-only: geometry is `Polygon: List<Vector2>` plus `Thickness: float`, so it works for panes, not arbitrary meshes. Recursive subdivision is bounded by `MinBreakArea` and tracked by `age: int`. Damage gating uses `health`, `MinImpactToBreak`, and `WhenBrokenITB` (a lowered threshold once already broken). Shards move to `toLayer`. Shard randomness comes from `NormalizedRandom(float mean, float stddev)`. Crucially: BreakableSurface has NO Mirror members — no CMD_, no RPC_, no NetworkBehaviour plumbing.
findings.members: GK.BreakableSurface.Break(Vector3,float), GK.BreakableSurface.BreakAfterFixedUpdate(Vector3,float), GK.BreakableSurface.Fracture(Vector2), GK.BreakableSurface.FracturePhysic(Vector2), GK.BreakableSurface.MeshFromPolygon(List<Vector2>,float), GK.BreakableSurface.NormalizedRandom(float,float), GK.BreakableSurface.Shards, GK.BreakableSurface.MinBreakArea, GK.BreakableSurface.WhenBrokenITB, GK.BreakableSurface.SetDifficulty()
findings.modding: Because break state is decided locally with locally-seeded randomness, shard geometry differs on every client by design, and whether a pane is broken can diverge if the triggering event is client-local. Probe: two clients, one shoots a window, check the other client's pane renderer state. `SetDifficulty()` implies shard count scales with quality settings, so low-spec clients get different pane counts — another divergence source.

findings.title: Glass is registered globally on GameManager and reset via a per-instance Reload()
findings.detail: `GameManager.BreakableSurfaces: List<Il2CppGK.BreakableSurface>` is a global registry, and `BreakableSurface.Reload()` restores an individual pane. `GameManager` also has `ResetAllDoors()` and `Server_BeforeLoadScene(string sceneName)`. Bullets are integrated: `BulletInstance.breakableSurface: GK.BreakableSurface` carries the pane a round hit, and `SlapChargeExplosive.breakableSurface` lets a breaching charge detect it is stuck to glass rather than a wall or door.
findings.members: GameManager.BreakableSurfaces, GameManager.ResetAllDoors(), GameManager.Server_BeforeLoadScene(string), GK.BreakableSurface.Reload(), BulletInstance.breakableSurface, SlapChargeExplosive.breakableSurface
findings.modding: Note the asymmetry: there is a named `ResetAllDoors()` but no `ResetAllBreakableSurfaces()`. The registry plus per-instance Reload() are the ingredients, but the sweep is inside a method body I cannot read. If glass does not reset between operations that is a bug with an easy mod fix — iterate `GameManager.BreakableSurfaces` and call `Reload()` on scene load.

findings.title: SlapChargeExplosive is a directional shaped charge with surface sensing — the most sophisticated explosive in the game
findings.detail: Damage is a cone, not a sphere: `IsInFrontCone(Vector3 origin, Vector3 forward, Vector3 point, float halfAngleDeg, float maxRange) -> bool` and a planar variant `IsInFrontConePlanar(...)`, parameterised by `halfAngle`, `maxRange`, `baseDamage`, `distanceFalloffPower`, `angleFalloffPower`, with `damageMask` and `blockerMask` LayerMasks for occlusion. It senses what it is attached to: `door: DoorV2`, `breakableSurface: GK.BreakableSurface`, `attachedRB: Rigidbody`, with `doorSenseDistance: float` and `minDepthIfNoDoor: float` — i.e. if no door is found it assumes a nominal wall thickness. Sticking is networked via `CMD_StickCharge(Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot)` / `RPC_StickCharge`. Throwing reuses the grenade collider-ignore trick: `StartThrow(Vector3 launchVelocity, Collider[] ignoreColliders)`, `IgnoreCollidersTemporarily(Collider[], float duration)`, `RestoreIgnoredCollisions()`.
findings.members: SlapChargeExplosive.IsInFrontCone(Vector3,Vector3,Vector3,float,float), SlapChargeExplosive.IsInFrontConePlanar(...), SlapChargeExplosive.DamageLogic(), SlapChargeExplosive.CMD_StickCharge(Vector3,Quaternion), SlapChargeExplosive.doorSenseDistance, SlapChargeExplosive.minDepthIfNoDoor, SlapChargeExplosive.angleFalloffPower, SlapChargeExplosive.linkedDetonator
findings.modding: `linkedDetonator: GrenadeV2` means the charge and its igniter are two objects — the detonator is modelled as a grenade with `hasIgniter` plus `igniterFire`/`igniterEquip`/`igniterHolster` animation strings and `ActivateIgniter()`/`CMD_ActivateIgniter`/`RPC_ActivateIgniter`. A custom breaching charge must reproduce that pairing.

findings.title: Grenade fragmentation is real simulated ballistics sharing the bullet impact path
findings.detail: `GrenadeExplosive` spawns `shrapnelPrefab` governed by `fragmentCount`, `minSpeed`, `maxSpeed`, `fragmentGravity`, `fragmentLifetime`, `damageMask`. The fragments are `Il2Cpp.SimulatedShrapnel` (pooled via `ShrapnelPooled._shrapnel`), which manually integrates: `Initialize(Vector3 initialVelocity, float gravity, float lifetime, LayerMask damageMask, int _netid)`, `FixedUpdate()`, `ProcessHit(RaycastHit)`, `SpawnImpact(SurfaceInformation surfaceInfo, RaycastHit hit, bool isPen)`. No Rigidbody — it is velocity integration plus raycast sweep, and it feeds the same `SurfaceInformation` impact system bullets use, including penetration. `netID: int` carries the owner for kill attribution.
findings.members: SimulatedShrapnel.Initialize(Vector3,float,float,LayerMask,int), SimulatedShrapnel.ProcessHit(RaycastHit), SimulatedShrapnel.SpawnImpact(SurfaceInformation,RaycastHit,bool), SimulatedShrapnel.netID, GrenadeExplosive.fragmentCount, GrenadeExplosive.fragmentGravity, ShrapnelPooled._shrapnel
findings.modding: Frag lethality is emergent from fragment count and geometry, not a damage radius — so cover actually works against frags, and raising fragmentCount raises both lethality and per-explosion raycast cost linearly. The shrapnel pool is pre-sized by PoolInitializer, so a large fragmentCount can exhaust it without warning.

findings.title: Flashbangs run separate concussion paths for players and AI, and nudge the blast origin out of geometry
findings.detail: `GrenadeExplosive` has `CheckPlayerConcussion(bool flash, float distMax)` and `CheckAIConcussion(bool flash, float distMax)` as distinct methods, plus `isFlashbang`, `flashTime`, and two separate LayerMasks `flashMask` and `flashMask2` (two-stage line-of-sight test). `ResolveSafeOrigin(Vector3 origin) -> Vector3` exists to move the blast origin before the LOS checks so a grenade resting against geometry does not occlude itself. Multi-pop is supported via `multipleExplosions`, `multiDelay`, `timesExplode`, `timesExploded`. A real-time light is used and then cleaned up: `LightSource: GameObject` with `DeactivateLight()`. Visuals are split between `explosionVFX: UnityEngine.VFX.VisualEffect` (VFX Graph) and `explosionEffect: GameObject`.
findings.members: GrenadeExplosive.CheckPlayerConcussion(bool,float), GrenadeExplosive.CheckAIConcussion(bool,float), GrenadeExplosive.ResolveSafeOrigin(Vector3), GrenadeExplosive.flashMask, GrenadeExplosive.flashMask2, GrenadeExplosive.multipleExplosions, GrenadeExplosive.timesExplode, GrenadeExplosive.explosionVFX
findings.modding: AI are actually flashable through a dedicated path, so a mod tuning flash duration must touch both methods or players and bots desync in behaviour. `ResolveSafeOrigin` is the fix for the classic 'flashbang against a wall does nothing' bug — worth preserving if patching.

findings.title: Missile uses closest-approach detonation plus a hard lifetime cap, and networks its SFX variant choice
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.Missile` integrates in `FixedUpdate` with `_speed`, `_rotateSpeed`, `RotateRocket()`, guiding toward SyncVar `_target: Vector3` (`Network_target`). Detonation logic uses `_captureRadius` and `_prevDistanceToTarget` — the classic pattern of detonating when distance to target starts increasing. `_maxLifetime` and `_aliveTime` back the tooltip literal 'Hard cap (seconds) before the missile force-detonates so it can never glide/leak forever.' `_armed: bool` gates arming. Damage is `KillRadius`, `MaxRadius`, `DamageAmount: int`. It is called in by `_isr: Il2Cpp.ISR`. Audio is distance-selected and replicated by index: `ExplosionCloseSFX`/`ExplosionFarSFX: List<AudioClip>` with `explosionTrackClose`/`explosionTrackFar: int`, sent through `RPC_Explode(int track, int track2, Vector3 position)` so all clients play the same random pick.
findings.members: Missile.SERVER_Explode(Vector3), Missile.RPC_Explode(int,int,Vector3), Missile.Detonate(Vector3), Missile.RotateRocket(), Missile._captureRadius, Missile._prevDistanceToTarget, Missile._maxLifetime, Missile._isr, Missile.explosionTrackClose
findings.modding: Sending clip indices rather than letting each client roll its own is the correct pattern and worth copying for any modded networked audio. The `_maxLifetime` force-detonate is a leak guard — raising missile speed without raising it will cause long shots to detonate mid-air.

findings.title: ProximityExplosive is a ringing phone bomb with a decoy detonation stage
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.ProximityExplosive` arms on presence: `distanceToActivate`, `TimeWithinDistanceToActivate`, `_activationTimer`, `spawnedPlayers: List<PlayerNetworking>`. It plays ringtones through two sources, `ringtoneSource` and `ringtoneSource_vibrate`, selecting from `ringtones: Ringtones[]` where `Il2Cpp.Ringtones` is just a pair `{ ringtone: AudioClip, ringtone_vibrate: AudioClip }`, sequenced by `_songTime`/`_songTimer`. There are two detonation stages plus a fake: `SERVER_TriggerBoom()`/`RPC_TriggerBoom(int i)`, `SERVER_BigBoom()`/`RPC_BigBoom()`, and `FakeBoom()`. Meshes swap via `Explosive_mesh: GameObject[]`.
findings.members: ProximityExplosive.SERVER_TriggerBoom(), ProximityExplosive.RPC_TriggerBoom(int), ProximityExplosive.SERVER_BigBoom(), ProximityExplosive.RPC_BigBoom(), ProximityExplosive.FakeBoom(), ProximityExplosive.ringtones, Ringtones.ringtone_vibrate
findings.modding: `FakeBoom()` has no CMD_/RPC_ pair, so it is purely local — presumably a client-side scare/misfire effect. Adding ringtones is pure data (a Ringtones array entry), one of the easiest content extensions in this area.

findings.title: Landmine passes the victim's Health object straight into a Command — a likely trust boundary hole
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.Landmine` triggers from `OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)` and calls `CMD_Explode(Il2Cpp.Health victim)`, with `RPC_Explode()` for the visuals and `hasExploded` as a SyncVar (`NetworkhasExploded`). It has two colliders, `detecterCollider` and `hardCollider`, plus `distanceToExplode`, `ExplosivePrefab`, `ExplosionVFX`, `LandmineGFX`, `ExplosionSFX`, and a field named `specialBoy: bool`.
findings.members: Landmine.OnTriggerEnter(Collider), Landmine.CMD_Explode(Health), Landmine.RPC_Explode(), Landmine.hasExploded, Landmine.detecterCollider, Landmine.specialBoy
findings.modding: A landmine is a scene object, so for a client to call CMD_Explode at all the Command must be declared `requiresAuthority = false`. If so, any client can invoke `CMD_Explode(anyHealthComponent)` and kill an arbitrary player regardless of proximity. Probe: read the Mirror command attribute via `NetworkBehaviour` metadata at runtime, or simply call `CMD_Explode` from a non-authoritative client against a remote player's Health and see whether the server honours it. Contrast with `DoorV2`, which does validate — it has `TakeDamageServer` and `Server_CheckDoorDamageResults` behind `CMD_TakeDamage`.

findings.title: Thrown grenades are separately-spawned networked objects with an authority handoff and a netId retry coroutine
findings.detail: `GrenadeV2` (the held item) spawns a distinct networked projectile rather than converting itself. Server side: `ServerSpawnProjectile(NetworkConnectionToClient owner)`, `ResolveSpawnedGrenadeIdentity() -> NetworkIdentity`, `ServerReassignSpawnedGrenadeAuthority(NetworkConnectionToClient conn)`, `ServerClearSpawnedGrenadeAuthority()`. Clients learn about it through SyncVar `spawnedGrenadeNetID: int` with hook `OnSpawnedGrenade(int previous, int current)`, then resolve it with `ResolveSpawnedGrenade(uint netId) -> IEnumerator` — a coroutine, i.e. a poll-until-arrives workaround for the netId arriving before the spawn message. Throw velocity is explicit, not force-based: `ComputeThrowVelocity(Vector3 fallbackEuler, float speed, float upwardBias)` with `overhandLaunchSpeed`/`underhandLaunchSpeed`/`overhandUpwardBias`/`underhandUpwardBias`, matching the literal 'Bot grenade launch speed (m/s). Replaces the old AddForce-based throw.' `CollectThrowerColliders()` feeds the ignore list.
findings.members: GrenadeV2.ServerSpawnProjectile(NetworkConnectionToClient), GrenadeV2.ResolveSpawnedGrenade(uint), GrenadeV2.OnSpawnedGrenade(int,int), GrenadeV2.ComputeThrowVelocity(Vector3,float,float), GrenadeV2.ServerReassignSpawnedGrenadeAuthority, GrenadeV2.CollectThrowerColliders(), GrenadeV2.CMD_ThrowGrenade(Vector3,Vector3,Vector3,float)
findings.modding: The older `Il2Cpp.Grenade` class (`\Assets\Scripts\Grenade.cs`, with `throwGrenade()`, `spawnGrenade(Vector3,Vector3)`, `GrenadeType`) still exists alongside GrenadeV2 and is very likely dead — mod against GrenadeV2. The coroutine resolve means a modded grenade must tolerate a frame or more where SpawnedGrenade is null.

findings.title: ObjectPooler is the real pooling system, with bounded LRU reclaim and a 'park' mode instead of deactivation
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.ObjectPooler` (singleton `instance`, `\Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\Pooling\ObjectPooler.cs`) keys pools by prefab GameObject: `PooledObjects: Dictionary<GameObject, List<PooledObject>>`. Two notable mechanisms. (1) Bounded pools: `BoundedPrefabs: HashSet<GameObject>` plus `ActiveByPrefab: Dictionary<GameObject, LinkedList<PooledObject>>` and `ReclaimOldestIfBounded(GameObject prefab)` — an LRU that steals the oldest live instance when the pool is exhausted, with `PooledObject.ActiveNode: LinkedListNode<PooledObject>` giving O(1) removal. (2) Parking: `ParkedPrefabs: HashSet<GameObject>` and `PooledObject.ParkPosition: Vector3` — idle instances are teleported away rather than SetActive(false), avoiding OnEnable/OnDisable churn. There is also defensive recovery: `PooledObjectDestroyedUhOh(GameObject prefab, PooledObject instance)` and `ResetDestroyedPools()`.
findings.members: ObjectPooler.InstantiatePooled(GameObject,Vector3,Quaternion), ObjectPooler.TryInitializePool(GameObject,int,bool,bool), ObjectPooler.ReclaimOldestIfBounded(GameObject), ObjectPooler.PooledObjectDestroyedUhOh(GameObject,PooledObject), ObjectPooler.ResetDestroyedPools(), PooledObject.ParkPosition, PooledObject.ActiveNode, PooledObject.OnSpawned/OnPooled/OnInitialize
findings.modding: `ObjectPooler.instance.InstantiatePooled(prefab, pos, rot)` is the sanctioned spawn path and there is a generic overload too. Never call UnityEngine.Object.Destroy on something with a PooledObject — that triggers the PooledObjectDestroyedUhOh recovery path. Custom pooled behaviours override the `PooledObject` lifecycle trio rather than using Awake/OnEnable.

findings.title: Decal and VFX pool sizes are divided from a global budget across surface prefabs — adding a surface shrinks every other pool
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.PoolInitializer` computes pool sizes at load rather than authoring them: `CountDecalPrefabs() -> int`, `CountImpactVFXPrefabs() -> int`, then `InitSurfacePools(SurfaceInformation info, int perDecal, int perVFX)`. The budget knobs are `TotalDecalBudget`, `DefaultDecalBudget`, `MinDecalsPerPrefab`, `MaxDecalsPerPrefab`, `TotalVFXBudget`, `MinVFXPerPrefab`, `MaxVFXPerPrefab`, plus fixed counts `NumBullets`, `NumBloodBullets`, `NumBloodDecals`, `NumEachGore`, `NumEachImpactEffect`, `NumEachDecal`. Per-instance lifetimes are centralised rather than per-object Update: `PoolTimerManager` keeps three flat lists (`delayedList`, `vfxList`, `bloodList`) with Register/Unregister pairs and a generic `SwapRemove<T>(List<T>, int index)`.
findings.members: PoolInitializer.InitSurfacePools(SurfaceInformation,int,int), PoolInitializer.CountDecalPrefabs(), PoolInitializer.TotalDecalBudget, PoolInitializer.MinDecalsPerPrefab, PoolTimerManager.RegisterVFX(PooledVFX), PoolTimerManager.SwapRemove, PooledImpactDecal.placed, PooledImpactDecal.RemoveAllDecals()
findings.modding: Direct consequence: registering a new SurfaceInformation with its own decal and VFX prefabs divides the same global budget more ways, shrinking every existing pool toward MinDecalsPerPrefab. A mod adding surfaces should raise TotalDecalBudget/TotalVFXBudget in step. Also `PooledImpactDecal.unparentOnInitialize` means decals detach from their hit object — decals will not follow moving geometry, a deliberate fake.

findings.title: There are two independent pooling systems; the second is HDRP's water sample, and it is actually wired to the player
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.PoolManager` is NOT the game's pool — its script path is `\Assets\Samples\High Definition RP\17.0.3\Water Samples\Scripts\PoolManager.cs`. It is a primitive ring-buffer pool: `Instances: Dictionary<InstanceType, PoolManager>`, `getNextAvailable() -> GameObject`, `recycle: bool`, `recycleIndex: int`, `maxCount: float`, `type: InstanceType`, `prefab`. Likewise `DeformationManager`, `SpawnDeformation` and `CharacterControllerSpawnDeformation` are all Water Samples scripts. But they are not inert: `CharacterControllerSpawnDeformation` holds `playerMovement: Il2Cpp.PlayerMovement` — the game's own movement class — alongside `controller: CharacterController`, `IsControllerMoving()`, and `TimeBtwnEachDeformation`. A full HDRP water suite is present (`Buoyancy`, `Floater`, `FitToWaterSurface`, `FitToWaterSurfaceBurst`, `FoamBuffer`, `FoamShore`, `ProjectCaustics`, `ShoreDecalTrigger`, `UnderwaterToggle`, `WaterZone`, `WaterTrigger`, `WaterSettings`, `FloatingIceberg`).
findings.members: PoolManager.getNextAvailable(), PoolManager.Instances, CharacterControllerSpawnDeformation.playerMovement, CharacterControllerSpawnDeformation.IsControllerMoving(), DeformationManager.SetAmplitude(float), DeformationManager.SetSpeed(float), SpawnDeformation.thresholdSpeed
findings.modding: Wading ripples are real HDRP WaterDeformers spawned on a rate limiter, recycled through this second pool — so water interaction is actually simulated, not a decal. Do not confuse `PoolManager` with `ObjectPooler` when hooking. `FloatingIceberg` surviving in the build is a strong hint this whole suite is mostly unpruned sample code; zero water assets appear in the addressable catalog, so probe whether any shipped map has a WaterSurface at all before relying on it.

findings.title: Grass trample is a real GPU simulation: a scrolling ping-pong RT with exponential decay, driven by an HDRP CustomPass
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.FoliageBendPass` is an HDRP CustomPass (`Execute(CustomPassContext ctx)`, `Setup(ScriptableRenderContext, CommandBuffer)`) using two RTHandles `rtA`/`rtB` flipped by `currentIsA`. Two hidden shaders do the work — literals confirm `Hidden/FoliageBendUpdate` and `Hidden/FoliageBendStamp`. The update pass scrolls history as the world center moves (`prevSnappedCenterXZ: Vector2`, shader id `ID_DeltaUV`) and applies `ID_DecayFactor` so grass springs back; the stamp pass draws a swept quad per interaction (`ID_Start`, `ID_End`, `ID_Radius`, `ID_RefStep`), matching the literal 'per-interaction swept-quad stamp.' Results are published globally via `ID_GlobalRT`, `ID_GlobalCenter`, `ID_GlobalExtent` so any foliage shader can sample them. `AllocateRTs(int resolution)` / `ReleaseRTs()` handle resize.
findings.members: FoliageBendPass.Execute(CustomPassContext), FoliageBendPass.AllocateRTs(int), FoliageBendPass.rtA, FoliageBendPass.rtB, FoliageBendPass.currentIsA, FoliageBendPass.prevSnappedCenterXZ, FoliageBendPass.ID_DecayFactor, FoliageBendPass.ID_GlobalRT
findings.modding: The bend map is world-space and persistent within its extent, so trails linger and decay. Because it publishes global shader properties, a custom foliage shader can read the same bend map for free. It is purely visual and never networked.

findings.title: FoliageInteractionController exposes a public CauseInteraction API any mod can call
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.FoliageInteractionController` is a singleton (`Instance`) with a actually public interface: `CauseInteraction(Vector3 start, Vector3 end)` and `CauseInteraction(Vector3 start, Vector3 end, float radius)`, plus `SetCenter(Vector3 worldPos)` and `SetCenter(Transform t)`. Queued work is exposed as `Pending: IReadOnlyList<Interaction>` with `ClearPending()`. Tuning: `Resolution` ('Resolution of the square bend RT. Higher = sharper trample edges, more VRAM.'), `WorldExtent`, `DecayHalfLife`, `MaxStep`, `StrengthReferenceStep` ('Segment length that produces full bend strength. Shorter steps scale down linearly.'), `defaultRadius`, `trampleResistance`. The companion `FoliageBendFollow` stamps per-transform in LateUpdate with `setCenter` ('Move the bend RT to follow this transform. Usually true on the player, false on other interactors'), `radius`, `stampWhenIdle` ('Keep stamping a small segment in the last-facing direction when not moving. Prevents grass from springing back under a standing player.'), `idleStampLength`, `lastPos`, `lastDirXZ`.
findings.members: FoliageInteractionController.CauseInteraction(Vector3,Vector3,float), FoliageInteractionController.SetCenter(Transform), FoliageInteractionController.Pending, FoliageInteractionController.trampleResistance, FoliageBendFollow.setCenter, FoliageBendFollow.stampWhenIdle, FoliageBendFollow.idleStampLength
findings.modding: This is the cleanest extension point in the whole area — one call bends grass along a segment, usable for vehicles, ragdolls, rotor wash, or dragged bodies. Just attach a FoliageBendFollow with setCenter=false to any new interactor. Because only one transform sets the center (the local player), remote interactors only register while inside WorldExtent of the local player.

findings.title: Terrain surface type is decided by highest-splat-weight-wins, with no blending
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.TerrainSurface` derives from `Il2Cpp.Surface` (it overrides the same three getters while adding only `_terrain: UnityEngine.Terrain` and `SurfaceProxies: Surface[]`). Resolution is `GetHighestSplatValue(Vector2 texCoord) -> int`, then `GetProxySurface(Vector2 texCoord) -> Surface`, feeding `GetSurfaceInformation`, `GetFootstepSurfaceInformation`, and `GetBulletImpactSurfaceInformation`. So the returned surface is whichever terrain layer has the single highest weight at that UV — a hard pick, no interpolation. The base `Surface` supports three independent surface types on one object: `SurfaceType`, plus `OverrideFootStep` -> `FootStepSurfaceType`/`FootStepSurfaceInfo` and `OverrideBulletImpact` -> `BulletImpactSurfaceType`/`BulletImpactSurfaceInfo`.
findings.members: TerrainSurface.GetHighestSplatValue(Vector2), TerrainSurface.GetProxySurface(Vector2), TerrainSurface.SurfaceProxies, Surface.OverrideFootStep, Surface.OverrideBulletImpact, Surface.BulletImpactSurfaceInfo
findings.modding: `SurfaceProxies` is an array indexed by terrain layer order — adding or reordering terrain layers without extending it yields wrong surfaces or an index-out-of-range. The hard pick means footstep audio snaps at splat boundaries rather than crossfading. The footstep/bullet-impact override split is useful: an object can sound like metal underfoot but spark like concrete when shot.

findings.title: SurfaceInformation carries the ballistics table, so penetration and ricochet are data-driven per material
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.SurfaceInformation` (a ScriptableObject per the established surface system) holds `penetrationResistance`, `speedReduction`, `penetrationDeflection`, `ricochetMultiplier`, `ricochetDeflection` alongside the presentation arrays `BulletImpactEffects`, `BulletImpactDecals`, `BulletImpactSounds`, `FootstepSounds`, `LandingSound`, and three shell-casing arrays selected via `GetShellImpact(ShellAudioType)`. `SFXDistance: Vector2` bounds attenuation. The consumer is `BulletInstance.Richochet(SurfaceInformation surface) -> bool` (misspelled in source) governed by `ricochetChance: int`, `maxRicochets`, `minRicochetAngle`, `penetrationAmount`, `armourPenetration`.
findings.members: SurfaceInformation.penetrationResistance, SurfaceInformation.ricochetDeflection, SurfaceInformation.GetShellImpact(ShellAudioType), SurfaceInformation.GetRandomImpactDecal(), BulletInstance.Richochet(SurfaceInformation), BulletInstance.SpawnImpactNewSystem(SurfaceInformation,RaycastHit,bool), BulletInstance.armourPenetration
findings.modding: Retuning wallbang behaviour is pure ScriptableObject data — no code patch needed. Note the method name `SpawnImpactNewSystem` implies a prior impact system was replaced and dead remnants may linger.

findings.title: A single bullet has a hard cap on how many impacts it may spawn
findings.detail: `BulletInstance` counts impacts as it penetrates: `maxImpactNonPenetration` and `maxImpactPenetration` are the caps, tracked by `currentImpactNonPenetrationCount`, `currentImpactPenetrationCount`, and separately `currentImpactSFXCount`. It also tracks `penetrationPoint: Vector3` / `hasPenetrationPoint: bool` and `impactPoint: Vector3`, and carries `ExplosiveImpact: BulletImpact` for explosive rounds.
findings.members: BulletInstance.maxImpactNonPenetration, BulletInstance.maxImpactPenetration, BulletInstance.currentImpactSFXCount, BulletInstance.penetrationPoint, BulletInstance.hasPenetrationPoint, BulletInstance.ExplosiveImpact
findings.modding: This is a perf guard against a round punching through many thin layers and spawning a decal per layer. A mod raising penetrationAmount without raising these caps will get penetration with no visual or audio feedback past the cap — a confusing failure mode.

findings.title: Trees are BRG-instanced draws, not GameObjects, kept alive by one camera-following proxy per prefab
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.NakedTerrainRenderer` is a two-member class (`Awake`, `terrain: UnityEngine.Terrain`) whose literal states 'Disable Unity's built-in tree and detail rendering (sets drawTreesAndFoliage = false).' Rendering is taken over by BRGInstancedRenderer. To stop the instanced draws being culled, `SpeedTreeProxyManager` (singleton, with `_cam: Camera` and a `LateUpdate`) instantiates one proxy object per tree prefab: `TreeProxyInstances: Dictionary<GameObject, Transform>`, refcounted by `TreeInstanceCounts: Dictionary<GameObject, int>` via `AddTreeProxy`/`RemoveTreeProxy`, with `SetupPrefabProxyMeshes(GameObject)` and `InstantiateTreeProxyObject(GameObject treePrefab, GameObject treeLOD, GameObject proxyObjectParent, Mesh proxyMesh, bool setBounds)`. `InstancedTreeProxyManager` is the non-SpeedTree twin, taking `Material[] proxyMaterials` instead of a LOD object.
findings.members: NakedTerrainRenderer.terrain, SpeedTreeProxyManager.InstantiateTreeProxyObject(GameObject,GameObject,GameObject,Mesh,bool), SpeedTreeProxyManager.TreeInstanceCounts, SpeedTreeProxyManager._cam, SpeedTreeProxyManager.LateUpdate(), InstancedTreeProxyManager.AddTreeProxy(GameObject)
findings.modding: A mod cannot raycast, GetComponent, or Destroy an individual tree — they do not exist as scene objects. Consequence to verify: with drawTreesAndFoliage=false Unity also stops generating terrain tree colliders, so trees may be non-collidable. Probe: raycast at a tree trunk in an operation scene and inspect the hit collider, or check `Terrain.activeTerrain.drawTreesAndFoliage` and `TerrainCollider` state at runtime.

findings.title: BreakerSwitch drives lights through a list, and DynamicLight randomizes which lights are even on
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.BreakerSwitch` holds `effectedLights: List<Il2Cpp.DynamicLight>` and `isNight: bool`, animates via `animator` with clip-name strings `turnOn`/`turnOff` plus `FinishAnimation()` as the animation event, and uses FinalIK for the hand (`interactionSystem: InteractionSystem`, `leftHand: InteractionObject`, `targetPlayerPosition: Transform`). Power state is SyncVar `PowerOn` (`NetworkPowerOn`) with `CMD_Interact(PlayerNetworking)`/`RPC_Interact` and `CMD_SetPowerState(bool)`/`RPC_SetPowerState(bool)`, plus a `buzzSource: AudioSource`. `Il2Cpp.DynamicLight` carries `onChance: float` — individual lights are randomly on or off — and fakes the visual off-state by material swap rather than only killing the Light: `lightMesh: MeshRenderer`, `offMaterial: Material`, `materialIndex: int`, plus a separate `blinds: MeshRenderer[]` with `blind_offMaterial` for window glow.
findings.members: BreakerSwitch.effectedLights, BreakerSwitch.CMD_SetPowerState(bool), BreakerSwitch.PowerOff(), BreakerSwitch.FinishAnimation(), BreakerSwitch.isNight, DynamicLight.onChance, DynamicLight.offMaterial, DynamicLight.blinds, DynamicLight.materialIndex
findings.modding: `onChance` means light layout is not deterministic across clients unless seeded from the server — worth probing whether two clients see the same lights lit. The emissive material swap is separate from the Light component, so toggling a Light directly leaves the bulb mesh glowing.

findings.title: DynamicLight has CMD_TurnOn with no matching RPC_TurnOn — an asymmetry in the power path
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.DynamicLight` exposes `CMD_TurnOff()` paired with `RPC_TurnOff()`, and `TurnOff()`/`TurnOffLocal()`. But `CMD_TurnOn()` has no `RPC_TurnOn` counterpart and there is no `TurnOn()`/`TurnOnLocal()` method at all. The only other replication channel is SyncVar `isOn` (`NetworkisOn`), and `OnStartClient` exists to apply state on join.
findings.members: DynamicLight.CMD_TurnOn(), DynamicLight.CMD_TurnOff(), DynamicLight.RPC_TurnOff(), DynamicLight.TurnOffLocal(), DynamicLight.isOn, DynamicLight.OnStartClient()
findings.modding: Turning power back on relies entirely on the `isOn` SyncVar, while turning off gets both a SyncVar and an explicit RPC. If the material swap and shadow refresh happen in the RPC/TurnOff path rather than a SyncVar hook, restoring power may leave the off-material or a stale shadow. Probe: flip a breaker off then on with two clients connected and compare bulb emissive and cast shadows against a fresh join.

findings.title: Every dynamic light owns a distance-banded on-demand shadow updater — a trap for mods that toggle lights directly
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.DynamicLightSetting` bundles `_light: Light`, `_lightData: HDAdditionalLightData`, and `_onDemandShadowMap: Il2Cpp.OnDemandShadowMapUpdate`. That updater is substantial: it refreshes the full shadow map, cascades, and subshadows on independent schedules (`UpdateShadowMap()`, `UpdateCascades()`, `UpdateSubshadows()`, `UpdateOnCameraMove()`, `ResetCounters()`), with per-band wait tables `fullShadowMapDistanceRefreshWaitFrames: Vector2[]` and `...WaitSeconds: Vector2[]`, per-cascade arrays `cascadesRefreshWaitFrames: int[]` / `cascadesRefreshWaitSeconds: float[]` and matching counter arrays, plus `updateOnPlayerMove: bool`, `playerToTrack: Transform`, `_disToCamera`, and enums `ShadowMapToRefresh` / `CounterMode`.
