findings.members: DynamicLightSetting._onDemandShadowMap, OnDemandShadowMapUpdate.UpdateShadowMap(), OnDemandShadowMapUpdate.UpdateCascades(), OnDemandShadowMapUpdate.fullShadowMapDistanceRefreshWaitFrames, OnDemandShadowMapUpdate.updateOnPlayerMove, OnDemandShadowMapUpdate.playerToTrack
findings.modding: Shadows are deliberately stale at distance. A mod that enables/disables a Light or moves a light without forcing `UpdateShadowMap()` will show a shadow that does not match the light for up to the configured wait. Always route light changes through DynamicLight so the shadow refresh fires.

findings.title: InteractableRangeTarget replicates through a SyncVar hook with no RPC, and its sway is animator-faked
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.InteractableRangeTarget` (the shooting-range popup target) has `CMD_OnInteraction(float value)` and `OnInteraction(float value)` but no RPC — replication is entirely SyncVar `currentValue` (`NetworkcurrentValue`) with hook `OnValueUpdate(float previous, float current)`. Motion is animator blend parameters cached as hashes `_hashBlend` and `_hashSwayBlend`, with sway decay driven by `OnSwayResetCurve: AnimationCurve` and `_swayResetTimer` — no physics. Audio is a three-part start/loop/end rig: `moveStart`, `moveLoop`, `moveEnd` AudioSources gated by `isMoving`. `InteractableRangeTargetHandle` is the separate lever with `Interact()` and `rangeTarget: InteractableRangeTarget`.
findings.members: InteractableRangeTarget.CMD_OnInteraction(float), InteractableRangeTarget.OnValueUpdate(float,float), InteractableRangeTarget.currentValue, InteractableRangeTarget._hashSwayBlend, InteractableRangeTarget.OnSwayResetCurve, InteractableRangeTargetHandle.Interact()
findings.modding: Target reaction to being shot is an animator blend plus a curve, not rigidbody response — so a mod cannot get physically plausible target knockdown without replacing the mechanism. The SyncVar-hook-only pattern means late joiners get correct state for free.

findings.title: InteractableSceneTransition is vote-gated, carrying its own operation parameters
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.InteractableSceneTransition` is the FOB-to-operation door. It holds the launch parameters directly: `sceneName: string`, `infilName: string`, `areaName: string`, `gameMode: GameMode`, `InfilTime: int`. Entry is `EnterScene()` and `SendRequest(string playerName)`, replicated by `CMD_SendRequest(string playerName, int requestAmount)` / `RPC_SendRequest(string playerName, int requestAmount)` against a counter `timesRequested: int`.
findings.members: InteractableSceneTransition.EnterScene(), InteractableSceneTransition.SendRequest(string), InteractableSceneTransition.CMD_SendRequest(string,int), InteractableSceneTransition.timesRequested, InteractableSceneTransition.sceneName, InteractableSceneTransition.infilName, InteractableSceneTransition.gameMode
findings.modding: `timesRequested` plus a broadcast carrying the requesting player's name is a ready-vote mechanism, distinct from the established `OperationsManager.StartOperation` path. Since sceneName and infilName are plain string fields on the component, retargeting an existing transition door to a different scene/infil is a field write, not a code patch.

findings.title: InteractableChair is a full-body IK seat that doubles as the helicopter seating system
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.InteractableChair` disables the player wholesale on sit: `scriptsToDisable: Behaviour[]`, `collidersToDisable: Collider[]`, `rigidBodysToDisable: Rigidbody[]`, plus `RemoveWeapon: bool`. Networking is `inUse` SyncVar (`NetworkinUse`) with `CMD_StartInteraction`/`RPC_ChairStartInteraction`, `CMD_Stand`/`RPC_Stand`, and `CMD_StartStanding`/`RPC_StartStanding`. Look freedom while seated is clamped by `rotationLimit: Vector2` against `rotationTrackingTarget` with per-axis toggles `RotationTracker_X/Y/Z`. Animation uses named clips `SitAnimation`, `StandAnimation`, and a variety pool `SitStyleAnimations: string[]`. Helicopter integration is explicit: `helicopter: HelicopterV3`, `SeatIndex: int`, `SEAT_NAME: string`, `colliderToDisableOnInfil: Collider`, `HeliStartStanding()`. Body placement runs through `fullBodyInteraction: FullBodyInteraction`, which owns `bodyIK`/`handIK`/`feetIK: InteractionObject`, `PrePlacePlayer()`, `Seat_OnSit()`, `Seat_OnStand()`, and `unseatHelicopter()`.
findings.members: InteractableChair.scriptsToDisable, InteractableChair.SitStyleAnimations, InteractableChair.rotationLimit, InteractableChair.helicopter, InteractableChair.SeatIndex, InteractableChair.colliderToDisableOnInfil, FullBodyInteraction.PrePlacePlayer(), FullBodyInteraction.Seat_OnSit()
findings.modding: Helicopter seats are just chairs with a HelicopterV3 reference and a SeatIndex, so adding seats to a custom insertion vehicle reuses this whole path. `Seat_OnSit`/`Seat_OnStand` are animation events — a custom sit clip must fire them or the player never fully commits or releases.

findings.title: Shipped shader registry extracted from globalgamemanagers.assets — ~180 real shader names across 12 families
findings.detail: I string-scanned D:\Games\OPERATOR\OPERATOR_Data\globalgamemanagers.assets (255 MB) and recovered the shipped shader-name table (full dump at (local scratch) ~483 lines, ~180 are real shader names, the rest are binary noise). NOTE: a trailing stray byte appears on some entries — 'HDRP/Water/Water5', 'Ultimate Scope Shaders/Scope5', 'Shader Graphs/MainShader5' are really 'HDRP/Water/Water', 'Ultimate Scope Shaders/Scope', 'Shader Graphs/MainShader'. findings.modding: This is the Shader.Find menu. Because these names live in globalgamemanagers.assets — the file that holds the always-included-shaders list, Resources/, and preloaded assets — they are the strongest Shader.Find candidates in the build, which matters directly for the established AssetBundle trap (bundles load but lose materials; you rebind with Shader.Find). For rebinding imported props use 'HDRP/Lit'; for imported decals 'HDRP/Decal'; for glass 'Shader Graphs/S_Glass'. Do NOT expect Shader Graph shaders to expose HDRP/Lit property names — SG shaders use their own _Property IDs, so a blind Shader.Find swap onto a SG material without warning loses maps.

findings.title: MicroSplat is NOT in this game — the terrain shader stack is InTerra (Ineffabilis Arcanum)
findings.detail: Correction to the established middleware list. 'MicroSplat' returns zero hits in D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\literals.txt, zero in all_types.txt, and there is no MicroSplat assembly and no MicroSplat/* shader in globalgamemanagers.assets. What actually ships is InTerra: assembly Il2CppIneffabilisArcanum.InTerra.Scripts.dll, namespace Il2CppInTerra, types InTerra_Data, InTerra_GlobalData, InTerra_Setting, InTerra_UpdateAndCheck, InTerra_Track, InTerra_TracksCameraSettings, InTerra_MeshTerrainData. InTerra_Data is a static config surface exposing per-pipeline shader-name strings — get_HDRPTerrainShaderName, get_HDRPTerrainTessellationShaderName, get_HDRPObjectShaderName, get_HDRPObjectTessellationShaderName, get_HDRPMeshTerrainShaderName, get_TessellationShaderFolder — plus the terrain->object data bridge: SetTerrainDataToMaterials(Vector3 terrainSize, Vector3 terrainPosition, Vector4 heightmapScale, Texture heightmap, Il2CppReferenceArray<Texture2D> controlMaps, Material terrainMaterial, Il2CppReferenceArray<TerrainLayer> tl, Material objectMaterial), TerrainLaeyrDataToMaterial [sic], SetTerrainFloatsToMaterial/SetTerrainVectorsToMaterial/SetTerrainTextureToMaterial/TerrainKeywordsToMaterial, CheckObjectShader(Material), CheckTerrainShader(Material), CheckPosition(Terrain, Vector2). The point of InTerra is object-into-terrain blending: shader 'InTerra/HDRP/Object into Terrain Integration' reads the terrain's splat/height data so rocks and props dissolve into the ground. It also drives runtime vehicle tracks: TracksUpdate(), CreateTrackRenderTexture(), EnableTracksCamera(bool), SetTracksFading(bool), SetTracksFadingTime(float).
findings.members: Il2CppInTerra.InTerra_Data, InTerra_GlobalData, InTerra_UpdateAndCheck, InTerra_Track, SetTerrainDataToMaterials, CheckObjectShader, EnableTracksCamera, CreateTrackRenderTexture
findings.modding: Any mod that places custom static meshes on terrain and wants them to blend must assign the InTerra object shader and let InTerra_Data.SetTerrainDataToMaterials feed it, not just Shader.Find('HDRP/Lit'). The tracks system (EnableTracksCamera/CreateTrackRenderTexture/SetTracksFadingTime) is a ready-made runtime deformation channel nothing else seems to expose.

findings.title: NVG is a real image-intensifier simulation: three HDRP CustomPasses plus a compute-shader auto-gate, not a green tint
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.NVGAutogateCustomPass : CustomPass. Execute(CustomPassContext ctx) fans out to ExecuteSceneAverage(CustomPassContext) and ExecuteBurnIn(CustomPassContext, Vector2 screenSizeMultiplier). Scene luminance is measured on the GPU: get_sceneAverageCompute() -> ComputeShader with two kernels get_kReduceTiles() -> int and get_kReduceFinal() -> int, writing get_SceneAvgPartials() -> RenderTexture and get_SceneAverageTexture() -> RTHandle, with per-zone results in get_zoneAvgBuffer() -> ComputeBuffer. Tube burn-in is a persistent history: get_BurnInTexture() -> RenderTexture, get_NvgBurnInTextureHandle() -> RTHandle, get_nvgBurnInMaterial() -> Material, get_BurnInSceneColorLOD() -> float, with asymmetric rates get_BurnInColorMoveSpeed()/get_BurnOutColorMoveSpeed(). Gain model: get_AutoGateColorMoveSpeed(), get_AutoGateGainUpSpeed(), get_ManualGainLevel(), get_ManualGainAdjustment(), get_MeterHighlightCeil(), get_zoneBlendWeight(). The 'meter' is per-lens: FillMeterCircles(Camera cam) -> int and ProjectCircle(Matrix4x4 proj, float tanHalfFov, Vector3 camPos, float lensRadius) -> Vector4 fill get_meterCirclesBuffer() -> Il2CppStructArray<Vector4>, feathered by get_meterEdgeFeather()/get_meterDisplayFeather(). Debug toggles ship: get_debugDisableMask() -> bool, get_debugZoneID() -> int, get_ScopeMeterActive() -> bool. Shader IDs are cached: get_colorLodID/moveSpeedID/moveOutSpeedID/manualGainAmountID -> int. Also present: SyncRenderTextureAspect(RenderTexture, Camera), get_customCopyShader() -> Shader, Cleanup(), get_executeInSceneView() -> bool.
findings.members: NVGAutogateCustomPass.Execute, ExecuteSceneAverage, ExecuteBurnIn, FillMeterCircles, ProjectCircle, sceneAverageCompute, kReduceTiles, kReduceFinal, zoneAvgBuffer, BurnInTexture, ManualGainLevel, debugDisableMask, debugZoneID
findings.modding: Every knob a NVG-tuning mod needs is a managed property with a setter (set_ManualGainLevel, set_AutoGateGainUpSpeed, set_BurnInColorMoveSpeed, set_debugDisableMask). Get the instance via the CustomPassVolume on the NVG camera, not FindObjectsOfTypeAll per frame. Because the auto-gate is per-zone and driven by a ComputeShader, a mod that only overrides ManualGainLevel will still get fought by the auto-gate unless AutoGate speeds are also pinned.

findings.title: The gate meter is driven by a static lens registry — NvgLensFollower/NvgScopeFollower — so gating is per physical tube, not per screen
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.NvgLensFollower has an all-static driver: get_AnyActive() -> bool, get_HasActiveLenses() -> bool, get_LensCount() -> int, get_LensRadiusMeters() -> float, get_PhosphorColorValue() -> Color, get_ActiveLensRenderers() -> Il2CppReferenceArray<Renderer>, plus private statics s_helmetCount, s_activeCount, s_driver (-> NvgLensFollower). Per-instance it carries get_NumLenses() -> int, get_LensRadius() -> float, get_LensOffsets() -> Il2CppStructArray<Vector2>, get_PhosphorColor() -> Color, get_LensRenderers() -> Il2CppReferenceArray<Renderer>, get_LensWorldCenters() -> Il2CppStructArray<Vector3>. Lifecycle is LateUpdate/OnEnable/OnDisable -> NotifyPassState() (private static) which is what flips HasActiveLenses. Il2Cpp.NvgScopeFollower subclasses it, overriding get_IsScope() -> bool and keeping its own s_scopeCount. So a 4-tube GPNVG-18 registers 4 lens circles; a clip-on NVG scope registers as a scope-class lens and the autogate meter (FillMeterCircles/ProjectCircle) projects each lens's world circle into screen space independently.
findings.members: NvgLensFollower.AnyActive, HasActiveLenses, LensCount, LensRadiusMeters, PhosphorColorValue, ActiveLensRenderers, LensWorldCenters, NotifyPassState, s_driver, NvgScopeFollower.IsScope, s_scopeCount
findings.modding: NvgLensFollower.AnyActive / LensCount / PhosphorColorValue are public static getters — the cheapest legitimate 'is the local player on NVGs and what colour' probe in the whole game, no FindObjectOfType needed. Adding a custom NVG device means adding a NvgLensFollower with the right NumLenses/LensOffsets/LensRadius; the autogate then picks it up for free.

findings.title: NVGGrainCustomPass renders a lens mask into a buffer before applying grain — grain is masked to the tube, not the frame
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.NVGGrainCustomPass : CustomPass. Setup(ScriptableRenderContext, CommandBuffer) / Execute(CustomPassContext) / Cleanup(). Private RenderLensMask(CustomPassContext ctx) writes get_lensMaskBuffer(), and there is a helper GetSubMeshCount(Renderer) -> int (static) implying it draws the actual lens Renderers submesh-by-submesh into the mask. Two shaders and two materials: get_grainShader()/get_lensMaskShader() -> Shader, get_grainMat()/get_lensMaskMat() -> Material, plus get_grainSource() -> RTHandle. Tunables: grainStrength, grainDensity, grainSpeed, grainEdge, grainOpacity, grainDarkBias (all float). Cached shader IDs s_GrainSource, s_LensMask, s_GrainStrength, s_GrainDensity, s_GrainSpeed, s_GrainEdge, s_GrainOpacity, s_GrainDarkBias. The matching shader names in the build are Hidden/Fullscreen/NVGFullscreenTexture and HDRPSamples/Custom Grain Unlit. Separately, Il2Cpp.NVGGrainController is a per-material animator: get_NightVisionMaterials() -> Il2CppReferenceArray<Material>, GetHaltonSequence(int index, int radix) -> float driving m_SampleIndex/k_SampleCount, writing Grain_Params1, Grain_Params2, GrainTex, Phase, GrainNoiseParameters (cached int IDs), with GrainIntensity, LuminanceContribution, Size floats and an get_isPVS30() -> bool device-variant flag.
findings.members: NVGGrainCustomPass.RenderLensMask, GetSubMeshCount, grainShader, lensMaskShader, lensMaskBuffer, grainDarkBias, NVGGrainController.GetHaltonSequence, NightVisionMaterials, isPVS30, GrainNoiseParameters
findings.modding: grainDarkBias + LuminanceContribution are the two properties that make NVG grain look right in shadows; both are plain float setters. isPVS30 selects a device grain profile — a mod adding a new NVG model can flip it rather than authoring new noise.

findings.title: NVG hardware set and the wear/unwear path: GPNVG18 + nvgController + MainCameraSingleton.SetNVGCamera
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.GPNVG18 is minimal — get_isOn() -> bool, get_nvgColour() -> Color, get_nvgStaticColour() -> Color, with OnEnable/OnDisable/OnDestroy only. The flip-down is Il2Cpp.nvgController: get_leftHand() -> Il2CppRootMotion.FinalIK.InteractionObject, get_interactionSystem() -> FinalIK.InteractionSystem, get_animator() -> Animator, get_EnableNVG()/get_DisableNVG() -> string (animation-state/trigger names), get_NVGLights() -> GameObject, get_playerNetworking() -> PlayerNetworking, get__menuNVGState() -> bool, with StartInteraction()/ResumeInteraction(). Camera side is Il2Cpp.MainCameraSingleton (get_instance): SetNVGCamera(bool state), ToggleNVGCamera(), DisableNVGCamera(), get_NVG() -> GameObject, get_MainCam()/get_GameCamera()/get_DefaultCamSettings() -> Camera, CopyCameraSettings(Camera camToCopy), ResetFPSCameraSettings(), and get_freeCamera() -> Il2Cpp.ScreenshotFreeCamera. The addressables catalog shows the modelled devices: GPNVG-18 in BLK/FDE with (GP) green-phosphor and (WP) white-phosphor variants, each with an optional 'with ECOTI' clip-on thermal overlay, plus 'L3 Harris F-PANO GP NVG', PVS14_nvg and NVG_PVS31 textures. NVG-specific reticle materials exist for optics (EXPS2/EXPS3/hws/acrop2/OKP7 'reticle nvg' .mat).
findings.members: GPNVG18.isOn, nvgColour, nvgStaticColour, nvgController.EnableNVG, DisableNVG, StartInteraction, MainCameraSingleton.SetNVGCamera, ToggleNVGCamera, CopyCameraSettings, ScreenshotFreeCamera
findings.modding: MainCameraSingleton.instance.SetNVGCamera(bool) is the one-call NVG toggle for a mod. nvgController.EnableNVG/DisableNVG are strings, so a mod can retarget the animation without touching the animator. ScreenshotFreeCamera hanging off MainCameraSingleton is a free cinematic-camera entry point.

findings.title: A complete undocumented capsule-shadow system ships: CapsuleShadows custom pass + CapsulesHandler + CharacterShadow
findings.detail: Not in the established middleware list. Il2Cpp.CapsuleShadows : CustomPass — Setup(ScriptableRenderContext, CommandBuffer), Execute(CustomPassContext), SetComputeParams(CustomPassContext), DispatchCharacterLight(CustomPassContext context, int charactersCount), CreateExclusionsBuffer(CustomPassContext), Cleanup(). It owns get_compute() -> ComputeShader with get_kernel()/get_lightKernel() -> int, get_unlit() -> Material, and RTHandles targetHandle/exclusionHandle/exclusionDepth, plus get_maskLayer() -> LayerMask and get_exclusionID() -> int. Tunables: EnableAPVShadows (bool), EnableAmbient (bool), AmbientIntensity, ShadowIntensity, ShadowSharpness, LuminanceBlend, IntensityResponse (floats). The registry is Il2Cpp.CapsulesHandler (get_Instance): AddCharacter/RemoveCharacter(CharacterShadow), AddPointLight/RemovePointLight(CapsuleShadowCaster), AddOccluder/RemoveOccluder(CapsuleShadowOccluder), UpdateLists(), InitializeBuffers(), UpdateBuffers(), DisposeBuffers(), InitializeCharacterShadows(), UpdateCharacterShadows(), UpdatePointLights(), with four ComputeBuffers (capsulesBuffer, charactersBuffer, pointLightsBuffer, occludersBuffer) and lists CharacterShadows, Casters, Occluders, Capsules (List<Il2Cpp.Capsule>), Characters (List<Il2Cpp.CapsuleCharacter>), Renderers, Lights (List<Il2Cpp.PointLightData>), OccluderData (List<Il2Cpp.OccluderBox>). Per-character: Il2Cpp.CharacterShadow — colliderToCapsule(CapsuleCollider) -> Il2Cpp.Capsule, AddCapsule/RemoveCapsule(CapsuleCollider), UpdateCapsulesArray(), RecalculateArrays(), SelfUpdate(), get_Capsules() -> Il2CppStructArray<Il2Cpp.Capsule>, get_thisChar() -> Il2Cpp.CapsuleCharacter, get_radius() -> float. Per-light: Il2Cpp.CapsuleShadowCaster — get_Light() -> Light, sharpness, intensity, shadowRange, capsuleBlend, wallFade (floats). Source paths show two origins: \Assets\_shaders\CapsuleShadows\* and \Assets\ACS\CharacterShadow.cs.
findings.members: CapsuleShadows.DispatchCharacterLight, CreateExclusionsBuffer, EnableAPVShadows, ShadowIntensity, LuminanceBlend, CapsulesHandler.Instance, AddCharacter, AddPointLight, AddOccluder, UpdateBuffers, CharacterShadow.AddCapsule, colliderToCapsule, CapsuleShadowCaster.wallFade
findings.modding: CapsulesHandler.Instance.AddCharacter(CharacterShadow) is how any new character/prop gets contact shadowing without a real shadow map — cheap and the right hook for a custom NPC or a mod-spawned model. AddPointLight(CapsuleShadowCaster) attaches a capsule-shadow-casting light. Note the buffers are fixed-capacity (allocatedLightsCount/allocatedOccludersCount) so a mod spawning many casters may need UpdateLists()/InitializeBuffers() to resize.

findings.title: ScopeDOF is one of the most elaborate custom passes in the game — a masked, weighted, depth-aware blur for scope eye relief
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.ScopeDOF : CustomPass. It overrides AggregateCullingParameters(ref ScriptableCullingParameters cullingParameters, HDCamera hdCamera) — i.e. it forces extra objects into the culling set for its mask pass. Pipeline: GenerateLensMask(CustomPassContext) -> GenerateBlurredColor(CustomPassContext, Vector2 blurCenter) -> CombineMask(CustomPassContext, RTHandle blurredDepth, RTHandle lensMask, RTHandle destination). Blur kernels: RadialBlur(ctx, Material, RTHandle src, RTHandle dst, Vector2 center01, float radiusPx, int samples), WeightedRadialBlur(... RTHandle weightMask, ..., bool invertDepth, float edgeFalloff), WeightedGaussianBlur(ctx, Material, RTHandle source, RTHandle destination, RTHandle tempTarget, RTHandle weightMask, float radius, int sampleCount, bool invertDepth, float edgeFalloff), with GetGaussianWeights(int weightCount) -> ComputeBuffer cached in get_gaussianWeightsCache() -> Dictionary<int, ComputeBuffer>. Seven RTHandles: depth, depthBlurred, downSampleBuffer, blurBuffer, blurBufferHalf, lensMaskBuffer, combinedMaskBuffer, colorCopy. Materials: QuadClipMaterial, BlurredDepthMaterial, BlurMaterial, DofMaterial, whiteRenderersMaterial; shaders compositeShader, whiteRenderersShader; get_shaderTags() -> Il2CppStructArray<ShaderTagId>; get_LensTransform() -> Transform and get_ScreenCenterSmooth() -> Vector2 track the optic. Matching build shaders: Scope DOF/BlurredDepth, Hidden/Custom/ScopeDOFBlur, Hidden/Renderers/QuadClip, Hidden/Renderers/WhiteRenderers.
findings.members: ScopeDOF.AggregateCullingParameters, GenerateLensMask, GenerateBlurredColor, CombineMask, WeightedGaussianBlur, GetGaussianWeights, LensTransform, ScreenCenterSmooth, EffectStrength, DownSample
findings.modding: get_EffectStrength()/set_EffectStrength(float) and set_DownSample(bool) are the two settings a performance mod would expose; referenceResolution scales the blur radius with resolution. AggregateCullingParameters means this pass has real culling cost even when strength is 0 — disabling the CustomPassVolume, not zeroing strength, is the actual perf win.

findings.title: Game post-processing is two HDRP CustomPostProcessVolumeComponents (MilkPostSettings, SuppressionPostFX) — and adding a third at runtime is gated
findings.detail: Both implement the HDRP custom post-process contract: get_injectionPoint() -> UnityEngine.Rendering.HighDefinition.CustomPostProcessInjectionPoint, IsActive() -> bool, Setup(), Render(CommandBuffer cmd, HDCamera camera, RTHandle source, RTHandle destination), Cleanup(). Il2Cpp.MilkPostSettings is the global grade — VolumeParameters intensity/Brightness/Gamma/Hue/Contrast/Saturation (ClampedFloatParameter) plus get_Material() -> MaterialParameter, resolved values IntensityValue/BrightnessValue/GammaValue/HueValue/ContrastValue/SaturationValue and cached IDs IntensityID/BrightnessID/GammaID/HueID/ContrastID/SaturationID; menu path literal 'Post-processing/Custom/MilkPost', shader Hidden/Shader/MilkPost. Il2Cpp.SuppressionPostFX is the being-shot-at effect — AddSuppression(float amount, float multiplier), ProccessSuppressionFrame() [sic], ClampIntensityMultiplier(), IntensityMultiplier/IntensityMultiplierTarget/IntensitySlowdownSpeed floats, and parameters MakeFullySuppressed (BoolParameter), intensity, BlurDistance, NoBlurZoneSize, VignetteIntensity, VignetteSmoothness, VignetteRoundness, ChromStrength (ClampedFloatParameter), VignetteColor (ColorParameter), VignetteCenter (Vector2Parameter), plus get_m_InternalSpectralLut() -> Texture2D and IDs ColorFilter, ChromStrengthID, BlurIntensityID, BlurDistanceID, NoBlurDistanceID, Vignette_Center, Vignette_Settings, Vignette_Color, PreviousFrame. Registration gate: HDRenderPipelineGlobalSettings exposes get_/set_beforeTransparentCustomPostProcesses, beforePostProcessCustomPostProcesses, beforeTAACustomPostProcesses, afterPostProcessBlursCustomPostProcesses, afterPostProcessCustomPostProcesses — all Il2CppSystem.Collections.Generic.List<string> — backed by m_CustomPostProcessOrdersSettings (CustomPostProcessOrdersSettings).
findings.members: MilkPostSettings.Render, injectionPoint, IntensityValue, SuppressionPostFX.AddSuppression, MakeFullySuppressed, ChromStrength, PreviousFrame, HDRenderPipelineGlobalSettings.beforePostProcessCustomPostProcesses
findings.modding: SuppressionPostFX.AddSuppression(float, float) is a directly callable screen-effect trigger. For MilkPostSettings the entire colour grade is settable through the Volume stack — a reshade-style mod needs no shader at all. But a NEW custom post-process type must have its type name appended to one of those List<string> properties AND HDRP builds its ordered pass list when the pipeline is constructed, so appending after boot probably will not take effect until the pipeline is rebuilt.

findings.title: HTraceAO ships all three AO backends including hardware RTAO, and it hijacks HDRP's own SSAO override
findings.detail: Il2CppHTraceAO.Rendering.HTraceAO drives six CustomPassObjects: _prePassObject, _mvPassObject, _gBufferPassObject, _ssaoPassObject, _gtaoPassObject, _rtaoPassObject, _finalPassObject (Il2CppHTraceAO.Rendering.HDRP.Infrastructure.CustomPassObject), selected via get_Profile() -> Il2CppHTraceAO.Rendering.Shared.Data.Profile.HTraceAOProfile and CheckProfile(). The telling members are get__ssaoOverrideComponent() -> UnityEngine.Rendering.HighDefinition.ScreenSpaceAmbientOcclusion, get__volumeComponent() -> UnityEngine.Rendering.Volume, CreateSSAOOverrideComponent(), SetSSAOOverrideComponentSettings(), SetupVolumeHDRP(), UpdateSSAO(), InitComponentsHdrp(), Ping(CustomPassObject) -> bool, ChangeObjectWithSerialization(). Source layout confirms three algorithms — \Assets\HTraceAO\Runtime\Shared\MainPasses\{GTAO,RTAO,SSAO}.cs with HDRP wrappers {GTAO,RTAO,SSAO}PassHDRP.cs plus PrePassHDRP.cs, GBufferPassHDRP.cs, FinalPassHDRP.cs, and settings types GTAOSettings/RTAOSettings/SSAOSettings. Supporting infra: HBlueNoise, HRenderer, HShaderParams, HDynamicBuffer, RTWrapper, IHistoryData, PatcherUtils. Metadata literals 'Thread Compaction', 'Occlusion Tracing', 'Temporal Filtering', 'Spatial Filtering', 'Contact Occlusion Rendering' are its debug pass names. RTAO is real ray tracing: Unity.UnifiedRayTracing.Runtime.dll ships.
findings.members: HTraceAO.CheckProfile, InitComponentsHdrp, UpdateSSAO, CreateSSAOOverrideComponent, SetSSAOOverrideComponentSettings, _rtaoPassObject, _gtaoPassObject, HTraceAOProfile
findings.modding: HTraceAO creates and owns a ScreenSpaceAmbientOcclusion volume override — a mod that sets HDRP's built-in SSAO through the Volume stack will be overwritten by SetSSAOOverrideComponentSettings on the next UpdateSSAO. Change the HTraceAOProfile instead. Whether the RTAO path is reachable on this build needs a runtime probe: read HTraceAO.Profile and log which pass objects Ping() true.

findings.title: The upscaler stack is far wider than 'FSR3' — 15 upscaler backends behind one static facade
findings.detail: Il2CppTND.Upscaling.Framework.UpscalerName enumerates None, FSR1, FSR2, FSR3, FSR4, ASR, DLSS3, DLSS4, XeSS1, XeSS2, SGSR1, SGSR2, Reserved1..3, PSSR. UpscalerQuality: Off, Custom, NativeAA, UltraQuality, Quality, Balanced, Performance, UltraPerformance. The facade Il2CppTND.Upscaling.Framework.TNDUpscaler (in Il2CppTND.Upscaling.Framework.Runtime.HDRP) is fully static-shaped: SetUpscaler(UpscalerName) -> bool, GetSelectedUpscaler() -> UpscalerName, GetActiveUpscaler() -> UpscalerName, SetQuality(UpscalerQuality), GetQuality() -> UpscalerQuality, GetScaling() -> float, SetSharpening(bool), GetSharpening() -> bool, SetSharpness(float), GetSharpness() -> float, SetAutoReactive(bool), GetAutoReactive() -> bool, GetUpscalerSettings(UpscalerName) -> UpscalerSettingsBase (plus a generic overload), ResetCamera(), GetSupported() -> List<UpscalerName>, GetSupported(List<UpscalerName>), IsSupported(UpscalerName) -> bool. Shipped plugin assemblies: TND.Upscaling.FSR3, TND.Upscaling.DLSS4, TND.Upscaling.HDRP.DLSS, TND.Upscaling.XeSS2, plus Framework Core/HDRP/Injectors. Build shaders Hidden/TND/Upscaling/AutoReactive, MergeReactive, Sharpen and Hidden/HDRP/DLSSBiasColorMask. Literal 'DisableUpscalers' exists as a console-command name.
findings.members: TNDUpscaler.SetUpscaler, SetQuality, SetSharpness, SetAutoReactive, GetSupported, IsSupported, ResetCamera, UpscalerName.DLSS4, FSR4, XeSS2, PSSR
findings.modding: TNDUpscaler.GetSupported()/SetUpscaler()/SetQuality() are clean static calls with no il2cpp field-accessor problem — a mod can expose DLSS4/XeSS2 even if the game's own settings UI does not list them. Verify at runtime with GetActiveUpscaler(), which is distinct from GetSelectedUpscaler() precisely because a selection can without warning fail to activate.

findings.title: CameraSettings is the graphics-quality god object, and it is per-camera (scope cameras included)
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.CameraSettings holds a static registry get_AllCameraSettings() -> Il2CppSystem.Collections.Generic.HashSet<Il2Cpp.CameraSettings>. Per instance: get_thisCamera() -> Camera, get_cameraData() -> UnityEngine.Rendering.HighDefinition.HDAdditionalCameraData, get_cinemachineCam() -> Unity.Cinemachine.CinemachineCamera, get_TND_upscaler() -> Il2CppTND.Upscaling.Framework.TNDUpscaler, get_isScopeCamera() -> bool, get_effectFOV()/get_effectFarPlane() -> bool, get__dynResEnabled()/get__dynResActive()/get__nvgon() -> bool. Methods: SetCamSettings(), SetVegetationLodBias(), StartToggleDynamicResolution(), ToggleDynamicResolution() -> IEnumerator, SetUpscalerSettings(), SetDLSSUpscalerSettings(), SetBloom(bool state), UpdatePostAntiAnalising() [sic], UpdateShadowsQuality(), SetMaxLod(). Note Cinemachine is in the camera path — Unity.Cinemachine.dll ships and CinemachineCamera is a direct field here.
findings.members: CameraSettings.AllCameraSettings, SetCamSettings, SetVegetationLodBias, SetMaxLod, UpdateShadowsQuality, SetBloom, ToggleDynamicResolution, isScopeCamera, TND_upscaler, cinemachineCam
findings.modding: Iterate CameraSettings.AllCameraSettings and skip isScopeCamera to avoid breaking optics when forcing quality. All of SetBloom/UpdateShadowsQuality/SetMaxLod/SetVegetationLodBias are plain instance methods — Harmony-patchable, unlike the il2cpp field accessors. This is the correct single place to hook a graphics-preset mod.

findings.title: Vegetation and props render through a custom GPU-driven BatchRendererGroup path with HZB occlusion, not Unity's renderers
findings.detail: Il2CppBRGInstancedRenderer.BRGRenderer is a singleton (get_Instance) sitting on Unity's BatchRendererGroup API — GetBatchID(int protoIndex) -> UnityEngine.Rendering.BatchID, BuildBatchMetadata(int protoIndex) -> NativeArray<UnityEngine.Rendering.MetadataValue>, and NativeArray<BatchDrawCommandIndirect> command stores. Registration: RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab(...), RegisterRenderSignaturesFromPrefab(...), AddInstance(int chunkId, ...), RemoveInstance(int chunkId, int ...), RequestBatchRebuild(BatchRebuildScope scope), IncAddPrototype/IncRemovePrototype(int protoIndex), IncAddPrototypeCommands/IncRemovePrototypeCommands, IncFlush(), IncFullRebuild(), MarkBatchesDirtyForFullRebuild(), FlushDirtyState(). Camera and shadow commands are tracked separately — EmitCameraCommands/EmitShadowCommands(int protoIndex, ...), AllocCameraCommand/AllocShadowCommand(ulong rangeKey, ...), FindOrCreateCameraRange/FindOrCreateShadowRange(ulong key, ...), get_ActiveCameraCommandCount()/get_ActiveShadowCommandCount() -> int. GPU culling is its own: get_cullingShader(), get_uploadShader(), get_OcclusionShader()/get__occlusionShader(), CameraHZBState, CameraCullingContext, useHZB flags. SpeedTree gets special handling: IsSpeedTreeProto(int protoIndex) -> bool, EnsureSpeedTreeBatchIDs(), UpdateSpeedTree(). Supporting types: RenderSignature, PrototypeData, BRGPrototypeGroup, BRGPrototypeExtraData, BRGRegistrationTracker, BRGMeshLodData, ChunkVisibilitySlot, ViewFadeState. A separate Il2CppBRGInstancedRenderer.HDRP assembly ships.
findings.members: BRGRenderer.Instance, RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab, AddInstance, RemoveInstance, RequestBatchRebuild, IncFullRebuild, IsSpeedTreeProto, UpdateSpeedTree, cullingShader, uploadShader, OcclusionShader, useHZB
findings.modding: Objects drawn by BRGRenderer have no GameObject/Renderer, so FindObjectsOfType, raycasts against renderers, and material swaps will all miss them — this is a real trap for any mod that tries to recolour or hide world foliage. To add instanced content the entry point is RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab followed by AddInstance; to force a redraw after mutating state, RequestBatchRebuild or IncFullRebuild.

findings.title: Lighting is amortised by a hand-rolled LOD manager, and two of its neighbours look like leftovers
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.LightOptimizeManager (get_instance) holds get_AllLightOptimizers() -> List<Il2Cpp.LightOptimize>, get_NumToUpdatePerFrame() -> int, get_LastUpdatedIndex() -> int, get_NumLights() -> int, with RegisterOptimizer(LightOptimize)/DeregisterOptimizer(LightOptimize) and an Update() that walks a slice per frame — a round-robin, not an all-lights-every-frame loop. Il2Cpp.LightOptimize carries get_Lightcomponent() -> Light, get_LightData() -> HDAdditionalLightData, get_Player() -> GameObject, get_Distance() -> float, get_updateInterval() -> float, get__Timer() -> float, LOD0_Distance..LOD3_Distance (int), get_disableLight() -> bool, get_LightShadowLevel() -> int, and a single UpdateLight(). Related: Il2Cpp.DirectionalLightResolution.SetShadowResolution() over get_dirlightData() -> HDAdditionalLightData; Il2Cpp.DynamicLightSetting bundles _light/_lightData/_onDemandShadowMap (Il2Cpp.OnDemandShadowMapUpdate). Two suspicious ones: Il2Cpp.RenderShadowAtStart holds a static List<RenderShadowAtStart> ShadowsToRender plus oldRenderDistance/oldLightRange floats but declares NO Start/Awake/Update/OnEnable method at all — only .ctor/.cctor and getters, so nothing in the type itself can ever run its logic. And Il2Cpp.DisableCamCull subscribes RenderPipelineManager_beginCameraRendering(ScriptableRenderContext, Camera) yet exposes fields literally named number1..number6 (float) — placeholder naming that survived to ship.
findings.members: LightOptimizeManager.instance, RegisterOptimizer, NumToUpdatePerFrame, LightOptimize.LOD0_Distance, LightShadowLevel, UpdateLight, RenderShadowAtStart.ShadowsToRender, DisableCamCull.RenderPipelineManager_beginCameraRendering, number1
findings.modding: LightOptimizeManager.instance.NumToUpdatePerFrame is a single int that trades CPU for light-LOD responsiveness. RenderShadowAtStart having zero Unity lifecycle methods means it is either driven entirely from outside or is dead — worth confirming with a runtime probe that counts instances and checks whether ShadowsToRender is ever non-empty.

findings.title: Shader warmup runs at boot behind the splash screen and pre-instantiates real gameplay prefabs
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.ShaderWarmup exposes a public static get_IsComplete() -> bool (backed by _IsComplete_k__BackingField) and runs WarmupRoutine() -> IEnumerator, WarmDecalsAndImpacts() -> IEnumerator, WarmBulletTracer() -> IEnumerator, plus WarmSurface(Il2Cpp.SurfaceInformation info, Vector3 warmPos, List<Il2Cpp.PooledObject> spawnedPooled) -> int. It holds get_shaderVariantCollection() -> UnityEngine.ShaderVariantCollection, get_prefabsToWarm() -> Il2CppReferenceArray<GameObject>, get_bulletPrefab() -> GameObject, and get_applicationSplashScreen() -> Il2Cpp.ApplicationSplashScreen — so the splash is held until warmup finishes. Companions: Il2Cpp.DecalWarmup with WarmupDecals(), WarmupSurface(Il2Cpp.SurfaceInformation info), get_DecalsWarmedup() -> bool, get_CubeDisableTimer() -> float; and Il2Cpp.KillPooledDecals which only has Start() — a one-shot cleanup of the warmup litter.
findings.members: ShaderWarmup.IsComplete, WarmupRoutine, WarmDecalsAndImpacts, WarmSurface, WarmBulletTracer, shaderVariantCollection, prefabsToWarm, applicationSplashScreen, DecalWarmup.WarmupDecals
findings.modding: ShaderWarmup.IsComplete is the correct gate for a mod that wants to touch materials/shaders at startup — running Shader.Find or spawning custom VFX before it goes true risks a hitch or a missing variant. It also means the ShaderVariantCollection is loaded by then, which is why the globalgamemanagers shader names should be Shader.Find-resolvable in-game; confirm with a runtime probe that calls Shader.Find on a sample from each family and logs nulls.

findings.title: Dev-only render commands exist and are gated by a hardcoded Steam64 allowlist
findings.detail: Metadata literals include the console-command names DisableUpscalers, SetFoliageQuality, SetTerrainQuality, ToggleNVGAutogate, SetRealtimeShadows, SetCameraOcclusionCulling, ToggleISR_RenderTexture (QFSW Quantum Console). At least one binds to a real signature I confirmed: Il2Cpp.TerrainQualitySwitch.SetTerrainQuality(int value) and SetAllTerrainQuality(int value) (static-shaped over get_AllTerrains() -> List<TerrainQualitySwitch>). Access is controlled by Il2Cpp.DevConsole: IsDeveloper(ulong steam64) -> bool, IsPlaytester(ulong steam64) -> bool, HasDevAccess(ulong steam64) -> bool, get_IsLocalDeveloper() -> bool, get_LocalHasDevAccess() -> bool, RequireDevAccess() -> bool, ApplyDevCommandFilter(), backed by get_DeveloperIds()/get_PlaytesterIds() -> Il2CppStructArray<ulong> and get__devOnlyCommandNames() -> HashSet<string>, get__filterApplied() -> bool. Note Il2Cpp.DevCommandAttribute is the marker. Il2Cpp.PlayerConsoleCommands only carries KillPlayer/CheckHealth/TakeDamage/ShowRandomizeMovieButton, so the render commands live on the render components themselves.
findings.members: DevConsole.HasDevAccess, RequireDevAccess, IsLocalDeveloper, ApplyDevCommandFilter, _devOnlyCommandNames, DevCommandAttribute, TerrainQualitySwitch.SetTerrainQuality, SetAllTerrainQuality
findings.modding: HasDevAccess/RequireDevAccess/IsLocalDeveloper are methods and property getters, not il2cpp field accessors, so Harmony can patch them to return true and unlock the dev render commands locally. _devOnlyCommandNames is a HashSet<string> that ApplyDevCommandFilter populates — clearing it before the filter applies is the less invasive route. This is client-side only; nothing here implies server authority.

findings.title: Terrain quality is a runtime material/shader swap between tessellated and non-tessellated variants
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.TerrainQualityContainer is the asset holder — get_TesselationShader()/get_NoTesselationShader() -> UnityEngine.Shader and get_TessMat()/get_NoTessMat() -> UnityEngine.Material, populated in Awake(). Il2Cpp.TerrainQualitySwitch is the per-terrain component with a static get_AllTerrains() -> List<TerrainQualitySwitch>, SetAllTerrainQuality(int value), SetTerrainQuality(int value), and its own get_TesselationShader() -> Shader / get_TesselationMaterial() -> Material, with OnLoad/OnEnable/OnDestroy maintaining the list. This matches the two InTerra shader names in the build ('InTerra/HDRP Tessellation/Terrain (Lit with Features) 2023.1 or Heigher' vs the non-tess basemap variants) and InTerra_Data's paired get_HDRPTerrainShaderName / get_HDRPTerrainTessellationShaderName. Separately Il2Cpp.NakedTerrainRenderer holds only get_terrain() -> UnityEngine.Terrain and an Awake().
findings.members: TerrainQualitySwitch.AllTerrains, SetAllTerrainQuality, SetTerrainQuality, TerrainQualityContainer.TesselationShader, NoTesselationShader, TessMat, NoTessMat, NakedTerrainRenderer.terrain
findings.modding: TerrainQualitySwitch.SetAllTerrainQuality(int) is a one-call global terrain-tessellation toggle, and the exact int->quality mapping is the one thing a static read cannot give you — probe it at runtime by calling it with 0/1/2 and reading the resulting Terrain.materialTemplate.shader.name.

findings.title: VectorTimeOfDay's rendering rig: four reflection-probe sets, two LocalVolumetricFog volumes, and a networked day/night flag that lives elsewhere
findings.detail: Beyond the already-established weather bugs, the lighting rig itself is: get_SunLight()/get_MoonLight() -> UnityEngine.Light with get_SunData()/get_MoonData() -> HDAdditionalLightData, get_Orbit() -> GameObject, get_isStaticLighting() -> bool, get_timeOfDay()/get_orbitSpeed()/get_axisOffset() -> float, SetTimeOfDay(float time), ProgressTime(bool editor), UpdateSkyboxSettings(). Reflections are baked-set swapping, not realtime by default: get_useReflectionProbes() -> bool, get_useReflectionProbesRealtime() -> bool, get_sunRiseProbes()/get_sunSetProbes()/get_DayProbes()/get_NightProbes() -> GameObject, get_reflectionProbeParent() -> Transform, get_reflectionProbes() -> List<UnityEngine.ReflectionProbe>. Weather uses two HDRP LocalVolumetricFog instances — get_rainLocalFog() and get_sandVolumetricFog() — plus get_rainFogVolume() -> UnityEngine.Rendering.Volume. Debug entry points ship: DEBUG_SetSunIntensity(float), DEBUG_SetMoonIntensity(float), DEBUG_Skybox_Disable(), DEBUG_Reflections_Disable(). Note a SECOND, independent day/night authority exists: Il2Cpp.SunSettings is a Mirror NetworkBehaviour with CMD_Switch(), get_NetworkisNight() -> bool, SerializeSyncVars/DeserializeSyncVars, get_sunIntensityNight()/get_sunIntensityDay() -> float, get_sun() -> Light and get_PlaceHolderSun() -> GameObject — and it is SunSettings, not VectorTimeOfDay, that carries the syncvar. Il2Cpp.LinkDirectionalToCustomNightSky pushes the sun direction into a night-sky material: get_SkyMat() -> Material, get_Dir() -> Vector3, get_mainLight() -> Light, previousIntensity/previousColor.
findings.members: VectorTimeOfDay.SetTimeOfDay, ProgressTime, UpdateSkyboxSettings, DEBUG_SetSunIntensity, DayProbes, NightProbes, rainLocalFog, sandVolumetricFog, SunSettings.CMD_Switch, NetworkisNight, LinkDirectionalToCustomNightSky.SkyMat
findings.modding: Two independent day/night systems is a real hazard — a mod that only drives VectorTimeOfDay.SetTimeOfDay will desync from SunSettings.NetworkisNight (and vice versa) since only SunSettings replicates. The DEBUG_* methods are ordinary public methods and are the cheapest lighting-override hooks in the game. Probe at runtime which of the two is actually present in a given operation scene.

findings.title: Dead or vestigial rendering middleware shipping in the build
findings.detail: (a) AmplifyImpostors: Il2CppAmplifyImpostors.Runtime.dll ships and \Assets\AmplifyImpostors\Plugins\Scripts\{AmplifyImpostor,Preferences,VersionInfo,Triangulator}.cs appear in script_paths, but NO shader named AmplifyImpostors/* exists in the build, and every game-side impostor type — Il2Cpp.HDRPHemiOctahedralImpostor, Il2Cpp.FoliageHemiOctahedralImpostor, Il2Cpp.SpeedTreeHemiOctahedralImpostor — resolves to Il2CppProjectDawn.Impostor.Impostor / Il2CppProjectDawn.Impostor.CapturePoints, matching the shipped 'Shader Graphs/Lit Hemi Octahedral Impostor' family. Two impostor packages, one in use. (b) Unity.Postprocessing.Runtime.dll (PPv2) ships and its shaders are in the build (Hidden/PostProcessing/Debug/Waveform, Hidden/PostProcessing/Debug/Vectorscope, Hidden/PostProcessing/SubpixelMorphologicalAntialiasing) but all actual post-processing is HDRP VolumeComponents. (c) Michsky.UI.Dark.QualityManager and Michsky.UI.Shift.QualityManager literals — UI-pack demo quality managers. (d) Il2CppInTerra.InTerra_HDRPTerrainShaderSelection is compiled into Assembly-CSharp (not the InTerra assembly) and its source path is \Assets\InTerra\HDRP\Demo Scene\Terrain\... — an InTerra demo-scene script that leaked into the game assembly; it has only Update() and no members. (e) Il2Cpp.RenderingLayerMask_Test — OnEnable() and get_rlm() -> uint, a test scaffold. (f) TheVisualEngine (Boxophobic) already known-unused; also present are Ultimate Scope Shaders/Demo/TestGrid and several HDRPSamples/* shaders (ObjectEdgeDetection, ObjectHighlightFullscreen, HighlightDrawToCustomColor, NightSky_ToCubemap).
findings.members: Il2CppAmplifyImpostors.Runtime, Il2CppProjectDawn.Impostor.Impostor, HDRPHemiOctahedralImpostor, FoliageHemiOctahedralImpostor, Unity.Postprocessing.Runtime, InTerra_HDRPTerrainShaderSelection, RenderingLayerMask_Test
findings.modding: DEV-CONFIRMED: the OPERATOR developers confirm this middleware is not used. Edgegap in particular is never touched and is present only because Mirror bundles it. Do not build against AmplifyImpostors or PPv2 — patching them will have no visible effect. The HDRPSamples/* fullscreen shaders (ObjectHighlightFullscreen, ObjectEdgeDetection, HighlightDrawToCustomColor) ARE in the build and are ready-made outline/highlight effects a mod could mount on a CustomPassVolume without authoring a shader. Confirm the Amplify-is-dead call at runtime by counting AmplifyImpostor component instances in a loaded operation scene.

findings.title: Misc render components worth knowing: CameraDepthBake, NonDualRender, SpotLightFakeGI, GroupDistanceCuller
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.CameraDepthBake : CustomPass — Execute(CustomPassContext ctx), get_executeInSceneView() -> bool, get_bakingCamera() -> Camera, and three targets get_depthTexture()/get_normalTexture()/get_tangentTexture() -> RenderTexture with a get_render() -> bool latch: an offline G-buffer bake pass. Il2Cpp.NonDualRender fades the non-dominant-eye scope render — get_renderers() -> Il2CppReferenceArray<MeshRenderer>, get_localADS() -> bool, get_weaponV3() -> Il2Cpp.WeaponV3, targetAlpha/alpha/targetSpeed floats, get_isCamera() -> bool, get_mainCamera() -> Camera — matching build shader 'Shader Graphs/_NonDualRender RealisticScopeEffect'. Il2Cpp.SpotLightFakeGI fakes bounce with raycast-placed lights: get_RaycastMask() -> LayerMask, get_MyLights() -> Il2CppReferenceArray<Il2Cpp.FakeGILight>, Strength/ConeAngle/LightDistance/Pushoff floats, OnEnable/Update. Il2Cpp.GroupDistanceCuller is a naive per-Update distance cull — get_ParentObjectToDisable() -> GameObject, get_DistanceToCull() -> float, get_culled() -> bool — with an Update() on every instance (no manager amortisation, unlike LightOptimizeManager). Il2Cpp.GlobalFlashLightMultiplier.UpdateFlashLightMultiplier() over get_MultiplierValue() -> float is the single global weapon-light scalar. Decals: Il2Cpp.PooledImpactDecal with static get_placed() -> HashSet<PooledImpactDecal>, RemoveAllDecals(), MaxNumDecalsChanged(), get_unparentOnInitialize() -> bool; Il2Cpp.BloodDecalCycle with get_material() -> UnityEngine.Rendering.HighDefinition.DecalProjector and get_allBloodSprays() -> Il2CppReferenceArray<Texture2D>.
findings.members: CameraDepthBake.bakingCamera, depthTexture, normalTexture, tangentTexture, NonDualRender.localADS, targetAlpha, SpotLightFakeGI.MyLights, FakeGILight, GroupDistanceCuller.DistanceToCull, GlobalFlashLightMultiplier.MultiplierValue, PooledImpactDecal.placed, RemoveAllDecals
findings.modding: PooledImpactDecal.placed (static HashSet) + RemoveAllDecals() is a ready-made bullet-hole cleanup for a performance mod. GlobalFlashLightMultiplier.MultiplierValue is a one-float global for weapon-light brightness. GroupDistanceCuller running Update() per instance with no manager is the obvious cheap perf win if a map has many of them — count instances at runtime before deciding it matters.

findings.title: Occlusion is a batched RaycastCommand job, one ray per source, time-sliced across frames
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.AudioOcclusionJobManager (singleton `Instance`, static `OnLoad`) owns `List<OccludeSource> sources` + `HashSet<OccludeSource> sourceSet`, `NativeArray<RaycastCommand> commands`, `NativeArray<RaycastHit> results`, `Il2CppStructArray<Vector3> cachedPositions`, `JobHandle jobHandle`. Flow proven by method set: Update() -> schedule, LateUpdate() -> CompleteJob() -> ApplyResults() -> SmoothSources(). Registration is explicit: RegisterSource(OccludeSource) / UnregisterSource(OccludeSource), called from OccludeSource.OnEnable/OnDisable. Tuning fields: occlusionMask (LayerMask), updateInterval, framesToSpread + currentSlice + sliceStart + sliceCount (round-robin batching), skinWidth, occludedCutoff/clearCutoff, occludedVolume/clearVolume, lowPassSmoothingSpeed/volumeSmoothingSpeed, CutoffSnapEpsilon/VolumeSnapEpsilon, listenerPos. Per-source state on Il2Cpp.OccludeSource: CurrentCutoff/TargetCutoff, CurrentVolume/TargetVolume, initVolume, wasPlaying, filter (AudioLowPassFilter), source (AudioSource), plus toggles influenceVolume, influenceLowpass, clampLowpass+lowpassMinimum, clampVolume+volumeMinimum, isAmbience, isInteriorAmbience, bounceAudio. One RaycastCommand per source means occlusion is BINARY per source — there is no partial/multi-ray obstruction, no portal or diffraction model; smoothing is what hides the pop.
findings.members: AudioOcclusionJobManager.RegisterSource, UnregisterSource, CompleteJob, ApplyResults, SmoothSources, occlusionMask, framesToSpread, occludedCutoff, clearCutoff, occludedVolume, clearVolume, skinWidth; OccludeSource.ApplyCutoff, GetStuff, filter, influenceLowpass, bounceAudio
findings.modding: Cleanest lever in the whole audio stack. Add AudioOcclusion to a modded AudioSource by attaching an OccludeSource (needs an AudioLowPassFilter on the same GO) — OnEnable self-registers. Globally retune occlusion by writing AudioOcclusionJobManager.Instance's float fields; they are plain properties on the il2cpp object so an interop setter works. `bounceAudio` is declared but its effect is unprovable statically.

findings.title: Three independent, coexisting occlusion implementations ship in the build
findings.detail: (1) Il2Cpp.AudioOcclusion — legacy V1 from Assets\Scripts\AudioOcclusion.cs. (2) Il2Cpp.OccludeSource + AudioOcclusionJobManager — V2 from Assets\Scripts\AudioOcclusionV2\. (3) Il2CppAxelF.Occlusion — Unity's Book of the Dead framework, with its own LateUpdate(), Test(float dt), GetTarget()/GetCurrent(), separate `_lowPassFilter` AND `_highPassFilter`, and a ScriptableObject singleton Il2CppAxelF.OcclusionSettings{layerMask, highPassRange, lowPassRange, speedOfSound}. AxelF's is the most sophisticated (high+low pass, speed-of-sound delay) and is entirely disconnected from the game's own two.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.AudioOcclusion, Il2Cpp.OccludeSource, Il2CppAxelF.Occlusion, Il2CppAxelF.OcclusionSettings.speedOfSound
findings.modding: Do not assume one occlusion path. A mod that retunes AudioOcclusionJobManager will not touch AxelF emitters or anything still on V1. Runtime probe: FindObjectsOfType counts of OccludeSource vs AudioOcclusion vs AxelF.Occlusion in a loaded operation scene.

findings.title: Il2Cpp.AudioOcclusion (V1) is a pure data blob driven externally by GameManager — nothing to hook
findings.detail: AudioOcclusion's complete non-ctor method list is exactly one entry: `Start()`. Everything else is fields exposed as properties (readOnly, raycastMask, audioSource, isAmbient, ambientCullWithoutInteriorCollider, AffectVolume, AffectVolumeAI, volume, TargetVolume, somethingAbove, networkIdentity, fpsController, brainAI, weapon, audioMixer, originalAudioMixer, raycastTransform, bulletShell, rb, mainCamera, gunshot, isOwned). The driver is Il2Cpp.GameManager, which holds `List<Il2Cpp.AudioOcclusion> audioOccluders`, `List<Il2Cpp.WeaponSFX> weaponSFX`, plus a round-robin cursor pair `weapSFX_numOccluders` / `_lastUpdatedWeapSfxOccluder` and an `occlusionMixer` AudioMixerGroup. So GameManager amortises weapon-SFX occlusion updates across frames by mutating AudioOcclusion's fields directly.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.AudioOcclusion.Start (only method); GameManager.audioOccluders, GameManager.weaponSFX, GameManager.weapSFX_numOccluders, GameManager._lastUpdatedWeapSfxOccluder, GameManager.occlusionMixer
findings.modding: Blocks the obvious approach: Harmony cannot patch il2cpp field accessors, and AudioOcclusion has no method to patch. The only interception point for V1 occlusion is GameManager's per-frame method (name not visible in the signature dump — locate by hooking GameManager.Update/LateUpdate). Mutating an AudioOcclusion instance's fields directly from a mod works but will be overwritten on the next round-robin tick.

findings.title: Weapon audio has two full generations in the build; WeaponSFX is the live one
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.WeaponSFX (current): five WeaponSfxAudioSource slots — ShotClose, ShotFar, Suppressed, SuppressedFar, Interior — plus loop clips LoopClose/LoopFar/LoopSuppressed/LoopSuppressedFar/LoopCloseTail/LoopSuppressedTail and one-shot lists OneShot/DistOneShot/InteriorTail/SuppOneShot/SuppDistOneShot. API: Fire(), FireSuppressed(), FireOneShot(), FireOneShotSuppressed(), Fire_StartLoop()/Fire_StopLoop(bool), FireSuppressed_StartLoop()/_StopLoop(bool), StartLoop()/StopLoop()/StartLoopSuppressed()/StopLoopSuppressed(). State: DistanceToCamera, inInterior, inInteriorOpen, somethingAbove, interiorTailCutoff, _hasSuppressedFar. Fire paths are cached as Il2CppSystem.Action delegates (_fireOneShotAction, _startLoopAction, ...) to avoid per-shot allocation. Il2Cpp.WeaponSFXCompoment (legacy, note the typo) reimplements the same thing with as_Loop/as_DistLoop/as_SuppLoop AudioSources, acs_* clip lists, vol_* per-bus floats, its own CreateAudioSources()/Setup(), pitch pair unsuppressedPitch/suppressedPitch, shellPrefab/spawnShellRate, and a raycastTransform + `_hitUp` RaycastHit used to compute `somethingAbove` (roof over head => interior tail). Il2Cpp.WeaponAudio is the per-weapon container: weaponSFX plus weaponSFX_Short/_Medium/_Long (three distance variants), Fire_Empty, Trigger + triggerPulled/triggerReleased, LightAudioSource + LaserToggle[]/LightToggle[].
findings.members: WeaponSFX.Fire, FireSuppressed, Fire_StartLoop, ShotClose, ShotFar, Suppressed, SuppressedFar, Interior, InteriorTail, interiorTailCutoff; WeaponSfxAudioSource{audioSource, audioSourceReverbFilter, originalAudioMixer}; WeaponSFXCompoment.CreateAudioSources, acs_OneShot, vol_Loop, _hitUp; WeaponAudio.weaponSFX_Short/_Medium/_Long
findings.modding: Replacing a weapon's sound = swapping AudioClip properties on the WeaponSFX component of the weapon prefab in LoadoutManager.singleton.Game_Weapons BEFORE it is instantiated (per-prefab, so no network index concern). Every clip is a direct property, no name lookup, no clip registry. Which of the two generations a given weapon prefab actually carries is per-prefab — probe with GetComponentInChildren<WeaponSFX>() vs <WeaponSFXCompoment>() on each entry of Game_Weapons.

findings.title: Suppressed / indoor / outdoor tails are separate audio sources chosen by two booleans and a raycast, not by a reverb system
findings.detail: WeaponSFX carries inInterior and inInteriorOpen as distinct flags plus somethingAbove. WeaponSFXCompoment computes somethingAbove itself with an upward raycast (raycastTransform, raycastMask, `_hitUp`). The Interior slot plus the InteriorTail clip list and interiorTailCutoff give the indoor tail; ShotFar/SuppressedFar give the distance layer. There is no AudioReverbZone anywhere in the game assembly — the only reverb components are AudioReverbFilter instances on AudioCustomCurves.reverbFilter, WeaponSfxAudioSource.audioSourceReverbFilter, and MainCameraSingleton.underwaterFilter. So 'indoor sound' is entirely a clip-swap + filter-parameter decision, not spatial reverb.
findings.members: WeaponSFX.inInterior, inInteriorOpen, somethingAbove, Interior, InteriorTail, interiorTailCutoff; Il2Cpp.InteriorCollider; AudioCustomCurves.PlayInteriorSFX(AudioClip, bool _muteTail, float fadeDuration), PlayInteriorTailOnly(AudioClip)
findings.modding: To add convincing indoor variants you populate InteriorTail and set interiorTailCutoff; you do not need a reverb zone. Il2Cpp.InteriorCollider is an EMPTY marker component (only ctors, no methods, no fields) — it exists purely as a layer/tag for trigger and raycast tests, so a mod can drop one on any collider to make a space count as interior.

findings.title: SoundFunctionLibrary is the central one-shot spawner and pooling layer
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.SoundFunctionLibrary (singleton `Instance`) holds seven AudioSource PREFABS keyed by the nested enum SoundFunctionLibrary/AudioSourceType {audioSourceMain, audioSourceShort, audioSourceVeryShort, audioSourceDistant, audioSourceTail, audioSourceSuppressed, audioSourceAmmunitionCasings}, plus `Dictionary<AudioSourceType, Queue<AudioCustomCurves>> oneShotPool`. Core API: PlayClipAtLocation(Transform parentFolder, AudioClip audioClip, AudioSourceType audioSourceType, Vector3 pos, float cutoffTime, bool Occluded, float distance, bool inInterior, bool inOpenInterior, AudioClip interiorTailAudioClip, float gunshotCutoffDelay, float volume, float pitch); GetPooled(GameObject prefab, AudioSourceType) -> AudioCustomCurves; ReturnPooled(AudioCustomCurves, AudioSourceType); CreateAudioSource(Transform parentFolder, AudioClip clip, AudioSourceType, bool isLooped) -> AudioSource; GetAudioSourcePrefab(AudioSourceType) -> GameObject.
findings.members: SoundFunctionLibrary.Instance, PlayClipAtLocation, GetPooled, ReturnPooled, CreateAudioSource, GetAudioSourcePrefab, oneShotPool, SoundFunctionLibrary/AudioSourceType
findings.modding: THE clean way for a mod to play a positional sound: SoundFunctionLibrary.Instance.PlayClipAtLocation(...). It inherits the game's pooling, mixer routing, occlusion flag, interior tail and cutoff behaviour for free. For a persistent looping source use CreateAudioSource(parent, clip, type, true) so you get the game's prefab (correct mixer group + rolloff curve) instead of a bare AudioSource.

findings.title: AudioCustomCurves is the pooled voice object: a source + tail source + 3 filters + a hand-rolled fade state machine
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.AudioCustomCurves holds source, sourceTail, highPass (AudioHighPassFilter), lowPass (AudioLowPassFilter), reverbFilter, HighpassLevelCustomCurve (AnimationCurve), defaultSourceMixer/defaultTailMixer (AudioMixerGroup), defaultSourceVolume/defaultTailVolume, poolType, returnTimer/waitingToReturn. Two independent fade machines: a main-source fade (mainSourceFading, mainFadeInitialized, mainFadeTarget, mainFadeDuration, mainFadePerSec) and a loop fade driven by the nested enum AudioCustomCurves/LoopFadeState {None, FadingIn, WaitingToFadeOut, FadingOut} with loopFadeTarget/loopFadeStartVolume/loopFadeDuration/loopFadeDelayTimer/loopFadePairedDistant/loopFadeOwner. API: FadeInLoop(float playDelay, bool occluded, AudioMixerGroup originalMixer, float distance, WeaponSFXCompoment owner, float targetVolume, float fadeTime), FadeOutLoop(AudioSource pairedDistant, bool occluded, AudioMixerGroup originalMixer, float distance, float playDelay, WeaponSFXCompoment owner, float startVolume, float fadeTime), CancelLoopFade(), ReturnToPoolAfter(float delay, AudioSourceType), PlayInteriorSFX, PlayInteriorTailOnly. Constants FADE_OUT_SPEED / FADE_OUT_THRESHOLD are instance fields, not consts.
findings.members: AudioCustomCurves.FadeInLoop, FadeOutLoop, CancelLoopFade, ReturnToPoolAfter, loopFadeState, LoopFadeState, HighpassLevelCustomCurve, defaultSourceMixer, defaultTailMixer
findings.modding: The pooled loop API is typed to `Il2Cpp.WeaponSFXCompoment owner` — the LEGACY weapon system. A mod cannot reuse FadeInLoop/FadeOutLoop for its own looping sound without supplying a WeaponSFXCompoment instance. Use GetPooled + drive source/sourceTail manually, or CreateAudioSource, instead.

findings.title: Third-party gunshots are a separate pooled 3-layer object that doubles as the AI hearing stimulus
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.Gunshot is a static-pooled component: `Queue<Gunshot> pool`, static Get(GameObject gunshotPrefab, Vector3 position, Quaternion rotation) -> Gunshot, static Return(Gunshot), Initialize(), Start(), FixedUpdate(), static OnLoad(). It carries THREE AudioSources — CloseGunshot, MidGunshot, FarGunshot — selected by distance bands FlatDistance / MediumDistance / FarDistance / MaxDistance against `playerDistance`, with per-layer length caches _closeLen/_midLen/_farLen and presence flags _hasClose/_hasMid/_hasFar, plus Volume, Pitch, TimeCutoff, debugMode. It also holds a SphereCollider, `Shooter` (Transform), `ShooterBrain` (BrainAI) and `ShooterTeam` (TeamID) — i.e. the same object that plays the report is the trigger volume that notifies AI of the shot. Il2Cpp.AudioOcclusion has a `gunshot` field, so gunshot objects run through V1 occlusion. GameManager exposes SetGunshotAudioVolume(float), GunshotAudioGroup (AudioMixerGroup) and defaultGunshotVolumeLevel.
findings.members: Gunshot.Get, Gunshot.Return, CloseGunshot, MidGunshot, FarGunshot, FlatDistance, MediumDistance, FarDistance, MaxDistance, sphereCollider, ShooterBrain, ShooterTeam, TimeCutoff; GameManager.SetGunshotAudioVolume, GunshotAudioGroup
findings.modding: Coupling audio and AI perception in one pooled object means a mod that suppresses or replaces distant gunshot audio by disabling the Gunshot prefab will ALSO silence AI reaction to gunfire. Change the AudioSources' clips instead of the object's active state. Hearing radius and audio falloff are the same authored numbers.

findings.title: Surfaces drive footsteps, impacts and casings through a ScriptableObject table — the single best global sound-replacement point
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.SurfaceManager (singleton `instance`, static OnLoad) holds `SurfaceInformation[] DefaultSurfaceTypes` indexed by the nested enum SurfaceManager/SurfaceTypeEnum {Custom, Default, Wood, Concrete, Grass, Sand, Gravel, Carpet, Metal, Brick, Dirt, Flesh, Glass, Water, Mud} (15 values) plus a dedicated FleshSurfaceInfo. Il2Cpp.SurfaceInformation is the SO holding BulletImpactEffects[], BulletImpactDecals[], BulletImpactSounds[], FootstepSounds[], LandingSound[], PistolCasingImpact[], RifleCasingImpact[], ShotgunCasingImpact[], SFXDistance (Vector2), plus ballistics (penetrationResistance, speedReduction, penetrationDeflection, ricochetMultiplier, ricochetDeflection). Accessors: GetRandomImpactSound(), GetRandomFootstepClip(), GetRandomLandingClip(), GetRandomPistolCasingImpactClip(), GetRandomRifleCasingImpactClip(), GetRandomShotgunCasingImpactClip(), GetShellImpact(BulletShell/ShellAudioType {Pistol, Rifle, Shotgun}). Il2Cpp.Surface is the per-renderer component with three independent overrides: SurfaceType/SurfaceInfo, OverrideFootStep + FootStepSurfaceType/FootStepSurfaceInfo, OverrideBulletImpact + BulletImpactSurfaceType/BulletImpactSurfaceInfo, resolved per-UV via GetSurfaceInformation(Vector2 texCoord) / GetFootstepSurfaceInformation / GetBulletImpactSurfaceInformation.
findings.members: SurfaceManager.instance, DefaultSurfaceTypes, FleshSurfaceInfo, SurfaceTypeEnum; SurfaceInformation.FootstepSounds, BulletImpactSounds, LandingSound, GetShellImpact; Surface.GetFootstepSurfaceInformation
findings.modding: Overwrite the clip arrays on SurfaceManager.instance.DefaultSurfaceTypes[i] and every footstep, landing, bullet-impact and casing sound in the game changes at once, for players and AI, on any map. These are ScriptableObject assets shared by reference, so the mutation is process-wide — cache the originals and restore on unload, and note the change is purely local (nothing about surface audio is networked).

findings.title: Footsteps: timer-driven on the player, replicated as a bare volume float; AI has a parallel path
findings.detail: Player: MasterController owns footstepTimer, footstepCount, characterAudio, breathingAudioSource, sprintBreathingClips[], outOfBreathClips[], UpdateSprintBreathingSFX(). It calls into PlayerNetworking, which owns footstepAudio (AudioSource), footstepClips (List<AudioClip>), FootStepInfo (SurfaceInformation), footstepDetectionMask, lastFootstepMaterial (string), and GetFootstepMaterial(). Network: CMD_SEND_FOOTSTEP_SFX(float volume) -> RPC_SEND_FOOTSTEP_SFX(float volume), receive side UserCode_RPC_SEND_FOOTSTEP_SFX__Single(float). ONLY a volume float crosses the wire — surface type and clip choice are resolved locally on each client from its own raycast/lastFootstepMaterial. AI: Il2Cpp.FootstepAudioController mirrors it with Start(), CallUpdate(), GetFootstepMaterial(), SEND_FOOTSTEP_SFX(float volume), footstepTimer, footstepAudio, FootStepInfo, WaterSurfaceInfo (a second SurfaceInformation the player path lacks), footstepDetectionMask, lastFootstepMaterial, brainAI, characterAudio. Il2Cpp.CharacterAudio is a data-only component (no methods at all): baseAudioSourceVolume, baseFoleyVolume, multiplierudioSourceVolume [sic], w_footStepTimer, j_footStepTimer, FootstepMaterialMask.
findings.members: PlayerNetworking.CMD_SEND_FOOTSTEP_SFX(float), RPC_SEND_FOOTSTEP_SFX(float), UserCode_RPC_SEND_FOOTSTEP_SFX__Single, GetFootstepMaterial, lastFootstepMaterial; FootstepAudioController.SEND_FOOTSTEP_SFX(float), CallUpdate, WaterSurfaceInfo; CharacterAudio.baseFoleyVolume
findings.modding: Hook UserCode_RPC_SEND_FOOTSTEP_SFX__Single to intercept remote footsteps and FootstepAudioController.SEND_FOOTSTEP_SFX for AI — both are real methods, patchable. Because only volume is replicated, a client-side mod can change footstep clips per-surface with zero desync risk. CharacterAudio has no methods, so its volumes can only be changed by writing fields (no Harmony hook possible).

findings.title: Foley exists but is misspelled and lives on PlayerNetworking; there is no FoleySource type
findings.detail: No type named FoleySource (or containing 'Foley' in any casing) exists in all_types.txt, script_paths.txt or the metadata literals. The real foley surface is on Il2Cpp.PlayerNetworking: weaponStanceFoley (AudioSource), weaponStanceFoleyClipsUp[], weaponStanceFoleyClipsDown[], weaponStanceFoleyClipsAll[], replicated by CMD_Play_Folely_F_All(bool footstep) -> RPC_Play_Folely_F_All(bool footstep) — 'Folely' is a typo in the shipped method name, and it is the wire name Mirror registered. Volume scaling comes from CharacterAudio.baseFoleyVolume.
findings.members: PlayerNetworking.CMD_Play_Folely_F_All(bool), RPC_Play_Folely_F_All(bool), UserCode_RPC_Play_Folely_F_All__Boolean, weaponStanceFoley, weaponStanceFoleyClipsUp/Down/All
findings.modding: Hook UserCode_RPC_Play_Folely_F_All__Boolean — spell it with the typo or the patch will without warning never bind.

findings.title: Voice chat is MetaVoiceChat over Mirror, not Dissonance — and two dead voice implementations remain in the build
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.PlayerVoice.VoiceChatComponent is typed `Il2CppMetaVoiceChat.MetaVc`. MetaVc: StartClient(INetProvider, bool isLocalPlayer, int maxDataBytesPerPacket), SendFrame(int index, float[] samples), ReceiveFrame(int index, double timestamp, float additionalLatency, ReadOnlySpan<byte> data), StopClient(), SetIsSpeaking(bool), with audioInput (VcAudioInput), audioOutput (VcAudioOutput), encoder (Opus.VcEncoder), decoder (Opus.VcDecoder), jitter (VcJitter), and reactive props isDeafened/isInputMuted/isOutputMuted/isSpeaking. Codec config is Il2CppMetaVoiceChat.VcConfig exposing Il2CppConcentus.Enums types (OpusBandwidth/MaxBandwidth, OpusMode, OpusApplication, OpusFramesize, OpusSignal, complexity) plus SamplesPerSecond, framePeriodMs, samplesPerFrame, jitterTimeWindow, outputMinBufferSize. Transport is Metater's MirrorNetProvider. Il2CppDissonanceVoip.dll is present with a full pipeline but nothing in the game assembly references it. Two further orphans: Il2Cpp.VoiceChat (Cmd_SendData(byte[], uint) / Target_PlaySound(byte[], uint), one AudioSource) and Il2Cpp.SteamworksVoiceChat (full Steam voice API path: StartRecordingVoice, StopRecordingVoice, SendDataToServer, ReceiveVoiceDataClient, OnAudioRead, OnAudioReadRadio, WriteToClip, optimalRate, voiceBuffer, and its OWN radio chain localVoip/radioVoip/radioNoise/radioStartBeep/radioEndBeep) — superseded by PlayerVoice, which duplicates that radio chain.
findings.members: PlayerVoice.VoiceChatComponent -> Il2CppMetaVoiceChat.MetaVc; MetaVc.SendFrame, ReceiveFrame, StartClient; VcConfig; Il2Cpp.VoiceChat, Il2Cpp.SteamworksVoiceChat
findings.modding: DEV-CONFIRMED: the OPERATOR developers confirm this middleware is not used. Edgegap in particular is never touched and is present only because Mirror bundles it. Corrects the standing note 'Dissonance+Concentus (voice)': Concentus serves MetaVoiceChat's Opus encoder/decoder; Dissonance is dead weight. Patch MetaVc.ReceiveFrame / SendFrame for voice interception. Do not waste effort on Dissonance's API or on SteamworksVoiceChat.

findings.title: Radio vs local voice is a SyncVar toggle with a filter chain, entirely client-authoritative on presentation
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.PlayerVoice: SyncVar `IsRadioChat` (NetworkIsRadioChat) with hook OnChatTypeChanged(bool oldValue, bool newValue) and Mirror hook delegate _Mirror_SyncVarHookDelegate_IsRadioChat, set via CMD_SetChatType(bool isRadio). Presentation: VoipSource (AudioSource), voipVolumeGroup (AudioMixerGroup), RadioLowpass (AudioLowPassFilter), RadioHighpass (AudioHighPassFilter), RadioNoise/RadioStartBeep/RadioEndBeep (AudioSources). Methods: ActivateRadio(), DeactivateRadio(), LocalRadioSwitch(bool playing), ResetRadioState(), RemoveVoipAudioGroup(), ReAddVoipAudioGroup(), SetPlayerVolume(float), SetPlayerMuted(bool), getAudioTransform(), GetPosition(), ResetForSceneChange(). Local-only mirrors _localIsRadioChat, _toggleInputRadio, _toggleInputLocal.
findings.members: PlayerVoice.CMD_SetChatType(bool), UserCode_CMD_SetChatType__Boolean, OnChatTypeChanged, RadioLowpass, RadioHighpass, RadioNoise, RadioStartBeep, RadioEndBeep, SetPlayerVolume(float), SetPlayerMuted(bool)
findings.modding: Per-player mute/volume already has clean public methods — SetPlayerVolume/SetPlayerMuted — no need to touch the mixer. RemoveVoipAudioGroup/ReAddVoipAudioGroup exist specifically to bypass the mixer group, implying the radio effect chain is applied outside the mixer.

findings.title: AI barks are server-authoritative by INDEX into a ScriptableObject list — appending lines client-side desyncs meaning
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.VoiceLineLibrary (SO): List<VoiceCategoryBlock> VoiceGroups, float Volume, GetBlock(VoiceCategory) / GetList(VoiceCategory) -> List<VoiceLineEntry>. Il2Cpp.VoiceLineEntry: Clip, loop, Weight, CooldownSeconds. Il2Cpp.VoiceCategory is an ENUM with 56 members: Idle, CombatThreats, CombatIntimidation, TargetSighted, TargetDown, WasSighted, Hit, HitBadly, Death, NearDeath, Bleeding, BleedoutDeath, Reload, ReloadAngry, ReloadAngryAlone, ThroatShots, then the pilot set PILOT_INFIL_ONE_MINUTE/THREEZERO/LANDED/HOLDING/RTB, PILOT_EXFIL_ONE_MINUTE/THREEZERO/LANDED_WAIT/LANDED_WAITLONG/EXFILING/INBOUND_GENERIC and INBOUND_{A,B,C,D,E,H,P}{1..4} (28 landing-zone-specific inbound calls). Flow: Il2Cpp.CharacterVoicePlayer{Librarys[] (VoiceLineLibrary), Source (AudioSource), GlobalCooldown, RespectPerLineCooldowns, TryPlayByIndex(List<VoiceLineEntry>, int)} is the local player; Il2Cpp.NetworkedCharacterVoicePlayer is the NetworkBehaviour — PlayRandom(VoiceCategory, bool bypassCooldown), PlayExact(VoiceCategory, int), Client_TryPickIndex(List<VoiceLineEntry>, ref int chosen), Cmd_ClientProposedPlay(VoiceCategory, int index, uint nonce, float clientTime), Server_PlayRandom/Server_PlayExact/Server_TryPickIndex, GetSrvCooldowns(List<VoiceLineEntry>) -> float[], Rpc_Play(VoiceCategory, int index, uint nonce). Which voice actor a character uses is SyncVar `currentLibraryIndex` (hook OnLibraryIndexUpdate(int previous, int current), setter UpdateLibraryIndex(int), server picker ServerSetRandomLibraryIndex()). Server-side cooldown state: Dictionary<List<VoiceLineEntry>, float[]> _srvCooldowns, _srvNextGlobalTime, _effectiveGlobalCooldown; anti-dup nonce _lastSentNonce; WeightToFloat(float w).
findings.members: NetworkedCharacterVoicePlayer.Cmd_ClientProposedPlay, Rpc_Play, UserCode_Rpc_Play__VoiceCategory__Int32__UInt32, currentLibraryIndex, ServerSetRandomLibraryIndex; VoiceLineLibrary.VoiceGroups; VoiceLineEntry.Clip/Weight/CooldownSeconds; VoiceCategory (56 values)
findings.modding: Adding barks is easy but index-fragile: both Rpc_Play and currentLibraryIndex carry raw ints into the VoiceGroups list and the Librarys array. Appending entries in a client-only mod means every peer resolves a different clip. Safe patterns: (a) REPLACE VoiceLineEntry.Clip in place — index space unchanged, works client-only; (b) append only if the mod runs on every peer including the host, and append at the END. Hook UserCode_Rpc_Play__VoiceCategory__Int32__UInt32 for the receive side. The 28 PILOT_EXFIL_INBOUND_{A..P}{1..4} entries mean per-LZ pilot callouts are already fully authored.

findings.title: AudioPreloadManager exists specifically to preload and declick clips — mod-added clips should register with it
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.AudioPreloadManager (singleton `instance`, static OnLoad, Awake, Start): AudioClip[] ClipsToPreload, Dictionary<AudioClip,int> LoadedClips (refcount), HashSet<AudioClip> _declicked. API: RegisterClip(AudioClip clip, bool declick), DeRegisterClip(AudioClip clip), static WaitAndDeclick(AudioClip) coroutine, static DeclickClip(AudioClip clip, float fadeInSeconds, float fadeOutSeconds). Declicking mutates raw sample data (fade in/out envelopes applied to the clip itself), which is why _declicked is a set — it must run at most once per clip.
findings.members: AudioPreloadManager.instance, RegisterClip(AudioClip, bool), DeRegisterClip(AudioClip), DeclickClip(AudioClip, float, float), LoadedClips, _declicked, ClipsToPreload
findings.modding: A mod loading clips from an AssetBundle should call AudioPreloadManager.instance.RegisterClip(clip, true) so the clip is resident before first play (avoids the first-shot hitch) and gets the same declick treatment as shipped audio. Because DeclickClip rewrites sample data in place, do NOT call it twice on the same clip and do not call it on a clip you also expect to read back unmodified. Il2Cpp.AudioFader is the separate, general fade-out helper: static FadeOut(AudioSource, float duration, bool stopOnComplete, bool restoreVolume, bool unscaled) and static Cancel(AudioSource), driven by its own singleton Update over a List<Fade>.

findings.title: AxelF (Unity's Book of the Dead audio framework) ships complete and self-contained in its own assembly
findings.detail: Il2CppAxelF.dll, 52 types, from Assets\_artassets\_environments\BookOfTheDeadAssets\Features\AxelF\. Il2CppAxelF.Heartbeat is the driver (Awake/Update/LateUpdate) holding listenerTransform, playerTransform, an AudioMixer (the ONLY bare AudioMixer reference in the entire build), rotationAngleParameter (string, an exposed mixer param name), ambienceWindStrength/ambienceWindThreshold/ambienceWindInterpolatedThreshold, AxelFGetAverageAmplitude(), StartRecording(string)/StopRecording() via Il2CppAxelF.RecordToFile. Il2CppAxelF.Synthesizer is a real voice allocator: Stack<SourceInfo> freeSources, double-buffered List<ActiveSource> activeSources0/1 with Swap<T>, handle-based KeyOn(...)->uint / KeyOff(uint, float release, EnvelopeMode) / IsKeyedOn(uint) / SetModVolume(uint, float) / Stop(uint) / StopAll(), plus Activate overloads for Patch, AudioProgram, AudioSequence and ActivateStatic(AudioMixerGroup, AudioClip, Parameters, AudioSource, float delay, float volume, float pitch). Spatial model: Il2CppAxelF.Zone (allZones list, parent/children hierarchy, radius, volumeExclusion/volumeInfluence/parentExclusion, UpdateProbes/UpdateActivation/UpdateInfluence/UpdateExclusionDepthFirst) and AudioZone (OnTriggerEnter/Exit, OnProbe(Vector3 lpos, int thisFrame), peripheralFade, Ownership). Il2CppAxelF.AudioSlapback does early-reflection point finding: static HashSet<AudioSlapback> allSlapbacks and FindClosest(Vector3 p, ref Vector3 rp, ref Vector3 rd).
findings.members: Il2CppAxelF.Heartbeat.audioMixer, rotationAngleParameter, ambienceWindStrength; Synthesizer.KeyOn/KeyOff/Activate/ActivateStatic; Zone.UpdateExclusionDepthFirst; AudioZone.OnProbe; AudioEmitter.CueIn/CueOut/CueOutWithRelease; AudioSlapback.FindClosest; OcclusionSettings.speedOfSound
findings.modding: Far more capable than anything the game wrote itself (voice stealing, envelopes, zone exclusion graph, slapback reflections, speed-of-sound). Whether any shipped scene instantiates a Heartbeat is NOT provable statically — runtime probe: FindObjectOfType<Il2CppAxelF.Heartbeat>() and Il2CppAxelF.Zone.allZones.Count in a loaded operation. If Heartbeat is alive, its `audioMixer` is the handle a mod needs for AudioMixer.SetFloat/GetFloat on exposed params — no game type holds a bare AudioMixer.

findings.title: The mixer surface is tiny and fragmented across four unrelated types; only two audio settings persist
findings.detail: AudioMixerGroup references exist on exactly seven game types: AudioCustomCurves (defaultSourceMixer, defaultTailMixer), AudioOcclusion (audioMixer, originalAudioMixer), GameManager (occlusionMixer, GunshotAudioGroup), PlayMenu (voiceChatMixer, musicMixer), PlayerVoice (voipVolumeGroup), WeaponSFXCompoment (audioMixer, originalAudioMixer, as_Loop_Mixer, as_DistLoop_Mixer, as_SuppLoop_Mixer), WeaponSfxAudioSource (originalAudioMixer). Every occlusion-capable type keeps an `originalAudioMixer` alongside the live one — occlusion is applied by REROUTING the source to a different mixer group and restoring it afterwards, not only by filter parameters. Exposed mixer parameter names found in metadata literals: `mastervolume` and `tailLevel` (AxelF also uses a runtime-named `rotationAngleParameter`). Settings API on Il2Cpp.PlayMenu: SetVolume(float), SetMusicVolume(float), SetAIVolume(float), SetVoiceChatVolume(float); GameManager adds SetGunshotAudioVolume(float) with defaultGunshotVolumeLevel. But of PlayMenu's ~40 `Key_*` persistence strings, only Key_MasterVolume and Key_MusicVolume are audio — there is no Key_AIVolume, Key_VoiceChatVolume or Key_SFXVolume.
findings.members: PlayMenu.SetVolume, SetMusicVolume, SetAIVolume, SetVoiceChatVolume, Key_MasterVolume, Key_MusicVolume, voiceChatMixer, musicMixer; GameManager.SetGunshotAudioVolume, GunshotAudioGroup, occlusionMixer; literals `mastervolume`, `tailLevel`
findings.modding: Two probable shipped bugs: AI volume and voice-chat volume have setters and sliders but no persistence key, so they should reset to default every launch (probe: set them, restart, re-read). Also, because occlusion works by swapping mixer groups and stashing `originalAudioMixer`, a mod that assigns its own AudioMixerGroup to a live occluded AudioSource will have it without warning reverted the next time occlusion state flips — set `originalAudioMixer` too.

findings.title: Asset-store demo audio code shipped in the retail build, and shell-impact audio is duplicated with a mismatched material list
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.WeaponSound is an asset-pack demo driver still in Assembly-CSharp: Fire(), StopFiring(), SwitchWeaponUp()/SwitchWeaponDown(), InitFiremode(), InitSuppressor(), AutoFireForTesting(), SwitchWeaponColor(int), ChangeWeaponColor(Transform, string color), with `weapons` (Transform), selectedWeapon, weaponsMax. Il2Cpp.SoundFunctionLibrary itself carries IsDemoScene() / isDemoScene and PlayMusic() / musicSource. Separately, Il2Cpp.ShellSFXComponent hardcodes its own twelve per-material clip lists + volumes — acs_Concrete, acs_Acid, acs_Electrical, acs_Fabric, acs_Glass, acs_Grass, acs_Gravel, acs_Metal, acs_Mud, acs_Sand, acs_Water, acs_Wood — which does NOT match SurfaceTypeEnum: Acid, Electrical and Fabric are not surface types at all, and Carpet, Brick, Dirt, Default, Flesh are missing. Meanwhile SurfaceInformation already provides PistolCasingImpact/RifleCasingImpact/ShotgunCasingImpact and GetShellImpact(ShellAudioType). So casing impact audio has two competing implementations, one of them keyed to a foreign material taxonomy.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.WeaponSound.AutoFireForTesting, SwitchWeaponColor; SoundFunctionLibrary.IsDemoScene, PlayMusic; ShellSFXComponent.acs_Acid, acs_Electrical, acs_Fabric; SurfaceInformation.GetShellImpact(ShellAudioType)
findings.modding: If a mod replaces casing sounds via SurfaceInformation only, shells using ShellSFXComponent keep the old audio (and vice versa). Determine which is live per bullet-shell prefab: BulletShell carries AudioClip arrays too, and Il2Cpp.AudioOcclusion has a `bulletShell` field, so shells route through V1 occlusion.
