Runtime probe: check whether spawned shell prefabs have a ShellSFXComponent.

findings.title: Listener-side effects live on MainCameraSingleton with two competing lowpass overrides
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.MainCameraSingleton holds lowPassFilter (AudioLowPassFilter), underwaterFilter (AudioReverbFilter) and two independent boolean overrides: overrideLowpassForHeadsetEffect and overrideLowpassForUnderwater. Il2Cpp.PlayerNetworking additionally owns a `Tinnitus` AudioSource. Ambience: Il2Cpp.AmbienceManager (singleton, static OnLoad, Awake/Update/OnDestroy) is a single crossfading AudioSource with exteriorVolume, interiorVolume, targetVolume, transitionSmoothness and a `triggersEntered` counter driven by setInterior()/setExterior(); Il2Cpp.AmbienceDynamic is the trigger side (Start, findPlayer, OnTriggerEnter(Collider), OnTriggerExit(Collider), localPlayer Transform).
findings.members: MainCameraSingleton.lowPassFilter, underwaterFilter, overrideLowpassForHeadsetEffect, overrideLowpassForUnderwater; PlayerNetworking.Tinnitus; AmbienceManager.singleton, setInterior, setExterior, triggersEntered, transitionSmoothness
findings.modding: AmbienceManager is refcounted by `triggersEntered`, so nesting or overlapping AmbienceDynamic triggers is supported, but a trigger destroyed while the player is inside it will leak the count and pin the ambience to interior — a plausible bug worth probing (walk into an interior, unload the trigger, check AmbienceManager.singleton.triggersEntered). Two independent lowpass override booleans on one shared filter is the classic setup for headset and underwater effects clobbering each other; unprovable statically, probe by triggering both at once.

findings.title: SaveManager is a fully static PlayerPrefs-shaped façade over Easy Save 3 with a 6-value file router
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.SaveManager (source: \Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\Save\SaveManager.cs) is static-only. Core API: Initialize(), GetSlotPrefix()->string, get_CurrentSaveSlot()->int, SetSaveFile(int saveID), DeleteCurrentSave(), HasKey/DeleteKey(string), GetString(string,string)/SetString(string,string), GetInt(string,int)/SetInt(string,int), GetFloat(string,float)/SetFloat(string,float), OpenES3SavePath(), GetCacheSettings(string filePath)->Il2Cpp.ES3Settings, IsLocalFileCorrupted(string), IsAllNullBytes(Il2CppStructArray<byte>), EnsureFileLoaded(string), GetFilePath(SaveFileType)->string, FlushDirtyFiles(). Routing enum is NESTED: Il2Cpp.SaveManager/SaveFileType with exactly {Other, GameProgression, PlayerSettings, AudioSettings, Controls, KeyBinds}. Typed generic entry points: SaveSteamStorage<T>(string key, T value, SaveFileType)/LoadSteamStorage<T>(string key, SaveFileType, T defaultValue), plus private string-filePath overloads, HasSteamKey(string,SaveFileType), DeleteSteamKey(string,SaveFileType). Note the untyped SetInt/GetInt/SetString/GetFloat family takes NO SaveFileType — it must default to one file internally.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.SaveManager, SaveManager/SaveFileType, GetFilePath, SaveSteamStorage, LoadSteamStorage, FlushDirtyFiles, EnsureFileLoaded, GetCacheSettings, SetSaveFile, GetSlotPrefix, DeleteCurrentSave, OpenES3SavePath
findings.modding: Every save read/write in the game funnels through ~14 static methods with plain string/int/float signatures. All are real methods (NativeMethodInfoPtr present), so Harmony can prefix/postfix SaveManager.GetInt / SetInt / GetString / LoadSteamStorage to fabricate or intercept any progression, achievement, or stat value without touching files.

findings.title: Saves are UNENCRYPTED, human-readable ES3 JSON at a fixed LocalLow path — verified on disk
findings.detail: Real layout at C:\Users\<user>\AppData\LocalLow\VECTOR INTERACTIVE\OPERATOR\Saves\Save0\ : GameProgression.es3, Other.es3, PlayerSettings.es3, AudioSettings.es3, KeyBinds.es3, plus subdirs Loadouts\Version2\ and WeaponPresets\Version2\. Every .es3 opens as plain ES3 JSON, e.g. GameProgression.es3 = {"CleanHouse_Completed":{"__type":"int","value":1},"afghan01Completed":{...},"darkwatersExtracted":{...},"depotMexico":{...},"voaCompleted":{...},"georgia01Completed":{...},"afghan02..05Completed":{...}}. No AES, no obfuscation, despite ES3Crypto/AESEncryptionAlgorithm being present in the build. Metadata confirms the literal filenames GameProgression.es3, PlayerSettings.es3, AudioSettings.es3, KeyBinds.es3, Other.es3 and the slot format strings "Saves/Save{0}/" and "Saves/SaveInfo.es3".
findings.members: GameProgression.es3, Other.es3, PlayerSettings.es3, AudioSettings.es3, KeyBinds.es3, Saves/Save{0}/
findings.modding: A mod (or a plain text editor) can grant every mission unlock by writing int 1 under the unlock-code key in GameProgression.es3. No signing or checksum exists to defeat. Equally, a mod can ship a curated save without any game API.

findings.title: Progression keys and achievement keys live in DIFFERENT files — GameProgression.es3 holds only unlock codes; everything else is dumped in Other.es3
findings.detail: On-disk proof: GameProgression.es3 contains ONLY mission unlock codes (CleanHouse_Completed, afghan01Completed…afghan05Completed, armenia01Completed, georgia01Completed, darkwatersExtracted, depotMexico, voaCompleted). Other.es3 is the junk drawer: all achievement flags, all per-map best-time/kill/score stats, lifetime killCount (6133) and killStreak, tutorial-seen flags (CharCusTutorial, DoorTutorial, laptopTutorial, weaponCusTutorial, player_firstBoot, LoreDisclaimer), graphics settings (CurrentUpscalerNew, CurrentUpscaler_2026, dlssSettingsNew, lodcrossfade_setting, maxfps19823839183jnSliderValue, maxbulletholes8190241SliderValue), weapon eye-offsets, per-optic reticle indices, AND the character preset. Since the untyped SetInt/GetInt overloads carry no SaveFileType and all these keys land in Other.es3, the PlayerPrefs-shaped API almost certainly hard-routes to SaveFileType.Other, while progression writes explicitly pass SaveFileType.GameProgression through SaveSteamStorage<int>.
findings.members: killCount, killStreak, ACHIEVEMENT_*, NEW_ACHIEVEMENT_*, CharacterPreset, CharacterPresetMods, player_firstBoot, CharCusTutorial
findings.modding: If you want a value to survive a 'reset progression' you must know which file it lands in. Writing progression via SaveManager.SetInt() will put it in Other.es3, NOT GameProgression.es3, and the opboard will not see it. Use SaveSteamStorage<int>(key, 1, SaveFileType.GameProgression).

findings.title: 'SteamStorage' is a misnomer: the Steam-named methods are the ordinary local ES3 path, and no game-side Steam save/stat wrapper exists
findings.detail: SaveSteamStorage/LoadSteamStorage/HasSteamKey/DeleteSteamKey all resolve through GetFilePath(SaveFileType)->string and GetCacheSettings(string filePath)->ES3Settings, and the resulting files are the plain local LocalLow .es3 files listed above. The only game-side Steam type is Il2Cpp.SteamManager (Instance, Initialized, InitializedSafe, ForceEarlyInit, ForceShutdown, SteamAPIDebugTextHook) — a stock Steamworks.NET bootstrapper with no stat/achievement/remote-storage members. There is no Il2Cpp AchievementManager, no SetAchievement/StoreStats wrapper type in Assembly-CSharp (the only AchievementManager in the build is Discord's SDK). Steamworks' ISteamUserStats/ISteamRemoteStorage bindings exist but are unwrapped.
findings.members: Il2Cpp.SteamManager, SaveSteamStorage, LoadSteamStorage, HasSteamKey, DeleteSteamKey
findings.modding: Do not assume cloud arbitration or server-side validation of saves — there is none in managed code. Runtime probe to settle whether Steam is touched at all: hook SaveManager.SaveSteamStorage and log, then check whether SteamUserStats.SetAchievement / SteamRemoteStorage.FileWrite are hit in the same call window (or just watch for a Steam overlay achievement toast after writing a NEW_ACHIEVEMENT_ key directly).

findings.title: Save writes are cached in memory and only flushed by FlushDirtyFiles() — a crash loses progression
findings.detail: SaveManager keeps HashSet<string> _loadedFiles and HashSet<string> _dirtyFiles, gates reads through EnsureFileLoaded(string filePath), builds per-file ES3Settings via GetCacheSettings(string filePath) (ES3 Location.Cache), and only commits on FlushDirtyFiles(). Nothing in the signature set schedules that flush — there is no autosave timer method on SaveManager. Complementing this, IsLocalFileCorrupted(string localPath) and IsAllNullBytes(Il2CppStructArray<byte> data) exist specifically to detect the classic all-zero-bytes .es3 that results from a kill during write.
findings.members: _dirtyFiles, _loadedFiles, EnsureFileLoaded, GetCacheSettings, FlushDirtyFiles, IsLocalFileCorrupted, IsAllNullBytes
findings.modding: A mod that calls SetInt/SetString and then expects the file to change on disk will see nothing until the game calls FlushDirtyFiles(). Call SaveManager.FlushDirtyFiles() explicitly after mod writes. Conversely, editing the .es3 on disk while the game is running is futile — the cached copy will overwrite it on the next flush.

findings.title: Multi-save-slot machinery is fully implemented but SaveInfo.es3 has never been written — the slot system is dead in shipping builds
findings.detail: SaveManager exposes get_CurrentSaveSlot()->int, SetSaveFile(int saveID), private _currentSaveSlot, DeleteCurrentSave(), and a static string field SaveInfoFile whose value is the metadata literal "Saves/SaveInfo.es3". GetSlotPrefix() composes the metadata format string "Saves/Save{0}/". On a heavily-played install, Saves\SaveInfo.es3 does not exist and only Save0 exists — so nothing has ever called the slot-registry write path, and no UI exercises SetSaveFile with a non-zero id.
findings.members: SaveInfoFile, CurrentSaveSlot, SetSaveFile, _currentSaveSlot, GetSlotPrefix, DeleteCurrentSave, Saves/SaveInfo.es3
findings.modding: A mod can enable multi-profile support cheaply: call SaveManager.SetSaveFile(n) then FlushDirtyFiles(). Every path helper already interpolates the slot, so Saves\Save1\… will be created correctly. This is the lowest-effort 'new feature' in the whole save layer.

findings.title: Three-stage save migration left a full duplicate tree, and appears to have dropped weapon presets
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.SaveManager.MigrateToSavesDirectory(), MigrateRootFilesToSlot0(), MoveDirectory(string src, string dest); Il2Cpp.PlayerPrefsMigration.MigrateAll()/TryMigrateKeyInt(string,SaveFileType)/TryMigrateKeyFloat/TryMigrateKeyString/TryMigrateLoadoutKeyInt(string oldKey,string newKey,int slot)/TryMigrateLoadoutKeyString; Il2Cpp.WeaponPresetMigration.MigrateAll()/MigrateOldTxtPresets()/MigrateES3Presets()/WritePresetToPath(string json,string presetName,string weaponFamily,string slotPrefix). Metadata carries both the legacy key format "<Scene> Best Time" (e.g. "Afghan Urban Day Best Time", "Suburb Night Best Time", "IndustrialMap Best Time") and the current "{0} {1} Best Time", confirming PlayerPrefs->ES3 key rewriting. On disk, a full parallel tree survives at ...\OPERATOR\Save0Migrated\ alongside ...\OPERATOR\Saves\Save0\. Comparing them: Save0Migrated\WeaponPresets\Version2\SPR\ holds Delta.txt, MARSOC.txt, MASRIC.txt and MK46\ holds 'Delta 2.txt', MARSOC.txt — none of which exist under Saves\Save0 (which has only SPR\SPR.txt and MK46\FDE.txt).
findings.members: MigrateToSavesDirectory, MigrateRootFilesToSlot0, MoveDirectory, PlayerPrefsMigration.MigrateAll, WeaponPresetMigration.MigrateOldTxtPresets, WeaponPresetMigration.MigrateES3Presets, Save0Migrated
findings.modding: Save0Migrated is a free pre-migration backup a mod can read to restore lost presets. Caveat before calling this a confirmed bug: the user may simply have deleted those presets in-game after migrating. Runtime probe to settle it: hook WeaponPresetMigration.MigrateOldTxtPresets/MigrateES3Presets, point a clean profile at a seeded legacy tree with awkward names (spaces, unicode, empty filename — note an actual '.txt' with an empty basename exists under MP5\ and Noveske\), and diff input vs output.

findings.title: Weapon presets are loose per-preset .txt files, and the shipped defaults sit unpacked in OPERATOR_Data with stray Unity .meta files
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.SaveManager.GetWeaponPresetLocalDir(string weaponFamily)->string, GetDefaultPresetDir(string weaponFamily)->string, SaveWeaponPreset(string presetName, string json, string weaponFamily), LoadWeaponPreset(string presetName, string weaponFamily)->string, DeleteWeaponPreset(string presetName, string weaponFamily), IsDefaultPreset(string presetName, string weaponFamily)->bool, GetWeaponPresetNames(string weaponFamily)->Il2CppStringArray. Metadata format strings: "WeaponPresets/Version{0}/{1}/" and "DefaultWeaponPresets/{0}/{1}". User presets: ...\Saves\Save0\WeaponPresets\Version2\<Family>\<PresetName>.txt — preset name IS the filename, family IS the directory. Shipped defaults: D:\Games\OPERATOR\OPERATOR_Data\DefaultWeaponPresets\2\<Family>\<Name>.txt (families 870, APC9, AR-15, AR10, Benelli, FN FNX, Glock17, HK416, HK416D, M&P 9 2.0, M17, MCX, MK17, MP5, MP7A2, Noveske, R700, TT 2011, XM5) — and every one of them shipped with its Unity .meta sidecar (e.g. 'AR-15\MK18.txt.meta', 'AR10.meta'), i.e. an editor folder was copied into the build verbatim. Payload schema = Il2Cpp.Save_WeaponPreset { List<string> WeaponModName; List<Il2Cpp.ModSavePathList> ModParentDirectory; List<UnityEngine.Vector3> WeaponModPosition; float EyeOffset } serialized as {"WeaponModName":[...],"ModParentDirectory":[{"path":["MOD_Barrel","MOD_Handguard"]},...],"WeaponModPosition":[{"x":..}],"EyeOffset":0.0}.
findings.members: Save_WeaponPreset, ModSavePathList, GetWeaponPresetNames, IsDefaultPreset, GetDefaultPresetDir, SaveWeaponPreset, DefaultWeaponPresets/2/
findings.modding: Shipping curated weapon builds needs NO code: drop .txt files into OPERATOR_Data\DefaultWeaponPresets\2\<Family>\. IsDefaultPreset presumably makes them undeletable in the UI (WeaponPresetButton.DeletePreset / DisableDeleteButton exist for exactly this). The 'Version{0}' in both format strings means a future bump to Version3 without warning orphans every user preset — a mod that writes presets should read the version from the game rather than hardcode 2.

findings.title: Achievements have no manager type — they are three inline methods on GameManagerNetwork plus opboard-authored gates
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.GameManagerNetwork.CheckAchievements(), CheckTier1Challenge(), CheckTier1NightChallenge() are the entire achievement system; they sit next to the end-of-mission chain CompleteOperation() -> ShowMissionCompleteScreen() -> SetEndTimeStats/SetEndStatus/SetEndHealthStatus/SetEndStats/SetMiscInfo/CalulateRating [sic]. Per-mission gating data lives on Il2Cpp.CerebusOpboard as authored fields: AchievementName (string), achievement_aiDifficulty (AIDifficulty), achievement_min_ai_amount (int), TargetRaidTime (float). The name is carried to the server as a SyncVar: OperationsManager.StartOperation(string sceneName, int prepTime, string displayName, string infilTime, string _activeAchievement, float targetTime) -> CMD_StartOperation(same six) -> activeAchievementName / NetworkactiveAchievementName. Full key set from metadata — legacy: ACHIEVEMENT_COMPLETEFIRSTMISSION, _FASTRAID, _FIRSTDEATH, _HIGHKILLCOUNT, _LASTMANSTANDING, _LOWHPWIN, _MISSIONFAILED, _MOZAMBIQUE, _PERFECTRAID, _TEAMKILL, _WARCRIME; current: NEW_ACHIEVEMENT_CompleteTier1Achievements, _DUMBASS, _OWN_THE_NIGHT, _COPCOBRA, _Tier1AfghanCompounds, _Tier1AfghanStreets, _Tier1AfghanistanKandahar, _Tier1Armenia, _Tier1Boat, _Tier1Gerogia [sic, misspelled Georgia], _Tier1House, _Tier1MexicoDepot, _Tier1Syria01, _Tier1Ukraine; night variants are the same keys with a literal "NIGHT_" prefix. Also present: TEST_ACHIEVEMENT_01.
findings.members: CheckAchievements, CheckTier1Challenge, CheckTier1NightChallenge, CerebusOpboard.AchievementName, achievement_aiDifficulty, achievement_min_ai_amount, activeAchievementName, NIGHT_, TEST_ACHIEVEMENT_01
findings.modding: To make a custom opboard mission grant an achievement, set AchievementName + achievement_min_ai_amount + achievement_aiDifficulty on the CerebusOpboard and the existing StartOperation path carries it. Note the misspelled key NEW_ACHIEVEMENT_Tier1Gerogia is the real key — spell it wrong or it won't match. TEST_ACHIEVEMENT_01 is a dev leftover; ACHIEVEMENT_HIGHKILLCOUNT and ACHIEVEMENT_LOWHPWIN are defined but absent from a completionist save, so they may be unreachable.

findings.title: The anti-cheat gate is one patchable property, and the devs shipped the bypass as a console command
findings.detail: Il2Cpp.OperationsManager exposes get_EffectiveHasCheated()->bool as a REAL method (NativeMethodInfoPtr_get_EffectiveHasCheated_Public_get_Boolean_0, and there is NO NativeFieldInfoPtr_EffectiveHasCheated), backed by two storage locations: HasCheated (a plain field — NativeFieldInfoPtr_HasCheated) and the Mirror SyncVar NetworkHasCheated (get_/set_NetworkHasCheated, real weaver methods). A shipped QFSW Quantum Console command literal reads "dev-bypass-cheatcheck" with help text "Toggles ignoring the 'has cheated' flag locally so achievements / best times still register after using cheats. Developer only." A second literal, "Use server authority for cheat safety.", indicates the flag is meant to be host-authoritative.
findings.members: OperationsManager.EffectiveHasCheated, HasCheated, NetworkHasCheated, dev-bypass-cheatcheck
findings.modding: This is the single decisive hook. get_EffectiveHasCheated is Harmony-patchable (postfix -> false) which re-enables achievement and best-time recording for a modded session. HasCheated itself is a field, so its accessors are il2cpp-interop-generated and are NOT Harmony-patchable — patch the property, not the field. Because it is also a SyncVar, a client cannot clear it for the server; a modded host can.

findings.title: Stat keys are composed at runtime from seven format strings — the schema is fully recoverable
findings.detail: Metadata carries the exact composers: "{0} {1} Best Time", "{0} {1} Best Time Survival", "{0} {1} Best Kills Normal", "{0} {1} Best Kills Survival", "{0} {1} Best Score", "{0} {1} Best Round", "{0} {1} Best Intel Collected". {0} = map display name, {1} = game mode. Confirmed against the live save: "Operation Room PVE_WAVESURVIVAL Best Score" = 3570, "Afghan Base PVE_WAVESURVIVAL Best Round" = 12, "Suburb Night StandardPVE Best Time" = 59.08083, "Violence Of Action PVE_FINDINTEL Best Time" = 711.2672, "Armenia Day PVE_ASSETDESTROY Best Time" = 1090.69446. Observed modes: StandardPVE, PVE_HVTKILL, PVE_FINDINTEL, PVE_ASSETDESTROY, PVE_WAVESURVIVAL. GameManagerNetwork holds lastPreviousBestTime (float) and the UI fields missionCompleted_PersonalBestTime / missionFailed_PersonalBestTime / survival_PersonalBestTime (TextMeshProUGUI). Survival stat writers are separate: Survival_SetEndTimeStats/Survival_SetRoundStats/Survival_SetPointsStats/Survival_SetKillStats/Survival_SetDeadlistOperator [sic]. Global counters killCount and killStreak are string-keyed with no backing field anywhere.
findings.members: {0} {1} Best Time, Best Time Survival, Best Kills Normal, Best Kills Survival, Best Score, Best Round, Best Intel Collected, lastPreviousBestTime, killCount, killStreak
findings.modding: A custom map's stats will key off its display name, so a mod map named identically to a stock map will without warning share and overwrite its leaderboard entries. Legacy pre-migration keys ("Afghan Urban Day Best Time", no mode segment) are still in metadata, so PlayerPrefsMigration is still expected to run against old profiles.

findings.title: Mission unlocking has no IsUnlocked() anywhere — it is authored strings compared inline, with a separate exfil-only unlock channel
findings.detail: Unlock authoring is spread across Il2Cpp.CerebusOperation, Il2Cpp.CerebusTargetPackage and Il2Cpp.CerebusOpboard: unlockCode (string, all three), progressionUnlockCode (string, Operation + TargetPackage only), MissionRequiredForUnlock (CerebusTargetPackage reference, Operation + TargetPackage), and isLocked / isCompleted (plain bool FIELDS, not computed properties). CerebusOpboard additionally carries exfilUnlockingKey (string) and UnlockOnExfil (string); exfilUnlockingKey is mirrored onto both GameManagerNetwork and OperationsManager. A metadata literal reads "this now uses MissionRequiredForUnlock.progressionUnlockCode", i.e. the indirection through a required prior mission is the current scheme and bare unlockCode is the legacy one. No CheckUnlock/IsUnlocked/EvaluateUnlock method exists in Assembly-CSharp — the comparison is inlined in CerebusOpboard.CreateInstance / CerebusOperation.OnCreated. The exfil channel is visible in the save data: GameProgression.es3 has "darkwatersExtracted", distinct from the "*Completed" family.
findings.members: unlockCode, progressionUnlockCode, MissionRequiredForUnlock, isLocked, isCompleted, exfilUnlockingKey, UnlockOnExfil, CerebusOpboard.CreateInstance, CerebusOperation.OnCreated
findings.modding: Because isLocked is a field on a runtime instance and the evaluation is inlined, you cannot patch a single 'unlock check'. Two workable routes: (a) write the key into GameProgression.es3 (or SaveSteamStorage<int>(code, 1, SaveFileType.GameProgression)) before the laptop UI builds, or (b) postfix CerebusOpboard.CreateInstance(Transform, MissionLaptop) and clear isLocked on the instance. Route (a) is what the game itself does.

findings.title: A complete duplicate CERBERUS_* type family shadows the live Cerebus* family — a dead, half-migrated system
findings.detail: Both exist in Assembly-CSharp simultaneously: the live set Il2Cpp.CerebusOpboard / CerebusOperation / CerebusTargetPackage (note the misspelling 'Cerebus') and the older set Il2Cpp.CERBERUS_OPBOARD / CERBERUS_OPERATION / CERBERUS_TARGETPACKAGE. Both carry unlockCode and isLocked; both Operation/TargetPackage variants carry progressionUnlockCode. The discriminator is MissionRequiredForUnlock (CerebusTargetPackage type) — present on CerebusOperation and CerebusTargetPackage, absent from CERBERUS_OPERATION and CERBERUS_TARGETPACKAGE. OperationsManager references only the new family: get_ActiveOperations()->Il2CppReferenceArray<Il2Cpp.CerebusOperation> and get_SimulationOperations()->same; CurrentOpInfo.get_CerebusOpboard()->Il2Cpp.CerebusOpboard. CerebusOpboard is also where the live mission-authoring surface lives: MapPrefab, AvailableInfils, MinAI/MaxAI, Difficulty, PrepTimeInSeconds, TARGETPACKAGE (TARGETPACKAGE_DETAILS[]), GameModeOverride/AffectGamemode, requireEnoughInfils/requireEnoughExfils, HVTSpawnIsRandom, SelectedInfiltrationTime, Start_Operation().
findings.members: CerebusOpboard, CerebusOperation, CerebusTargetPackage, CERBERUS_OPBOARD, CERBERUS_OPERATION, CERBERUS_TARGETPACKAGE, OperationsManager.ActiveOperations, CurrentOpInfo.CerebusOpboard
findings.modding: Target the Cerebus* (single-R, misspelled) family — the CERBERUS_* uppercase set is dead weight and patching it does nothing. This corrects the previously-established note that the live chain is CERBERUS_OPERATION -> CERBERUS_TARGETPACKAGE -> CerebusOpboard: OperationsManager's arrays prove the whole live chain is CerebusOperation -> CerebusTargetPackage -> CerebusOpboard. Also note CerebusOpboard.requireEnoughInfils/requireEnoughExfils are hard gates a custom map must satisfy.

findings.title: Character presets are a single unnamed slot stored as two escaped JSON strings in Other.es3
findings.detail: Two string keys in Saves\Save0\Other.es3: "CharacterPreset" and "CharacterPresetMods", each an escaped JSON blob shaped {"CharacterModName":[...],"CharacterModParentName":[...]}. CharacterPreset holds the 13 worn garments with parent "None" for every entry (matching the established fact that garments are direct CharacterCustomisation properties, not modParents). CharacterPresetMods holds child attachments with real parent socket paths like "Ops-Core FAST MT Super High Cut_MOD_NVG", "JPC Breacher Coyote_MOD_ArmourPlate", "Balaclava (Over Mouth)_MOD_Color". The backing type is Il2Cpp.Save_CharacterPreset { List<string> CharacterModName; List<string> CharacterModParentName; string DefaultJson; string DefaultModsJson } — DefaultJson/DefaultModsJson are fields carrying the factory-default operator. There is exactly ONE preset key pair — no naming, no indexing, no list. Related debug-only types: Il2Cpp.SetCharacterModPreset (\Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\debug\) and Il2Cpp.ApplyWeaponPresetDebug.ApplyPresetFromSaveString().
findings.members: Save_CharacterPreset, DefaultJson, DefaultModsJson, CharacterModName, CharacterModParentName, CharacterPreset, CharacterPresetMods, SetCharacterModPreset
findings.modding: This is the asymmetry that motivates a multi-slot outfit mod: weapons get a whole file-per-preset directory tree, characters get one overwritten key. A mod adding named character slots should write sibling keys (e.g. CharacterPreset_<name>) into Other.es3 via SaveManager.SetString and reuse the same two-blob format, then FlushDirtyFiles.

findings.title: Loadouts are per-slot ES3 files whose weapon payload is a denormalized JSON string, and Save_WeaponPreset is reused verbatim
findings.detail: SaveManager.SaveLoadout<T>(string key, T value, int slot) / LoadLoadout<T>(string key, int slot, T defaultValue); metadata format string "Loadouts/Version{0}/{1}.es3" under the slot prefix. Real file ...\Saves\Save0\Loadouts\Version2\0.es3 keys: PrimaryWeapon / PrimaryWeaponModsJSON / PrimaryFireMode / PrimaryLastAdsIndex, the same quartet for Secondary, SecondPrimary and SpecialPurpose, plus LastWeaponSlot, Loadout_Grenades ({"values":["Slap Charge",...]}), Loadout_Mags ({"presets":[{"magazineModName":"D-60","ammoModName":"338 Lupua ELD Precision Tracer","AttachedModSlots":[],"AttachedMods":[]},...]}), and one "<Optic Name>(Clone) reticle setting" int per sight (~45 of them, keyed on the Unity clone name). The *WeaponModsJSON values use the identical Save_WeaponPreset schema as the standalone preset .txt files. Writers: Il2Cpp.WeaponMods.SetLoadoutString() and SetLoadoutStringOnExtraction(); GameManagerNetwork.SaveLoadout(); PlayerPrefsMigration.TryMigrateLoadoutKeyInt(string oldKey,string newKey,int slot)/TryMigrateLoadoutKeyString.
findings.members: SaveLoadout, LoadLoadout, Loadouts/Version{0}/{1}.es3, PrimaryWeaponModsJSON, Loadout_Mags, Loadout_Grenades, LastWeaponSlot, WeaponMods.SetLoadoutString
findings.modding: Loadout slots are already parameterized by int — the file layout supports N loadouts today even if the UI exposes one (0.es3). Reticle settings key off the runtime clone name ('Trijicon RMR(Clone) reticle setting'), so a mod that renames or re-instantiates an optic prefab will orphan the player's saved reticle choice. SetLoadoutStringOnExtraction is the hook that persists whatever the player exfils with.

findings.title: SaveFileType.Controls is an enum value with no file — keybinds go to KeyBinds.es3 only
findings.detail: The nested enum declares both Controls and KeyBinds, but on a fully-played profile only KeyBinds.es3 exists in Saves\Save0 (alongside GameProgression, PlayerSettings, AudioSettings, Other). The keybind API is Il2Cpp.InputLayer: LoadKeyBinds(), SaveAllKeyBinds(), SaveSingleKeybind(Il2Cpp.InputKey), SetSingleKeybind(Il2Cpp.InputKey, InputKeyBind), ResetAllKeyBinds(), ResetSingleKeyBind(InputKey), ResetSingleKeyBindPressType(InputKey), SetupDefaultBinds(), GetConflictedBinds()->List<InputKey>, ConfigureAllBindTypes(), with storage arrays Binds / SingleKeyBinds / DoubleKeyBinds (InputKeyBindInstance[]) and KeyBindNames (string[]) / NumKeyBinds.
findings.members: SaveFileType.Controls, InputLayer.SaveAllKeyBinds, SaveSingleKeybind, ResetAllKeyBinds, GetConflictedBinds, Binds, DoubleKeyBinds, KeyBindNames
findings.modding: A mod adding a keybind must grow KeyBindNames/NumKeyBinds/Binds in lockstep or LoadKeyBinds will index past the authored arrays. Controls is a free unused routing slot if a mod wants its own settings file without colliding with the game's five.

findings.title: DreamOSDataManager is a second, entirely separate persistence system that the game does not use for saves
findings.detail: Il2CppMichsky.DreamOS.DreamOSDataManager: InitializeProfile(), GetProjectName()->string, GetTempDataPath(DataCategory)->string, ContainsJsonKey(DataCategory,string)->bool, WriteStringData/WriteIntData/WriteFloatData/WriteBooleanData(DataCategory,string,T), ReadStringData/ReadIntData/ReadFloatData/ReadBooleanData(DataCategory,string), DeleteData(DataCategory,string), DeleteDataCategory(DataCategory); fields profileID, subPath, jsonExtension, dataPath. Nested enum DreamOSDataManager/DataCategory = {User, System, Apps, Widgets, Network, DateAndTime}. This is the stock Michsky DreamOS asset-pack store (the same pack supplying the in-game laptop UI — ChatLayoutPreset, MailAttachmentPreset, PhotoGalleryPreset all appear in the build). No DreamOS-authored directory exists under the game's LocalLow folder, and no SaveManager path touches it.
findings.members: DreamOSDataManager, DataCategory, WriteStringData, ReadIntData, GetTempDataPath, profileID, subPath, dataPath
findings.modding: Available as a ready-made, independent JSON key-value store a mod can use without colliding with SaveManager's dirty-file cache — but it writes to its own path derived from profileID/subPath/dataPath, so anything stored there will NOT be captured by a save backup and will NOT follow SaveManager's slot. Runtime probe: log DreamOSDataManager.GetTempDataPath(DataCategory.User) to learn where it actually lands before relying on it.

findings.title: Settings persistence key names are ad-hoc and version-suffixed, indicating repeated schema breakage
findings.detail: Real keys observed in Other.es3 and metadata: "maxfps19823839183jnSliderValue", "maxbulletholes8190241SliderValue", "fovSaveSetting125412SliderValue", "adssfovSaveSetting125412SliderValue", "adszoomsetting", "CurrentUpscalerNew" (=0) alongside "CurrentUpscaler_2026" (=1), "dlssSettingsNew", "lodcrossfade_setting", "cacheModelV2" and "cacheModelV3", "LogErrors", "LoreDisclaimer" (=2), "weaponOffsetX1"/"weaponOffsetY2". The random digit suffixes are cache-busters: rather than migrate a changed setting, the devs mint a new key and abandon the old, which is why both CurrentUpscalerNew and CurrentUpscaler_2026 coexist with contradictory values.
findings.members: maxfps19823839183jnSliderValue, fovSaveSetting125412SliderValue, CurrentUpscalerNew, CurrentUpscaler_2026, cacheModelV2, cacheModelV3, LoreDisclaimer
findings.modding: Never assume a settings key is authoritative — check for a newer suffixed sibling first. A mod that persists its own settings should follow the same convention (its own suffixed key in SaveFileType.Other) to avoid being clobbered by a future game patch reusing a plain name.

findings.title: Interop namespace is Il2CppMichsky.*, NOT Il2Cpp.Michsky.* — anchor every UI regex on this
findings.detail: Il2CppInterop prefixes the ROOT namespace, it does not insert an `Il2Cpp.` package segment. Game types with no namespace become `Il2Cpp.PlayMenu`; asset-pack types keep their namespace and become `Il2CppMichsky.MUIP.ButtonManager`, `Il2CppMichsky.DreamOS.WindowManager`, `Il2CppMichsky.UI.Shift.MainPanelManager`. A run of `.\run.ps1 "^Il2Cpp\.Michsky\."` returns ZERO rows and looks like the pack is absent; `^Il2CppMichsky\.` returns the whole pack. Same rule applies to Mirror (`Il2CppMirror.*`), TMP (`Il2CppTMPro.*`), QC (`Il2CppQFSW.QC.*`). Note also that `all_types.txt` (785 names) only lists the namespace-less `Il2Cpp.*` game types, so no Michsky/TMP type appears there — use `literals.txt`, which stores `namespace|typename` pairs, to enumerate third-party types.
findings.members: Il2CppMichsky.MUIP, Il2CppMichsky.DreamOS, Il2CppMichsky.UI.Shift, Il2CppMichsky.UI.Dark
findings.modding: Prevents an hour of false negatives. Any mod reflecting on UI components must use the Il2CppMichsky prefix; a wrong prefix fails without warning as 'type not found' rather than erroring.

findings.title: Five Michsky UI packs ship; only three are wired. 'Dark - Complete Horror UI' is entirely dead code
findings.detail: script_paths.txt shows Assets\_ui\ containing: Modern UI Pack, DreamOS - Complete OS UI, Shift - Complete Sci-Fi UI, Dark - Complete Horror UI, Loading Screen, Damage indicators. I scanned EVERY game type (`^Il2Cpp\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` across Assembly-CSharp) for members typed as Michsky classes. Result: `Michsky.DreamOS` is referenced by 5 game types, `Michsky.MUIP` by 1 (PlayMenu, 40 members), `Michsky.UI.Shift` by 2 (MenuControllerV2, playerBoardItem). `Michsky.UI.Dark` has ZERO references from any game type — the whole Horror UI pack (MainPanelManager, DropdownManager, QualityManager, SplashScreenManager, UIDissolveEffect, UIParticleRenderer, ScrollRectElement...) is compiled-in dead weight. Also unreferenced by game code: `Michsky.UI.Shift.ServerBrowserManager`, `FriendsPanelManager`, `QuickMatchButton`, and the entire DreamOS app suite (WebBrowserManager, MailManager, MusicPlayerManager, CalculatorManager, GameHubManager, TicTacToe, SpeechRecognition, MessagingManager, BSODManager, SetupManager, ModManager).
findings.members: Il2CppMichsky.UI.Dark.*, Il2CppMichsky.UI.Shift.ServerBrowserManager, Il2CppMichsky.DreamOS.WebBrowserManager
findings.modding: Dark's prefabs/animators are dead but still loadable — a mod can appropriate its widgets without colliding with game code. Conversely, do not assume a Michsky type being present means the game drives it. The unused DreamOS apps are a ready-made surface for a laptop mod (a working web browser / notepad / music player already exists in the build).

findings.title: Three distinct visual languages, one per shell surface — a mod must pick the right pack per screen
findings.detail: Main menu = `Il2Cpp.MenuControllerV2`, styled with the SHIFT pack: `get_mainPanelManager() -> Il2CppMichsky.UI.Shift.MainPanelManager`, and three `Il2CppMichsky.UI.Shift.ChapterButton` fields (primaryWeaponLoadoutButton, secondaryWeaponLoadoutButton, grenadeTacticalWeaponLoadoutButton). Its dropdowns are still raw `Il2CppTMPro.TMP_Dropdown` (MapsDropdown, primaryWeaponDropdown, resolutionDropdown, LevelsDropdown, overallQualitySettings). In-game pause/settings = `Il2Cpp.PlayMenu`, styled with MUIP: 40 fields typed `Il2CppMichsky.MUIP.CustomDropdown` (aaSettings, dofSettings, shadowQualitySettings, UpscalerSettings, waterSettings, ...) plus raw `UnityEngine.UI.Slider` for aoIntensitySlider/camFarPlaneSlider/maxFPS_v. Mission laptop = DreamOS. So the SAME conceptual control (resolution dropdown) is a TMP_Dropdown in MenuControllerV2 and a MUIP CustomDropdown in PlayMenu — both exist and both are live.
findings.members: MenuControllerV2.mainPanelManager, MenuControllerV2.primaryWeaponLoadoutButton, PlayMenu.resolutionDropdown, PlayMenu.overallQualitySettings
findings.modding: Adding a graphics option to the pause menu means instantiating an MUIP CustomDropdown; adding a main-menu panel means a Shift MainPanelManager PanelItem. Mixing them produces a visibly foreign control.

findings.title: Panel registration structs — the exact shape a mod must append to inject a screen
findings.detail: Nested types resolve under `/` in the inspector (`Il2CppMichsky.UI.Shift.MainPanelManager/PanelItem`). Shift `PanelItem` = {string panelName; GameObject panelObject; GameObject buttonObject}. Its manager exposes `OpenPanel(string newPanel)`, `OpenFirstTab()`, `NextPage()`, `PrevPage()`, `get_panels()`, `get_currentPanelIndex()`, and four animator state-name strings `panelFadeIn/panelFadeOut/buttonFadeIn/buttonFadeOut/buttonFadeNormal`. DreamOS `WindowPanelManager/PanelItem` = {string panelName; Animator panelObject; DreamOS.PanelButton panelButton; DreamOS.ButtonManager altPanelButton} with `OpenPanel(string)`, `OpenPanelByIndex(int)`, `NextPanel()`, `PrevPanel()`, `onPanelChanged` (PanelChangeEvent), plus an `indicator` RectTransform driven by `MoveIndicatorToParent(Transform)`/`SetIndicatorHeight(float)`. MUIP `WindowManager/WindowItem` = {string windowName; GameObject windowObject; GameObject buttonObject; GameObject firstSelected} with `OpenWindow(string)`.
findings.members: MainPanelManager/PanelItem{panelName,panelObject,buttonObject}, WindowPanelManager/PanelItem{panelName,panelObject,panelButton,altPanelButton}, WindowManager/WindowItem{windowName,windowObject,buttonObject,firstSelected}
findings.modding: Injection recipe: clone an existing PanelItem's panelObject+buttonObject (inherits fonts, colors, animator controller for free), rewrite panelName, append to the manager's list, then call OpenPanel(yourName). Because lookup is BY STRING, not by index, appending is safe and order-independent — unlike LoadoutManager.Game_Weapons which syncs by index.

findings.title: PlayMenu is a ~150-method god singleton and the single richest hook surface in the shell
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.PlayMenu.get_singleton()` is static. It owns every graphics/audio/gameplay setter, all void and all safely Harmony-patchable (they are methods, not il2cpp field accessors): SetOverallQuality(int), SetShadowCascades/SetSunShadowResolution/SetRealtimeShadows/SetShadowDistance(int), SetGTAOQuality/SetVolumetricQuality/SetFoliageQuality/SetTerrainQuality/SetSSRQuality/SetNVGGIQuality/SetVolumetricCloudQuality/SetCharacterMeshQuality/SetMeshDetailDistance(int), SetUpscaler/SetUpscalerQuality/SetDLSSpreset/SetCameraAA(int), SetFOV/SetADSFOV/SetNVGFOV(float), SetWeaponOffsetX/Y/Z(float), SetHunchControl(float), SetSensitivity(float) AND SetSensitivity(string) (two overloads — patch the wrong one and nothing fires), SetVolume/SetMusicVolume/SetAIVolume/SetVoiceChatVolume(float), Linear01ToDb(float)->float, plus seven presets SetUltraSettings()...SetUltraLowSettings(). Shell control: `OpenSubmenu(string submenuName)`, `AllSubMenus` (GameObject[]), `SetUiCanvasGroupEnabled(bool)`, `UICanvasGroup`, `MainWindow`, `CloseMenu()`, `ToggleCursorLogic()/EnableCursorLogic()/DisableCursorLogic()/UnlockCursor()`, `EnableAdvancedOptions()/DisableAdvancedOptions()` gating an `advancedOptions` GameObject[]. Also `operationsUI -> Il2Cpp.OperationsUI` and `menuController -> Il2Cpp.MenuControllerV2` back-references. Console integration: `SetConsoleLoggingLevel(Il2CppQFSW.QC.LoggingThreshold)`.
findings.members: PlayMenu.singleton, OpenSubmenu(string), AllSubMenus, SetUiCanvasGroupEnabled(bool), advancedOptions, SetSensitivity overloads
findings.modding: Cleanest mod-settings injection: clone a submenu GameObject, append to AllSubMenus, then drive it with OpenSubmenu("YourName"). Cursor state is centralized in ToggleCursorLogic/EnableCursorLogic — a mod window must go through these or it will fight the game for the cursor. I cannot see bodies, so whether OpenSubmenu matches on GameObject.name or a serialized label is unproven: probe at runtime by dumping AllSubMenus[i].name and comparing to a string that OpenSubmenu accepts.

findings.title: Il2Cpp.KeyboardManager is a completely empty stub — the real rebinding system is InputLayer/InputKey
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.KeyboardManager` exposes ONLY `.cctor`, `.ctor()` and `.ctor(nint)`. No fields, no methods, no properties. It is a dead type. The live system is `Il2Cpp.InputLayer`: `GetKey(Il2Cpp.InputKey key, bool ActivatedThisFrame) -> bool`, `LoadKeyBinds()`, `SaveAllKeyBinds()`, `SaveSingleKeybind(InputKey)`, `SetSingleKeybind(InputKey, InputKeyBind)`, `GetConflictedBinds() -> List<InputKey>`, `ResetAllKeyBinds()`, `ResetSingleKeyBind(InputKey)`, `SetupDefaultBinds()`, `ConfigureAllBindTypes()`, plus `Keybinds` (Dictionary<InputKey, InputKeyBindInstance>), `DefaultActions` (Dictionary<InputKey, InputKeyBind>), `Binds`/`SingleKeyBinds`/`DoubleKeyBinds` arrays, `KeyBindNames` (string[]), `NumKeyBinds`, `MouseSensitivity`, `DoubleClickCoolDown`, and static-ish state `MouseMovement`, `MouseMovementUnscaled`, `MouseInputSuppressed`, `InputDisabled`, `CheckMouseInputSuppressed()`. The `InputKey` enum has ~89 members including 8 ATAK entries (OpenATAK, ATAKZoomIn/Out, ATAKZoomCycleFLIR, ATAKZoomMoveUp/Down/Left/Right, ATAKDropBomb), NVGGainIncrease/Decrease, Vault, Kick, FreeLean, HoldBreath, ScopeZeroUp/Down, ReticleBrightnessIncrease/Decrease. The rebind ROW widget is `Il2Cpp.KeybindAssignment`: StartListening(), AssignKeybind(), SaveKeybind(), GetKeyPressed()/GetSecondKeyPressed() -> KeyCode, SetPressType(int)/SetPressTypeHoldOrToggle(int)/SetPressTypeContinuousOrToggle(int), ResetKeyBind(), and three background GameObjects Dark/Light/ConflictBackground. Also legacy and separate: `Il2Cpp.Keybind{action:string, keyCode:KeyCode}` and `Il2Cpp.Binding{Key:KeyCode, Command:string}` (the latter is Quantum Console command binding).
findings.members: InputLayer.GetKey(InputKey,bool), InputLayer.Keybinds, InputKey (89 values), KeybindAssignment.StartListening, InputLayer.InputDisabled
findings.modding: A mod adding a keybind should extend the InputLayer dictionary rather than polling UnityEngine.Input, so it inherits conflict detection (GetConflictedBinds) and the InputDisabled/MouseInputSuppressed gating that stops input leaking while a UI is open. InputKey is a plain int enum, so a mod can use an unused high value, but SetupDefaultBinds/LoadKeyBinds likely iterate the enum — confirm at runtime whether an out-of-range InputKey survives LoadKeyBinds() or throws.

findings.title: Settings persist through SaveManager (ES3 + Steam Cloud, slotted), not PlayerPrefs — with a one-shot migration
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.SaveManager` is the settings backend: `GetFloat/SetFloat`, `GetInt/SetInt`, `GetString/SetString`, `HasKey(string)`, `DeleteKey(string)`, `FlushDirtyFiles()`, `EnsureFileLoaded(string)`, `GetFilePath(SaveFileType)`, plus Steam Cloud generics `SaveSteamStorage<T>(string key, T value, SaveFileType)` / `LoadSteamStorage<T>(string key, SaveFileType, T defaultValue)` / `HasSteamKey` / `DeleteSteamKey`. Nested enum `Il2Cpp.SaveManager/SaveFileType` = {Other, GameProgression, PlayerSettings, AudioSettings, Controls, KeyBinds}. Save slots exist: `CurrentSaveSlot`, `SetSaveFile(int saveID)`, `GetSlotPrefix()`, `DeleteCurrentSave()`, `SaveLoadout<T>(key, value, int slot)`, plus migrations `MigrateToSavesDirectory()` and `MigrateRootFilesToSlot0()`. Corruption handling: `IsLocalFileCorrupted(string)`, `IsAllNullBytes(byte[])`. Separately `Il2Cpp.PlayerPrefsMigration.MigrateAll()` with TryMigrateKeyInt/Float/String(string key, SaveFileType) and TryMigrateLoadoutKeyInt/String(oldKey, newKey, slot) — i.e. the game USED to be on PlayerPrefs and moved to ES3. PlayMenu's ~40 `Key_*` static string properties (Key_vSync, Key_AAMode, Key_MasterVolume, Key_PlayerSens, Key_TextureQuality, Key_DLSSPreset, Key_WeaponOffsetX, Key_AdvancedSettings, Key_FPSCounter, Key_LogErrors ...) are the key names fed to these.
findings.members: SaveManager.SetFloat/GetFloat, SaveManager/SaveFileType, PlayerPrefsMigration.MigrateAll, PlayMenu.Key_*
findings.modding: A mod's settings should go through SaveManager.SetFloat/SetInt with a namespaced key so they land in the correct ES3 file and ride Steam Cloud, and must call FlushDirtyFiles() (writes are buffered — a mod that only Sets and never Flushes will without warning lose data on a hard exit). Do NOT write PlayerPrefs: it is the legacy path and PlayerPrefsMigration only migrates a fixed key list.

findings.title: Localization is Unity's Localization package with 10 locales; DreamOS's own localization system is dead
findings.detail: catalog_strings.txt shows Addressable groups `localization-locales`, `localization-assets-shared`, and ten `localization-string-tables-<lang>(<code>)_assets_all_<hash>.bundle` entries: en, de, es, fr, ja, ko, pl, pt, ru, zh-Hans. The binder is `Il2Cpp.LocalizationTMPEvent`: `StringReference` (UnityEngine.Localization.LocalizedString), `TMP` (TextMeshProUGUI), `SetNewStringReference(LocalizedString)`, `HandleStringChanged(string localizedValue)`, `LocaleChanged(UnityEngine.Localization.Locale)`, `OnUpdateString` (UnityEventString), plus two layout-repair members `FixLayout()` and `TryUpdateFont()` and a coroutine `updateParent()`. Meanwhile `Il2CppMichsky.DreamOS.LocalizedObject` / `LocalizationManager` / `LocalizationSettings` / `LocalizationTable` / `LocalizationLanguage` are all present with a full API (GetKeyOutput(key), GetKeyOutput(tableID, tableKey), GetKeyOutputAudio, GetKeyOutputSprite, CheckLocalizationStatus, RebuildLayout) but are referenced by NO game type. UI text fields on game components come in two flavours: localized ones are typed `Il2Cpp.LocalizationTMPEvent` (MissionLaptop.OperationBriefingText, OperationBoardUI.SituationReportText, OperationSelectionUI.NameTextBox/SecondTextBox/ThirdTextBox), non-localized ones are raw `Il2CppTMPro.TextMeshProUGUI`.
findings.members: LocalizationTMPEvent.StringReference, LocalizationTMPEvent.TryUpdateFont, UnityEngine.Localization.LocalizedString
findings.modding: To add localized mod text, attach a LocalizationTMPEvent and set StringReference — this also gets you TryUpdateFont, which matters because CJK locales swap the TMP font asset; a mod that sets TMP.text directly will render tofu in ja/ko/zh. Registering a new string table requires the Unity Localization runtime, not the DreamOS tables.

findings.title: MissionLaptop is a three-class split with a shared, fully networked UI state singleton (19 SyncVars)
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.MissionLaptop` = per-laptop instance: `AccessLaptop(PlayerNetworking)` / `ExitLaptop()`, `SpawnOperations()`, `SpawnTargetPackages(CerebusOperation)`, `SpawnTargetPackagePlanning(CerebusOpboard)`, `AppMinimizedStatusChanged(bool)`, and DreamOS wiring: `CerebusWindow`/`NotepadWindow` (DreamOS.WindowManager), `cerberusWindowPanelManager` (DreamOS.WindowPanelManager), `computerManager` (DreamOS.WorldSpaceManager), `desktopDragger` (DreamOS.ItemDragContainer), `uiRaycaster` (GraphicRaycaster), `osCanvas`, `LaptopPlayerCamera`, `PlayerBlocker`, `ShitToKillWhenNotUsing` (GameObject[]), `timeBeforeExit`/`_timerBeforeExit`, and content transforms ActiveOperationsList / SimulationOperationList / TargetPackageParent / opBoardParent. `Il2Cpp.MissionLaptopDisplayer` = the view (SetCurrentPage, SetSimulationPage, SetMinimized, SpawnTargetPackages, SpawnOperationBoard, SetOpBoardInfo, ToggleFullscreenMap, SetMissionStarting) holding SelectedOperation/SelectedTargetPackage/OpBoardUI. `Il2Cpp.MissionLaptopNetworkState` = a singleton (`get_instance`) with `AllMissionLaptops` (List<MissionLaptopDisplayer>) and 19 SyncVars each with a hook: CerebusMinimized, CurrentLaptopPage, OnSimulationPage, SelectedOperationLocked, CurrentSelectedOperation, SelectedTargetPackageLocked, SelectedTargetPackageSimulation, CurrentSelectedTargetPackage, ShowingSimulationOperation, ActiveInfilMask (long bitmask!), CurrentSelectedInfilTime, CurrentSelectedPrepTime, FullscreenImage, SelectedEnemyCount, SelectedHVTEnemyCount, SelectedDifficulty, HVTSpawnType, PVPParameter1, PVPParameter2, ShowingStartMissionConfirmation. Infil selection is a 64-bit mask: `SetInfilActive(int index, bool)`, `IsInfilActive(int)`, `SetAllInfilsActive()`, `OnActiveInfilMaskChanged(long previous, long current)`.
findings.members: MissionLaptopNetworkState.instance, ActiveInfilMask (long), OnActiveInfilMaskChanged, MissionLaptop.CerebusWindow, MissionLaptopDisplayer.SpawnOperationBoard
findings.modding: Every laptop in the level shows the SAME state — this is a shared planning screen, not per-player UI. A mod must not mutate MissionLaptopDisplayer directly; go through MissionLaptopNetworkState setters (SetCurrentPage, SetSelectedInfilTime, SetDifficulty...) or clients desync. Hook the `On*Changed(previous, current)` hooks for the receive side. The long ActiveInfilMask caps a map at 64 infils.

findings.title: LaptopWindowNetworkNotify is the exact bridge pattern for networking a DreamOS window — copy it
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.LaptopWindowNetworkNotify` holds `Window -> Il2CppMichsky.DreamOS.WindowManager` and `missionLaptop -> Il2Cpp.MissionLaptop`, with `Reset()`, `Awake()`, `OnDestroy()` and four handlers `OnOpen()`, `OnClose()`, `OnMinimize()`, `OnMaximize()`. DreamOS.WindowManager exposes exactly four matching UnityEvents: `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onMinimize`, `onFullscreen`. The Awake/OnDestroy pair is the subscribe/unsubscribe. WindowManager's own API is `OpenWindow()`, `CloseWindow()`, `MinimizeWindow()`, `FullscreenWindow()`, `FocusToWindow()`, `InitializeWindow()`, with state readbacks `isOn`, `isNormalized`, `isFullscreen`, `isNavbarOpen`, and layout config windowContainer/windowContent/navbarRect/windowDragger/resizePreset/minWindowSize/useBackgroundBlur/hasNavDrawer/minNavbarWidth/maxNavbarWidth/navbarCurve.
findings.members: LaptopWindowNetworkNotify.OnOpen/OnClose/OnMinimize/OnMaximize, DreamOS.WindowManager.onOpen/onClose/onMinimize/onFullscreen
findings.modding: A mod adding its own laptop app should mirror this: instantiate a DreamOS WindowManager-based window and attach a notify component subscribing the four UnityEvents in Awake and unsubscribing in OnDestroy. Note the game's handler is named OnMaximize but the event is onFullscreen — the naming does not line up.

findings.title: CerebusUiBase is the designed extension point for laptop list entries (virtual, with click/double-click)
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.CerebusUiBase`: `CreateInstance(UnityEngine.Transform parent, Il2Cpp.MissionLaptop laptop)`, then overridable `OnCreated()`, `OnUpdate()`, `OnClick()`, `OnSingleClick()`, `OnDoubleClick()`, with click disambiguation state `clickcount`, `clickcountTime`, `clickcountTimer`, and a `lastFrameUpdate` int (an explicit once-per-frame guard). It holds `missionLaptop` and `UI -> Il2Cpp.OperationSelectionUI`. `Il2Cpp.OperationSelectionUI` is the concrete row: NameTextBox/SecondTextBox/ThirdTextBox/SimulationTypeText (all LocalizationTMPEvent), RegionNameTextBox (raw TMP), `EnemyCountSetByUser` (LocalizedString), and two gating overlays `ClassfiedCover` and `RegionCover` (note the misspelling 'Classfied'). Source path is Assets\Prefabs\1_OPERATIONS\CerebusUiBase.cs — it lives with the prefabs, not in Scripts.
findings.members: CerebusUiBase.CreateInstance(Transform,MissionLaptop), OnSingleClick, OnDoubleClick, OperationSelectionUI.ClassfiedCover
findings.modding: This is the cheapest way to add a custom entry to the laptop's operations list. Whether a mod can subclass it is the open question — subclassing an il2cpp MonoBehaviour requires registering a managed type with Il2CppInterop (ClassInjector), and the virtual dispatch must reach managed code. Runtime probe: register a subclass via ClassInjector.RegisterTypeInIl2Cpp, AddComponent it, and verify OnCreated fires. If injection fails, the fallback is Harmony-patching OperationSelectionUI.OnClick and branching on a marker component.

findings.title: CERBERUS_OPBOARD is a dead legacy twin of OperationBoardUI (uppercase vs CamelCase naming split)
findings.detail: Two parallel opboards exist. `Il2Cpp.OperationBoardUI` is live: `Setup(CerebusOpboard opboard, MissionLaptop laptop)`, and it drives the full modern parameter set — SetAI_COUNT, SetAI_HVT_COUNT, SetHVTSpawnPoint, SetOpforDifficulty, SetPVPTimeLimit, SetPVPRoundLimit, SetFFATimeLimit, SetFFAKillLimit, SetPVPParam1/2, InfilTargetButtonPressed(int,bool), SetActiveInfilsMaskUI(long), ExecuteOperationButtonPressed, EnableConfirmationMenu, StartOperationButton, AbortOperationButtonPressed, EnterFullscreenButton/ExitFullscreenButton — with widgets typed DreamOS.HorizontalSelector (x9), DreamOS.SliderManager (x3), DreamOS.ModalWindowManager (ConfirmationWindow), plus MapInfilMarkers[] and FullscreenMapInfilMarkers[]. `Il2Cpp.CERBERUS_OPBOARD` is the older sibling: only SwitchToActiveOperation, SwitchToSimulationOperation, SetInfiltrationTime, SetInfiltrationTarget, SetPreparationTarget, SetOpforDifficulty, SetAI_COUNT, Start_Operation — no PVP, no FFA, no HVT, no infil mask, no fullscreen map. It has its own three HorizontalSelectors and a `missionLaptop` ref, plus `isLocked`/`unlockCode` and `TARGETPACKAGE -> TARGETPACKAGE_DETAILS[]`. No live UI type references it.
findings.members: OperationBoardUI.Setup(CerebusOpboard,MissionLaptop), OperationBoardUI.SetActiveInfilsMaskUI(long), CERBERUS_OPBOARD.Start_Operation, CERBERUS_OPBOARD.unlockCode
findings.modding: Target OperationBoardUI, not CERBERUS_OPBOARD — a mod wired to the legacy class will compile and find the type but never receive callbacks. The uppercase-underscore names (CERBERUS_OPBOARD, TARGETPACKAGE_DETAILS, CERBERUS_OPERATION) are the v1 generation; CamelCase (CerebusOpboard, CerebusOperation, CerebusTargetPackage) is v2. Whether CERBERUS_OPBOARD prefabs still exist in any shipped scene is unprovable statically — probe with FindObjectsOfTypeAll(CERBERUS_OPBOARD) once, at scene load, never per frame.

findings.title: HintManager.SpawnPopup is the zero-asset way for a mod to show styled UI text, and it has a networked twin
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.HintManager` has a static `get_singleton()` and `SpawnPopup(string _popupText, PopupType _popupType, bool spamDelay, bool slient)` plus `hintPopup` (prefab GameObject), `hintPopupParent` (Transform), and rate-limit state `spamTimer`/`spamTime`. `PopupType` is nested in `Il2Cpp.Popup` — `Il2Cpp.Popup/PopupType` = {YellowWarning, RedWarning}. The `Il2Cpp.Popup` prefab component has `SetPopup(string _popupText, PopupType _popupType)`, `Fadeout()` coroutine, `canvasGroup`, `popupText` (TMP), `FadeTime`, an `audioSource` with `RedSound`/`YellowSound` clips, and two mutually-exclusive GameObjects amusingly named `YellowTelliTubby` and `RedTelliTubby`. There is also a SERVER-driven variant on `Il2Cpp.ExfilZone`: `RPCHint(string message, PopupType type)` (broadcast) and `TargetHint(NetworkConnectionToClient conn, string message, PopupType type)` (single client), with the usual UserCode_/InvokeUserCode_ pair.
findings.members: HintManager.singleton.SpawnPopup(string,PopupType,bool,bool), Il2Cpp.Popup/PopupType{YellowWarning,RedWarning}, ExfilZone.RPCHint, ExfilZone.TargetHint
findings.modding: One call gives a mod on-brand feedback with correct fonts, colors and SFX — no prefab, no bundle, no Shader.Find rebinding. The `slient` (sic) bool suppresses audio and `spamDelay` engages the shared rate limiter. For server-authoritative mod messages, ExfilZone's RPCHint/TargetHint is the only existing hint RPC in the build; a mod wanting its own needs its own NetworkBehaviour, or can Harmony-patch UserCode_RPCHint on the receive side.

findings.title: OnScreenNotification is a separate HUD text channel with four independent lines and a shake effect
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.OnScreenNotification` exposes a static-style `get_CurrentInstance()` and four setters: `SetMagCheckString(string)`, `SetLaserString(string)`, `SetFlashlightString(string)`, `SetNotifcationString(string)` (sic — 'Notifcation'), plus `SetNotificationShake(float magnitude, float speed)` and `EnableThisThing()`. Each channel has its own alpha and enabled flag (MagCheckAlpha/LaserTextAlpha/FlashTextAlpha, MagCheckEnabled/LaserEnabled/FlashlightEnabled) and its own TMP object (MagCheckText/FlashLightText/LaserText), driven by a shared `TextDuration` and `FadeCurve` (AnimationCurve). Shake state is InitialShakeStrength/ShakeStrength/ShakeSpeed with `flashlightInitialPosition` cached as a Vector3. A master flag `ShowFlashlightsAndLasers` gates two of the channels — this is what PlayMenu's EnableUI_WeaponNotifcations()/DisableUI_WeaponNotifcations() and Key_WeaponNotification toggle.
findings.members: OnScreenNotification.CurrentInstance, SetNotifcationString(string), SetNotificationShake(float,float), ShowFlashlightsAndLasers
findings.modding: This is the in-world HUD channel (weapon state feedback), distinct from HintManager's popup channel (warnings). A mod reporting weapon/equipment state should use SetNotifcationString to sit in the right place visually. Note the misspelled method name — reflection by string will fail on the correct spelling.

findings.title: There is an ATAK tablet HUD app, and its screen still uses legacy UnityEngine.UI.Text rather than TMP
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.Tablet` is the held device: `StartInteraction()`, `ResumeInteraction()`, FinalIK integration (`leftHand -> Il2CppRootMotion.FinalIK.InteractionObject`, `interactionSystem -> InteractionSystem`), an `animator` plus six animator state-name strings (Enable, Disable, ZoomInHold, ZoomInRelease, ZoomOutHold, ZoomOutRelease), button handlers PushZoomInHoldButton/ReleaseZoomInReleaseButton/PushZoomOutHoldButton/ReleaseZoomOutReleaseButton/PushFireButton/PushFLIRSwitchButton, foley coroutines PlayJoystickFoley(float)/PlayButtonFoley(float), network smoothing (`smoothSpeed`, `syncTime`, `syncTimer`, `joystickBlend` Vector2), and `ATAK_ScreenParent` (Transform). `Il2Cpp.AtakScreen` is the display: `NorthRotation`/`NorthRotationChild` (Transform), `CompassHeading` typed **UnityEngine.UI.Text** — not TextMeshPro — and `ISRparent`/`NoISRparent` GameObjects. `Il2Cpp.atakMarker` is a billboard marker with `keepRotation` and OnEnable/OnDisable registration. Eight InputKey enum entries are dedicated to it (OpenATAK, ATAKZoomIn/Out, ATAKZoomCycleFLIR, ATAKZoomMoveUp/Down/Left/Right, ATAKDropBomb).
findings.members: Il2Cpp.Tablet, AtakScreen.CompassHeading (UnityEngine.UI.Text), atakMarker.keepRotation, InputKey.ATAKDropBomb
findings.modding: ATAKDropBomb implies a fire-support feature reachable from the tablet — a strong mod hook. The uGUI Text on the compass means the ATAK screen predates the TMP conversion and will not pick up the localization font swap; a mod adding ATAK text must decide whether to match (uGUI Text) or fix (TMP). ISRparent/NoISRparent suggests an ISR (drone feed) mode that is toggled by presence of an asset — whether it is reachable in shipped content is unprovable statically; probe by enabling ISRparent at runtime.

findings.title: MenuController (v1) is a live-weaved but superseded Mirror NetworkBehaviour built on raw uGUI
findings.detail: Fully dumped in D:\OperatorHSR\re\interop_seam.txt lines 303-390. `Il2Cpp.MenuController` is a NetworkBehaviour with SyncVars operationValue/maxPlayersValue/maxBotValue (Network* accessors + SerializeSyncVars/DeserializeSyncVars) and two commands `CMDselectPlayerMaxAmount(float)` and `CMDselect_operation(string selected_operation, int i_dropdown)` with UserCode_/InvokeUserCode_ pairs — so it IS weaved and would function. Its widgets are entirely vanilla: pWeaponDropdown/sWeaponDropdown/grenadeDropdown/operationSelectionDropdown (TMP_Dropdown), startButton/prepareOpButton (UnityEngine.UI.Button), maxPlayersSlider/maxBotSlider (UnityEngine.UI.Slider), maxPlayers_t/maxBot_t (TMP_Text). Scene-mode flags `isLobby_Scene`/`isMissionPrep_Scene`. It is superseded by MenuControllerV2 (Shift-styled) + MenuControllerV2_Sync (which carries the equivalent SyncVars selectedOperation/maxPlayers/expectedEnemies). MenuControllerV2 additionally reaches into `menuController_Sync -> Il2Cpp.PlayerMaster`, i.e. the v2 sync path routes through PlayerMaster, not through MenuControllerV2_Sync alone.
findings.members: MenuController.CMDselect_operation(string,int), MenuControllerV2_Sync.selectedOperation, MenuControllerV2.menuController_Sync -> PlayerMaster
findings.modding: Do not patch MenuController expecting main-menu behaviour. Because it is weaved, a stale prefab could still instantiate — confirm which of MenuController / MenuControllerV2 / OfflineMenuController is actually alive per scene with a single FindObjectsOfTypeAll sweep at scene load. OfflineMenuController is a third variant (startHost_KCP/startHost_Steam as coroutines, Init(bool state)) used for the offline path.

findings.title: Michsky widgets in this build carry no shared theming asset — clone prefabs, do not construct widgets
findings.detail: `Il2CppMichsky.MUIP.ButtonManager` exposes SetText(string), SetIcon(Sprite), Interactable(bool), UpdateUI(), Initialize(), AddUINavigation(), CreateRipple(Vector2), the full pointer/submit interface (OnPointerClick/Down/Enter/Exit, OnSelect, OnDeselect, OnSubmit), state coroutines SetNormal/SetHighlight/SetDisabled, LayoutFix(), and data buttonText/buttonIcon/normalText/highlightedText (TextMeshProUGUI)/enableText/enableIcon/onClick/onHover (UnityEvent)/useCustomContent/useCustomIconSize/useCustomTextSize/useUINavigation/checkForDoubleClick/animationSolution. Crucially there is NO `UIManagerAsset` property on ButtonManager, CustomDropdown, SliderManager, SwitchManager, HorizontalSelector, WindowManager, ModalWindowManager or NotificationManager in this build — colors/fonts are not pulled from a shared ScriptableObject by the widget itself. script_paths.txt confirms the separate applier components exist (Modern UI Pack\Scripts\UI Manager\UIManagerButton.cs, UIManagerSlider.cs, UIManagerSwitch.cs, UIManagerDropdown.cs, UIManagerHSelector.cs, UIManagerWindowManager.cs, UIManagerFontChanger.cs, UIManagerColorChanger.cs). Other useful APIs: CustomDropdown.CreateNewItem(string title, Sprite icon, ...) and CreateNewItem(string title, bool notify), RemoveItem(string, bool notify), SetDropdownIndex(int), ChangeDropdownInfo(int), UpdateItemLayout(), onValueChanged (DropdownEvent), items/index/isOn; HorizontalSelector.CreateNewItem(string)/CreateNewItem(string, Sprite)/RemoveItem(string)/NextItem()/PreviousItem()/UpdateUI()/UpdateIndicators()/defaultIndex/index/onValueChanged (SelectorEvent).
findings.members: MUIP.ButtonManager.SetText/SetIcon/UpdateUI, CustomDropdown.CreateNewItem, HorizontalSelector.CreateNewItem, UIManagerButton (component, not property)
findings.modding: The reliable recipe is Instantiate an existing in-scene widget, then call SetText/SetIcon/CreateNewItem and rewire onClick — the clone brings the UIManagerX applier, animator controller, ripple prefab and sprites with it. Building a ButtonManager from AddComponent on a bare GameObject will render unstyled because the applier component and its serialized references are absent. This also sidesteps the known constraint that AssetBundle-loaded materials lose their shader binding. Always call UpdateUI() after mutating data — most of these widgets only refresh on OnEnable/Initialize.

findings.title: PanelManager is Unity's stock UI-sample class, vestigial; QuickStartGuide/ToggleHelpUI are copy-paste twins
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.PanelManager` is verbatim the old Unity Standard Assets UI sample: `initiallyOpen` (Animator), `m_OpenParameterId` (int), `m_Open` (Animator), `m_PreviouslySelected` (GameObject), constants `k_OpenTransitionName` and `k_ClosedStateName`, with OpenPanel(Animator), CloseCurrent(), FindFirstEnabledSelectable(GameObject), SetSelected(GameObject), DisablePanelDeleyed(Animator) coroutine (sic, 'Deleyed'). Nothing in the game's own menu stack (MenuControllerV2 / PlayMenu / MissionLaptop) references it — they use Shift MainPanelManager, PlayMenu.AllSubMenus and DreamOS WindowPanelManager respectively. Separately, `Il2Cpp.QuickStartGuide` (allCategories GameObject[], SelectCategory(string), CloseMenu(), isOpen, canvasGroup, playerMaster) and `Il2Cpp.ToggleHelpUI` (canvasGroup) share an identical, identically-named pair of members `SetStateNerd()` and `enabledShit` — the same toggle logic pasted into two classes. PlayMenu.StartQuickStartGuide() drives the former.
findings.members: PanelManager.k_OpenTransitionName, PanelManager.DisablePanelDeleyed, QuickStartGuide.SetStateNerd, ToggleHelpUI.enabledShit
findings.modding: Ignore PanelManager. QuickStartGuide.SelectCategory(string) + allCategories is a clean, string-keyed place to append mod documentation pages into the existing help UI with no new chrome.

findings.title: Laptops are world-space DreamOS canvases with per-laptop Cinemachine cameras; the projector re-renders one to a RenderTexture
findings.detail: The runtime scene dump D:\OperatorHSR\re\runtime_dump\scene_tree.txt shows the repeated structure at lines 1647-1701: each `Mission Laptop*` root has children `LaptopFixed (15) > LaptopScreen`, a `Cinemachine Camera` (with its own Global Volume and a screen-space Canvas child), `World Space Resources (90s) > [World Space Manager, ------------------, DreamOS Canvas]`, and a `PlayerBlocker`. Four variants are present in that scene (Mission Laptop, Mission Laptop_2, Mission Laptop Screen Variant, Mission Laptop Screen Variant_1 with active=False, plus a 'crackable screen lol' object). Separately, `Il2Cpp.LaptopProjector` is a Mirror NetworkBehaviour with SyncVar `ProjectorActive` + hook `OnProjectorToggled(bool previous, bool current)`, `CMD_Toggle()`, `Interacted()`, `SetProjectorActive()`, and rendering fields sourceCanvas (Canvas), uiCam (Camera), rt/spotRT (RenderTexture), OutputMaterial + two material property names MaterialProperty/MaterialProperty2, AreaLight + SpotLight (Light), opacity, DisableWhenNotActive (GameObject[]), meshRenderersToSet (Renderer[]).
findings.members: LaptopProjector.CMD_Toggle, LaptopProjector.sourceCanvas/uiCam/rt, MissionLaptop.osCanvas, DreamOS Canvas
findings.modding: UI added to the laptop must be parented under the DreamOS Canvas (world-space) and will be picked up by MissionLaptop.uiRaycaster — a screen-space canvas will not raycast there. The projector path re-renders sourceCanvas through uiCam into a RenderTexture blitted onto OutputMaterial, so a mod's laptop UI automatically appears on the projected surface too, but only if it is under sourceCanvas and its layer is in uiCam's culling mask.

findings.title: Remaining shell pieces: infil map, scoreboard rows, loading screen and armory panels
findings.detail: `Il2Cpp.InfilSelectorDisplayer` (singleton via get_instance) is the deploy/extract map: SpawnMap(GameObject mapPrefab), SetInfilEnabled(int,bool), ShowInfilSelection(), CloseInfilSelection(), UpdateMarkers(int), RequestInfilIndex(int)->bool, EnableExfilMode(), SERVER_SetCanExtract(bool) + RPC_CanExtract(), SetInfilConfirmText/SetExfilConfirmText(string), with a pooled icon system (playerIconPool Stack<GameObject>, playerIconsActive List<GameObject>, GetMapIconFromPool(), RefreshPlayerIcons(), playerIconsDirty flag, work done in LateUpdate) and MapInfilMarkers[]. `Il2Cpp.playerBoardItem` is the scoreboard/lobby row — a NetworkBehaviour with SyncVar hooks OnNameChanged/OnSteamIDChanged/OnPingDisplayChanged/OnKillsChanged/OnDeathsChanged/OnPointsChanged/OnTeamKillsChanged/OnIntelPickupChanged/OnHVTKilledChanged/OnPlayerMasterChanged, admin actions KickPlayer/BanPlayer/SERVER_KickPlayer/SERVER_BanPlayer/TARGETRPC_SetDisconnectReason(NetworkConnection, string), voice controls MutePlayer(bool)/SetPlayerVolume(float), SelectTeam(int), SetPFP(ulong), and a `switchState -> Il2CppMichsky.UI.Shift.SwitchManager`. `Il2Cpp.bl_LoadingScreenUI` is the Lovatto loading screen (SceneNameText/DescriptionText/ProgressText/TipText all legacy UnityEngine.UI.Text, cacheTips List<string>, cacheBackgrounds List<Sprite>, TipsLoop() coroutine, UpdateLoadProgress(float,float), TransitionToScene(), SetupUIForScene(bl_SceneLoaderInfo)). Armory: `Il2Cpp.MagManagerUI` (InitializeMagManager, AddMagToPouch(string magName, string magAmmo, string[] modParentNames, string[] ModNames), AddGrenadeToPouch(string), RefillAllMags, RefreshMags, ClearAllMags/ClearAllGrenades) and `Il2Cpp.ModUI` (Init(WeaponModParent, WeaponModding), AddAttachment(int), AddAttachmentActual(int index, bool UpdateString, bool notifyOthers), AddRandomAttachment(bool includeNone), SetAttachmentOffset(float), ToggleCollapse/SetCollapsable/CalculateCollapsed(bool), AddMagazineToPouch). Also present: HighScoreUI, LeaderBoardPlayer, SteamLeaderBoard, ChatController (TMP_InputField + TMP_Text + Scrollbar, AddToChatOutput(string)), HoverTooltip, DamageIndicator, CursorLock/CursorLockHide, HealthUI (throttled by bpmUIupdateTimer/_uiUpdateTimer, Parts -> HealthUIPartGFX[]).
findings.members: InfilSelectorDisplayer.instance, playerBoardItem.TARGETRPC_SetDisconnectReason, MagManagerUI.AddMagToPouch, ModUI.AddAttachmentActual, bl_LoadingScreenUI.cacheTips
findings.modding: bl_LoadingScreenUI.cacheTips is a List<string> a mod can append to for free branding on every load. ModUI.AddAttachmentActual's `notifyOthers` bool is the network-suppression flag — a mod applying a saved build should pass false while batching and notify once, matching the loadout-preset pattern. InfilSelectorDisplayer pools icons, so a mod must return icons to playerIconPool rather than Destroy them.
